I had granted them in this spirit of sincerity, so that this happiness might be perpetual for them, who are now wretched only in this, that by the ambition of some they are prevented from enjoying the goods offered them.

units.la: Unde nec dubito futurum aliquando ) cum ita Deo visum fuerit ) ut fideles & depurati affectus populi mei eos obsequii & amoris [?] fructus mihi vel saltem posteris meis retri-buere invicem contendant, ut hinc abunde compensetur, quantum illis confisus, quanta pi-[?] illis passus fuerim, quæ (Deum Testem appello) nec pauca nec exigua, nec brevi tempore fuerunt: ex hac orta fiducia præcipue, quod existimarem non posse me hominem [?] professione sua subditis meis, cæteroquin singularem quandam Religionem. & austeram pietatem professis, vel nimia Indulgere, vel nimis parum diffidere.
units.tr: Hence I do not doubt that it will one day come about (when it has pleased God) that the faithful and purified affections of my people will strive among themselves to render to me, or at least to my posterity, the fruits of obedience and love. In this way what I trusted them with, and how much I suffered for them (which, I call God to witness, were neither few nor slight, nor of short duration), may be abundantly repaid. This confidence arose chiefly from my thinking that I could not, being a man, either indulge too much or distrust too little subjects who professed a singular religion and a stern piety.

units.la: Summa vero omnium Injuria est, quâ me alii odiosè onerant, quasi Ipse perversâ quadam voluntate, in me & populum meum Calamitates has omnes accersivissem, dum (quod illi magna fiduciâ sed, Deum testor, falsò afflicerant) adversus hoc Comitiorum per me factum stabilimentum fremens & indignabundus, vi posteà & professâ hostilitate conabar infeinfectum reddere quod jam Regio assensu confirmaveram. Equidem inconsiderati valde animi, vel extremæ potius amentiæ fuisset ligare manus meas iis ipsis Rogantibus, in quos mox eram gladium districturus. Novit Deus Me, licet non sine sensu hujus injuriæ fuerim, haud tamen tam atrocem concepisse, ut bello omnino persequendam ducerem; Nec enim statim impellebar, (quod postea evenit) alios mihi porro injurias inferre, cùm Isti candidè collatam hanc Gratiam, haud eodem candore administrarent. Tumultus revera qui tunc vigebant, omnia Gratiæ Indulta violare & in lasciviam corrumpere minabantur. Arbitrabar tamen nec sine argumento ipsos proprios Eorum terrores qui pravis suis & vere Dæmoniacis artibus Turbulentos hos Spiritus excitârant, eosdem denuò abigere, & demergere penitus hortaturos.
units.tr: But the greatest injustice of all is that others burden me with hateful charges, as if I myself, by some perverse will, had brought all these calamities upon myself and my people; when, fuming and indignant against this enactment of the assembly confirmed by me, I tried by force and by open hostility to undo what I had already confirmed with my royal assent. Indeed, it would have been a sign of a rash mind, or rather of utmost madness, to bind my own hands in the presence of those very men against whom I was soon to draw the sword. God knows that, although I was not without a sense of this injury, I did not conceive it so atrociously as to think it should be pursued by war altogether; nor was I at once driven (as happened afterwards) to inflict further injuries on them, since they did not administer with the same candour the grace so frankly bestowed. The tumults which then flourished threatened to violate all the indulgences granted and to corrupt them into licence. Yet I thought that these same spirits, stirred up by their own wicked and truly demonic arts, would be induced, not without reason, to drive them out again and to bid them sink utterly away.

units.la: Imo si acriori aliquo sensu tactus fuissem Injuriarum quæ plurimæ mihi & meis inferebantur, num eram tum temporis ulciscendo idoneus hostili præsertim & Bellica ratione eos, quos minoris plebeculæ affectu tam firmè munitos noveram, ut nihil hostibus gratius facere potuissem, nec in meipsum damnosius, quàm, si indignâ Principe levitate illos Armis invadere, & discutere tentassem, quos nuper Actu Parlamentario tam solenni stabiliveram?
units.tr: Indeed, if I had been moved by some keener feeling at the many injuries done to me and mine, was I then in a position to take revenge on them, especially by hostile and military means? I knew they were so firmly supported by the affection of the common people that nothing could have pleased my enemies more, or harmed me more, than if, with unworthy princely levity, I had tried to attack them with arms and break up those whom I had lately established by so solemn a Parliamentary Act.

units.la: Deus scit, me nil adeo in votis habuisse, quam ut ego & subditi mei tot mearum Concessionum fructibus tranquillè gauderemus.
units.tr: God knows I had nothing more at heart than that my subjects and I should joyfully enjoy the fruits of so many of my Concessions.

units.la: Certe improbum facinus fuislet[?], periculique juxta & infamiæ plenum, ense[?] statim excindere quod ita dudum plantaveram; nec in subditorum meorum magis, quam meum gaudium: nisi timuissent nonnulli, ubi nulla erat causa metus, qui securi esse non poterant nisi aliorum terrore.
units.tr: Certainly it would have been a wicked deed, full of danger and infamy alike, to cut down at once with the sword what I had so long planted. It would have been no less a grief to my subjects than to me, unless some had feared where there was no cause for fear, and could not be secure except through the terror of others.

units.la: Mihi verò (Deo Gratias) ita perspecta & explorata est fynceritas & integritas Cordis mei in Lege illa sancienda, quæ superiorum Temporum vota superabat; ut licet minus apud homines cautus videar, & à Politicâ prudentiâ instructus, tamen nullis coram Deo opus habeo vel occultis distinctionibus, vel arguto, quo evadam, Sophismate. Porro nulla erat in Lege illâ ferendâ Refervatio in Anima mea, nulla deinceps facti pœnitentia, dum id tandem perspicerem, me, permisso nonnullis in summum Templi Pinnaculum ascensu, tentationem etiam iis subjecifle ut me[?] illinc darent præcipitem.
units.tr: But to me (thanks be to God) the sincerity and integrity of my heart in enacting that Law, which went beyond the wishes of earlier times, has been so clearly perceived and tested that, although I may seem less cautious among men and less instructed in political prudence, I have no need before God of hidden distinctions or some subtle sophistry to escape by. Moreover, there was no reservation in my soul when I enacted that Law, and afterwards no repentance of the deed, until I at last perceived that, by allowing some to climb to the highest pinnacle of the Temple, I had also exposed myself to the temptation that they might throw me headlong from it.

units.la: Id enim secum cogitabant, mecum una Monarchiam in præceps actam, nisi miraculum obstaret, frustillatim spargendam. Deus illis pro misericordia sua ignoscat, tandemque illis notum faciat, etiam tot Mundi Regna quot Diabolus ostendit Salvatori Nostro, & eorum Gloriam (si simul omnibus frui licuisset) tanti non esse, ut flagitiosâ ingratitudine, & infami aliquo facinore acquirantur: unde Animæ periculum creatur omnibus Regnis, & Mundis potiori.
units.tr: For they thought this among themselves: that together with me the Monarchy, driven headlong, would be scattered in pieces unless a miracle intervened. May God in his mercy forgive them, and make known to them at last that even all the kingdoms of the world, which the Devil showed our Saviour, and their glory (even if it were lawful to enjoy all of them together), are not so great a thing that they should be gained by shameful ingratitude and some infamous crime. Whence danger to the soul is created for all kingdoms and worlds, and for the more powerful ones especially.

units.la: Deus vero me hactenus custodivit, fecitque ut intelligam haud mirum esse oportere, si homines Affectuum suorum Impotentiae relicti, vel multa ipsi mala faciant vel aliorum Bonitate abutantur, cujus ingrata Nausea, Morbus omnium deploratissimus & Insanabilis.
units.tr: But God has kept me safe until now, and has made me understand that it is no wonder if men, left to the impotence of their own passions, either do much harm to themselves or abuse the goodness of others. Ingratitude towards such goodness is the most deplorable and incurable of all diseases.

units.la: Haud tamen propterea liquido jam pofsum affirmare, poenituisse me hujus consilii, cum in illud intuear non ut voluntatis meae crimen sed ut errorem Judicii in Charitatem impendio propensi. Id tantum dolet, aliorum oculos improbos factos, quia mei boni erant.
units.tr: Yet I cannot yet affirm clearly that I repent of this counsel, since I look upon it not as a crime of my will but as an error of judgement, inclined to charity at great cost. I grieve only that the wicked eyes of others have been made so, because my intentions were good.

units.la: Te Domine semper appello, cujus omnia explorans Justitia per humana quaecunque velamina, & fallaces cordium tenebras clare penetrat.
units.tr: I always call upon you, Lord, whose Justice, searching out all things, penetrates clearly through every human veil and the deceitful darkness of hearts.

units.la: Tu mihi cor dedisti ut haec subditis meis concederem, jam corde praeparato opus est, quo multa ab illis vicissim tolerem.
units.tr: You gave me a heart to grant these things to my subjects; now that the heart is prepared, there is need that I in turn should endure many things from them.

units.la: Fiat voluntas tua, nostrae quantumvis contrariæ[?], etiam tum cum speravimus & voluntati tuæ & eorum morem gerere, qui nil praeter tuam jactabant.
units.tr: Thy will be done, however contrary to ours it may be, even when we hoped both to obey your will and to comply with the wishes of those who professed nothing but yours.

units.la: Erudiat me Gratia tua æquè frui Sapienter fru-strationibus his meis, ac sit spes meas optimas & speciosissima desideria explevisses.
units.tr: May your grace teach me to enjoy wisely these frustrations of mine, just as you would have fulfilled my best hopes and most splendid desires.

units.la: Dum aliorum timoribus mederi cogitabam, meos auxi, & illos demum sedando meipsum tur-bavi.
units.tr: While I was thinking of how to heal the fears of others, I increased my own; and by finally calming them, I troubled myself.

units.la: Ita reddiderunt mihi malum pro Bono, & odium pro dilectione mea.
units.tr: Thus they have repaid me evil for good, and hatred for my love.

units.la: Sis mihi (Domine) Gubernator in tenebrosa hac nimis & ancipiti procella, in qua nec remearcad[?] Portum datur unde solverim, nec incolumem ut volui, & famâ integrâ ad alium contendere.
units.tr: Be my Governor, Lord, in this too dark and perilous storm, in which I am granted neither to return to the harbour from which I set out, nor to make for another with my reputation intact, as I wished.

units.la: Tu me facile tutum custodies in amore & fiducia Populi mei, Tu me Saluum præstabis inter odia injusta, & suspiciones multorum, quas eo hactenus invalescere in me permisisti ut maximas quas unquam indulsi Gratias cum fiducia de illis summâ conjunctas, corrumpant omnes & in me abutantur.
units.tr: You will easily keep me safe in the love and trust of my people; you will make me safe amid the unjust hatreds and suspicions of many, which you have hitherto allowed to grow so strong against me that they corrupt and abuse all the greatest favours I ever bestowed, together with the fullest trust in them.

units.la: Nullæ vero à me collatæ Gratiæ magis unquam in abutentium crimen cedent, quam illæ Tuæ in me Domine crebræ & ingentes, quibus me turpiter abusum agnosco.
units.tr: Indeed, no favours I have ever conferred will be more counted as the crime of those who abuse them than those of yours to me, Lord, so frequent and so great, by which I acknowledge myself shamefully abused.

units.la: Des mihi & illis (precor) eam pœnitentiam qualem tu accepturus es, & eam Gratiam insuper quâ non abutamur: Eâ saltem me becs[?] (Domine) ut rectè utar aliorum injuriis, & per eorum in me delictâ, meas rursum in Te offensiones cum dolore Reformante intuear.
units.tr: Grant to me and to them (I pray) that repentance which you will accept, and moreover that grace by which we may not abuse your gifts. At least, Lord, grant me this: that I may rightly use the injuries of others, and through their offences against me may again look upon my own offences against you with a sorrow that reforms.

units.la: Ita quanquam temporalibus in tuis beneficiis per aliorum quidem peccata, sed propter mea destituar, fœlix tamen fruar misericordiarum tuarum Solatiis, per quæ gravissima perpessi in sanctorum Gloriam assurgunt.
units.tr: So although, in your temporal benefits, I am deprived, indeed through the sins of others but on account of my own, yet I happily enjoy the consolations of your mercies, through which the most grievous things suffered rise up to the glory of the saints.

units.la: 6. De recessu Regis à Westmonasterio.
units.tr: 6. On the King's departure from Westminster.

units.la: Quàm invitus à Westmonasterio me subduxerim, eorum esto judicium quos commeatu & armamentis destitutos Tempestas unquam compulit in altum Mare; quod tamen potius faciendum, quàm ut oram legentes, littori, cum Naufragii periculo, allidantur.
units.tr: How unwillingly I withdrew from Westminster, let those judge who have been driven by a storm onto the open sea with no supplies or equipment. Yet it had to be done, rather than have my readers dashed against the shore and put in danger of shipwreck.

units.la: Perstiti tamen usque in Alba Aula dum pudore magis quàm metu pellerer, cùm eum barbarum furorem, & audaciam Tumultuantium cernerem, ut jam quidvis impudenter exposcerent, nullâ mihi relictâ nec ipsis Parlamenti Membris, Rationis aut Conscientiæ, libertate, quâ illis quicquam omnino nega-rcutis[?].
units.tr: I nevertheless held out until Whitehall, though I was driven more by shame than by fear, when I saw that barbarous frenzy and the audacity of the rioters, who now shamelessly demanded anything at all. No freedom was left to me, nor even to the members of Parliament themselves, of reason or conscience, by which they might deny them anything whatever.

units.la: Unde nec mihi soli hæc Injuria illata est, quamquam mihi præcipuè intoleranda; ferre enim sècunque poterant Proceres, cæterique Depurati, (si libertate suffragandi sibi permissâ, minori postea numero vincerentur.
units.tr: So this injury was not done to me alone, though it was especially unbearable for me. The nobles and the other Purged members could in some way endure it, if, after being granted freedom to vote, they were afterwards outvoted by a smaller number.

units.la: Eorum vero omnium concordantia suffragantium nulla Lex aut Ratio permittit, ut judicium meum astringant, vel Assensum includant, aut complectantur, cùm nullo modo hic Mei partes agunt vel Personam sustineant: atque adeò haud amplius tencor ullis eorum suffragiis asfentiri, quàm quatenus ipsa primò in Dei mandata, Justa mea jura Regia, tum commune Populi Bonum consensisse perspexerim. Vidi eos (quod inter multos solet) raro omnes in eâdem sententia, & id crebro etiam videre est, in Majori eorum Parte deteriorem pollere.
units.tr: No law or reason permits them to bind my judgment, or to include or embrace my assent in the agreement of all who vote, since in no way do they here act my part or sustain my person. So I am no longer bound to assent to any of their votes, except insofar as I have seen that they first agreed with God's commands and my just royal rights, and then with the common good of the people. I have seen (as usually happens among many) that they are rarely all of one opinion, and it may often be observed that the worse view prevails among the greater part of them.

units.la: Satis jampridem demonstraveram sobriis & modestis hominibus, quam cupidè omnibus Satisfactum vellem, cùm tot eorum Rogatione Leges Sancirem, quibus & securitati prospiceretur[?], & votis omnium abundè Satisfieret, ni Hydropica quorundam appetentia quo largius biberet, eò largius sitiret, quos nec ipse Fons Regiæ Beneficentiæ saturare potuisset, obstinatos illum penitus exhaurire, vel barbarè obstruere.
units.tr: I had long since sufficiently shown to sober and modest men how eagerly I wished to satisfy everyone, when at their request I sanctioned so many laws by which both security was provided and the wishes of all were abundantly satisfied. But the dropsical craving of certain men, which the more it drank the more it thirsted, and which not even the fountain of royal beneficence could satiate, would drain him utterly, or barbarously block him up.

units.la: Certè haud amplius Consilium appellari debet ubi non Rationibus persuademur ut Homines, sed vi quadam & terrore pecudum more adigimur, ad cuicunque rei assentiendum quæ à Turbarum Patronis excogitantur. Dignus est qui in æternum serviat nullo prorsus miserante, qui id pati potest, ut Rationale suæ Animæ Imperium, Verborumque & Voluntatis Libertas, ita omnia simul mancipentur.
units.tr: Surely it should no longer be called counsel when we are not persuaded by reasons as men, but are driven like cattle by a certain force and terror to assent to whatever the patrons of the mob devise. He deserves to be a slave forever, with no one pitying him, who can suffer the rational rule of his soul, and the liberty of his words and will, to be surrendered all at once in this way.

units.la: Ego verò nec tanti Regna mea facio, ut illa velim Servare Libertatis dispendio, quæ cum mihi ut Homini & Christiano debetur, multo minus Regi neganda est, qui nullius superiotis [?] præter Dei dictata, ut consensum obligantia agnoscam. Emori satius est sub hoc Regno Animæ meæ, qua Deo solum subjicior, Ratione & Religione me dirigente, quam inanem Regis Titulum usurpantem constrictum me ita & captivum vivere, ut nec conscientiæ nec Rationis usus permittatur, quo quid probem, quid improbem, (prout Regem decet) declarem.
units.tr: I do not value my kingdoms so highly as to wish to preserve them at the cost of liberty. Liberty is owed to me as a man and a Christian, and must much less be denied to the King, who, I acknowledge, is bound to no superior except God's dictates, which bind consent. It is better to die under this kingdom of my soul, to which I am subject to God alone, with reason and religion guiding me, than to live constrained and captive, usurping the empty title of King, so that the use of neither conscience nor reason is permitted to me, by which I might declare what I approve and what I disapprove, as befits a King.

units.la: Absit enim ut illud unquam credam, Majestatem Coronæ Angliæ ita obstrictam teneri Coronationis suæ Juramento, ut in quæcunque subditorum suorum in Parlamentis postulata, cœcâ quadam & brutâ verborum Formulâ, consentire necesse habeat, quod tamen inferunt nonnulli, qui, dum hoc mihi Negativæ Vocis jus, ut Regi, eripiunt, eâdem operâ impudenter me privant omni illa Rationis, & Conscientiæ Bonæ Libertate, quâ Ipsi, & Tota Angliæ Communitas (quatenus influit in Publicum) gaudet, qui omnes ægre admodum paterentur non licere in quacunque re contradicere, quam vel Ipse ut Rex, vel mecum unâ Domus Parium, non jam amplius (si sic fieret) rogare videremur, sed exigere. Arbitror me in hoc satis fidem juramenti liberasse, cum secundum eas Leges regâ, quas Populus juxta cum Proceribus, Me ipso adsentiente comprobavit.
units.tr: Far be it from me to believe that the Majesty of the Crown of England is so bound by its Coronation oath that it must consent, by a blind and brutish formula of words, to whatever its subjects demand in Parliaments. Some nonetheless maintain this, and while they snatch from me the right of the negative voice as King, they shamelessly deprive me, by the same stroke, of all that liberty of reason and good conscience which they themselves, and the whole community of England (so far as it bears on the public), enjoy. All of them would take it very ill if it were not permitted to contradict anything at all, which either the King himself or the House of Peers together with me might seem no longer to request, but to demand, if it were so done. I think I have sufficiently freed myself from the faith of the oath in this, since I act according to those laws of the realm which the People, together with the Peers, approved with my own assent.

units.la: Certe Conscientiâ meâ non teneor Conscientiæ meæ adversari, quod proculdubio facerem, si, quibus Ratio, Justitia, Honos, Religio, negandum jubet, Novis his Rogationibus annuerem.
units.tr: Surely my conscience does not bind me to act against my conscience. Undoubtedly I would do so if I assented to these new bills, to which reason, justice, honour and religion bid me say no.

units.la: Ita tamen sibi districte cavent nonnulli, ne Arbitrario Regimini, id est alienae voluntati sine proprio consensu subjiciantur, ut haud interim attendant quanto probro & insulsitate Regem suum cum solum esse velint, qui aliorum voluntati mancipetur, uni illi interdicto Rationis usu, vel per se, vel per alium, exercendo.
units.tr: Yet some take such strict precautions against being subjected to arbitrary government, that is, to the will of another without one's own consent, that they meanwhile fail to notice with what disgrace and absurdity they want their King alone to be handed over to the will of others, with the use of reason forbidden to him alone, whether exercised by himself or through another.

units.la: Detur vero id (quae nonnullorum suspicio est, & malevola Calumnia) me, Errore, vel Opinione, vel Infirmitate actum, vel ipsa (ut vocant) Pervicaciâ, (quam non verum aliquod Judicium, sed Perturbatio potius & vehemens praejudicium animo meo impresserat) à sententiis eorum discordasse, haud tamen quisquam aliter, quàm ut servilem Contumeliam acciperet, importunâ quadam vi, & barbaro impetu hanc qualemcunque Erroris sui, & Passionum caliginem (Vmbram certè Rationis, & quae hactenus sufficere debet foliidiore destitutis) ita penitus discuti & dissipari. Coram Deo & Hominibus culpam haud meretur, qui rerum optimam Rationem perspiciendi cupidus, ei demum optemperat quod sibi maxime videtur Rationi consentaneum: & si forte in errorem per inscitiam prolabatur, excusabit illum mentis Rectitudo. Nemo navis Rectorem incusabit, quod cum Stellam Polarem non videat, ad eas saltem, quas videt, cursum dirigat. Mihi certe magno argumento est laborare Rationum inopiâ, & Solidis Argumentis destitui, qui Vim istam Auxiliatricem ad propugnanda sua Infirma consilia, & Rogationes promovendas accersunt. Profiteor in Veritate & Sinceritate cordis mei, me nulli unquam Rei recto more propositæ, libereque & integrè in Utraque Domo agitatæ, ulterius contradixisse, quam quo Ratio suadebat, & sic posse à me fieri, & sic oportere.
units.tr: Let it be granted (which is the suspicion of some and a malicious calumny) that I differed from their opinions through error, or opinion, or weakness, or what they call obstinacy, which was impressed on my mind not by any true judgment but rather by agitation and a vehement prejudice. Yet no one would take it otherwise than as a servile insult, when by an unseemly force and barbarous assault they would thus utterly dispel and scatter this so-called mist of my error and passions (surely a shadow of reason, which hitherto ought to suffice for the more foolish). He does not deserve blame before God and men who, eager to perceive the best reason of things, at last submits to what seems most consonant with reason to him; and if he perhaps slips into error through ignorance, the rectitude of his mind will excuse him. No one will blame the helmsman of a ship because, not seeing the Pole Star, he at least directs his course by the stars he does see. It is surely a great proof to me that they lack reasons and are destitute of solid arguments, when they summon that auxiliary force to defend their weak counsels and to promote their bills. I profess, in the truth and sincerity of my heart, that I have never contradicted any matter proposed in due order and freely and fully debated in either House, except insofar as reason persuaded me that it could and ought to be done by me.

units.la: Nec mihi quicquam magis cordi fuit, quàm, ubi conspirante meo simul cum eorum Judicio, salvâ possem Conscientiâ illis assentiri; Imo in rebus plurimis, ubi, non contra militabat Absoluta & moralis Rationis Necessitas, sed de præsenti tantum Commodo meo & Honore agebatur, mihi potius quàm illis negandum censui; ea quæ Illi opinabantur tantum in populi Bonum necessaria iis semper antepònens [?], quæ mihi solùm expedire compereram.
units.tr: Nothing was dearer to me than, when my judgment agreed with theirs, to be able to assent to them with a clear conscience. Indeed, in very many matters, where no absolute and moral necessity of reason stood in opposition, but only my present advantage and honour was at stake, I judged that I should rather deny it to myself than to them. I always placed those things which they thought necessary for the public good before those which I had found merely expedient for me.

units.la: Patiar enim forte in iis, (quorum me Dominum esse arbitror) privata scilicet Re mea, & Personalibus Privilegiis cedere: quodverò ad Veritatem, Iustitiam, Iura Ecclesiæ & Coronæ & regnorum meorum Publicum Bonum Spectat, quæ omnia, quantum in me est, tueri debeo, hic [?] firmus sum, & stabilis, & idem usque perstabo in nullius unquam hominis gratiam in ea consensurus, in quibus Cor meum, Linguam vel Manum redarguet, nec id coram Hominibus affirmaturus, quod in Conscientia mea coram Deo negavi, Spineam potius Coronam cum Servatore Meo gestare malim, quam illam mihi debitam Auream in ejusmodi Plumbeam commutare, cujus vilis & dis[?] titis[?] materia in quamvis facile formam inflectatur, nec Diversis modo Factionum, sed Adversis sibi invicem, & pugnantibus placitis obscequatur, cum sub obtentu Rationis, & Publici commodi, revera nil nisi Privata Partium Res agitur, quæque à studiis iniquis, & Impotentia Affectuum profluxerunt.
units.tr: For perhaps I will yield in those matters of which I consider myself the lord, namely my private affairs and personal privileges. But as for what concerns truth, justice, the rights of the Church and Crown, and the public good of my kingdoms, all of which I must defend as far as in me lies, here I am firm and steadfast, and I will persevere in the same course, never consenting, for the favour of any man, to those things in which my heart, tongue or hand would convict me, nor affirming before men what I have denied in my conscience before God. I would rather bear a crown of thorns with my Saviour than exchange the golden crown due to me for one of lead, whose base and distorted material, however easily it is bent into any shape, complies not only with the various designs of factions but with designs opposed to one another and contending. For under the pretext of reason and the public advantage, really nothing is at issue but the private affairs of parties, and these have flowed from unjust zeal and the impotence of the passions.

units.la: Nil prorsus dignius novi Christiano Principe, quàm ut id semper firmum habeat Conscientiam suam Regnis anteponere.
units.tr: Nothing is more worthy of a Christian prince than always to hold his conscience firm and to put it before his kingdoms.

units.la: Custodi (Deus meus) famulum Tuum in hac Naturali, Rationali, & Religiosa libertate. Ita enim te velle credo, ut hanc tueamur: quislicet juste exigas ut Intellectus nostros, & voluntates, Tuæ submittamus, cujus sapientia & Bonitas nec errare potest, Ipsa, nec in errorem inducere, & carnali nostræ Rationi eosque negemus cum de Sacris mysteriis & Mandatis agitur, ut simus hîc credere & parere potius, quam disputare promptí, cum tamen à nobis exspectas Cultum Rationalem, ut nec quicquam adversum Conscientiæ nostræ etiam Tui causâ, faciamus: quæ vero ab Hominibus expectuntur, & ea omnia explorare præcepisti ad Rationis & Legum Indicem (Civilis scilicet Institutæ Normam unicam) atque ita demum assensum nostram in quæ Iudicio probamus, profiteri.
units.tr: Keep, my God, your servant in this natural, rational and religious liberty. For I believe that you wish us to guard it: although you justly require that we submit our intellects and wills to yours, whose wisdom and goodness can neither err nor lead into error, you do not want us to surrender our carnal reason in matters of sacred mysteries and commands, so that here we are ready rather to believe and obey than to dispute. Yet you expect from us a rational worship, so that we do nothing contrary to our conscience, even for your sake. As for what is expected from men, you have commanded us to test everything by the measure of reason and of the laws (namely the sole rule of civil institution), and so at last to profess the assent that we approve by judgment.

units.la: Nôsti (Domine) quam illibenter locum illum de[illegible, ~3 letters] in quo Tu me collocâsti, & ad quem præsentì Regnorum ecclesiarum vocabar.
units.tr: You know, Lord, how unwillingly I came to that place [illegible] in which you placed me, and to which I was called by the present state of the kingdoms and the Church.

units.la: Vellem mihi Populus Meus, quanta mihi liberter negassem, eorum quæ in arbitrio meo posuisti.
units.tr: I would wish, my people, to grant you willingly as much as I have denied you of those things you have placed in my power.

units.la: Quæ in Ingrata Importunitate, & turbulentis [?] iniqua Flagitantium, prodar illi degeneri, & indignæ viro servituti, ut illos Consen-[?]me in iis corroborem, quæ Conscientiâ meâ perimadvertor & tuæ Gloriæ, & subditorum Meorum recordando, tum, quod penitus Rationi & Iustitiæ deluco, & alterari.
units.tr: These demands, made with ungrateful importunity and the unjust turbulence of those who press them, would betray me to that degenerate servitude unworthy of a man, if I were to strengthen them by consenting to what my conscience, and regard for your glory and my subjects, forbids me to see, since it is wholly opposed to reason and justice and cannot be altered.

units.la: Fac ut solent patiar summas contumelias & quibus maximè me premunt injurias, quàm ut vel minimum patiatur adversus Conscientiam meam admittam.
units.tr: I would sooner suffer the greatest insults and the most grievous wrongs, which weigh most heavily upon me, than admit the least thing against my conscience.

units.la: Salvæ manerent Populi mei (quod sanè possunt) Iuræ libertatis; dum id rectò & debito more fiat animâ meâ nequaquam mancipatâ.
units.tr: My people's rights of liberty would remain safe (as indeed they can), provided this is done rightly and in the proper manner, with my soul not enslaved.

units.la: Quoniam Regis Christiani potentia Gratia tuâ immutatis, ne me unquam patiaris Afflictionibus & Consiliis, quæ à Ratione, Iustitia, Religione aliena prorsus videtur, Ratione meam subjicere.
units.tr: Since by your grace the power of a Christian king has been changed, may you never allow me, in afflictions and counsels that seem wholly alien to reason, justice and religion, to submit my reason to them.

units.la: Ista Tibi usa, inserviam in veritate & integritate cordis mei, licet his hominibus parum placeam.
units.tr: Using these things for you, I will serve in the truth and integrity of my heart, although I may please these men but little.

units.la: Quanquam ab illis penitus expulsus fuero, denerent Gratia Tua, quâ coram Te integrè possim conversari.
units.tr: Even though I should be utterly driven out by them, may your grace not fail me, by which I may live uprightly before you.

units.la: Dirige me in via veritatis & Iustitiæ: has enim scitas, me ad pacem olim Tecum, & fœlicitatem perducturas, quanquam plurimas inter homines, [?]bitas, molestias perferam. Hoc à Te peto Servatoris mei Gratia.
units.tr: Direct me in the way of truth and justice, for I know that these will in time lead me to peace and happiness with Thee, though I must bear very many bitter troubles and annoyances among men. This I ask of Thee, by the grace of my Saviour.

units.la: 7. De Reginæ discessu, & extra Angliam absentia.
units.tr: 7. On the Queen's departure, and her absence abroad.

units.la: Quanquam discessu illo Uxoris Mexæ[?] à Me & è Regnis meis, multam, meritamque molestiam caperim, haud tamen ita cruciôr Illius absentiâ, quam necessitatis illius Scandalo quæ Illam hinc abegit: coactam nempe fuisse à subditis meis, inque Protestantium Nomen serentibus, ut ob suam Incolumitatem, excederet. Certe Primum hoc exemplum extitit Protestantium subditorum qui contra Regem Protestantium Arma sumpserunt. Id enim in Anglia non secus contemplor, quàm Tragediæ in Scotia inchoatæ Actum secundum, cujus male extinctæ faces hic in alteram Flammam eruperunt. Nimis vereor, ne Tumultus hujusmodi, quibus parum honestatur Protestantium Causa) ad abalienandum ejus animum porro valeant, & afsectum longius abducendum ab illa Religione, in quâ hactenus solùm discrepavimus.
units.tr: Although I have felt much and deserved annoyance at my wife's departure from me and from my kingdoms, I am not so tormented by her absence as by the scandal of the necessity that drove her hence: namely, that she was compelled by my subjects, who bear the name of Protestants, to withdraw for her own safety. Certainly this has been the first example of Protestant subjects taking up arms against a Protestant king. For I regard this in England as nothing other than the second act of the tragedy begun in Scotland, whose ill-extinguished torches have here broken out into another flame. I greatly fear that tumults of this kind, by which the Protestant cause is little honoured, will serve to alienate his mind further and to draw his affection far away from that religion, in which hitherto we have differed only.

units.la: Quod tamen Deus potest, veneror-que ut velit aliquando remouere[?], neque hæc sinat quaqualiacunque facinora Judicio Illius officere· cum ab iis fere Hominibus profecta sint, quibus Religio sua adhuc quaerenda est, nec quid certi adhuc de Doctrina, vel Regimine, aut Moribus constitutum; atque adeo nullo modo Anglicanis Protestantibus imputanda, qui Illis Primis suis Principiis & constitutis Legibus adhaerent.
units.tr: God can, however, and I pray that he will one day remove this, and will not allow such deeds, whatever they are, to harm his judgment, since they have come almost entirely from those men whose own religion is still to be sought, and nothing certain has yet been settled concerning doctrine, government or morals; and so they are in no way to be imputed to the English Protestants, who adhere to their first principles and their established laws.

units.la: Dolet, nostram cum Illa conjunctionem, tam praeclara meritae Foeminae periculum & aerumnas creasse, cujus virtutes vel inter feros Pador [?] praesidium sibi invenissent; cum minus his capitaliter infensa sit agrestis eorum Barbaries, quam ficta quorundam Afjuncia [?]: quamquam paucos eâ Malitiâ crediderim, ut perinde Ipsius causa oderint. Crimen Illi est nostrum conjugium.
units.tr: I grieve that our union with her has brought danger and hardship to so distinguished and deserving a woman, whose virtues would have found protection even among the savage Pador [?]; for their rough barbarism is less fiercely hostile to her life than the feigned [?] of certain men. Yet I do not believe that few of them hate her with such malice as if they hated her for her own sake. Her crime is our marriage.

units.la: Iure ergo optimo, haud secus quam Affectu proprio impellor, ut illius securitati prospiciam, quae meâ solâ causâ periclitatur: In me omnes incumbant Tempestates: fuerim omni vento jactatus, & naufragus, dum Illa tuto in Portu conquiescat.
units.tr: Therefore, by the best right, and no less by my own affection, I am driven to provide for her safety, which is endangered for my sake alone. Let all storms fall upon me: let me be tossed by every wind and be shipwrecked, provided she rests safe in harbour.

units.la: Hoc saltem solatio ex Illius incolumitate in mediis meis malis fruar, quòd sim dimidio mei duntaxat, Illa salva, periturus, in Cujus saltem Memoria, & spem nostram solantibus liberis [?], superstes usque fiam Inimicorum malitiae, licet nec sanguine meo saturandae.
units.tr: In this at least I may find some consolation in my misfortunes, that, while she is safe, I am to perish only in half of myself; and that, surviving in her memory and in the hope of our children to comfort us, I shall be left to the malice of my enemies, though it cannot be glutted with my blood.

units.la: Illam ergo Amori & Fidei Bonorum subditorum commendo, & Illius in primis Patrocinio, qui severe plectens Principum Crimina, non minori asperitate factas Illis Injuriae ulciscitur, cùm ab iis praesertim inferantur, qui omnibus officii & obsequii vinculis ad eam Illis incolumitatem praestandam, in qua Lex Regibus praecipuè cavet, obligantur.
units.tr: I therefore commend her to the love and loyalty of my good subjects, and above all to the protection of him who, severely punishing the crimes of princes, avenges with no less harshness the injuries done to them, especially when they are inflicted by those who are bound by every tie of duty and obedience to secure that safety for them in which the law chiefly provides for kings.

units.la: Sed frustrà Speratur Humanitas, ubi Fides[?] in Principem disputatur, aut quocunque nexu Regio & parentelâ munitam tuto posse inter Illos versari qui, quo firmius Religionem suam amplecti credantur, omne prorsus obsequium projecerint.
units.tr: But humanity is vainly hoped for where loyalty to the prince is called in question, or where anyone supposes that he may safely live among those who, the more firmly they believe they embrace their religion, have cast off every obedience, however fortified by royal bond or kinship.

units.la: Deplorandum interim, Animam istam Generosam Pacisque amantissimam, id videre, multo magis id pati potuisse ab eorum Ferocia, queis, quod deest Justitiae, immanitate, & Impudentia supplendum.
units.tr: Meanwhile it is to be lamented that this noble soul, most devoted to peace, should have seen and been able to suffer so much more from the ferocity of those men, whose lack of justice must be supplied by their savagery and impudence.

units.la: Elucescet Illius aliquando (hac mecum in adversis meis sympathia) velut in obscura Nocte stella, virtus clarior, & Invido Orbi ostendet Illam Ate.non Fortunas meas amasse.
units.tr: Her virtue will one day shine forth more clearly, like a star in a dark night (such is our sympathy in my adversities), and will show to the envious world that she loved not my fortunes.

units.la: Faciles ad Ignoscendum Vterque fumus, vulgo praesertim Hominum, in quos utcunque Inhumanos, magna pars hujus Criminis non cadit. Itaenim Deo visum est experiri Patientiam nostram novo quodam & seipsum[?] aliquando ulturo Scelere, Eorum Scilicet, Ingratitudine, qui pasti Pane nostro, & Munificentia ditati, superbè se contra Nos extulerunt, è Domesticis facti Adversarii. Deus Illis hoc Peccatum non imputet, qui cætera omnia (in quae maximè obligantur officia) Religionis hoc Curbana excusant, & ægrius aspiciunt, quam quàm peccant in Eos, qui non Principes illis magis, quàm Patroni benefici exiterant.
units.tr: We are both ready to forgive, especially as most men are concerned, and in whom, however inhuman they may be, a great part of this crime does not fall. For it has pleased God to try our patience with a new kind of wickedness, which will one day avenge itself: namely the ingratitude of those who, fed with our bread and enriched by our generosity, have proudly raised themselves against us, having become adversaries from within our household. May God not impute this sin to them, who excuse all their other duties, in which they are most bound, by this pretext of religion, and who regard it with less distress that they sin against those who were not merely princes to them but benefactors and patrons.

units.la: Eo verò forsan excusatior est Inimicorum meorum in hac parte, prudentia, quo magis necessarium videretur Eorum coniugis[?], ut probrosis Criminationibus, & omne genus Insolentiis illam è Regnis meis pellendam curarent, ne Exempli Ipsius Influxu (rarae certè in conjugem Charitatis, in Regem Fidei) Eos omnes, quos corrumpere satagebant, vel ad amorem mei & obsequium pertraheret, vel in iis constantes retineret.
units.tr: Perhaps my enemies are the more excused in this matter by prudence, since it seemed the more necessary for them to take care, by reproachful accusations and every kind of insolence, that she should be driven from my realms, lest by the influence of her example (rare indeed in a wife for charity, in a king for faith) she should draw all those whom they were eager to corrupt either to love and obedience toward me, or keep them constant in these.

units.la: Quò minus gaudeam jam Illius Consortio, eò magis intrò secedam[?] ad Deum Meum, & Cor meum, unde nulla eam malitiæ[?] profligabit. Invideant mihi licet Hostes mei, haud tamen unquam eripient, ne Virtutibus Illius, dum Meipso frui datur, simul fruar.
units.tr: The less I now rejoice in her company, the more I withdraw inwardly to my God and my own heart, whence no malice will ever drive her out. Let my enemies envy me as they will; they will never snatch away from me that I may enjoy her virtues at the same time, while I am allowed to enjoy myself.

units.la: Tu (Domine) cujus Iustitiæ in præsens visum est nos ita distrahere, re-unias nos invicem Tua tempore, Tua Misericordia, idque in Terris, si ita sibi placuerit, Ambos vero utcunque ad Cœlestè Tuum Regnum perducas.
units.tr: You, Lord, whose justice has seen fit for the present to part us in this way, reunite us again in your own time and by your own mercy, and that on earth, if it so pleases you; but in any case bring us both to your heavenly kingdom.

units.la: Libera nos à Manibus Inimicorum nostrorum Perniciem & virus spirantium, & Perpessionibus Nostris præpara nos in Tuum Conspectum.
units.tr: Deliver us from the hands of our enemies, who breathe destruction and poison, and prepare us for your presence through our sufferings.

units.la: Licet in nonnullis in Re Religionis (quæ mihi maxima est in Mundo Infelicitas) discrepamus, dones tamen (Domine) & accipias sinceritatem Affectuum Nostrorum, qua omnem Tui veritatem, quærere, invenire, amplecti concupiscimus. Consentiant Corda utriusque nostrum in Amore Tui, & Christi pro Nobis Crucifixi.
units.tr: Although we differ in some matters of religion (which to me is the greatest unhappiness in the world), yet, Lord, accept and receive the sincerity of our affections, by which we desire to seek, find and embrace all your truth. May the hearts of us both agree in the love of you and of Christ crucified for us.

units.la: Doceas nos ea quæ tu sciri possislas [?] quæcunque Gloriæ Tuæ, Officiis Nostris Publicis, vel Alterno Animarum Bono necessaria, & fac ut sedulò agamus quod Bonum Scimus.
units.tr: Teach us those things which you know to be necessary for your glory, for our public duties, or for the mutual good of souls, and grant that we may diligently do the good that we know.

units.la: Nulla cognitu necessarii Ignorantia, nec in iis quæ cognoscimus Incredulitas, vel Inobedientia, cedat in miseriam nostram, aut voluntarium Peccatum.
units.tr: Let no ignorance of things necessary to know, nor unbelief or disobedience in those things we do know, turn to our misery or to wilful sin.

units.la: Quin nec Ingens istud Scandalum à subditis Meis, eandem mecum Religionem profitentibus, obstet Illi in amore veritatis, quam tu Illam perdiscere, vel in quocunque Errore induret quem in illi illustrari voluisti.
units.tr: Nor let that great scandal given by my subjects, who profess the same religion as I do, stand in the way of her love of the truth, which you have willed her to learn thoroughly, or harden her in whatever error you wish to enlighten in her.

units.la: Adversus hujus Exempli venenum, Mea sit & aliorum Constantia Antidotus.
units.tr: Against the poison of this example, may my constancy and that of others be the antidote.

units.la: Vera illa, quam profiteor, Religio exhibeatur Illius Iudicio cum speciosâ illâ facie Humilitatis, Fidelitatis, Charitatis, & Pacis, quos revera peculiares sibi Fructus & ornamenta habet, haud vero amplius odiosa & deformi larva Levitatis, Schismatis, Hæreseôs, Novitatis, Sævitiæ, & Perfidiæ, quàsnunnullorum [?] facinora Illam nuper [?] induerunt.
units.tr: Let that true religion which I profess be shown to her judgment with its fair face of humility, faithfulness, charity and peace, which truly has these as its own proper fruits and ornaments, and not with the hateful and deformed mask of levity, schism, heresy, novelty, cruelty and perfidy, with which the deeds of certain men have lately clothed it.

units.la: Videat Sacras Tuas & Salvificas veritatis prout Tuæ sint, ut sic credat, amet, obsequatur ut Tuis, ab omni Scoria, & Rubigine Humanarum Administrationum [?] expurgatis.
units.tr: May he see Your sacred and saving truth as Yours, so that he may believe it, love it and obey it as Yours, with all the dross and rust of human administrations purged away.

units.la: Vt in speculo veritatis tuæ Te contempletur in ea Tua misericordia, quam Tu nobis exhibuisti in Filio Tuo Iesu Christo Seruatore nostro Vnico, & illum cultum tibi exhibeat denuo: in omnibus illis sanctis officiis, quae Sacrosanctae tuae Doctrinae consentiant & exemplo in primis imitando.
units.tr: That in the mirror of Your truth he may behold You in that mercy which You have shown us in Your Son Jesus Christ, our only Saviour, and may offer You that worship anew: in all those holy duties which agree with Your most sacred doctrine, and above all in imitating his example.

units.la: Experti, in hac nostra Dissipatione, & Eclypsi; quam vana prorsus & fluxa est Humana omnis Gloria, & Magnitudo, eò Studiosius ambiamus perpetuis illis Honoribus, & Perfectione potiri, quam in Te solum invenire fas est, & per Iesum Christum acquirere.
units.tr: Having learned, in this our dispersion and eclipse, how utterly vain and fleeting all human glory and greatness is, let us the more eagerly strive after those everlasting honours and that perfection, which may be found in You alone and obtained through Jesus Christ.

units.la: 3. De Exclusione Regis ad Hullam urbem, & Hothamiorum fatis.
units.tr: 3. On the King's Exclusion at Hull, and the Fate of the Hothams.

units.la: CUm ab Hulla excluderer, visum est primâ facie tam insolens facinus, & aperta obsequii Detrectatio, ut Ipsi mei Inimici vix auderent tanquam suum agnoscere. Erat hoc quidem Primum illis Patientiae meae Tentamen, quàm scilicet æquo possem animo Spoliari Regnis.
units.tr: When I was shut out of Hull, the act seemed at first sight so outrageous, and so open a refusal of obedience, that my own enemies could scarcely dare to own it as theirs. This was indeed the first trial of my patience, namely how calmly I could bear being stripped of my kingdoms.

units.la: Quo tamen (Deus novit) non tam Ira mea commota est ob acceptam injuriam quàm Dolor summus pudorque, id ab iis Flagitii admissum, quod jam nullo erat colore excusandum.
units.tr: Yet (God knows) it was not so much anger roused by the injury I had received as the deepest grief and shame that such a crime had been committed, one which could no longer be excused by any pretext.

units.la: Volui tamen hoc utcunque concoquere, atque alia complura : quanquam satis videremrem vix intra unum hoc facinus continere le [?] jam amplius posse, queis vel illud patrandi, vel propugnandi Audacia non defuerat. Erat Hoc Manus tantùm Inchoantis Nubeculæ quæ paullò post per Totum Regnum diffusa, Confusione omnia & Tenebris miscebat.
units.tr: Still, I resolved to digest this somehow, along with several other things, though I saw well enough that they could hardly keep themselves within this one deed, since they lacked neither the audacity to commit such acts nor to defend them. This was only the hand of a cloud just beginning, which a little later, spread through the whole kingdom and mixed everything with confusion and darkness.

units.la: Viget enim hoc Improbum inprimis inter audaces Aggressores & Perduelles Axioma. ἀξίως[?] nefariis ejusmodi deteriora semper subjungenda : satius esse non inchoari, quàm non ad finem perduci, Plus in Recessu, quàm Fronte periculi, & quovis Crimine exitialius esse, resipiscere.
units.tr: For this wicked maxim holds especially among bold assailants and traitors: that worse things must always follow such nefarious deeds; that it is better not to begin than not to carry through to the end; that there is more danger in retreat than at the front, and that repentance is more deadly than any crime.

units.la: Hoc demum mihi oculos aperuit, ut jam per omnes eorum Pias Fraudes, & Blandissima Integumenta perspicerem, quorum verba oleo molliora jam in Gladios desitura prævideram.
units.tr: This at last opened my eyes, so that I now saw through all their pious frauds and most smooth disguises. I had foreseen that their words, softer than oil, would end in swords.

units.la: Adversus hæc, cum nil aliud tùm effet quod opponerem præter Bonam Conscientiam, prudentissimum duxi, patienter id ferre, cui mederi non poteram. Et in hoc (Deo Gratias) vici Hothamium; quòd indignè licet ab Illo acceptus, nullo odio incensus, aut præcipiti Iracundia ita abreptus fuerim, ut quicquam dicerem, vel facerem Me Ipso Indignum, vel illâ Animi Moderatione, quæ cum ad Magnum Christi Exemplum proximè accedit, Christianum inter Maximas Injurias ostendere decet.
units.tr: Against these things, since I had nothing else to set against them but a good conscience, I judged it most prudent to bear patiently what I could not cure. And in this (thanks be to God) I overcame Hotham: though treated unworthily by him, I was not inflamed with hatred, nor so carried away by headlong anger that I said or did anything unworthy of myself. I kept that moderation of mind which comes closest to the great example of Christ, and which it becomes a Christian to show amid the greatest injuries.

units.la: Quin Illius potius memor esse semper cupio, Christianum Me esse quam Regem: quod tuum huius Majestas merito asperneretur Charissimus Lubens tolerat: quod Sublimitas Animo ad ulciscendum stimulat Humilitas Christiana Ignoscendum docet; omnem eam Pestilentem Impotentiam intra justos Cancellos cùcumscribens, quarum Excessum plus vel Ipsis Gravissimis Hostibus damni inferunt: [?] per hos demum ad Animas usque nonnullas pervadat eorum Malitia, quæ alias nec longiùs extendi poterat, nec vehementer noceret.
units.tr: Indeed I always wish rather to remember that I am a Christian than a King. What your Majesty would rightly have spurned, my most beloved gladly endures. What loftiness of spirit urges to revenge, Christian humility teaches to forgive, confining all that pestilent impotence within just limits, the excesses of which do more harm even to the gravest enemies. Through these, at last, their malice penetrates even to some souls, which otherwise could not extend further nor do serious harm.

units.la: Haud tamen Illud præterire debeam, quod non multo post ita egit Deus & vindicavit Causam meam præ totius Mundi oculis, ut nemo esset tam pervicaciter cæcus, qui non hoc vel invitus cernere, metuque aliquo, & gravi sensu cogeretur Memorabilem illam plagam, & ultionis Divinæ Præsagium agnoscere.
units.tr: Yet I ought not to pass over this: not long afterwards God so acted and vindicated my cause before the eyes of the whole world that no one was so stubbornly blind as not to be compelled, even against his will and with some fear and grave feeling, to recognise that memorable blow as a presage of divine vengeance.

units.la: Ioannes enim Hutbamius[?] nullis à me Conviciis acceptus, nullis Minis, nullis aut verborum, aut Secreta animi mei Imprecatione devotus, sed Conscientiâ sceleris sui tantum percitus, & ab una Inconstantia ad Aliam delapsus, brevi, suo & Filii sui Majoris joris Capite, poenas luit tantæ Perfidiæ, ab iis Ipsis multatus, à quibus aliam Mercedem uterque sperare poterant, quàm ut Capita sic illis à Corporibus disjungerent, quorum Cordæ juxta erant à Rege suo divisa.
units.tr: For John Hotham, received by me with no reproaches, threatened by no menaces, devoted to no curses either in words or in the secret of my mind, but stirred only by the consciousness of his own crime, and sliding from one inconstancy to another, soon paid the penalty of such treachery with his own head and that of his elder son. He was punished by those very men from whom each of them had hoped for another reward than that they should sever from their bodies the heads of those whose hearts were near, though divided from their king.

units.la: Neque haud ita mirandum est, Eos qui in Re tanti Momenti, & tàm Prospera opera Illorum usi fuerant Misericordiam non invenifse, quâ tam præclarè de se meritis ignoscerent; Apostasia enim ad Fidem Pristinam Sceius est nonnullis omnium maximè Irremissibile.
units.tr: Nor is it so surprising that those who had used these men's services in a matter of such great moment, and so successful, found no mercy by which they might so nobly pardon them their desertions. Apostasy from the former faith is to some the most unpardonable of all.

units.la: Sed nec ultio sufficeit solitaria, nec uniũs è Familia Capitis abscisione expiatur satis[?] Contumelia summo Capiti Reipublicæ infli-cta: Involucendus est Major Natu Filius eodem ipso supplicio, eodem ipso cum Patre crimine adversus Patriæ Parentem, maculatus. Germen & Radicem Deus voluit uno Die exscindere.
units.tr: But neither is vengeance on one man sufficient, nor is the insult offered to the supreme head of the commonwealth atoned for by cutting off one member of the family. The elder son too must be involved in the same punishment, stained with the same crime against the Parent of the country as his father. God willed to root out the shoot and the root in one day.

units.la: Occurrent hæc facile cuivis. Quoad[?] me attinet, tantum abfui ut lætarer Hothamii perniciè, (quod tamen cùm ab iis orta esset quibus Ministerium suum Primus contra Me locaverat, vel sitim Maximam vindictæ explere potuisset) ut Illius tanto gravius mise-reret, quo Eum magis adversatum Conscientiæ suæ, quàm in Eadem causa cæteros, arbitrarer.
units.tr: These things will readily occur to anyone. As far as I am concerned, I was so far from rejoicing at Hotham's ruin (although, since it came from those men to whom he had first entrusted his service against me, it might have satisfied the greatest thirst for vengeance) that I pitied him all the more deeply, the more I judged that he had opposed his own conscience more than the others in the same cause.

units.la: Nunquam enim ea habitus est superstitiosa Morositate, quam nonnulli præ se ferunt in Religionis Causa, quæ ita tenebras offundit Judicio, ut nil prorsus malum esse, aut perfidum appareat in quibuscunque utuntur in [?]m Medius, quo ad Religionis suae (ut vocant) Iudiar. Reformatio fiat; atque id dicunt Pietatis quicquid Zeli quadam ipsius [?] & Fervoris coruscat.
units.tr: For he was never of that superstitious moroseness which some display in the cause of religion, which so clouds judgment that nothing at all appears wicked or treacherous in whatever means are used, provided the reformation of their religion (as they call it) is achieved. They call it piety whatever zeal and fervour of a certain kind flashes forth.

units.la: Longe ab his diversum censeo Ioannem Flu- [?]ianum, atque adeo crassae Illi Ambitionis Tomanum [?] faciliorem, quae nullo Fuco, aut [?] Religionis, vel sibi, vel aliis imponit.
units.tr: Far different from these I judge John Flu-ianus, and indeed much easier to deal with than that gross ambition, which deceives neither itself nor others with any disguise of religion.

units.la: Eo vero magis Illius miseret, quod cùm [?]sic in poenitentiam coepisset, & Peccatum [?]tamen adhuc officio aliquo redimere conatus [?] tamen infeliciter cum eo actum fuerit, illorum potius Iustitiae Manus, quàm in Misericordiae incideret, qui aeque facilem hunc veniam dare, quàm Ille à Me petere.
units.tr: All the more do I pity him, because, though he had begun to repent and tried by some service to redeem his sin, yet with him it went unhappily, and he fell into the hands of men of justice rather than of mercy, who would have granted this pardon as easily as he had sought it from me.

units.la: Clementiam enim Debitum quoddam exigunt persolvendum Petentibus, iis saltem, quos credibile est haud in malum deinceps lapsuros, cum Deus Ipse nihil aliud à Nobis in Misericordiae suae Pretium, quam Preces, & Laudes accipiat.
units.tr: For they exact as a kind of debt, to be paid by those who ask it, clemency, at least from those who are believed will not afterwards fall into evil; whereas God himself asks nothing from us as the price of his mercy but prayers and praises.

units.la: Heu Hominem Infoelicem! qui Monumentum jam extat Infiustae [?] Perfidiae: Simulque Orbi Documentum tristi Mortis suae & acerbo Spectaculo, quas secum poenas trahit (tanquam umbram Corpus indivisam) Insolentia subditi in Principem. In his enim plerunque savi illi maxime & Implacabiles, quibus primo haec opera navatur.
units.tr: Alas, unhappy man! He now stands as a monument of unhappy treachery, and at the same time a lesson to the world by the sad and bitter spectacle of his death, showing the penalties which the insolence of a subject against a prince drags along with it, like a body inseparable from its shadow. For among these, those are commonly the most cruel and implacable by whom this work is first undertaken.

units.la: Quaeret de Hoshamio Posteritas, an plus in [?]ulla Ignominiæ vel in Arcis Londinensis Col-le contraxerit; quanquam id verum sit, nullo ita supplicio contaminari Honorem, quàm sic sponte patrato Inhonesto Facinore, quod, præter vulnus conscientiæ, æterno Infamiæ stigmate urit Nomen & memoriam in omnem Posteritatem, quæ à studiis Sæculi, & Partibus libera incorruptius multo judicabit.
units.tr: Posterity will ask whether Hotham gained more disgrace in the Tower of London or on Tower Hill. Though it is true that honour is stained by no punishment so much as by a shameful deed freely done, which, besides the wound of conscience, brands name and memory with the eternal stigma of infamy for all posterity. Posterity, free from the passions of the age and from parties, will judge far more uncorruptly.

units.la: Tu vero ( Domine ) qui tam insigni exemplo Famulum Tuum vindicasti, ne me inde patiaris quid secretæ voluptatis haurire, nec Mors Illa, quâ, pro Injuria mihi facta satis luitur, ulli Amplius Affectui Meo gratificetur, nec Vindictam Tuam, Meam faciam: & plus admissam in me contumeliam, quàm in Te peccatum intuear.
units.tr: But you, O Lord, who by so remarkable an example have vindicated your servant, do not suffer me to draw any secret pleasure from this, nor let that death, by which satisfaction is made for the injury done to me, be pleasing to any further affection of mine. Nor let me make your vengeance my own, but rather regard the insult committed against me as less than the sin committed against you.

units.la: Tu sane absque ullo Conatu meo, vel desiderio fecisti ut convertatur Malum Ejus in Caput Ejus & in verticem Ipsius Iniquitas ejus descendat. Suscepisti causam meam coram filiis hominum, ut sciant quia manus tua haec, & tu Domine fecisti eam.
units.tr: You indeed, without any effort or wish of mine, have brought it about that his evil is turned upon his own head, and his iniquity descends upon his own crown. You have taken up my cause before the sons of men, that they may know that this is your hand, and that you, O Lord, have done it.

units.la: Haud enim dicam, haud ausim dicere, si pereant omnes Inimici mei. Imo (Domine) Veniam sis potius, & Poenitentiam dones, &c. (si Benedicta tua voluntas fuerit) Impunitatem.
units.tr: For I will not say, I dare not say, that all my enemies should perish. Rather, O Lord, be pleased to grant them pardon and repentance, etc. (if your gracious will be so) impunity.

units.la: Ne praeveniat Tua Justitia Objecta, & opportunitates Mee Misericordiae, Imo vivant, & emendentur qui in Me tam atrociter deliquerunt, ut Illos Saltem condonandos habeam, quorum in me of-sensae, Meis sunt in Tuam Majestatem simillimae, quas jam spero Misericordiā Tuam mihi ignovisse.
units.tr: Lest your justice anticipate its objects and the opportunities of my mercy; nay, let those live and be amended who have so atrociously offended against me, so that I may have at least those to forgive whose offences against me are most like their offences against your Majesty, which I now hope your mercy has already forgiven me.

units.la: Ne statuas Illis (qui adhuc vivunt) Peccata sua in Condemnationem, sed Conscientiæ duntaxat ut emendentur. Fulmen istud quo Unus tam atrociter perculsus est, omnes terreat.
units.tr: Do not set their sins against them for condemnation, but only for their conscience, that they may be amended. Let that thunderbolt by which one man was so atrociously struck terrify them all.

units.la: Detege ignorantibus Peccatum suum, & à Peccato Scelerata Prævaricationis abstergere[?], ut anticipantes Iudicia Tua vera Pænitentia, Iræ Tuæ Æternæ plagas effugiant.
units.tr: Reveal to the ignorant their sin, and wipe away from them the guilt of wicked transgression, so that, anticipating Your judgments by true repentance, they may escape the plagues of Your eternal wrath.

units.la: Et Tu Domine stabilias Thronum Meum in Misericordia & veritate sibi obviantibus: floreat Corona mea in Justitia & Pace osculantibus.
units.tr: And You, O Lord, establish my throne in mercy and truth, which meet together; let my crown flourish in justice and peace, which kiss each other.

units.la: Exaudi Preces meas (Domine) qui nos orare docuisti pro Inimicis Nostris, iisdemque benefacere, & Tui causâ, amare, qui ultro Amorem Tuum exhibens nos Hostes Tuos prævenisti, & misisti Filium Tuum Iesum Christum, qui pro Nobis moreretur, cùm Nos Illum parati essemus Crucifigere.
units.tr: Hear my prayers, O Lord, You who taught us to pray for our enemies and to do good to them, and for Your sake to love them; You who, offering Your love freely, came before us when we were Your enemies, and sent Your Son Jesus Christ, who died for us when we were ready to crucify Him.

units.la: 9. De Exercitibus conscriptis, & contra Regem levatis.
units.tr: 9. On the armies raised and levied against the King.

units.la: IN Eodem me adhuc statu agnosco, quo fui, cùm Aliba[?] Aula coactus discederem.
units.tr: I acknowledge that I am still in the same state I was in when I was forced to leave the Court at Aliba[?].

units.la: Quod Tumultus non poterāt, jam facturus est Exercitus: qui nil aliud revera est quam Tumultus Conscripti & methodo quadam meliori, sed in eundem prorsus Finem ordinati. Crevit Illis ex Discessu nico [?] Fiducia posse Me etiam & vinci.
units.tr: What the tumults could not do, the army is now going to do. In truth it is nothing other than a tumult that has been enlisted and arranged in a somewhat better method, but ordered to exactly the same end. Since my departure they have gained confidence that I too can be conquered.

units.la: Quod quidem perfacile est, si quis Robur Meum Externum spectet, perexiguum certè aut Nullum. Animus verò mihi superest (Dei Gratia Roborante) Invictus, quo superiorem me futurum haud dubito, si cum modum Constantiæ Deus dederit, ut Illum potius quàm Homines metuam, & Internam Conscientiæ Pacem cuivis Externæ Quieti anteferam.
units.tr: That is indeed very easy, if one looks only at my external strength, which is very small or certainly nothing. But my spirit remains to me, unconquered (God strengthening it), and I have no doubt that I shall prevail, if God grants me a measure of constancy, so that I fear Him rather than men, and prefer the inner peace of conscience to any outward quiet.

units.la: Ergo jam Vi oppugnandus sum, quia Rationes quas opponant, non habent? Erige Te Anima mea & confortare: Agnoscunt scilicet Imbecillitatem suam, quamque sint à Veritate, & Justitia inopes, qui sic Armis malint quàm Argumentis Contendere.
units.tr: So am I now to be assailed by force, because they have no arguments to set against me? Rise up, my soul, and be strong. Clearly they acknowledge their own weakness, and how destitute they are of truth and justice, when they prefer to contend with arms rather than with arguments.

units.la: Hanc ergo mihi Gratiam referunt, hanc mihi mercedem rependunt tot ob Leges Benignè Sancitas, & ob ea quæ indignè pertulerim? Nulla ergo ratio superesset, quâ Princeps tandem Gloriosus nisi ex Perpessionibus meis efficiar?
units.tr: Do they then repay me with this favour, this reward for so many laws graciously enacted and for what I have undeservedly endured? Would no reason remain by which I might at last become a glorious prince, other than through my sufferings?

units.la: Anxia sanè & difficilis optio Amanti Populum Principi, & ab iis vicissim amari cupido, ut vel suos occidat, vel à suis occidatur.
units.tr: An anxious and difficult choice for a prince who loves his people, and who in turn desires to be loved by them: whether to kill his own, or to be killed by his own.

units.la: Ergo Belli Civilis Miseriam & Pericula in ipsis Florentissimi Regni mei visceribus supremum tandem Fructum percipio Regni per Septem-decem annos administrati, eâ Iustitiæ Pacis, Affluentiæ & Religionis mensurâ, ut vicinis circùm Gentibus admirationi esset vel Invidiæ? etiamsi fieri posset ut Abusus nonnulli irreperent, pravis forsan Eorum consiliis qui ad suos tantum Fines collimârunt, vel lividâ aliorum Morositate, qui quicquam Publicæ Rei sine seipsis administrari invidebant, vel Arcano potius Regnorum & Insuperabili Fato, quàm ullâ mei Ingenii ad Injurias, aut Oppressiones, ut spero, proclivitate.
units.tr: So do I now receive, in the very heart of my most flourishing kingdom, the miseries and dangers of civil war as the final fruit of a kingdom administered for seventeen years, with such a measure of justice, peace, plenty and religion that it was an object of admiration, or of envy, to the neighbouring nations all around? Even if it could be that some abuses crept in, perhaps through the wicked counsels of those who aimed only at their own ends, or through the envious peevishness of others who begrudged that any public affair should be managed without themselves, or rather through a hidden fate of kingdoms and an insuperable destiny, and not through any inclination of my nature, as I hope, to wrongs or oppressions.

units.la: Cujus enim unquam Toto Regni Mei Tempore, innocentem sanguinem fudi, ut sic Irae meæ, Libidini, Avaritiæ litarem? Quæ Viduæ aut Orphani Lachrymæ in Testimonium Me contra producentur, ut eorum Justis clamoribus sanguine Meo Satisfieret? Idem enim Omnium in Bello periculum: nec Discrimen Personarum Glans Sclopeti agnoscit.
units.tr: For in my whole reign, when did I ever shed innocent blood, so as to sacrifice to my anger, my lust or my avarice? What tears of widow or orphan will be produced against me as a witness, so that by my blood their just cries might be satisfied? For the danger in war is the same for all, and the musket ball does not recognise any distinction of persons.

units.la: Frustra igitur Personam Meam excipiunt, Supervacuâ Verborum Parenthesi, cum tot Manus in me Gladiis armantur.
units.tr: In vain, therefore, do they except my person, with a superfluous parenthesis of words, when so many hands are armed with swords against me.

units.la: Testis mihi est Deus, quàm seriò huc animum intenderim, ut quibus Justitiæ Fundamentis Bellum Hoc inniteretur, perspicerem, ut Æquissimis Conditionibus delatis, vel tempestive occurrerem Intestino huic Motui, vel maturè terminarem: qui plerisque haud immerito videtur, è Longæ Pacis Nausea, & Lascivia Animorum fluxisse, vel Privatis potius Æmulationibus, Ambitione & studiis quàm in solida ulla Causa fundari, quasi aut Publica Justitia interclusa esset, aut Parlamentorum Privilegia violata.
units.tr: God is my witness how earnestly I have turned my mind to this: to perceive on what foundations of justice this war rests, so that, with the most equitable conditions offered, I might either timely meet this internal disturbance or bring it to a speedy end. Most people think, not unreasonably, that it has flowed from the weariness of a long peace and the wantonness of minds, or is founded on private rivalries, ambition and partisan zeal rather than on any solid cause, as if either public justice were shut out or the privileges of Parliaments were violated.

units.la: Quod tamen cùm obtendunt, incumbit Mihi maximè diluendum, coram Deo saltem in Conscientia Mea, quanquam nolint Mihi fidem habere nonnulli, ne seipsos condemnent.
units.tr: When they allege this, it falls chiefly to me to refute it, before God at least, in my own conscience, although some will not believe me, lest they condemn themselves.

units.la: Cùm primùm ab Aiba Aula secederem, eo prorsus Consilio, ut Tumultuantium Infolentiam sedarem (quos non antea fuisse oppressos, concesso praesertim quo id fieret Armato satellitio, nulla alia potest causa afferri, quàm,ut Meam, & utriusque Ordinis Libertatem pronunciandi fecundum Conscientias Nostras tollerent) in quo amplius tunc temporis impedita Justitia est quàm, quod uni Justum, alii forte non item videbatur?
units.tr: When I first withdrew from the Court at Aiba, with the sole purpose of quelling the insolence of the rioters (who, it is said, had not been oppressed before, especially since this was done with an armed guard, and no other cause can be given than that they might take away my freedom and that of both Houses to declare what we think according to our consciences), in what was justice then more impeded than that what seemed just to one party perhaps did not seem so to another?

units.la: Ecquis unquam Poteptiâ[?] mea contra Parlamenti Justitiam protectus?
units.tr: Who was ever protected by my power against the justice of Parliament?

units.la: Quod vero Nonnulli recesserint, Iniquitatem Judiciorum suspicantes, & Straffordii Fato admoniti (eadem adhuc Plebe interminante, Ipsis nempe Interitum, & de judicibus eorum fe cogniturös) ex Illo fluxit Instinctu Naturæli quo fe omnes velint confervare. Si qui Alii fe sistere recusarent, cùm id clarè perspicerent, ita Justitiæ & Libertatis? cursum ab Iluvie illa Populi obstrui & turbari, ut nec Legitimi fui Judices vel in Domos venire audesent[?], vel sensus suos liberè & tuto profiteri mirum haud videri debet æquo homini, cùm vel Publico semel odio objici fatis effet ad cujufquam perniciem. causâ omninò inaudita, vel nondum cognita. His si minus fuissent Factionum Tumultibus, utriusque Domus Libertas & Honos oppressa, si Iustitiam suam contra Illos asseruissent, aditumque tutuin[?] Omnibus ad Conscientias suas Declarandas praestitissent, neminem mihi novi tam charum, cui vel omnino consuluissem secedere, vel ut citatus negaret comparere; ab iis praesertim, quorum Sententiæ secundum Legem prolatæ omnem subditum opinor stare oportere.
units.tr: As for some having withdrawn, suspecting the injustice of the judgments and warned by Strafford's fate (while the same mob still threatened them with ruin and with knowledge of their judges), this arose from the natural instinct by which all wish to preserve themselves. If others refused to present themselves, when they clearly saw that the course of justice and liberty was obstructed and disturbed by that flood of the people, so that not even their lawful judges dared to come into the houses, or to declare their opinions freely and safely, it ought not to seem strange to a fair-minded man, since to be exposed once to public hatred, in a cause entirely unheard or not yet examined, was enough for anyone's destruction. Had the tumults of factions not been present, the liberty and honour of each House would have been oppressed; if they had asserted their justice against those men, and given everyone a safe access to declare their consciences, I know of no one so dear to me that I would have advised him either to withdraw altogether or, when summoned, to refuse to appear, especially those whose sentences, pronounced according to law, I think every subject ought to abide by.

units.la: Creverat sane ita in immensum hic Furor (quia his vulgi Insolentiis haud tempori itum est obviam) ut hoc maximum esse Crimen Eorum quos ut Noxios deposcebant, & damnabant suffragiis, quòd Scilicet ab his se Tumultibus in Ordinem cogi, nec à Patronis eorum contineri paterentur, nec suffragiis suis denique aut Praesentiâ obsecundarent illorum Consiliis qui Res Novas agitabant cum Ecclesiæ & Status pernicie.
units.tr: Indeed this fury had grown so immensely (because no one went to meet these insolences of the mob in time) that the greatest crime of those whom they demanded as guilty and condemned by their votes was this: that they refused to be forced into line by these tumults, nor to be restrained by their patrons, nor finally to comply with the counsels of those who were stirring up new affairs to the ruin of the Church and the State, either by their votes or by their presence.

units.la: In quo quidem Constantiam eorum & Cautelam laudo, ultra nihil cujusquam Contumacia indulsi adversus Domum statuta & Privilegia, quibus nil magis optavi, quam ut Libertas Illis sua, & Incolumitas, & Integer Numerus constaret.
units.tr: In this I commend their steadfastness and caution, and I have indulged no one's obstinacy against the statutes and privileges of the House, of which I wished nothing more than that their liberty, their safety and their full number should stand.

units.la: Res autem sic se habet. Nonnulli eorum atque iinon[?] pauci, cum æquo & Recto Parlamentorum more (ubi liberè Consultandi, & suffragandi locus) majorem partem Procerum & Communitatis in sententiam suam traherent desperarent, huc demum incumbuerunt, ut præcipiti sedulitate factiosorum[?] Tumultuum absterrerent Illos omnes & penitus exigerent, quos pessimis suis Consiliis adversari perspexerant.
units.tr: The matter, however, stands thus. Some of them, and not a few, when they despaired of drawing the greater part of the nobles and the Commons to their opinion by the fair and right custom of Parliaments (where there is room for free deliberation and voting), at last set themselves to this: to terrify all those whom they saw opposing their wicked counsels, by the headlong zeal of factious tumults, and to drive them out completely.

units.la: Quoties enim in Re illa Episcopali an Loco suo Antiquo & Indubiis Privilegiis in Domo Parium gauderent, obtinuit eorum Causa, Majore Parte Procerum secundum Illos pronunciante? Hæc tamen adversus Illos Rogatio quinquies licet repudiata rursum Contra Fas omne & Morem, per vim & Turbam obtrusa & à Paucis admodum perlata est, cum plærique è Proceribus eâdem vi coacti necessario abessent.
units.tr: For how often, in that matter of the Episcopal office and the bishops' ancient place and indubitable privileges in the House of Peers, did their cause prevail, the greater part of the nobles pronouncing in its favour? Yet this bill against them, though five times rejected, was again forced through against all right and custom, by violence and a mob, and was carried by very few, since most of the nobles, compelled by the same violence, were necessarily absent.

units.la: Quemadmodum etiam & Lex Illa de Radice & Germine Omni Tumultuantium clamore, & Schismaticis Terroribus promota, haud tamen utique ferri poterat, dum in Vtramque Domum infrequentiâ jam suâ Rarefactam postremò vi invalescerent.
units.tr: Likewise that law "concerning root and branch", promoted by all the clamour of the rioters and by schismatic terrors, could not indeed be carried while they were thinned by absence in both Houses, until at last, by force, they grew strong.

units.la: His ergo Studiis inquis dum (prout Ratio, Justitia, Religio exigit) Conscientia prohibeor adstipulari, cæterasque eorum sententias, consensu meo Acta Parlamentaria efficere, propter hoc jam Armis impugnor, atque in eam necessitatem redigor, ut vel Me & Regnum Meum (dum me coner defendere) in Extremum Discrimen adducam, vel cæca quadam Obedientiâ Conscientiam Meam iis prosternam, qui Superstitioso quodam Zelo vel credunt, vel simulant credere, se Deo & Ecclesiæ melius inservire non posse, quam si Primitium[?] Apostolicum, & Antiquitus Universale Ecclesiae per Episcopos Regimen exstinguant penitus, & abolcant.
units.tr: Therefore, while conscience forbids me (as reason, justice and religion require) to agree with these undertakings, and to give my consent so that their other opinions become acts of Parliament, I am now assailed with arms for this, and driven into such necessity that either I must bring myself and my kingdom into the utmost danger (while I try to defend myself), or, by a certain blind obedience, prostrate my conscience to those who, by a kind of superstitious zeal, either believe or pretend to believe that they cannot serve God and the Church better than by utterly extinguishing and abolishing the apostolic and ancient universal government of the Church by bishops.

units.la: Quod quidem cùm Alii mero judicio suo ducti fatis se credant ad tuendum obligari, vel saltem ne in Illius Abolitionem consentiant, quanto hoc mihi incumbit vehementius, qui praeter ea Fundamenta Judicii mei mihi cum Aliis communia, etiam Juramentum suscepi in Conscientiam meam, Rigidum prorsus & Indifpenfabile, ad hunc Ipsum Ordinem & Ecclesiae Jura confervanda: quod fi unquam consensu meo violarem, atque adeo sacrilego & deteftando Perjurio Christiano Rege indignissimo illigarer, supra omnes miserias ducerem quaecunque mihi jam obtigerunt, vel unquam possint obtingere: cùm vel minimum peccatum plus in fe mali habeat Calamitate Maxima quacunque. Illud tamen fi protinus feciffem, & Factioni Isti Anti-Episcopali in hac sua Rogatione indulsissem, Furenti eorum Avaritiae, aut Ambitioni, aut vindictae postremò Appetitui, Ecclesiae Regimine & Proventibus immolatis, statim Illa speciosa Neceffitas conscribendi Exercitus quo Delinquentes videlicet ad poenas traherent, omnis fuisset evanitura.
units.tr: Since others, led by their own bare judgment, believe that they are sufficiently bound to defend this, or at least not to consent to its abolition, how much more does this weigh upon me, who, besides those foundations of judgment I share with others, have also taken upon my conscience an oath, quite rigid and indispensable, to preserve this very order and the rights of the Church. If I should ever violate it with my consent, and so be bound by a sacrilegious and detestable perjury, most unworthy of a Christian king, I would count it above all the miseries that have already befallen me, or could ever befall me, since even the smallest sin has in itself more evil than the greatest calamity. But if I had immediately done that, and indulged this anti-episcopal faction in its present bill, sacrificing the government and revenues of the Church to their furious avarice, ambition, or finally appetite for revenge, that specious necessity of raising an army, namely to drag offenders to punishment, would have vanished at once.
