units.la: Quod in Legem eam consenserim quae Epifcopos exclusit è Domo Parium, ex ea maximè fluxit Fiducia, quâ sperabam aequanimiter illos laturos detrahi aliquid in praefens Juri suo & Honori ( in Mei & Reipublicæ gratiam ) quàm vel minimò ab Illis obice posito Mihi & Regnis Meis periculum creari. Ne verò porro consensum meum adjiciam ad extirpandum penitus illud Regimen ( quod tamen æquâ & commoda Ratione Regulandum sæpe ultro proposui) eò amplius Conscientiâ meâ obstringor, quatenus illud Religiosum & Apostolicum, imò ita sacrum prorsus & Divinum censeam, ut non modò non aboleri, sed omninò cum Illo dispensarinon possit, cum quæ à Civili Gratiâ, Honoris Privilegia Illius Ordinis Hominibus concessa fuerint, liceat forsan eorum, quorum interest, consensu abrogari.
units.tr: The reason I gave my consent to that law which excluded the bishops from the House of Peers was chiefly the confidence that they would bear calmly the loss of some part of their right and honour for the present, for my sake and the commonwealth's, rather than let an obstacle be raised against me and my kingdoms that would endanger us in any way. But so that I may not add my consent further to the total abolition of that government (which I have often offered, of my own accord, to have regulated in a fair and suitable manner), I am bound in conscience all the more, since I judge it so religious and apostolic, indeed so sacred and divine altogether, that it cannot not only be abolished but cannot be dispensed with at all. The privileges of honour granted to that order of men, by the civil grace of the crown, may perhaps be revoked with the consent of those whose interest it is.

units.la: Hæ nempe sunt illæ Obstructiones, quas in Iustitiam, & Authoritatem Parlamentariam factas passim divulgabant, cùm (Deum Testem appello) nullas scirem illius Momenti, ut vel Belli mentione opus esset, cùm non aliæ prorsus fuerint, quàm, quas Iustitia, Ratio, & Religio meæ & Aliorum Conscientiis suggesserant.
units.tr: These, of course, are the obstructions which they were everywhere spreading abroad as having been put in the way of justice and the authority of Parliament, though (I call God to witness) I knew of none of such weight that there was any need even to mention war. They were nothing other than what justice, reason, and religion had suggested to my own conscience and to the consciences of others.

units.la: Postea quidem Magna species Delinquentium apparuit: quod necessario erat secuturum subducentibus se Plurimis exemplo meo, & se ab Impetu Illorum tutantibus. At hæc prima Conscribendi exercitus causa esse non poterat, in quo tantùm abest ut eos prævenerim ( quod crebrò ab Illis jactatur, quo scilicet Favorabilem suam Causam reddant tanquam in sui Defensionem excitati, in me verò, ut Primum Aggressorem odium omne, & Invidiam transfundant) ut (Deum conscium appello) nec spes ulla Exercitus Animum Meum tentaverit. Si enim, edito in Facinorosos exemplo Tumultus Isti efficaciter & Honorificè repressi fuissent, & Libertas Domorum ita vindicata, ut utriusque Ordinis Membra, eo Honore & securitate (quæ Senatum ejusmodi decebat) & accedere, & profiteri Conscientias suas potuissent, compos fuissem illius, cujus voto recessera, & multò celerius rediissem quàm tunc abieram, cum illud solum Necessitate fecerim, hoc Sponte essem facturus.
units.tr: Afterwards, indeed, a great show of offenders appeared, which was bound to follow, since many would withdraw from the Parliament following my example and would protect themselves from the violence of those men. But this could not be the first cause of raising an army. So far was I from anticipating them (as they often boast, so that they may make their cause look favourable, as though roused in their own defence, and may pour all hatred and odium upon me as the first aggressor) that, I call God to witness, no hope of an army even tempted my mind. For if, once an example had been made of the wrongdoers, those tumults had been effectively and honourably suppressed, and the liberty of the Houses so vindicated that members of both orders could approach and profess their convictions with the honour and security that befit such a Senate, I would have obtained the very thing I went away wishing for, and I would have returned much more quickly than I departed. I had done that only out of necessity; I would have done this of my own accord.

units.la: At nimis gnari Nonnulli, me idem mecum quod extuleram Iudicium & Constantiam relaturum, quæ haud perinde eorum Consiliis quadrare potuisset: invitantes licet reditum meum, & de Absentia mea graviter querentes,* satis illam libenter pertulerunt; præsertim postquam Novum illum & speciosum Prætextum excogitassent, ideo Arma sumendi ut Delinquentes repeterent, dum interim pessima illa & minimè omnium ferenda Tumultuantium Delicta ac eorum Authores impunè habiti, qui Barbaris & Indignis contumeliis Me & tot ex utroque Ordine à Loco suo depulerant, quem non minùs inviti deserebant, ac His erant libentibus pulsi, ut hinc ansam arriperent illos Hostilibus Injuriis persequendi qui haud satis fracto animo Turpis cesserant.
units.tr: But some men, all too aware, feared that I would bring back the same judgement and constancy which I had carried away, and these would not have suited their plans so well. So although they invited my return and complained bitterly of my absence, they readily bore it well enough, especially after they had devised the new and specious pretext of taking up arms so as to pursue the offenders. Meanwhile, the worst crimes of the rioters, which are least of all to be borne, and their authors went unpunished. These men had, with barbarous and unworthy insults, driven me and so many from both orders from our place, which they themselves deserted no less unwillingly, and which they were glad to have us driven from, so that they might seize the occasion to persecute with hostile injuries those who, not sufficiently broken in spirit, had shamefully withdrawn.

units.la: Hunc vero Rerum fuisse Statum, & præcipuum eorum Consilium qui contra Me Arma ceperant, ita liquet ex iis quæ secuta sunt, ut nullum postea colorem admittat. Cùm enim diversis subinde Propositionibus, & Tractatuum Articulis significarent, quid à me potissimum expeterent, nihil unquam ullius Momenti, vel quoad ipsas Leges, vel Justitiæ Administrationem, exhibitum ab Illis, vel postulatum: id solum (inter alia minora quæ novari voluerant) acerrimè urgebant, Abolendum Episcopale, & Presbyterorum Regimen Con-stituendum.
units.tr: That this was the state of affairs, and the chief purpose of those who took up arms against me, is so clear from what followed that it admits no pretence afterwards. For when, at various times, in different proposals and articles of treaty, they indicated what they chiefly required of me, they never put forward or demanded anything of any importance, whether concerning the laws themselves or the administration of justice. The only thing (among other minor matters which they had wished to change) that they pressed most vehemently was this: the abolition of episcopacy and the establishment of the government of presbyters.

units.la: Cætera omnia quovis tempore propositā, vel nihil omnino facientia ad Belli causam, vel a Me facile concessa, vel denique erant hujusmodi quæ Numerum tantum implebant, aut accedebant postea ut confecutiva Belli jam ab illis Injuste inchoati.
units.tr: All the other things proposed at any time either had nothing whatever to do with the cause of the war, or were readily conceded by me, or were of such a kind that they merely filled up the number, or came afterwards as consequences of a war which they had unjustly begun.

units.la: Penes me non est quid alii credant efficere, (ii præcipuè, quos illa species Pietatis & Clamor, tum studium Religionis, & Reformandi fervor ita occupant plerunque Præjudicio, ut lux omnis Judicii, & æquitas simul obstruatur.) Hæc tamen (quantum observare potui) vera fuit & est inter nos controversia, & Armorum Causa, quæ hoc fine, in initio ceperunt, ut vel os mihi penitus occluderent, vel consensum vi exprimerent. Et in hac porro Veritate, (quam Deo Teste confirmo) tam remotum me fuisse a Belli Cogitatione, quam eram Mundo coram ab omnibus Rebus Imparatissimus ita acquiescit conscientia Mea, & id invenit solatii in mediis suis Adversis, & calamitofis[?] hujus Belli Eventibus, ut nec inde Me quicquam denigrari, nec vel minimam quamcunque maculam Innocentiæ meæ offusam agnoscam, unde nec illâ Integritate & Pace coram Deo destituor, ut non Humili Fiduciâ ad Eum preces dirigam.
units.tr: It is not for me to say what others may believe (especially those whom that appearance of piety and clamour, along with their zeal for religion and their fervour for reformation, so commonly occupy with prejudice that all the light of judgement and fairness is blocked out at the same time). Yet this (as far as I have been able to observe) was and is the true controversy between us and the Cause of the arms, which they took up at the beginning with this end in view: either to silence me altogether, or to extort my consent by force. And in this truth (which I confirm with God as witness) my conscience rests so securely that I was as far from any thought of war as I was, before the world, most unprepared for all things. It finds comfort in the midst of its adversities and the calamitous outcomes of this war, so that I do not acknowledge that anything can be blackened thereby, nor any stain, however small, cast upon my innocence. And so I am not deprived of that integrity and peace before God, and I direct my prayers to him with humble trust.

units.la: Tu enim Domine per omnes Rerum Humanarum Nubes & involucra clarè perspicis. Tu sine præjudicio judicas. Tua Omnisciencia Æterna Iudicium tuum præstat ab Errore securum. Deus Meus Iniqui insurrexerunt super me, & Synagoga violentorum quæsiverunt animam meam, & non posuerunt te in conspectu suo.
units.tr: For you, Lord, see clearly through all the clouds and veils of human affairs. You judge without prejudice. Your eternal omniscience makes your judgement secure from error. My God, the unrighteous have risen up against me, and a synagogue of violent men has sought my soul, and they have not set you before their eyes.

units.la: Respice inimicos meos quoniam multiplicati sunt, & odio iniquo oderunt me.
units.tr: Look upon my enemies, for they have multiplied, and with unjust hatred they hate me.

units.la: Tu enim nosti, me nulla cupidine incitatum, nullo fine proprio, nullo denique apparatu instructum, quo sic Bello Interfini Regna Mea implicarem, ad quod certe nullo pretio invitabar, ut qui plus omnibus exponens periculo, minime omnium lucrari potuissem.
units.tr: For you know that I was not stirred by any greed, had no private end, and was furnished with no preparation, by which I might so entangle my kingdoms in war; to which I was surely not invited by any reward, since I, exposing myself to more danger than all, could least of all have gained anything.

units.la: Tu Domine testis mihi es, quàm crebrò ingemuerim, & id scrio laboraverim ut necessitatem illius averterem: qui haudquaquam ita impensè avidus existimari possum subditorum sanguinis, ut vitam meam propterea indiscrimen mittercm[?], quod sæpe feci coactus in hoc Bello Infælici, quodque multo potius factum oportuit in salutem Populi mei, quam in Perniciem.
units.tr: You, Lord, are my witness how often I have groaned and have laboured with all my might to avert the necessity of it. I can by no means be thought so eager for the blood of my subjects that I would therefore cast my life into peril, which I have often done, compelled in this unhappy war, and which ought much rather to have been done for the safety of my people than for their destruction.

units.la: Gratiâ Tua plurimùm indiggo[?] (Domine) ut patienpatienter adversa feramsquæ mihi inferri ab Hominibus permisisti, multo magis iniquas eorum calumnias qui haud contenti me Bello isto lædi maximè, id Mundo persuadere conantur me id primo excitasse, vel primam Causam dedisse excitandi.
units.tr: I ask most earnestly for your grace, Lord, that I may patiently bear the adversities which you have permitted to be inflicted upon me by men, and much more their unjust calumnies, since they, not content with the harm this war has done to me, are trying hardest to persuade the world that I was the first to stir it up, or that I gave the first cause for stirring it.

units.la: Ea falsi-loquarum Linguarum confidentia est, ut Mc propemodum in Innocentiæ Meæ sufficionem adducant. Imo vel libens paterer (meo saltem silentio) tantum in Me reatum suscipere, modo vel sic Hostium malitiam placare licuisset, populumque Meum ab hoc Bello Calamitoso redimere, cum tu Domine cognoscas Innocentiam Meam hac in Re.
units.tr: Such is the confidence of lying tongues that they almost bring me to the point of denying my innocence. Indeed, I would gladly suffer, at least by my silence, to take upon myself such guilt, if only thereby the malice of my enemies could be appeased and my people could be redeemed from this calamitous war, since you, Lord, know my innocence in this matter.

units.la: Tu viros sanguinum, & Dolosos inveniessquorum plurimi vix dimidiarunt dies suos, qui sibi Ipsis improbarum Machinationum fructus olim, & voluptatem spondebant.
units.tr: You will find men of blood and deceit, many of whom have scarcely lived out half their days, who once promised themselves the fruits and pleasure of wicked schemes.

units.la: Serva Domine famulum Tuum, quod adhuc fecisti, & dissipa Gentes quæ Bella volunt.
units.tr: Keep, Lord, your servant, as you have done until now, and scatter the nations that desire wars.

units.la: Exurge Domine, & exaltare in commotionibus hostium meorum, quæ jugiter crescunt, ascendunt semper: Ecce qui conceperunt dolorem, parturierunt Injustitiam, & pepererunt mendacium.
units.tr: Arise, Lord, and be exalted amid the uproars of my enemies, which grow continually and rise always. Behold, those who have conceived sorrow, have brought forth injustice, and have given birth to lies.

units.la: Tu scis, id maximè in hoc Bello agi, ut vel Personam Meam Interimant, vel vim faciant Judicio, vel me cogant Conscientiæ Meæ, & Veritati renunciare.
units.tr: You know that in this war the aim is chiefly this: either to destroy my person, or to do violence to judgement, or to compel me to renounce my conscience and the truth.

units.la: In hoc sum, ut (optione, illi Davidis contraria) optem potius illis Negando in Manus Hominum, crudeli utcunque Misericordia, quam in Tuas Manus incidere peccando adversus Conscientiam Meam, atque adeo contra Te (Domine) qui es Ignis Consumens. Satius multo ab illis perimi, quàm à Te damnari. Sis Tu Animæ Meæ usque præsidium, qui Salvos facis Rectos Corde.
units.tr: I am resolved, though the option is the opposite of David's, to choose rather, by denying, to fall into the hands of men, however cruel their mercy, than by sinning against my conscience to fall into your hands, and so against you, Lord, who are a consuming fire. It is far better to be destroyed by them than condemned by you. Be the constant defence of my soul, you who save the upright in heart.

units.la: Si nil jam præter sanguinem Meum vel Hostibus meis satisfacere, vel Regnorum Meorum flammas extinguere, vel Temporalem Tuam Iu-stitiam expiare potuerit, haud repugno (si ita Tua Voluntas sit) quin ab ipsis Meis subditis profun-datur.
units.tr: If nothing more than my blood could satisfy my enemies, or quench the flames of my kingdoms, or make expiation for Your temporal justice, I will not resist (if such is Your will) that it be poured out by my own subjects.

units.la: Sed ô Lavetur sanguis meus sanguine Illo In-nocentis, & Pacifici mei Redemptoris, quo Iustitiæ Tuæ non solum in præsenti sæculo, sed in æternum integrè satisfiat, tum ob Peccata mea, tum Populi mei, quem (Te Oro) usque Tuum agnoscas, & cum Iram Tuam Mors Mea seda-verit, Magnas Tuas erga Illos misericordias memineris, atque illis ignoscas. Ita Pater Meus, ignorant enim quid faciunt.
units.tr: But oh, may my blood be washed with that blood of Your innocent and peaceful Redeemer, so that Your justice may be fully satisfied, not only in the present age but for ever, both for my sins and for those of my people, whom (I pray You) acknowledge still as Yours; and when my death shall have appeased Your wrath, remember Your great mercies towards them and forgive them. So, Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.

units.la: 10. De Regio Armorum Thesauro, Monumentis, Classe, & Militia, à Parlamento occupatis.
units.tr: 10. Of the Royal Treasury of Arms, the Monuments, the Fleet, and the Militia, Seized by Parliament.

units.la: Vàm falsi Criminis arguar, quòd prior Illos Armis inuaserim, oculi eorum qui miserentur mei, & Fidelia Multorum pectora qui pro me tantum precari audent, abunde testimonio esse poterunt; quorum vix tot à Parte meâ palam stant, quot in Illâ Adversâ conscripti Milites; Ita enim prorsus ab omnibus imparatus suam [?] ad Bellum necessariis ut deterream plane opem laturos.
units.tr: Though I am falsely accused of having been the first to attack them with arms, the eyes of those who pity me and the faithful hearts of the many who dare to pray for me alone can bear ample witness. Scarcely as many men openly stand on my side as were enlisted as soldiers by that Adverse party, for they, altogether unprepared, were plainly going to bring help to war with everything it needed.

units.la: Quod, ut satis argumento est quàm invitus pugnârim, ita hoc insuper confirmat, me in Parte Defensiva versari, cum revera ita fit spes mea, & vires exiguae, quibus Alios offendam, ut nil restet quo Me-Ipsum tueor, & sim ab eorum Rapinis securus.
units.tr: This is sufficient proof of how unwillingly I fought. It further confirms that I am engaged in the defensive part, since my hope and my meagre forces are such that I can offend no one, so that nothing remains by which I may protect myself, and I am safe from their plunderings.

units.la: Haud erit dubium cuiquam, eos qui me ita Injuriis praevenerant, suis etiam Consiliis praevyc-[?] prævenisse, qui tanto me maturius prospe-xerant, ut paratissimi ad Bellum venirent, & Robur etiam Meum praeriperent: dùm, qui ab Illis non stant, Meam Partem profiteri non audent: Itâ Numero & minis Hostium oppressa omnium Fides & perterrita. Illud meum credo potius facile apud illos damnari, quod Innocentiæ Meæ confisus tam ab omnibus me parare neglexerim, quibus Ius meum & Honos affecteretur[?]: haud enim ita facile Bellum mihi indixissent, si Illos primo adoriri potuissem.
units.tr: No one will doubt that those who attacked me with injuries had also forestalled me with their plans. They had looked ahead so much earlier that they came to war fully prepared, and even snatched away my own strength, while those who are not on their side dare not profess my cause. Thus everyone's loyalty is overwhelmed and terrified by the number and threats of the enemy. I think it is easy for them to condemn in me this one thing: that, trusting in my innocence, I neglected to prepare myself in the way that all men would have expected, by which my right and my honour might have been protected. Indeed, they would not so easily have declared war on me if I had been able to attack them first.

units.la: Sed nimis bene norunt, nulla alia mihi Arma residua[?], quam (illa veterum Christianorum contra suos Persequutores) Preces Scilicet, & Lachrymas; quæ quidem Bono Viro, si non in Belli Victoriam, at, in Martyrii patientiam sufficiant.
units.tr: But they know very well that I have no other arms left than those of the ancient Christians against their persecutors: namely prayers and tears. These, indeed, will suffice for a good man, if not for victory in war, then for patience in martyrdom.

units.la: Itâ[?] interim Eorum præreptione occupari mihi Castella, Arces, Arma, Naves, Militiam eò usque mihi forsan proderit, ut non amplius confidam in brachio carnis, sed in Dei viventis me tutelam conjiciam, cui æquè facile est per Pauços admodum aut Nullos, ac per Multos servare.
units.tr: Meanwhile, the seizure by them of my castles, citadels, arms, ships, and militia may perhaps profit me so far that I no longer trust in the arm of flesh, but cast myself into the protection of the living God, to whom it is equally easy to save by few or no means as by many.

units.la: Qui voraces Ipsos vultures obsonari jussit Eliæ, & alimenta illi Ministrare, Me etiam externâ ope & præsidio destitutum tanquam opportuniorem sibi factum, patrocinio suo potest sublevare.
units.tr: He who ordered the ravenous vultures to provide food for Elijah, and to minister to him, can also support me, stripped of external help and protection, as one made more fit for his patronage.

units.la: Haud ita (Deo Gratias) de Militia mihi ereptâ laboro, quod sic Meipsum tutari, quàm quòd Populum meum amplius non possim. Horum multis & duris Oneribus ingemisco, Meis Malis factus jam superior. Subnixus alis precum & fidei, externi Roboris Manum non defidero.
units.tr: I do not grieve (thanks be to God) so much at the loss of the militia that was seized from me as a means of protecting myself, as that I can no longer protect my people. I groan under the many and harsh burdens of these men, having already been made superior by my misfortunes. Supported on the wings of prayer and faith, I do not desire the hand of external strength.

units.la: Mirâ vero Isti ratione Ænigma illud suum explicant, se, Gloriosum Me Regem effecturos, Potentiam Meam Regiam auferendo. Egregium sane Amicis Præsidium ero, & Inimicis Terror, cùm nec Illis opitulari, nec Hos valeam opprimere.
units.tr: By a wonderful reasoning they explain that enigma of theirs: that they will make me a glorious king by taking away my royal power. A remarkable protection indeed I shall be to my friends, and a terror to my enemies, since I can neither help the former nor crush the latter.

units.la: Ita enim rem instituerunt, mihique Novam prorsus excogitârunt Suprematus, & Dominationis Regiæ Formam, in qua Nulla vel Realis Potestas, vel obediendi Necessitas: ut Majestas Regum Angliæ instar Mahometis Illius Sepulchri, virtute quâdam Magnetica media pendeat inter jus & Privilegia Domorum, Phantasticâ nescio quâ, & Aereâ prorsus Regalitate.
units.tr: For they have arranged the matter thus, and devised for me an entirely new form of supremacy and royal dominion, in which there is neither any real power nor any necessity of obedience. So the majesty of the kings of England, like the tomb of that Mahomet, is to hang by some magnetic virtue between the law and the privileges of the houses, in a royalty of I know not what fantastic and utterly airy kind.

units.la: Sed credibile est, hanc Nimiæ Potestatis crapulam quam itâ avidè arripiunt Nonnulli, & penè totam deglutiunt, brevi nauseæ futuram & fastidio Reipublicæ, haud utique illam digesturæ: Suprema enim Civium Potestas, rarius arridet Stomacho Concivium.
units.tr: But it is credible that this surfeit of excessive power, which some seize so eagerly and almost swallow whole, will soon bring nausea and disgust to the commonwealth, and it will by no means digest it. For the supreme power of citizens rarely pleases the stomach of fellow citizens.

units.la: Volui tamen in hoc perpetuæ Militiæ Articulo, & Timoribus eorum, & Importunitati Satisfacere, ût vel sic Amicis meis securitatem præstarem, vincerem hostium odia, & paci omnium consulerem, Unicâ illâ Iuvandi & Nocendi Potestate exutus, cùm Illis cederem Militiam(Ius Meum indubitatum juxtà ac Coronam meam) ex utriusque Domus Arbitrio, durante Regni Mei Tempore disponendam.
units.tr: Yet in this article on the perpetual militia I wished to satisfy both their fears and their importunity, so that even so I might secure my friends, overcome the hatred of enemies, and provide for the peace of all, stripped of that single power to help and to harm. I yield to them the militia (my right, as indubitable as my crown), to be disposed of by the judgment of both houses for the duration of my reign.

units.la: Tam parato sum animo, quascunque de Me aliorum suspiciones extinguere, & citrà omnes de aliis vivere, ut non majorem mihi velim securitatem, quam Populo Meo, & Illis exopto; quos etiamsi mihi integrum esset de Militiæ statuere, tueri amplius non possem, quàm Illi Me, & seipsos vellent; unde mutua nobis invicem Militiæ utilitas, meipsum enim eo usq; tutari cupio, ut sim Bonos Meos subditos propugnandi Capax, ab eorum violentiâ & Fraude, qui suæ Improbitatis, & mali animi conscii, id Mundo persuasum cuperent, nulli tutius quàm Luporum custodiæ Gregem Ipsum cum Pastore committendum. Misero vero experimento didicerunt Subditi mei, (postquam mihi extorta Potestas contra Illos & Me simul adhibita fuerit) nullam utrinque incolumitatem restare, nisi eâ duntaxat ratione qua Lex Publicæ Saluti cavendum voluit.
units.tr: I am so ready in mind to extinguish whatever suspicions others have of me, and to live without any fear of others, that I do not wish for greater security for myself than for my people, and I desire it for them. Even if it were in my full power to decide about the militia, I could no longer protect them than they would wish to protect me and themselves. Hence the militia is of mutual benefit to us both. For I desire to protect myself only so far that I may be able to defend my good subjects from the violence and fraud of those who, conscious of their own wickedness and ill intent, would wish to persuade the world that the flock together with its shepherd should be entrusted to no one more safely than to the custody of wolves. But my subjects have learned by a bitter experience (since power was wrested from me and applied against them and me at once) that there is no safety on either side, except by that means which the law for public safety has decreed must be observed.

units.la: Hæc tamen in Exequendâ Militiâ ingens & immensa Concessio neutiquam Illis satisfacit, qui revera non mihi magis quàm Monarchico Regimini adversantur, atque adeò in posteros laborant tam malignas de Coronâ suspiciones transfundere, ut nunquàm amplius Iura sua Pristina (quantùm ad vim Potestatis) obtinere permittatur: cùm in hanc demum potestatem necesse sit Legem omnem desinere, ut quæ ab illa unicè sustentatur. Hic verò, Honos me rursum & Iustitia (quam successoribus meis debeo) prohibet, ne in futuram ab Illis penitus abalienationem Potestatis Istius, consentiam; quod quidem, Humanitatis & Officii ratio (ne dicam Honoris & Iustitiæ) vetuisset à me unquam expetere.
units.tr: Yet this vast and immense concession in carrying out the militia does not in the least satisfy those who in truth are opposed no less to me than to the monarchical government, and who labour so hard to pass on to posterity such malignant suspicions of the crown that the former rights (as far as the force of power is concerned) are never again permitted to be held. For at last all law must cease to exist in this power, since it is supported solely by that power. Here again, honour and justice (which I owe to my successors) forbid me to consent to the complete alienation of this power from them in future. Humanity and duty (not to mention honour and justice) would have forbidden me ever to ask this of myself.

units.la: Quanquam enim æquo animo feram, obscurari paulisper Radios meos, & deliquium quoddam pati & Eclipsin, ut eorum prospiciam timoribus, qui re illico torrendos vel obcæcandos metuerent, si pleno illo splendescerem Potestatis Regiæ Fulgore, quâ me Deus & Leges induerunt; nunquam tamen committam, ut Sol Ille supremi Dominatus, in Succedentibus mihi Regibus ita in omnem posteritatem extinguatur: ut ullâ Lege meâ vel Sanctione obstaculū fiat Illis vel Præjudicium, quo minus Iusta sua Iura, injuste Extorta & usurpata, Iure possint vindicare. Quod quidem si facerem, non Illis essem magis, quam Populo injurius, quos sane nollem in tam perditam conditionem relinquere, ut sint perpetuæ Lege obnoxii crebris Illis Factionum dissidiis, quæ Multiceps illam Hydram Dominationis necessario sunt consecuturæ[?], utcunque fucum faciat populo, Majoris (ut inter plures oculos) providentiæ, ea tandem reperietur, in quâ plura sunt Ora Hiantia, quæ necesse est omnia expleri. Porrò (ubi optime cum illâ agitur) aliquid forsan in se enorme habeat quo excedat, non perfectum, quo præ-stet stet Monarchiæ; in qua, sensus, consilium, suprema vero in Va-rios, velut sensus, ...
units.tr: For although I bear with equanimity that my rays should be somewhat dimmed, and suffer a certain fainting and eclipse, so that I may provide for the fears of those who dread being at once scorched or blinded if I shone with the full brilliance of the royal power with which God and the laws have clothed me, yet I shall never allow that Sun of supreme dominion to be so extinguished for all posterity in the kings who succeed me, that by any law or sanction of mine an obstacle or prejudice is put in their way, so that they cannot lawfully vindicate their just rights, unjustly extorted and usurped. If I did this, I should be no less unjust to them than to the people, whom I would surely not wish to leave in so ruined a condition that they remain always subject to those frequent dissensions of factions which must necessarily follow that many-headed Hydra of domination. Whatever deception it may practise on the people, as a greater providence (as among many eyes), it will at length be found to be one in which there are many gaping mouths that must necessarily all be filled. Moreover, where it is best managed, it may perhaps have something enormous in itself by which it exceeds, and nothing perfect by which it excels, the stet Monarchiæ; in which sense, counsel, and supreme power may be spread among many, as sense and counsel, but supreme power resides in one alone, as in the head.

units.la: stet Monarchiæ; in qua, spargi potest in Va-rios, velut sensus, consilium, suprema vero in Vno tantum ut in Capite, Potestas.
units.tr: stet Monarchiæ; in which the senses may be spread among many, as sense and counsel, but supreme power resides in one alone, as in the Head.

units.la: Forte, olim Horrores expertis & Malignas [?] Influentias ex hac meâ Obtenebratione & Eclipsi ( interpositâ videlicet illius Corporis umbrâ, quod à me solum ut Lunæ Lucem suam mutuatur ) gratior erit restituti sui Solis Gloria ; & in pretio majore fœlicitas.
units.tr: Perhaps the glory of its restored Sun will be more welcome to those who once suffered horrors and malign influences from this my obscuration and eclipse (namely, with the shadow of that body interposed, which borrows its light only from me, as the Moon does), and happiness will be valued more highly.

units.la: In præsentia, si hâc Juris mei diminutione in exercendâ Militia minus videar fidè Meam, & Juramentum tueri, quod in Populi defensionem suscperam, eorum culpa est (opinor qui mihi hanc necessitatem fecerunt, nova quadam & præpostera ratione fidem meam liberandi, dum sic videar Fidei commissa deferre, atque ita solum conservandi subditos meos, ut in pacem eorum, & quietem, me periculo autinfamiæ objiciam.
units.tr: At present, if by this diminution of my right in the exercise of the militia I seem to be less faithful, and to be failing to keep the oath which I took for the defence of the people, the fault is theirs (I think it is those who have brought upon me this necessity, by a new and preposterous plan of freeing my fidelity), since I seem to be discharging trusts committed to me, and so to be preserving my subjects only by exposing myself to danger or infamy for their peace and quiet.

units.la: Id enim, in Bello Civili, prævalente Parte una, aliter effici non potest, nisi cedat altera; quod tamen ut faciam, plus in me valet Amor Publici, & firma Auxilii Divini fiducia, (quæ è Bona Conscientia fluit) quam quæ unquam sperari possunt ab eorum Timoribus, qui (cum ex facinorum suorum Improbitate quantumvis prospera oriantur,) nunquam aliàs eos securos præstabunt, quam Militia & Gladio munitos, quæ tamen infirma admodum sunt munimina adversus Iræ Divinæ & Conscientiæ suæ flagella, quorum hæc, semper nefariè admissa comitantur, illa olim proculdubio deprehendent.
units.tr: In a civil war, one side can prevail only if the other yields. I shall have to yield, but my love for the public and my firm trust in divine help, which flows from a good conscience, count for more with me than anything that can be hoped for from the fears of those who, however prosperous their wicked deeds may seem, will never feel safe unless they are guarded by military force and the sword. Yet these are very weak defences against the scourges of divine wrath and of their own conscience, and those scourges, which always accompany wicked acts, will surely overtake them one day.

units.la: Mihi interim non videbor carere, quicquid Provida Necessitas, in Populi Mei Pacem, & Dei Gloriam Ereptura est. Hic mihi satis praesidio est, qui si unus adfuerit, abunde poterit compensare (ut olim Sancto suo Iob) quicquid Honoris, Potentiae, Libertatis, Chaldei, aut Sabei, vel Ipse etiam Diabolus abstulerit.
units.tr: Meanwhile I shall not think myself deprived of whatever that provident necessity is about to snatch away for the peace of my people and the glory of God. This is protection enough for me: if that one remains, he can more than make up (as he did for his servant Job) for whatever honour, power, liberty, Chaldeans or Sabeans, or even the Devil himself, may have taken away.

units.la: Eripiant mihi licet omne Armorum & Militiæ Robur ; omnia Arcium, & Muniminum in Terra refugia, omnem in Classe & Navigiis per Mare, fugam ; rapiant ipsa mihi etiam subditorum meorum Corda, (optimum Regis Thesaurum & propugnaculum) nunquam tamen Innocentiam, aut Dei misericordiam adimment, vel ad coelum mihi viam intercludent.
units.tr: Let them take from me all the strength of arms and of the military; all the refuges of citadels and fortifications on land, all flight by sea in fleet and ships; let them even snatch from me the hearts of my own subjects, the best treasure and bulwark of a king; yet they will never take away my innocence or God's mercy, nor will they close off the way to heaven.

units.la: Ad Te igitur (Deus Meus) & tuam opem confugio, Tu, si mihi adstare volueris, plus erit mecum, quam contra Me.
units.tr: To you therefore, my God, and to your help I flee. If you are willing to stand by me, you will be more on my side than all are against me.

units.la: Quid enim mihi est in cælo, & à Te quid volui super Terram, Etiam cum omnibus rebus dispolier Tu mihi fias potior omnibus. Ne elongaveris à me auxilium Tuum, qui non derelinquis eos qui confidunt in Te.
units.tr: For what do I have in heaven, and what do I desire upon earth besides you? Even though I be stripped of all things, you become more to me than all things. Do not remove your help far from me, you who do not forsake those who trust in you.

units.la: Vides nullum mihi Robur superesse, quod, contra Me venientibus opponam, qui, pro me pugnandi prætextu, animati, in me pugnant acerrime, sed ad Te oculos Meos dirigo.
units.tr: You see that no strength remains to me with which I might oppose those who come against me; they are roused, under the pretext of fighting for me, and they fight most fiercely against me. But I direct my eyes to you.

units.la: Tu non eges auxilio, nec Ipse porrò, si Tu adsis, eguero, quo pati possim saltem, si non vincere. Si salute mea, & prosperis haud delectaris, en me promptum in quodcunque de me vis fieri, cujus sepè Iudicia à Filiis tuis ordiuntur.
units.tr: You have no need of help, and I myself shall lack nothing further if you are with me, so that I may at least endure, if not conquer. If you take no delight in my safety and prosperity, behold, I am ready for whatever you wish to be done with me; your judgements often begin with your own sons.

units.la: Ipse nihil fiam ut Tu sis omnia.
units.tr: I myself shall be nothing, so that you may be all things.

units.la: Tu me docuisti Nullum Regem salvari multitudine Exercitus, Tu me potes servare Misericordiarum Tuarum Multitudine qui es Dominus Exercituum & Misericordiarum Pater.
units.tr: You have taught me that no king is saved by the multitude of an army. You can preserve me by the multitude of your mercies, you who are the Lord of hosts and the Father of mercies.

units.la: Subvenias mihi Domine undequaque oppresso[?], Tu meas partes suscipias, & non timebo quid faciat mihi Caro.
units.tr: Come to my aid, O Lord, I am oppressed on every side. Take up my cause, and I shall not fear what flesh may do to me.

units.la: Gloriam tuæ Iustitiæ in Adversis Meis, agnosco. O glorificet se Tua Misericordia in liberando Me ab iis qui Animam meam persequuntur.
units.tr: I acknowledge the glory of your justice in my adversities. O let your mercy be glorified in delivering me from those who pursue my soul.

units.la: Per peccata mea contra Te pugnavi, Tuus subditus, & Te Gloria Tua Spoliavi, jure ergo Tu optimo potes Me per subditos meos & spoliare Robore meo, & obscurare Gloriam.
units.tr: Through my sins I have fought against you, being your subject, and I have stripped you of your glory. Rightly, then, you may most justly strip me of my strength through my own subjects, and dim my glory.

units.la: Quin Te Monstres spes mea, & unicum Perfugium: Ne dicant Inimici mei, non est salus Ipse in Deo ejus.
units.tr: Indeed, show yourself, my hope and my only refuge, lest my enemies say, "There is no salvation for him in his God."

units.la: Perfice gressus meos in semitis Tuis ut non moveantur vestigia mea, ne nutent pedes mei.
units.tr: Direct my steps in your paths, that my footprints may not slip and my feet may not stumble.

units.la: Custodi me ut pupillam oculi, sub umbra alarum tuarum protege me.
units.tr: Keep me as the apple of your eye; under the shadow of your wings, protect me.

units.la: Infigniter ostende Bonitatem Tuam, tu qui servas dextra tua sperantes in Te, à resistentibus Dexterae Tuae.
units.tr: Show your goodness remarkably, you who save by your right hand those who hope in you, from those who resist your right hand.

units.la: Ab Impiis hominibus qui me opprimunt, & ab Inimicis, qui animam Meam circumdederunt.
units.tr: From wicked men who oppress me, and from enemies who have surrounded my soul.

units.la: Vias vitæ demonstra, adimplebis me lætitia cum vultu Tuo, delectationes in dextera Tua usque in finem.
units.tr: Show me the ways of life; you will fill me with joy in your presence, and with pleasures at your right hand forever.

units.la: II. De xix. Proposi- tionibus cum primum Regi exhiberentur, & iis quæ deinceps.
units.tr: II. On the Nineteen Propositions, when first presented to the King, and those that followed.

units.la: QUanquam plurima hîc postulantur; tamen si extrema sint ista quæ petunt, juvat tandem cognoscere, quod pretium ab Illis Incolumitati mcæ[?], & Paci Publicæ indicitur, quæ quidem nunquam existimabo me nimio posse redimere, modò id fiat sine Conscientiæ & Honoris jactura: Si non alias licuerit, eligam potius omnem illam Calamitatem & Infantiam[?], quam mihi possint Inimicissimi vel optare, vel infligere.
units.tr: Although very many things are demanded here, still, if these are the final terms they ask for, it is worth knowing at last what price is set by them for my safety and the public peace. I would never think I could redeem these at too high a cost, provided it is done without loss of conscience and honour. If it cannot otherwise be permitted, I would choose rather all that calamity and infamy which my bitterest enemies could either wish for or inflict upon me.

units.la: Quædam ex his quæ proponunt, olim à Me ultro Illis delata; alia sunt quæ facilè possunt concedi. Quod ad cætera, cùm jam pridem declaraverim Me illis salva Conscientia assentiri non posse, hâud æquum arbitror, ut districtis Gladiis, & Injuriis Belli obtrudantur. Mirum vero, nullam aliam Pacis iniri posse rationem, quàm, qua Bellum mihi necesse est Animæ meæ inferre.
units.tr: Some of the things they propose were formerly offered by me of my own accord; others are things that can easily be granted. As for the rest, since I declared long ago that I cannot assent to them with my conscience intact, I do not think it fair that they should be forced upon me with drawn swords and the injuries of war. It is a wonder indeed that no other way of making peace can be entered upon than that by which I must inflict war upon my soul.

units.la: Multa hic à me valdè expectunt, nil contra vicissim redhibent, quo, vel Honoris fiat grata commutatio, vel, quæ Illis jam indulserim, vel sim porrò indulturus, aliquo saltem ossicio compensentur: In hoc utique Honori meo favent, quod mihi Datoris tantum partes (quod Regum[?] quidem magis, & Divinum) assignent. Revera, haud plura flagitare possunt, quàm ego dare; servem mihi seorsim modò Incommunicabilem Conscientiæ meæ Gemmam, nec illam à me cogar amittere, cujus damnum nihil unquam vel resarcire potest, vel restituere.
units.tr: They expect much from me here and offer nothing in return, by which either a mutually honourable exchange might be made, or what I have already granted them, or what I may grant them in future, might be repaid by at least some service. In this they certainly favour my honour, in that they assign to me only the part of giver (which belongs more to kings, and even to God). Indeed they can demand no more than I can give. Let me keep for myself alone the incommunicable jewel of my conscience, nor let me be forced to lose it, for no loss of it can ever be made good or restored.

units.la: Quædam verò (quæ His rogare libuerit) ita mihi videntur omni prorsus Ratione aliena, ut, dum Ipse Rationis Compos sim, mirer illos potuisse consensum meum sperare: cùm hoc Ipsi ignorare non possint, nec cum Rege, nec Christiano, ut his omnino assentiatur, constare: Quod tot hactenus donaverim, auget illis fiduciam, me nihil negaturum.
units.tr: Some things, however (which they have been pleased to ask of me), seem to me so entirely alien to reason that, while I am myself in possession of reason, I wonder they could hope for my consent. They cannot be ignorant that it is consistent neither with the King nor with a Christian to assent to these at all. That I have granted so many things so far only increases their confidence that I will refuse them nothing.

units.la: Multum in me valet (fateor) amor populi mei & Pacis Publicæ, at Veritatis tamen studium, & Internæ Pacis plus pollet.
units.tr: The love of my people and of the public peace weighs heavily with me (I confess), but the zeal for truth and for inner peace weighs more.

units.la: Rogant enim hic à me nonnulla, quibus si annuerem, non tam externa mea conditio Regia debilior redderetur, quàm afflicta Conscientiæ quies, quæ mihi est, & esse debet atque etiam erit, Deo favente, omnibus Regnis potior.
units.tr: For they ask here for some things which, if I were to agree to them, would make not so much my outward royal condition weaker as my troubled quiet of conscience, which I have, and ought to have, and indeed will have, by God's favour, more precious than all kingdoms.

units.la: Quædam, quæ approbari forsan alias à Rege possent, interest tamen aliquando & prudentiæ & Honoris ut quibusdam Hominibus, & quibusdam etiam Temporibus negentur, ne sic omnia concedens videretur nil ausus negare, nimisque aliis animum faceret, improba & inverecunda postulandi.
units.tr: Some things, which perhaps could otherwise be approved by the King, it is nevertheless sometimes in the interest of prudence and of honour to refuse to certain men, and to certain times as well, lest by thus granting everything he should seem to have dared to refuse nothing, and should make others too bold in shameless and insolent demands.

units.la: Vt vero generali adeo, & implicito consensu (id enim inter caetera requirunt) in omnia ab Illis allata, vel proposita adstringar, tam cæcæ esset penitus obedientiæ, qualis nunquam à libero homine speraretur, quàm, cùm à nullo prorsus exigere debeamus, multo minus à Rege subditi, quorum unum-quemlibet fieri potest ut Prudentia haud minus, quàm Dignitate antistet.
units.tr: But that I should be bound by a general and implicit consent (for this is among the other things they require) to all the things brought forward or proposed by them would be a blind obedience of a kind never to be hoped for from a free man. All the more so, since we ought to exact it from no one at all, much less from a King by his subjects, each one of whom may be no less eminent in prudence than in dignity.

units.la: Idem enim prorsus videtur, ac si Sampson ille olim consensisset non in manus sibi solum colligandas & abradendos cincinnos. sed in oculorum etiam exclusionem, quo illi tutius Philistei illuderent; quod multò potius certè malebant, quàm mansuefactum in contumelias, & ludibriis opportunum statim perderet.
units.tr: For it would seem exactly the same as if that Sampson of old had consented not only to having his hands bound and his locks shaved, but also to having his eyes put out, so that the Philistines could mock him more safely. They certainly preferred this far more, than that a tamed man should at once be lost, fit for insults and ridicule.

units.la: Porrò hæc qualiscunque arrogantia quâ omnem mihi Negandi facultatem tollunt, Illos minimè omnium decere videatur, qui se Humiles Meos subditos, & demisse supplicantes profitentur, in quo, satis se agnoscunt Inferiores, & consequenter obligari, responso ejusmodi, quod superiorus sui Arbitrium vel Ratio dederit, etiamsi non integrè Satisfaciat, acquiescere. Cum penes illum fatentur Vim certe aliquam Rationis, & consentiendi ac diffentiendi libertatem, nimis sultè alioquin petituri, quod nec liberum negare, nec integrum illi foret concedere.
units.tr: Furthermore, this arrogance of whatever sort, by which they take from me every power of refusal, seems least of all to befit those who profess themselves to be my humble subjects and submissive suppliants. In this they acknowledge themselves to be sufficiently inferior, and consequently bound to acquiesce in whatever answer their superior's judgment or reason has given, even if it does not fully satisfy them. Since they confess that in him there is certainly some power of reason, and a freedom to consent and to dissent, they would otherwise be asking too rashly for what it would be neither right to refuse nor fully proper for him to grant.

units.la: Quod fi jus illud mihi utrinque competat, (tùm qua Ratio jubet, ut Homini, tum, qua Honos[?] proculdubio ut Principi;) quantâ jam & quam immani injuriâ circumscribunt Rationem Meam intra unam concedendi neceffitatem quicquid ipsis rogare placuerit? Ipsis, inquam, quorum mens & sententia (in rebus utique ad Honorem & Rationem spectantibus) à mea forsan longius recedit, quàm sint Fines nostri, & Conditio diversa; hanc enim Deus satis & Leges discriminârunt, cum me Regem fecerunt, Illos Subditos, à quibus opponi mi- hi hæc verius, quàm proponi dicantur, quæ ita Regiæ Authoritati necessario imponuntur. Haud enim Principis sui quisquam Rationem astringere,& cancellis præfinire laborabit, nisi qui id simul agitat,ut vel dividat Imperium, vel in Illum usurpet.
units.tr: But if that right belongs to me on both sides (both as a man, which reason commands, and as a prince, which honour doubtless requires), with how great and how monstrous an injury do they now confine my reason within the single necessity of granting whatever they have been pleased to ask? To them, I say, whose mind and opinion (in matters, to be sure, that concern honour and reason) perhaps depart from mine further than our boundaries and our differing condition are apart. For God and the laws have sufficiently distinguished these, when they made me King and them subjects; and these things are said to be imposed upon me rather than proposed, as things that are thus necessarily imposed upon royal authority. For no one of his prince's subjects will labour to bind and confine his reason within bars, unless he is at the same time aiming either to divide the empire or to usurp it against him.

units.la: Hoc vero, pro æquitate sua postulant, ut abdicato meo proprio Judicio, eorum me Arbitrio totum tradam, atque adeò me Eum ostendam (qualis à Nonnullis depingor) dignum scilicet, qui Pupillus eorum potius quàm Princeps audiam. Meo quidem ut non ita ingenio arrogo, quin lubens admittam aliorum Consilia, ita neque tam penitus diffido, ut me, bruto quodam more, quorumvis in dictata subjiciam & Rationis in Anima mea Imperio, & Coronæ Majestate subditis meis simul prodita. Certè, nulla unquam vel Argumenti umbra est, quâ eorum cupiditati obtemperare persuadear, qui sic suam & aliorum libertatem in Consessu & suffragiis Parlamentariis vel Ipsi impugnant, vel ab aliis im-pugnari negligunt.
units.tr: But they demand, in the name of their own fairness, that I should set aside my own judgment and surrender myself entirely to their decision, and so show myself (as some depict me) to be worthy of hearing their ward rather than their prince. Indeed, I do not claim so much for my own ability as to refuse gladly the counsels of others, nor do I distrust myself so deeply that I should, like a brute beast, submit myself to whatever they dictate, to the detriment of the rule of reason in my soul and the majesty of the Crown, betrayed at the same time to my subjects. Surely there is no shadow of argument by which I could be persuaded to obey the desires of those who, in the assembly and in the votes of Parliament, either themselves attack their own and others' liberty, or neglect to see it attacked by others.

units.la: Adhæc, omnes qui istos norunt, probè sciunt, quàm Tyrones sint penitus in Re Politica plærique istorum qui hæc postulant, ut sa-nè, dum me septem insuper annorum experientia docuerit, quam bene vel se ipsos regere, vel, quam à me jam extorserint, potentiam moderari valeant, omnium esset stolidissimus, & Fidei meæ commissi proditor, si remissas è Manu meâ Rationis & Regiminis habenas, in eorum statim traderem, qui jam pridem instar Ichu, præcipitanter ducuntur; & qui in Summam sedem insilire impotenter cupidi, plus multò Phaëthonta quam Phœbum referunt: Omen Deus avertat.
units.tr: Moreover, all who know them know well how entirely raw in Politics most of those are who make these demands. Since seven years' experience has taught me how well they can either govern themselves, or moderate the power they have already wrested from me, I would be the most foolish of men, and a traitor to the trust committed to me, if I were to hand over at once to them the reins of reason and government, released from my hand, to those who have for some time been led headlong like beasts, and who, impotently eager to leap into the highest seat, resemble Phaethon far more than Phoebus. God avert the omen!

units.la: Id utinam meminerint, se (ut optimè cum illis agatur) Sedere in hoc Consessu Subditos meos non Superiores; Consiliarios hùc vocari, non Dictatores. Ita enim Rescripti verba habent, ut Consilia sua proponant, non mihi parendi necessitatem.
units.tr: May they remember that they sit in this assembly (as things go best for them) as my subjects, not my superiors; that they are called here as counsellors, not dictators. For so the words of the rescript have it: that they should propose their counsels, not impose on me the necessity of obeying.

units.la: Cùm hoc primùm ad me allatum effet, Propositiones mihi aliquas exhibendas, id peti exspectabam, ut Leges Bonæ, vel jam longo tempore antiquatæ, vel incumbente morum corrucorruptelâ, oppressæ, in vim suam pristinam & vigorem restituerentur; vel ut pravæ nonnullæ præter Legem consuetudines & Personales Abusus tollerentur; vel, quod Ipse forsan aut alii detrimentum Publico tulissent, resarciretur; vel, ut æque mihi hujusmodi conditiones deferrentur, propter quas, (cùm illis cordi esse intelligerem Coronæ Meæ Privilegia) multo facilius inducerer ad iis Rogationibus acquiescendum, quæ ita populi Bonum spectabant, ut me non admodum minuerent, quem Lex, Natura, Ratio, & Religio primo loco jubent servare; sine quo, impossibile est Populum meum (prout Muneri meo par est) conservare.
units.tr: When it was first brought to me that some propositions were to be presented to me, I expected that there would be asked either that good laws, long since abrogated or suppressed by the creeping corruption of morals, be restored to their former force and vigour; or that some perverse customs and personal abuses contrary to law be removed; or that whatever detriment to the public had been caused by myself or others be made good; or that conditions of this sort be offered to me as well, on account of which (since I understood the privileges of my Crown to be dear to them) I would be much more easily led to acquiesce in those requests which so regarded the good of the people that they would not greatly diminish me, whom law, nature, reason, and religion first bid me preserve. Without this, it is impossible for me to preserve my people (as befits my office).

units.la: Illud saltem sperabam, in iis quæ prave admissa fuerant vel in Ecclesiastica Re vel Civili, tam moderata futura Reformandi studia, ut Fundamentum & Essentia utriusque Regiminis integra & salva manerent; haud vero ita utrumque conquassandum simul, & convellendum, nullâ prorsus ratione habitâ vel Legum jam obtinentium, vel Pietatis & Prudentiæ superiorum omnium Conventuum, vel Antiquæ & universæ Praxeos Christianæ Ecclesiæ, vel quæ ad Jura spectant & Privilegia Singularium: cum interim loco Illius, quod abolendum erat, nil omnino reponendum curarent, quod vel prioris Instituti bonum Finem attingeret, vel Defectus prætensos supplerct, vel Abusus reformaret, vel, Cordatis hominibus satisfaceret, qui non verbis Phaleratis & mollibus, zelum quendam singularem & pietatem crepantibus, ducuntur, sed id ferio expetunt scire, quàm solidis Argumentis, & vivis rationibus tùm divinis, tum humanis, tantarum Novationum præceps Impetus & necessitas possit fustentari.
units.tr: I hoped at least that in those things which had been wrongly admitted, whether in the Church or the Civil order, the efforts at reforming would be so moderate that the foundation and essence of both governments would remain whole and safe. They did not, however, intend to shake and overthrow both at once, taking no account at all of the laws now in force, or of the piety and prudence of all the earlier assemblies, or of the ancient and universal practice of the Christian Church, or of what pertains to the rights and privileges of individuals. Meanwhile, in place of what was to be abolished, they took no care to put anything at all in its place, which might attain the good end of the former institution, supply the alleged defects, reform the abuses, or satisfy prudent men. Such men are not led by painted and soft words crying up some singular zeal and piety, but earnestly desire to know with what solid arguments and living reasons, both divine and human, the headlong rush and necessity of such great innovations can be sustained.

units.la: At in istis quidem Propositionibus animadverto hujus generis perpauca vel in hunc prorsus finem. Nil in Legibus luxatum quod hîc volunt restitui, nulla Juris alieni usurpatio abdicanda, nulla Justitiæ obstructio removenda, nulla omnino Injuriarum Compensatio, vel quicquam æquæ hujusmodi Reformationis rogatur, cui vel Ratio vel Religio, vel Prudentia Politica, vel Humanum quodcunque Argumentum ad annuendum impellat.
units.tr: But in those Propositions I notice very few of this kind, or indeed any aimed at this end. Nothing in the laws that is out of joint is what they want restored. No usurpation of another's right is to be renounced, no obstruction of justice is to be removed, no compensation at all is asked for injuries, and no reform of this sort is proposed that reason, religion, political prudence, or any human argument whatever could urge me to accept.

units.la: Quod vero ad summam eorum attinet, quæ diversis temporibus perhibita, nova maximè & difficilia videbantur, id demum perspexi, ea, quæ olim in Regno seditiones & Ecclesiæ Schismata habita ac legibus propterea obnoxia, jam eò usque fiduciæ pervenisse (vulgi scilicet clamoribus & auxilio præcipuè propugnata) ut non satis habeant, ipsa, cum vanitate sua, novitate, confusione tolerari, nisi hoc insuper requirant, ut Leges omnes contra Illos abrogentur, quin & Regimen Illud extirpeur[?], cujus Jura jam quæfrunt invadere.
units.tr: As for the sum of what has been put forward at various times, which seemed new and difficult, I have at last perceived this: those things which were formerly in the kingdom regarded as seditions and in the Church as schisms, and for that reason liable to the laws, have now grown so bold (chiefly championed, of course, by the clamours and help of the common people) that they are not content to be tolerated with their vanity, novelty and confusion. They further demand that all laws against them be repealed, and that that very government be rooted out, whose rights they now seek to invade.

units.la: Hoc ad summum eorum quæ petunt: Cætera feré sunt chartæ ineptæ & supervacuæ, in quibus ista involvunt ideo, ut honestius paulo afferantur. Mihi vero haud perinde admirationi diversitas istarum aut detestanda novitas, cum nil sit adeo portentum, in quod aliqua Phantasia non pruriat.
units.tr: This is the sum of what they ask. The rest is mostly silly and superfluous paper, in which they wrap these things so that they may be put forward a little more respectably. For my part, the diversity of these things, or their detestable novelty, does not so much amaze me, since there is nothing so monstrous that some fancy does not itch for it.

units.la: Illud penitus obstupesco, quâ tandem ratione contingeret, ut Articuli istiusmodi sub Utrinsque Confessus nomine Parlamenti Anglicani exhiberentur, cum id certò affirmaverim vix esse quartam partem Membrorum utriusque Ordinis qui seorsim singulí & liberi tam perniciosas Mutationes in Ecclesiastico Regimine vel probare possunt, vel expetere.
units.tr: I am utterly astonished by what means it could have happened that articles of this kind were presented under the name of both Houses of the English Parliament, since I can affirm with certainty that scarcely a quarter of the members of each Order, taken singly and freely, could either approve or desire such pernicious changes in the ecclesiastical government.

units.la: Quin id etiam persuasum habeo, restare etiamnum in Majori Parte utriusque Confessus (modò Libertas illis sua & Numerus constet) eam scientiam, Rationem, Pietatem, & Moderationem æquanimem, ut ipsi satis discernant, quid recto rerum usui abusus, quid primæ Institutioni, Corruptio, quid ipsi Regimini, navi Regiminis, quid Archetypo Exemplari, posteriorum errata, & mendæ intersint.
units.tr: Indeed I am also persuaded that there remains even now in the greater part of both Houses (provided that their liberty is secure and their number is sound) such knowledge, reason, piety and even-tempered moderation that they can sufficiently discern what in the right use of things belongs to use and what to abuse; what belongs to the first institution and what to corruption; what belongs to government itself and what to the ship of government; what belongs to the archetypal pattern, and what to the errors and blemishes of later times.

units.la: Certè haud credibile erat, nullis ita vel tam levibus argumentis in contrarium adductos ita penitus renunciasse omni legum quæ jam vigebant reverentiæ, vel pietatis Majorum Reformantium, vel florentissimi priorum temporum Regni hujus & Ecclesiæ status sub præsenti illius Regimine.
units.tr: Certainly it was not credible that men, led to the contrary by no arguments, or by such slight ones, should so utterly have renounced all reverence for the laws then in force, or for the piety of the reforming forefathers, or for the most flourishing state of this kingdom and Church in former times under the present government.

units.la: Mira tamen nescio quâ fatalitate, quid per absentiam, silentium, incuriam supinamque & stupidam credulitatem, (qua nimis faciles nonnulli, zeli omnia & Reformationis fuco tincta, ut sinceraм pietatem agnoscere) abripi seutcunque patiebantur communi torrente, qui ex hoc (velut primo fonte) scatet Popularis Tumultu & Clamoribus, unde haud mirum animos&vires crevisse nefariæ eorum sedulitati, qui omni arte & industriâ ex præsentibus dissidiis Innovantia sua consilia promovebant.
units.tr: Yet by some strange fatality, through absence, silence, carelessness and a supine and stupid credulity (to which some men, too easily taken in, and dyeing everything with the zeal and rouge of reform, so that they recognise it as sincere piety, are far too prone), they allowed themselves to be swept along in some way by the common torrent. This gushes forth from this source, as from its first spring, with popular tumult and clamours. Hence it is no wonder that the spirits and strength grew of those men who, with every art and industry, were advancing their innovating designs out of the present dissensions.

units.la: Hæc propositionum Agmina ( cum nec tantillum ( meo Judicio ) Rationis, Justitiæ, Religionis ex eorum parte militaret, ut quæ a Turbis & factionibus inchoata ) jam nec solitaria incedunt, sed alio Militum Agmine sustentantur; quorum istud utcunque contra Personam meam invalucrit, haud tamen à prioribus illis me expugnari patiar, ulterius quàm causam video non enim Manu hîc & Numero agendum est, sed Justitiæ & Rationum ponderibus.
units.tr: These columns of propositions (since, in my judgement, not the least bit of reason, justice or religion fights on their side, as they were begun by mobs and factions) no longer march alone, but are supported by another column of soldiers. Though that column has somehow gained strength against my person, I shall not allow myself to be overcome by the former ones beyond what I see the case requires. For the matter is not to be decided here by hand and number, but by the weight of justice and reasons.

units.la: Enimvero, si uterque Confessus, pupillatu suo deposito, emancipasset se strenue ex hoc Tumultuantium Patronatu (qui nil aliud prorsus sunt quàm Canes quidam venatici stantes aure arrecta ad eorum hortatus, qui cum Regni & Ecclesiæ perniciem privatos suos fines & Consilia persequuntur) vel, si hoc mihi semel persuasum fuisset, esse hæc postulata ex pluribus eorum suffragiis, qui non minore Libertate utuntur quam Iure sedent; forte etiam judicium meum suspicari poteram, si minus plenè & alacriter ad eorum sententias accederem.
units.tr: Indeed, if both Houses, having laid aside their wardship, had vigorously freed themselves from this patronage of the rioters (who are nothing at all but hunting dogs standing with ears pricked at the urging of those who, while bringing ruin on kingdom and Church, pursue their own private ends and designs), or if I had once been persuaded that these demands come from the votes of many of them, who sit with no less liberty than right, perhaps I could even suspect my own judgement, if I did not agree with their opinions fully and eagerly.

units.la: Superest enim mihi Charitas quâ credam esse aliquos inter Illos prudentes, quin & humilitas etiam quâ agnoscam me Prudentia corum in nonnullis & egere posse, & uti oportere, cum hoc fine eos omnes ad hunc Conventum vocaverim: nunquam tamen illis concedam ita consummatam sapientiam, & ab erroribus securam, ut meipsum velim excludere: cum nemo prorsus sit eorum, cui incumbit, vel Personam tantum agere, vel illam Fidem liberare, vel eandem mecum Fortunam & Honorem tueri: atque adeo nulli valent sine Rationis meæ concursu (qui non secus ac sol in Naturalibus necessariò hîc debet influere )ullum Actum Perfectum, & Publicæ Prudentiæ Authoritate vestitum (quo Lex scitum constituitur) generare unquam vel producere.
units.tr: For I still have charity, by which I believe that some among them are prudent; and humility too, by which I acknowledge that I may both need and ought to use their prudence in some matters, since I have summoned them all to this assembly for this very purpose. Yet I will never grant them such consummate wisdom, free from error, that I would wish to shut myself out. For none of them is such that it falls to him either merely to play a part, or to free that faith, or to defend the same fortune and honour along with me. And so none of them can bring forth or ever produce any complete act, clothed with public authority (by which a decree of law is established), without the concurrence of my reason, which here must flow in as the sun necessarily does in nature.

units.la: Mihi vero haud certius constat de iniquâ absurditate quarundam ex his Propositionum, quam illud valdè exploratum habeo, nequaquam hîc libera fuisse, & conjuncta Vota Majoris eorum Numeri qui hîc jure sedent, & suffragantur..
units.tr: I am no less certain of the unjust absurdity of some of these Propositions than I hold it thoroughly established that they were by no means freely decided here, and that the combined votes of the greater number of those who sit here by right and cast their voice were not free.

units.la: Plurimæ enim ex istis, specie licet Reformandi præla-tâ, fermentum illud vetus redolent, corum scilicet Novatorum, qui sub duobus Decessoribus Meis, Principi simul & Parlamento negotium facessebant, & subinde minabantur: quo, licet vulgus statim Morbum haurire potuerit, haud ita frequens unquam infecta fuit Nobilitatis Massa, cæterique ex Equestri ordine, atque adeò haud ita derepente poterat in Majorem utriusque Domus partem illabi,ut sic unanimi voto conspirarent tot enormes,& plenas periculi in Ecclesia & Regno Novitates, omnes Praxi suæ, Judicio, Educationi adversantes invehere.
units.tr: For most of these, though they pretend the appearance of reforming, smell of that old leaven: that is, of those innovators who under my two predecessors gave trouble to the Prince and Parliament alike, and from time to time threatened. Although the common people could catch the disease at once, the mass of the nobility and the others of the knightly order were never so often infected, nor could they so suddenly slip into the greater part of either House, so as to unanimously agree in voting for so many outrageous novelties, full of danger to the Church and Kingdom, all opposed to their practice, their judgement and their upbringing.

units.la: Neque vero, me fugit, adscitos in huncOrdinem plurimos impetu & studiis Popularium: quorum nonnulli nil ardentius sitiebant, quàm ut offensas quas in Me vel in Aulam Meam, vel Clerum conceperant, acriter omnes ulciscerentur: nulla tamen ratio permittit, ut immensam hanc & subitaneam Novandi cupidinem, ultra quàm Paucis Illis imputem, qui se Turbâ hac Multicipiti[?] & Multimanâ armârant.
units.tr: Nor, I am aware, have many been admitted into this Order through the rush and zeal of the populace, some of whom thirsted for nothing more eagerly than to avenge sharply all the offences they had conceived against me, or against my Court, or the clergy. Yet no reason allows me to impute this immense and sudden desire for innovation to more than those few who armed themselves with this many-headed and many-handed mob.

units.la: Eadem interim me Ratio hortatur, Honorifque simul & Incolumitatis Respectus Ecclesiæ & Regno debitæ, ut ejusmodi mihi buccellas oblatas lente prius manducem quàm in Stomachum demittam: Sin conscientiæ meæ angustia impediar, quo minus eâ quâ alii facilitate deglutiam hos in Deum & homines sacrilegii & Injustitiæ Camelos, nulla causa est cur expostulent haud æquè vastum mihi guttur ac illis patere; Id Deo juvante fixum manet, nulla vel perturbatione, vel pervicaciâ, vel contradicendi libidine, vel inani Negativæ Vocis ostentatione ita transversum actum iri judicium meum, ut sim voluntati meæ obsequuturus, quicquam unquam negando, quod Conscientia mea & Ratio negare vetuerit.
units.tr: Meanwhile the same reason urges me, and the respect for honour and safety owed to the Church and Kingdom, to chew such morsels, offered to me, slowly at first, before I send them down into my stomach. But if the narrowness of my conscience prevents me from swallowing, with the ease that others have, these camels of sacrilege and injustice against God and men, there is no reason why they should complain that my throat is not as wide as theirs. With God's help this remains fixed: by no disturbance, nor obstinacy, nor lust for contradiction, nor the empty show of a negative voice, will my judgement be so turned aside that I shall be obedient to my will by denying anything ever which my conscience and reason have forbidden me to deny.

units.la: Contra, nulli unquam rei ultrà assentiar, nisi in quantum eâdem Ratione, Iustitia, Honore, & Religione persuadeor, futurum in Dei Gloriam, Bonum Ecclesiæ, Populique salutem & Pacem.
units.tr: On the contrary, I will never assent to any matter beyond the point to which I am persuaded by the same reason, justice, honour and religion that it will be for the glory of God, the good of the Church, and the safety and peace of the people.

units.la: Satisfacere quidem conabor Parlamento meo & Populo, sed ut ulli unquam Factioni quantumvis potenti gratificer, nec metu subigar nec adulatione. Hoc enim esset, detrimento Corporis, morbum alere.
units.tr: Indeed I shall try to satisfy my Parliament and my people, but I shall never gratify any faction, however powerful, nor be driven by fear or by flattery. For that would be feeding a disease to the detriment of the body.

units.la: Cæterum, licet fides multorum, & prudentia deterreantur, quo minus liberum illud mihi & fidele Consilium (quod & possent alioquin & vellent, & quo carere jam possum, impertiant) nemo tamen efficiet, ne Sapientiam implorem Admirabilis Illius Consiliarii qui & optima dictare potest, & cor meum ad obsequendum inflectere.
units.tr: Otherwise, although the good faith and prudence of many may be deterred from giving me that free and faithful counsel (which they could otherwise give, and would give, and which I can now do without), yet no one will prevent me from invoking the wisdom of that Wonderful Counsellor, who can both dictate the best things and bend my heart to obey.

units.la: O Tu Prima & Æterna Ratio, Cujus summa Sapientia omnipotentiâ armatur, instrue Famulum Tuum clara primum patefactione Veritatis, Rationis, Iustitiæ in intellectu Meo, deinde sic voluntatem adhærendi propositum confirmes, ut nullo terrore, vel injuriis, vel quacunque vi adhibita, cogant me Inimici mei in eas unquam Regulas peccare, quas tu per eas Conscientiæ Meæ implantavisti.
units.tr: O Thou First and Eternal Reason, whose supreme wisdom is armed with omnipotence, first instruct Thy servant by the clear manifestation of truth, reason and justice in my understanding; then so confirm the purpose of my will in adhering to them that no terror, no injuries, nor any force applied, may ever compel my enemies to make me sin against those rules which Thou hast implanted in my conscience through them.

units.la: Non me ideo Regem fecisti, ut minor essem Homine, nec auderem Etiam meum & Non prout causam video, profiteri, quæ libertas nec vel Infimæ Creaturæ denegatur, cui vel usus Rationis inest, & facultas loquendi.
units.tr: You did not make me king so that I should be less than a man, nor so that I should not dare to profess even my own opinion and my view of the case. This is a freedom not denied even to the lowest creature that has the use of reason and the power of speech.

units.la: Mihi ergo soli in crimen cedet, quod in aliis veracitas, & Constantia laudabilis.
units.tr: Yet this alone will be counted as a crime against me, though in others truthfulness and steadfastness are praised.

units.la: Vides (Domine) quàm pravis studiis, & quâ iniquitate illam mihi Regi suo libertatem negant, quam Tu omnibus dedisti, quamque ipsi pertinaciter sibi vendicant, cum sint ita valde solliciti, ne in minima quaque parte Privilegia sua laedantur.
units.tr: You see, Lord, with what wicked designs and what injustice they deny me, their king, that liberty which You have given to all, and which they stubbornly claim for themselves, being so anxious that the least of their privileges should be harmed in any part.

units.la: Ad te supplex confugio, qui solum Regulâ non errante ducere nos potes & dirigere per ambiguos Labyrinthos cogitationum nostrarum, & quae ab aliis difficilia proponuntur, quae, non sine causa, suspicor ultro mihi objecta ut laqueos, ut, seu offenserim illis, seu negaverim, iis usque anguſtiis constrictus hæream, quibus animæ meæ insidiantur.
units.tr: I flee as a suppliant to You, who alone can lead and direct us by an unerring rule through the ambiguous labyrinths of our thoughts, and through the difficult propositions put forward by others. I suspect, and not without cause, that these have been thrown in my way as snares, so that, whether I offend against them or deny them, I may be caught fast in the same straits by which my soul is beset.

units.la: Dirige Domine in conspectu tuo viam meam. Ne vitiosi mei affectus & perturbationes diverticulant illa unquam aut obnubilent, quæ à sancto tuo spiritu suggeruntur.
units.tr: Direct my way in Your sight, O Lord. Let my faulty affections and disturbances never turn it aside or cloud those things which are suggested by Your Holy Spirit.

units.la: Sit Gloria Tua, finis meus: Verbum Tuum Regula Mea: & Tua fiat Voluntas.
units.tr: Let Your glory be my end, Your Word my rule, and Your will be done.

units.la: Omnibus placere non possum; quibusdam placere nil moror. Felix eo sim, ut tibi placeam; haud magnopere metuendum, si cui alii displicuero.
units.tr: I cannot please everyone; I care nothing for pleasing some. May I be happy in this, that I please You; there is no great need to fear if I displease anyone else.

units.la: Tu qui Mundi Sapientiam stultitiam facis, & comprehendis in Consiliis suis qui sibi Sapientes videntur, me veritate tua Efficias, in Honorem Tuum, Regnorum Meorum Bonum Publicum, & Animæ meæ salutem satis sapere;atque hinc ero valde sollicitus quid à Mundo existimer vel in quo Numero habear.
units.tr: You who make the wisdom of the world foolishness, and who take the wise in their own conceits in Your counsels, make me, by Your truth, to be wise enough for Your honour, for the public good of my kingdoms, and for the salvation of my soul. Hence I shall be very anxious about what the world thinks of me, or among what number I am counted.

units.la: Quo mihi minus prudentiæ velint tribuere, eò magis demonstrabitur tuâ me Sapientia gubernans, dum nil dignum concedi pervicacia aut affectu degenem, & nil etiam quod merito negari debet, metu hominum concedam, aut adula-tione.
units.tr: The less prudence they are willing to attribute to me, the more it will be shown that I am guided by Your wisdom, provided that I yield nothing unworthy through obstinacy or passion, and nothing that ought rightly to be refused, either from fear of men or from flattery.

units.la: Ne me in crimen illud patiaris vel infortunium labi, ut (vel sponte, vel temere) cujuscunque hominis Consilia Bono Publico injuria promoveam, dum assensu meo rata faciam.
units.tr: Do not suffer me to fall into that crime, or into that misfortune, of promoting, whether willingly or rashly, the counsels of anyone to the public good's injury, by giving them my assent and making them valid.

units.la: Sed nec morosò unquam & perverso dissensu, obstem Bono Publico, aut fraudem faciam.
units.tr: Nor let me ever stand in the way of the public good, or defraud it, through a peevish and perverse dissent.

units.la: Dones me illa Charitate, humili, ut eorum etiam sequar Consilia cum expedire in Publicum videantur, quorum in me animi benevoli perexigua argumenta reperio.
units.tr: Grant me such humble charity that I may also follow those counsels which seem expedient for the public, even where I find only very slight evidence of goodwill towards me in those who propose them.

units.la: Tibi juxta facile est honestis erroribus beneaicere, ac fraudulenta consilia disiparc[?].
units.tr: It is easy for You to bring good out of honest errors and to scatter fraudulent counsels.

units.la: Cum de omni verbo malo & otioso ratio reddenda sit ad tuum Tribunal, fac (Domine) ut summa prius cura adhibita prodeant hae Sententiae meae, & Declarationes solennes ut quae sint maximè in Publicum vel Bonum, vel Malum valiturae.
units.tr: Since an account must be rendered at Your tribunal of every idle and evil word, grant, O Lord, that these my opinions and solemn declarations be put forth only after the greatest care has first been taken, since they are most likely to have a lasting effect for the public good or harm.

units.la: Quo minus isti quid petant cogitaverint, eo impensius me facias quid respondeam, sollicitum.
units.tr: The less I can tell what those men are seeking, the more earnestly You make me anxious about what I should answer.

units.la: Sint licet graves Meae, & populi miseriae, & pax omnis futura gratissima, nunquam tamen permittas (Domine) ut vel minimo Conscientiae impendio, vel illas unquam effugere, vel hanc vedim[?] comparare, eam Tu merito plus Illius, quam ego Dominus.
units.tr: Though my own troubles and those of the people be grave, and whatever peace may come be most welcome, yet never permit me, O Lord, at the cost of the least part of my conscience, either to escape those troubles or to buy this pardon, which You, rightly, hold more of than I, Your servant, do.

units.la: 12. De Rebellione Hi-bernica.
units.tr: 12. On the Irish Rebellion.

units.la: MOtus illi in Hybernia tam repentini e-rant & tanto impetu, ut difficile fit vel Principia eorum discernere, vel praecipitatæ jam Rebellioni remedium applicare.
units.tr: The uprisings in Ireland were so sudden and so violent that it is hard either to discern their origins or to apply a remedy to a rebellion that had already rushed headlong.

units.la: Revera mare illud sanguinis summâ illic saevitiâ & immanitate fuisse[?] satis est in æternum obruendo omni simul calamitate&dedecore, quemcunque Deus deprehenderit vel malitiosum Authorem, vel omninò Incentorem extitisse.
units.tr: Indeed, that sea of blood, with its extreme savagery and barbarity there, is enough to overwhelm for ever, along with all calamity and disgrace, whoever God shall find to have been the malicious author or the outright instigator.

units.la: Accedit verò mihi infælicissimè, ut hinc etiam quorundam Malitia in me telum arriperet, qui cum satis impudenter mihi quidvis imponere parati essent, hâc libenter sunt usi occasione sanguinaria quò me illâ aspergerent, cùm [illegible, ~2 letters] facinus esset procul dubio à quo Ipse maximè omnium abhorrere debeam, ut pleno in Deum sceleris, in me, perfidiæ, & in subditos ita exitiali.
units.tr: It has also fallen very unhappily upon me that the malice of certain people has taken up this as a weapon against me. Since they were quite shameless and ready to impute anything at all to me, they gladly seized on this bloody occasion to splash me with it, though the deed was undoubtedly one from which I ought most of all to shrink, being so full of wickedness against God, of treachery toward me, and so ruinous to my subjects.

units.la: Ægrè tamen ferebant nonnulli, parum sibi fidem abhibitam affirmantibus, quicquid ab Hyber-
units.tr: Some, however, took it badly, asserting that too little credit was given them when they said that whatever was done by the Irish-
