units.la: [illegible, ~2 letters]: Symbol or ink mark before "facinus" in the line "cùm ... facinus", unclear. Hybernicis perduellibus actitatum, me Conscio saltem fieri, fi non meo Mandato. Qui sic me calumniantes satis prius edocti erant haud quaquam novum esse subditis meis non solum absque Mandato, sed etiam contra Imperium meum, tum personam etiam pugnare, jactantes interim, se hoc Mea Authoritate, & pro mea incolumitate suscipere.
units.tr: [illegible] rebels was at least known to me, if not done by my command. Those who slandered me in this way had already been taught well enough that it is by no means new for my subjects to fight not only without a command but even against my authority and my person; yet meanwhile they boasted that they took this up under my authority and for my safety.

units.la: Utinam Populo Hybernia nihil esset quod ex istorum exemplo allegaret, quorum certè major culpa est, quâ Protestantium doctrina magis omni in Principes Rebellioni, quàm Papistarum adversatur. Rectè sit quantumvis Intentio, nec scandalum excusabit, nec exempli contagium.
units.tr: Would that the people of Ireland had nothing to allege from the example of those men, whose fault is certainly greater, in that the doctrine of the Protestants is far more opposed to every rebellion against princes than that of the Papists is. However upright the intention may be, it will excuse neither the scandal nor the contagion of the example.

units.la: Sed hoc Illis frequens. Qui officium in me suum neglexerit, mihi statim vertit vitio: hunc mihi semper honorem Hostes mei detulerunt, ut multum infra me censuerint modicas Injurias, in quibus scilicet haud satis clarum mei specimen edatur, vel quid pati ab illis possim, vel, quid Illis ignoscere.
units.tr: But this is common with them. Whoever has neglected his duty toward me immediately turns it into a fault against me. My enemies have always paid me this honour: they have thought so little of me that they judge slight injuries enough to show plainly what I can endure from them, or what I can forgive them.

units.la: Exquisitâ ergo virulentia, Calicem mearum Afflictionum Felle & Aceto Falsitatum & Ludibrii miscuerunt, inter alia mendacissima illud etiam objectantes, unde maximum in me damnum & infamia redundavit: quod eâ faciunt causâ, ut cum facinorum ejusmodi (quod omniis Ratio, Religio, & Politica Prudentia detestanda mihi maximè jubeant) particeps credar, tanto barbarus magis & inhumanus coram Mundo appaream. Monstrum nempe quoddam Cyclopicum, cui nil aliud in cibum & potum sufficiat, quàm Caro & Sanguis Mcorum Civium; cum quibus ut agatur prosperrimè, plus certè in Rem meam conducit, quàm his expedit hominibus omnia turbare: qui revera rem suam agere nisi in turbidis Temporibus non possunt, & tum demum callidissimè se egisse arbitrantur, cùm infœlicium eorum eventuum ( quibus ipsi oblectantur maximè, & non minima Causa extiterunt ) invidiam in alios transtulerint.
units.tr: Therefore, with exquisite venom, they have mixed the cup of my afflictions with the gall and vinegar of falsehoods and mockery. Among other most lying charges, they have alleged that deed which brought the greatest loss and infamy upon me. They do this so that, being thought a sharer in deeds of this kind (which every reason, religion and political prudence bid me above all to detest), I may appear the more barbarous and inhuman before the world: a kind of Cyclopean monster to whom nothing else suffices for food and drink but the flesh and blood of my fellow citizens. Yet to deal prosperously with them is surely more to my advantage than it is to these men to stir up everything in turmoil. They truly cannot manage their affairs except in troubled times, and they think they have acted most cunningly when they have shifted the odium of those unhappy events, in which they delight most and which were no small cause of them, onto others.

units.la: Sanè ita prudentiores arbitrantur præposterum illum rigorem, & iniquam ultra modum severitatem quam nonnulli præ se in Anglia ferebant, haud minimum his fomitem subjecisse, dum superiores irarum scintillas, (queis non decrat in Hybernia præparata Rebellioni materia) in horribilem illam flammam excitârunt: cum, satis jam exacerbatis animis, accedente desperatione, & ad cæteras graves molestias Extirpationis terrore, haud difficulter irritarentur ad apertam defectionem satis per se prompti in violenta erumpere, tum Religionis suæ quibusdam Maximis incitati, tum naturali libertatis desiderio, ut à præsenti se jugo eximerent, & futuræ asperitati obviarent, quam imminere sibi clarè [?]sperspexerant, ab avaro eorum zelo & iniquissimo furore, qui id multum pro Veritate Religionis suæ facere existimant, si non aliam præter suam patiantur.
units.tr: Indeed, the more prudent judge that the preposterous rigour and severity beyond measure which some displayed in England supplied no small fuel for this. While those in authority fanned the sparks of anger (and Ireland lacked no material prepared for rebellion) into that dreadful flame, minds were already sufficiently exasperated. With desperation added, and the terror of extirpation added to the other grave troubles, they were not hard to provoke into open revolt. They were ready enough by themselves to break out into violence, stirred partly by certain great principles of their religion and partly by a natural desire for liberty: to free themselves from the present yoke and to meet the harshness they clearly foresaw looming over them. This came from the greedy zeal and most unjust fury of those who think they do much for the truth of their religion if they allow no other besides their own.

units.la: Deum testor, me quemadmodum verè possum lavare Manus meas in Innocentia quod ad crimen hujus attinet Defectionis, ita lavare etiam posse & lachrymis ex tristi sensu meo, cum sic diffusam viderem, & omnia vastantem, idque eo præsertim tempore, cum propter dissidia, & suspiciones in Anglia, essent potius homines de Salute sua, & quos hic fines agitabant, solliciti, quàm de iis suppetias ferendo, qui inhumane quotidie in Hybernia trucidati: quorum sanguis & lachrymæ satis quidem per se fuissent, si non omnino extinguendis, at suffocandis paulisper & reprimendis Civilium discordiarum facULis, quas ita sedulo nonnulli spargebant.
units.tr: God is my witness that, just as I can truly wash my hands in innocence as regards the crime of this revolt, so I can also wash them with tears, from the sorrow I felt when I saw it spreading so widely and laying everything waste. This was especially so at a time when, because of the quarrels and suspicions in England, men were rather anxious about their own safety, and about the ends that drove them here, than about bringing aid to those who were daily butchered inhumanly in Ireland. Their blood and tears would indeed have been enough by themselves, if not to extinguish utterly, at least to smother for a while and suppress the torches of civil discord which certain men were so busily scattering.

units.la: Vtinam tristis hæc Hybernia conditio nemini minus quàm mihi doluisset: ultro illuc deposcebam proficisci, sed timebant nonnulli, ne vel unum Mihi esset Regnum tranquillum: aut id saltem dedignabantur, Inferiorem Me Scopum ferire, aut Internecionis Meæ Gloriam aliis concedere. Acceptassent modo quæ proposueram, fuisset proculdubio nec tam gravis Ruina, nec tam diuturna Calamitas, nec Remedia tam penitus deplorata.
units.tr: Would that this sad condition of Ireland had grieved no one less than me! I eagerly asked to go there myself, but some feared that even one kingdom might be quiet for me. Or at least they disdained to strike at me as an inferior target, or to yield to others the glory of my ruin. Had they only accepted what I proposed, there would undoubtedly have been neither so grave a ruin, nor so lasting a calamity, nor remedies so utterly despaired of.

units.la: Proximum ergo, ab ipsis Rebellionis Illius Authoribus, Eorum crimen est; qui, vel per domesticas seditiones obstabant, ne maturè occurreretur huic Malo, vel Auxilia intervertebant, vel ipsos postremo Rebel-les Ies[?] ad desperationem agebant extrema omnia minantes, non iis duntaxat, qui prima Belli Hujus Capita, & Faces fuerant, sed ipfi Genti Universæ, obstinati, omnes simul, viros, fæminas, infantes, Germen & Radicem perdere: nulla eorum ratione habitâ, quæ arguimenta plerumque in Misericordiam valida, quæque à propriis pectoribus suggesta fatis audiunt illi Victores, quos non omnis Humanitas deferuit, ne sæviant videlicet in Illos, quos è facie miserabili agnoscas plus à malis suis propriis, quàm malitiâ stimulatos: vel qui sexu aut ætate imbecilli nec contra manum levare, nec inter dexteram & sinistram distinguere potuissent. Quo quidem præpostero, & minimè omnium Euangelico zelo illos potius imitantur à Seruatore nostro reprehensos Discipulos, qui, quòd à paucis exclusi aut neglecti fuissent, haud mitius quam Igne cælitus totas Vrbes hausturo, vindicandam hanc Injuriam censuerunt; vel Illos filios Jacob à Patre cum execratione increpitos; cum Illa potius aspera & extrema optarint, queis ad præfractam desperationem redigantur homines, quàm moderata remedia, adhibere, qualia essent, nonnullos in exemplum castigare, alios veniâ supplicantibus ablatâ, armis exuere & in posterum tutos præstare à Gentilium suorum furoribus, qui eodem secum flumine natare recusantes prompti nimis essent submergere.
units.tr: The next fault, then, is that of the authors of the rebellion themselves. Some, through domestic seditions, hindered this evil from being met in time; some intercepted aid; and some finally drove the rebels themselves to desperation by threatening every extremity, not only against those who had been the first leaders and torches of this war, but against the whole nation, obstinately resolved to destroy men, women and infants, "branch and root" together. No account was taken of those arguments which are generally strong for mercy and which those victors (whom not all humanity has deserted) hear suggested well enough by their own hearts: that they should not rage against those whom you recognise by their pitiable faces to have been moved more by their own misfortunes than by malice, or against those who, weak by sex or age, could neither lift a hand against them nor tell right from left. In this preposterous zeal, which is least of all evangelical, they rather imitate the disciples reproved by our Saviour. Because a few had excluded or neglected them, those disciples judged that this injury should be avenged with fire from heaven, no less gently than that it would swallow whole cities. Or they imitate those sons of Jacob who were rebuked with a curse by their father. For they preferred to choose harsh and extreme measures, by which men are driven to stubborn despair, rather than to apply moderate remedies: such as punishing a few as an example, stripping of arms others whose pardon is begged, and making them safe in future from the furies of their own countrymen, who, refusing to swim in the same stream with them, were all too ready to drown them.

units.la: Est autem quoddam Zeli genus cui clemens æquanimitas Tepor est, quique immanem se haberi, quàm frigidum malit: quanquam crebro etiam hi homines (quicquid simulant) plus pellis suæ causâ ursum, quam maleficii occidant, cum fit his prœda fisci charitate illâ potior quæ aut vitas conservat aut fanat errores.
units.tr: There is, however, a kind of zeal for which gentle equanimity is mere lukewarmness, and which would rather be thought savage than cold. Yet often these men (whatever they pretend) kill the bear more for the sake of its skin than for the sake of the evildoer, since for them the spoil of the treasury is preferred to that charity which either preserves lives or heals errors.

units.la: Cùm ergo in Hybernia Protestantibus prævalente efferatorum hostium numero oppressis & novâ indies strage cumulatis omnia auxilia vel negata effent, vel interclusa, id mecum sedulo agebant, & enixe hortabantur omnes ferè in illis locis Protestantium primarii, ut Armorum aliqua cessatione facta spacium illis respirandi efficerem, sine quo vix posse credebant absque miraculo quæ superfuerant reliquias servare. Deus novit quàm tenero animo, & quàm sollicite hoc negotium curaverim, idque per viros Honorabiles & spectatæ integritatis, ut nec Rebellibus cresceret audacia, nec qui in officio manebant Protestantium fides & patientia frangeretur.
units.tr: Therefore, when in Ireland the Protestants were oppressed by the greater number of frenzied enemies, and were heaped with fresh slaughter each day, and when all aid had either been denied or cut off, the principal men of the Protestants in those places almost all urged me earnestly to this: that I should grant some cessation of arms, to give them room to breathe. Without it, they believed, they could scarcely save the remnants that were left, except by a miracle. God knows with how tender a heart, and how earnestly, I took up this business, and that through honourable men of proven integrity. This was so that the rebels' boldness might not grow, and that the loyalty and patience of the Protestants who remained in their duty might not be broken.

units.la: Cum vero hoc commodissima (qua licebat) ratione, in hâc rerum angustia, & difficultate perfecissem, jam mihi nova de integro subeunda infamia, quod non passus sim perduelles exiguum illud quod erat reliquum Protestantium devorare.
units.tr: When I had carried this out in the most convenient way I could, given the narrowness and difficulty of our affairs, a new infamy had to be borne by me: that I had not allowed the rebels to devour the small remnant of Protestants that was left.

units.la: Abitrabar quidem & merito, spacio hoc & mora Belli, haud ita quicquam accessurum Perduellium partibus, quàm Salutí & Paci Protestantium tum in præsens, & in futurum confultum: quod proculdubio fuisset, si durante Induciarum tempore, cordi magis nonnullis fuisset afflicta Hyberniæ, quò illa studia deponerent, quæ tam impensè promovebant, qui dexterius multo Sanguinem emittere, quàm fluentem sistere callebant.
units.tr: I judged, and rightly, that from this truce and delay in the war nothing would accrue to the rebels' side so much as safety and peace for the Protestants, both for the present and for the future. This would undoubtedly have been so, if during the time of the Truce the afflicted Ireland had been of more concern to some, so that they would lay down those pursuits which they promoted so eagerly. They knew how to let out blood far more skilfully than how to stop it once flowing.

units.la: Vt ut verò finistre nostra omnia recepta fuerint, (in quibus (nescio quomodo) procliviores sunt hominês quod falsum & deterius est credere, quàm, quod verum & bonum diligere) ut nullum supra me Judicem præter Deum, agnosco, ita magno mihi solatio est, quod ad Illius omniscientiam appellandum habeam, qui non ideo Innocentiam mihi aufert, quia, ut olim Sanƈti sui Iob, Patientiam meam haƈtenus experitur.
units.tr: However, though all our actions have been received unfavourably (for men are, I know not how, more inclined to believe what is false and worse than to love what is true and good), and though I acknowledge no judge above me but God, it is a great comfort to me that I have his omniscience to appeal to. He does not take away my innocence because, as once with his saint Job, he is testing my patience thus far.

units.la: Satis mihi abunde est, si conscientiæ mæ prospiciam, fidemque meam in Commisso, ut Regi, liberem: quod ad illa convitiorum examina, quæ ex ore quorundam & pectoribus, non secus ac fumus è fornace & scintillæ evomuntur, vix iis vacat attendere, nedum prolixis Apologiis satisfacere conari, Illis præsertim hominibus, qui Abyssi Improbitatis suæ conscii, ægre quenquam serpsis minus Improbum agnoscunt.
units.tr: It is quite enough for me if I look to my conscience and keep my faith in the trust committed to me, as to the King. As for those examinations of abuse which pour out of the mouths and breasts of some, like smoke from a furnace and sparks, I have hardly time to attend to them, much less to try to satisfy them with lengthy apologies. This is especially so with men who, conscious of the abyss of their own wickedness, scarcely acknowledge anyone less wicked than themselves.

units.la: Regium est, bene facere, male audire, Illud faciam modo, hoc feram libens. (Deo gratias ago) patienter audire possum etiam quæ mihi affingunt Inimici deterrima. Spero quoque me plus boni facturum, quam aut merentur Isti, aut cupiunt.
units.tr: It is a king's part to do good and to be ill spoken of. I will do the former, and gladly bear the latter. (Thanks be to God) I can patiently hear even the most wicked things my enemies attribute to me. I hope too that I shall do more good than either they deserve or desire.

units.la: Olim (credo) manifestum fiet, eos qui cætera mea Regna turbare cæperant, reos esse magnam partem etiam horridi istius in Hybernia cruoris, si non quâ primo fusi, at quâ tardè repressi.
units.tr: In time (I believe) it will become clear that those who began to disturb my other kingdoms are guilty of a large part even of that dreadful bloodshed in Ireland, if not in how it was first shed, then in how slowly it was checked.

units.la: Quem certè (quicquid ipsi dicant vel sentiant) non aliter accipio, quàm è venis meis haustum tantum sanguinis, cum nemo prorsus, sat[?] scio, plus hâc effusione debilitetur. Quanquam verò infariata[?] sit hominum sævitia, spero Dei misericordiam Iustitiæ Ipsius aliquando dicturam, sufficit, & Civilium Bellorum Gladium in vaginam suam recondi iussuram, cum misericors Illius Iustitia non perniciem nostram velit, sed Medicinam: ut sit scelerum diminutio, non gentis excidium.
units.tr: This blood, whatever they say or think, I certainly take as nothing other than blood drawn from my own veins, since, as I well know, no one is weakened more by this outpouring. Although the cruelty of men has grown furious, I hope that God's mercy will one day say to his justice, "It is enough," and will order the sword of civil wars sheathed again. For his merciful justice wills not our destruction but our healing, so that there may be a lessening of crimes, not the destruction of the nation.

units.la: Præveniasnos (Deus Meus) repetitis tuis Misericordiis, quèus[?] Ego & Populus Meus sumus valde abusi, necsut[?] unquam restituantur, mereri possumus.
units.tr: Anticipate us, (my God), with your repeated mercies, which I and my people have greatly abused, nor can we ever deserve that they be restored.

units.la: Vides quanta inter Christianos immanitas sub Religionis specie exercetur, quasi Chri-stians stianis esse non licuerit, nisi nos sic mutuo crucifigeremus.
units.tr: See what immense cruelty is practised among Christians under the appearance of religion, as if Christians could not be permitted to live unless we crucified one another in this way.

units.la: Quia virtutem Tuam non dileximus, nec charitatem exercuimus, Tu spiritum Erroris & Acerbitatis, Mutuique & feralis odii inter Nos exoriri permisisti.
units.tr: Because we have not loved your virtue nor exercised charity, you have allowed the spirit of error and bitterness, and of mutual and deadly hatred, to arise among us.

units.la: Ignosce (Domine) in quo peccavimus, & quæ perpessi sumus, sanctifica,
units.tr: Forgive, (Lord), what we have sinned, and sanctify what we have suffered,

units.la: Qui per ingentia peccata cecidimus, liceat ex pœnitentia exsurgere.
units.tr: We who have fallen through great sins, may it be permitted to rise again through repentance.

units.la: Ne tibi parvæ videantur quas Ego & Regna mea ærumnas pertulimus, sed peccata nostra reddas conscientiis nostris qualia in speculo Iudiciorum Tuorum exhibentur, conspicua : haud enim parva delicta tam atrociter soles castigare.
units.tr: Do not let the troubles which I and my kingdoms have endured seem small to you. Rather, show our sins to our consciences as they are plainly displayed in the mirror of your judgments; for you are wont to punish not small offences so severely.

units.la: O ergo pro magnarum Tuarum Misericordiarum multitudine, ignosce peccatis nostris, & Iudicia Tua removeas vehementer multa, & gravia.
units.tr: Therefore, O Lord, according to the multitude of your great mercies, forgive our sins, and remove your judgments, which are very many and grievous.

units.la: Premant tamen Nos usque peccata nostra, grauius faxis quam Iudicia, fac nos magis in refipiscentiam, quam in liberationem gestire ; Da nobis inprimis pœnitentis Conscientiæ pacem, & tranquillitatem deinde in Conjunctione Regnorum.
units.tr: Yet let our sins press upon us all the more, and make us long for repentance more than for deliverance. Give us first the peace of a penitent conscience, and then tranquillity in the union of the kingdoms.

units.la: In seruatoris nostri sanguinis Mari, obruas precor peccata nostra, & per Rubrum hoc nostri sanguinis Mare, ad stationem aliquam Pietatis, Pacis, Affluentiæ perducas.
units.tr: I beg you, overwhelm our sins in the sea of our Saviour's blood, and through this Red Sea of our blood lead us to some station of piety, peace and plenty.

units.la: Vt pro Publico Meo Munere, quo omnes contingo, Populi mei perpessionibus consocior, itæ faxis eo sensu eorum efficiar, qui Christianum Regem deceat, & Patrem Populi Amantissimum.
units.tr: So that, in my public office, by which I touch everyone, I may share in the sufferings of my people, grant that I may be made to feel as they do, as befits a Christian King and a most loving Father of the people.

units.la: Probra illa & injustæ in me sparsæ calumniæ, sint mihi lenis instar spiritus qui miscrationem meam accendat: Da prunas ardentes charitatis super caput eorum coarcervare; ut ab illis colliquefcant qui malitia aut crudeli Zelo acti vel accenderunt has flammas, vel extinguì victuerunt, quæ sic tria mea Regna devastarunt.
units.tr: Let those reproaches and unjust calumnies cast against me be to me like a gentle breeze that kindles my compassion. Grant that I may heap burning coals of charity upon their heads, so that they may melt who, moved by malice or cruel zeal, either kindled these flames or wished them extinguished, flames which have thus laid waste my three kingdoms.

units.la: O subvenias & liberes miseros illos in Hibernia Protestantes quos tu hactenus servasti superstites.
units.tr: O help and free those wretched Protestants in Ireland, whom you have hitherto preserved as survivors.

units.la: Et duc eos in semitis salvificæ Tuæ veritatis qui aut inscitia sua aut errore perniciosis his Dogmatis & perduellionem spirantibus imbuuntur, atque hæc interim agentes tibi obsequium se credunt præstare.
units.tr: And lead into the paths of your saving truth those who, through their ignorance or error, are steeped in these pernicious dogmas that breathe rebellion, and who, while doing this, believe they are rendering you obedience.

units.la: Sit tuæ Manus Justitiæ contra Illos, qui malitia sua & virulentia vel excitarunt Bella Illa sæva & immania, vel illis fomitem dederunt.
units.tr: Let the hand of your justice be against those who, by their malice and virulence, have either stirred up those savage and monstrous wars or given fuel to them.

units.la: Tu qui non amas perdere cum nocente innoxios, & errantes pariter cum malitiosis; qui misertus es Niniveh propter multos infantes, o ne totam stirpem Pupulosæ hujus & deceptæ Gentis objicias eorum furori, quos avaritia sua facit crudeles, nec iracundiæ vehementer seroci atque adeo juste execrandæ.
units.tr: You who do not love to destroy the innocent along with the guilty, nor the erring together with the malicious; who had pity on Nineveh for the sake of its many infants: O, do not deliver the whole stock of this misled and deceived people to the fury of those whom their avarice makes cruel, nor to a wrath that is very fierce and rightly to be execrated.

units.la: Serves, (si voluntas tua fuerit) etiam in media severæ tuæ Justitiæ fornace, semen Posteritatis Misericordiam Tuam laudaturæ.
units.tr: Preserve, (if it be your will), even in the midst of the furnace of your severe justice, the seed of a posterity that will praise your mercy.

units.la: Et age mecum non secundum injusta hominum opprobria, sed secundum innocentiam manuum mearum in conspectu Tuo.
units.tr: And deal with me not according to the unjust reproaches of men, but according to the innocence of my hands in your sight.

units.la: Si concupiverim omnino, vel delectatus fuerim in hac die calamitosa miserabilium mihi Regnorum, si non serio laboraverim, & huc omni studio incubuerim, ut sanguinolenta haec dissidia quoquo modo praevenirem, vel componerem, tum sit manus Tua contra Me, & Domum Patris mei. Vides (Domine) satis mihi inter Homines, hostium extare, & propterea nec opus habeo, nec revera auderem ita mihi, & [?] Meis imprecari, ni mihi testis esset Integritatis Conscientia Mea, quam Tu (Domine) satis novisti, nequaquam tamen merito meo, sed misericordiis tuis confido. Parce Domine, ac ne irascaris in aeternum.
units.tr: If I have at all desired, or taken delight in, this calamitous day for my wretched kingdoms, or if I have not seriously laboured and devoted all my zeal to prevent or settle these bloody dissensions in whatever way I could, then let your hand be against me and my father's house. You see, Lord, that I have enough enemies among men, and therefore I have no need, nor would I truly dare, to call down such curses upon myself and mine, unless my conscience of integrity, which you, Lord, know well, were witness to me. Yet I trust not in my merit but in your mercies. Spare, Lord, and do not be angry forever.

units.la: 13. De Scotis in An- gliam evocatis, & eo- rum adventu.
units.tr: 13. Of the Scots summoned into England, and their arrival.

units.la: Gentem Scotorum praeter illa (cum Patre meo felicis memoriae Communia) Naturae, Dominii, Beneficentiae vincula, multis etiam recentibus beneficiis devinxeram; nonnullis inter eos acribus viris & industriis eousque indulgens, ut viderer
units.tr: Besides the ties of nature, lordship and kindness that I shared with my father of happy memory, I had bound the Scottish nation to me by many recent benefits. I had indulged some of its keen and industrious men so far that I seemed to be serving their desires more than either my own affairs or my honour.

units.la: plus illorum hominum desideriis quàm vel Rei meæ propriæ, vel Honori consulere: At jam video, è Regiâ munificentiâ audaciam nonnullis crescere ultra fines Modestiæ & Gratitudinis, agendi simul & flagitandi.
units.tr: But I now see that from the royal generosity some men's boldness has grown beyond the limits of modesty and gratitude, both in what they do and in what they demand.

units.la: Charitas mea vetat & Lex illa Pacificationis ne in superiora respiciam, in quibus, procul à me absit, ut ingratitudine cujusquam vel inconstantia in poenitentiam eorum adducar, quæ in Publicum Bonum concessi. Faxit Deus ut in bonum cedant.
units.tr: My charity forbids me, and that law of the Pacification, to look back at past things. Far be it from me to be drawn by anyone's ingratitude or fickleness into penalizing them for what I granted for the public good. May God grant that it turns out for good.

units.la: Ut verò denuò in Angliam Pars Illa cum exercitu rediret, nullam aliam ob causam, nisi ut Ecclesiam Nostram ad Novam illam Suam formam cuderent, certè haud minus iniquum videtur, quàm, ergò se fuissent arbitrati, si hinc eadem in Ipsos tentassemus.
units.tr: As for that party returning into England with an army, with no other purpose than to shape our Church into their own new form, it seems no less unjust than if they had thought the same thing would be done to them if we had tried it on them in Scotland.

units.la: Aliud verò quod hîc agerent, nunquam scivi, (missis illis vulgaribus Religionis & libertatis nugis) quàm ut exemplar suum Presbyterale ita recens formatum, firmius hac ratione efficerent, cum à nostra deinde Ecclesia (vel sanguineo Characlere) describeretur.
units.tr: What else they meant to do here I never knew, apart from those common trifles about religion and liberty. Their aim was, by this means, to make their Presbyterian model, so newly formed, firmer, and then to have it copied into our Church with a bloody character.

units.la: Quod Consilium eorum & Finis, an satis Divinæ Justitiæ tam violenti Medii usum approbaverit, eorum Conscientiis relinquo, qui hujus Medii calamitates experti, nondum Finis optati beneficium, vel in Hoc, vel in Illo Regno perceperunt.
units.tr: As to whether divine justice has approved their counsel and end, and the use of so violent a means, I leave to the consciences of those who, having experienced the calamities of this means, have not yet received the benefit of the desired end in either kingdom.

units.la: Multi enim hic nodi occurrent, & non levia ubique offendicula, quæ impedient quo minus Ista ( cui sic plauditur ) tanquam unica esset justa Reformatio , Disciplinæque & Regiminis recta Constitutio ) ita securo pede transeat , quo in Scotia dudum pervagata est , & quod nonnulli etiam in Anglia crediderunt futurum , cum tot è clero Anglicano seu levitate , seu irâ , seu pejori aliquo affectu incitati , deserta sua pristinâ in Episcopos fide & obsequio , ad Presbyteratum omnes circumagerentur.
units.tr: Many knots will meet us here, and everywhere no slight obstacles, which will prevent this thing (so much applauded, as though it were the only just reformation, and the right constitution of discipline and government) from passing on so safe a foot as it has long spread about in Scotland, and as some also believed it would in England, when so many of the English clergy, stirred up either by levity, anger, or some worse feeling, abandoned their former faith and obedience to the bishops and were all turned round to Presbyterianism.

units.la: Mihi quidem itâ videtur , esse hoc Hominum se quærentium & in quos privati affectus plus pollent quàm Zelus verus , & pia prudentia ; ut aliquod exterum Regnum vel Ecclesia ea aliis remedia præcipiat , quæ Ipsi cum successu magis quam cum laude ufurparunt ; haud interim secum reputantes , idem sæpe medicamentum pro diversa corporum temperatura , diverso modo operari , idque alium sanare , quo alius occiditur.
units.tr: This seems to me to be the mark of men who seek their own ends, and in whom private affections carry more weight than true zeal and holy prudence; so that they prescribe to some foreign kingdom or church those remedies which they themselves have used with success rather than with praise, without considering that the same medicine works in different ways according to the differing constitution of bodies, and that what heals one kills another.

units.la: Sed nec ullos in Ecclesiæ Anglicanæ constitutione ita malignos humores vel sic tenaces compereram , ut non Pharmaco multo mitiori , quàm vi Armata pellerentur : Neque sane ita congruum videtur Piæ Reformationi ut sic se Gladio incidi , & quasi exsciari permittat , sed ut legitimis & æquis Difputationibus poliatur , eorum scilicet ad quos lis hæc spectat maximè , nec vi ullâ, sed Ratione expugnandos.
units.tr: But I have found in the constitution of the Church of England no malignant humours so stubborn that they could not be driven out by a much gentler remedy than armed force. Nor indeed does it seem fitting to a holy reformation to let itself be cut with the sword and, as it were, scraped out. It should rather be polished by lawful and fair disputations, namely among those to whom this dispute chiefly pertains, and it should be overcome not by any force but by reason.

units.la: Id vero isti agebant, ut Disputationem potiùs omnem præcederent, quàm æquam ullam & Rectam procurarent. Hoc enim ante statuerant, omninò clerum Angliæ ad Scoticum Instar conformandum, quàm vel unquam audiretur quid vel Illi in causa sua, vel contra ipsos essent dicturi.
units.tr: Yet those men acted so as to forestall any disputation, rather than to bring about anything fair or right. For they had decided beforehand that the clergy of England must be wholly conformed to the Scottish pattern, before anyone would hear what those men might say in their own cause, or against them.

units.la: Æquior utinam fuisset procedendi ratio. Certè famæ suæ meliùs consuluissent (qui hæc tantâ vi urgent) tùm aliorum Conscientiis, queis, non æquè dubia sua expedire idonei Milites in acie pugnantes, quàm in docta & libera Synodo disputantes Scholastici.
units.tr: I wish their method of proceeding had been fairer. Certainly those who press these things with such force would have better consulted their own reputation, and also the consciences of others, to whom their doubts would not be resolved as well by soldiers fighting in the line as by scholars disputing in a learned and free synod.

units.la: Si quidem in Re Religionis, eæ maximè veritates in Judicia & conscientias nostras valent, quas secularis violentia minimè omnium obtrudit, quæ veritatem præjudiciis[?] infirmat & nullâ prorsus ratione usurpari debet, nisi, cùm omnibus ad rationaliter evincendum frustra mediis adhibitis jam, cùm excusari non possit ignorantia, pervicacia merito castigatur.
units.tr: For in matters of religion, those truths carry the most weight with our judgements and consciences which secular violence least of all imposes. Such violence weakens the truth by prejudices, and it ought never to be used at all, except when, after every rational means of proving the point has been tried in vain, and ignorance can no longer be excused, obstinacy is rightly punished.

units.la: Id quod nulla charitas suspicetur de tot piis & eruditis Ecclesiasticis in Anglia, qui cum semper educati fuerint Episcopali Regimini conformes, haud ita facilè existimentur antiquæ suæ sententiæ, & Praxi renunciasse, hoc solum argumento persuasi, quia sic parti Scoticæ collibuit, se cum simili sibi in Anglia Factione conjungere, ut summâ ope & viribus Ministros omnes (velut oves) in eandem Presbyteratus caulam compellerent; certi alias vel eos perdere, vel ad cutim usque attondere gregis sui beneficio destitutos. Quod si etiam probari posset Presbyteratum hunc Scoticum unicum omnium Ecclesiarum Regimen fuisse à Iesu Christo institutum, vix tamen &, ægrè credo probaturos, Christum unquam in mandatis dedisse vel his Ipsis Scotis, vel alii cupiam è Subditis meis, ut in quocunque Regno meo fine meo Consensu, mero Gladii jure, erigere tur.
units.tr: No charity should suspect this of so many pious and learned churchmen in England, who, having always been brought up in conformity with episcopal government, cannot easily be thought to have renounced their old opinion and practice. They have been persuaded by this one argument alone: that the Scottish party chose to join themselves to a similar faction in England, so that with all their might and strength they could drive all ministers, like sheep, into the same fold of Presbyterianism, being sure that otherwise they would either destroy them or shear them down to the skin, deprived of the benefit of their flock. And even if it could be proved that this Scottish Presbyterianism was the one government of all churches instituted by Jesus Christ, I scarcely think they would ever prove, or be readily believed, that Christ ever commanded in his precepts, either to these very Scots or to any of my subjects, that in any kingdom of mine it should be set up without my consent, by the sheer right of the sword.

units.la: Satis patet in Euangelio quantam Christus Ipse & Apostoli, Illis, sub quibus degebant, Principibus Reverentiam & obsequium præstabant: An vero Ipse vel Illi, paritatem hujusmodi Presbyterorum, eâ quâ Scoti isti conantur, ratione instituendam unquam præceperint, extra omnem (opinor) controversiam est.
units.tr: It is plain enough from the Gospel how much reverence and obedience Christ himself and the apostles paid to the princes under whom they lived. But whether they ever commanded such an equality of presbyters to be established in the way these Scots try to establish it, is, I think, beyond all controversy.

units.la: Etenim si in tali Suprematu Presbytera-tus à Christo institutus fuerit; ejusmodi plane institutum est, quod est cæteris Ejus omnibus diversum. Imò, primus omnium & solus Christianismi Articulus, qui tanto sanguine Christiano plantari & irrigari necesse habuit; in quo quicquid unquam effusum est, fluit cursu longè contrario primis Illis Christianismum & Episcopatum plantantibus, qui hoc sanguine suo patienter fuso, non aliorum profuso peregerunt. Nimis vero istud homines sapit, parum Christi; cujus nulla omninò Institutio Ambitionis aut Avaritiæ stimulis vel initia sua debet vel incrementa, cùm utriusque hîc vehemens suspicio.
units.tr: For if such a supremacy of Presbyterianism had been instituted by Christ, it would be a kind of institution quite unlike all his others. Indeed, it would be the first and only article of Christianity that needed to be planted and watered with so much Christian blood. Whatever blood has ever been shed for it flows in a course quite contrary to that of those first men who planted Christianity and episcopacy, who accomplished this by patiently shedding their own blood, not by spilling the blood of others. This smells much more of men and very little of Christ. No institution of Christ owes its beginnings or growth to the goads of ambition or avarice, and here there is a strong suspicion of both.

units.la: Nil tamen aliud afferebant hi Scoti quod alicujus momenti videretur, quoties me vel armis urgere, vel per Delegatos suadere conabantur, (ferio subinde obtestantes, mox, pio suo more minantes) quàm hoc unicum & præcipuum, Magnam jam necessitatem incumbere constituendi in Anglia Presbyteratus ad vitandas scilicet futuras Belli miserias, quod nonnulli hoc fine inchoatum, necessitatem sibi fecerant persequendi.
units.tr: Yet these Scots had nothing else of any weight to offer, whenever they tried either to press me with arms or to persuade me through delegates. (They would often solemnly protest, and soon after threaten in their pious way.) Their one chief argument was this: that there was now a great necessity to establish Presbyterianism in England, namely to avoid the miseries of future war, and that some, having begun it for this purpose, had made it necessary for themselves to go on.

units.la: Rogo jam quid obstabit (si huic sententiæ & exemplo acquiescendum) quo minus omnes Sectæ, Schismata, Hæreses, Numeris modò & Viribus, & Opportunitate instructa) eâdem prorsus violentiâ Insanias suas erigant passim & stabiliant. Et tamen hæc Presbyterales odiosè exagitant, & omni modo coercenda æquum putant: cùm revera id cordati homines & docti censeant, nulla Schismatis & Sectæ manifestiora indicia quàm in hoc genus Presbyteratu ostendi, tum, quòd secus fit ab Antiquo & jam maximè, universali Ecclesiæ Regimine, tùm ab ipsis etiam in Ecclesia Anglicana Constitutis Legibus, quæ nondum sunt abrogatæ : nec à me unquam abrogandæ, ni argumentis melioribus Rationis pariter & Religionis edocear, quàm quæ ἐperà [?] militari depromenda.
units.tr: I ask now, if we are to acquiesce in this opinion and example, what would prevent all sects, schisms and heresies, equipped with numbers, strength and opportunity, from raising and establishing their follies everywhere by the very same violence? And yet these men fiercely denounce the Presbyterians and think they should be restrained by every means. Indeed, wise and learned men judge that no clearer signs of schism and sect can be shown than in this kind of Presbyterianism. This is so, because things are otherwise in the ancient and, above all, universal government of the Church, and also in the laws established in the English Church itself, which have not yet been repealed, and which I shall never repeal unless I am taught by better arguments, both of reason and of religion, than those to be drawn from military force.

units.la: Deo eventum relinquo, qui ubi semel opinionum stultitiam, & impotentiam Affectuum sustulerit, multifariam potest instillare illas Verae Rationis, & pacificae Prudentiae regulas, quae supernè descendens, ad Dei Gloriam maximè, & Ecclesiae Bonum contendit: quibus me conscientia mea obligat eò curâ impensiori, & sollicito magis zelo attendere, quantò cætera Republicâ Ecclesiam, Christi Gloriam meâ præpriâ, denique Salutem Animarum, omni Corporum, & Facultatum conservatione duco potiorem.
units.tr: I leave the outcome to God, who, once he has removed the folly of opinions and the powerlessness of the passions, can instil in many ways those rules of true reason and peaceful prudence which descend from above and aim chiefly at the glory of God and the good of the Church. My conscience binds me to attend to these with all the more careful concern and anxious zeal, as I count the Church, the glory of Christ, and above all the salvation of souls more important than the preservation of the commonwealth, of my own person, and of bodies and property.

units.la: Nefas interim (meo judicio) & improba. præsumptio, ut ulli omnino mortales, in Ecclesias meæ fidei, & tutelæ concreditas, Formas has suas & fabricas, suo fictas arbitrio, & ad fines suos accommo-datas vi & armis conentur inducere, nec consensu meo impetratâ, nec vel Mea, vel aliorum conscientiis ullâ vi Rationum expugnatis.
units.tr: Meanwhile, in my judgment, it is a wicked and shameless presumption for any mortals at all to try to force these forms and contrivances of their own, devised at their own pleasure and fitted to their own ends, upon the churches entrusted to my faith and protection, by force and arms, neither obtained with my consent nor overcome by any force of reasons upon my conscience or that of others.

units.la: Quod ad caeteros Illos Turbidos Motus, qui nec hominem nec Christianum nec fidelem subditum decant, nullius apud me unquam momenti erunt, vel ad confirmandam mihi Religionem , vel quacunque in parte labefactandam : nec arbitror futuros apud quenquam alterum , qui saltem norit quid sit Religio, & quàm abhorreat factionibus , quibus machina una & Organum , Vis est: belluarum arbitratrix non hominum, nedum humilium Christianorum, & Subditorum Fidelium in re præsertim Religionis.
units.tr: As for those other turbulent movements, which become neither a man, nor a Christian, nor a faithful subject, they will never carry any weight with me, either to confirm my religion or to weaken it in any part. Nor do I think they will carry any weight with anyone else who at least knows what religion is and how much it abhors factions, in which one machine and instrument is force: the arbiter of beasts, not of men, much less of humble Christians and faithful subjects, especially in a matter of religion.

units.la: Sed ita inflari plærique faciles, & magnificè de seipsis sentire, ut sint parum solliciti, quid in Dogmata sua & placita impendant, maximè si spes aliqua lucri ostendatur, quo cætera damna, & pericula compensent.
units.tr: But most easy-going people are so puffed up and think so highly of themselves that they are little concerned about what they stake on their doctrines and opinions, especially if some hope of gain is held out, by which they might offset all other losses and dangers.

units.la: Haud vero magis sum offensus Scotorum Armis, qui sic Regnum meum, me invito intrabant, ruptis omnibus officii, & gratitudinis vinculis, quam sum illos hic nostros admiratus, potuisse scilicet in tantum Divino Auxilio diffidere, qui ita Dei causam venditabant Populo, tanquam certa Revelatione Divina confirmati, ii praesertim, qui jam satis superque instructi erant Armis Civium, & apparatu Bellico, quibus & in Mari Classis mea & in Terra propugnacula, Arces, Praesidia, & tot Urbes munitæ superant.
units.tr: I am no more offended by the arms of the Scots, who entered my kingdom against my will, having broken all the bonds of duty and gratitude, than I am amazed at these men of ours, that they could so distrust divine help as to peddle the cause of God to the people as if it were confirmed by a certain divine revelation, especially those who were already more than sufficiently equipped with the arms of citizens and military preparations, by which my navy at sea and my bulwarks, citadels, garrisons and so many fortified cities on land surpass them.

units.la: Illud potius hinc colligo, homines ejusmodi, quibus suspicio est causam suam & consilia haud ita posse coram Deo probari, nunquam satis se arbitrari humanis Viribus instructos, ut hoc opus suum, quantumvis populare, perficiant. Valde enim muniri opus habet quod nec Religione, nec Lege defenditur.
units.tr: Rather, I infer from this that men of this sort, who suspect that their cause and plans cannot be so well proved before God, never think themselves sufficiently equipped with human strength to complete this work of theirs, however popular it may be. For a cause that is defended neither by religion nor by law needs to be heavily fortified.

units.la: Ea tamen plærumque Inconstantia violenta consilia comitatur, ut quos alii summo opere in auxilium sibi accersunt, alii statim pertæsi cum fastidio quodam, & nauseâ ejiciant, quod illi firmum sibi posteâ sperabant, & in perpetuum figendum, accedente Scotorum Influentiâ, id hi penitus repudiant & aspernantur, & una pariter totam Scoticæ Ecclesiæ Disciplinam & Regimen, uno opere irrita facientes illa magis onerosa quam Anglica auxilia. Poterat enim Ecclesia Anglicana (si ita visum fuisset,) & Veritatem Reformati Regiminis, & Disciplinæ (si defuisset fœlicitatem,) multo minoris conciliasse, si vel optimos in Europa Theo-logos suo sumptu invitasset in plena & Libera Synodo consulturos; quod me libente & cupido facturi essent, ut sic rebus sine studio compositis, satisfactum magis omnibus foret & diuturnius manerent stabilita.
units.tr: Yet violent counsels are commonly accompanied by such inconstancy that those whom some have summoned to their aid with great eagerness, others, soon wearied of them, cast out with a certain disgust and nausea. What they had hoped would be firm and fixed for ever, with the Scottish influence added, these men utterly reject and spurn, and at the same stroke they nullify the whole Scottish church discipline and government, making them more burdensome by one act than the English aids. For the English Church could (had it seen fit) have secured the truth of a reformed government and discipline, and happiness too if it had been lacking, at much less cost, if it had invited at its own expense the best theologians in Europe to consult in a full and free Synod. They would have done so gladly and eagerly with me, so that, with affairs settled without partisanship, satisfaction would have been greater for all and what was established would have lasted longer.

units.la: Sed omnino aliter fieri non potest, quin patefaciat se tandem Divina Justitia, & homi-num fatuitas, per prætextus illos omnes & Religionis velamina, quibus improbi Politici arcana sua consilia involvunt, frustra enim speratur, inædificari pietatem his Fidei in Principem & obsequii Ruinis. Nec durare diu possunt istiusmodi Molitiones, cum versuram Fidei suæ faciant subditi, ut quæstuosius Religionis artificium instituant.
units.tr: But it is by no means possible for divine justice and human folly not to reveal themselves in the end through all those pretexts and veils of religion with which wicked politicians wrap their secret plans. For it is vain to hope that piety can be built upon these ruins of faith and obedience towards the Prince. Nor can such contrivances last long, when subjects barter away their faith so as to set up a more profitable trick of religion.

units.la: Cæterum, ut pars optima in Scotia me nunquam deseruit, ita nec plærosque eorum (credo) tam longè à me discessisse, & instar prodigi illius omnem in me amorem & reverentiam consumpsisse, ut de reditu eorum desperem, cum, præter illa Naturæ & Conscientiæ (quibus omnes tenentur) vincula, ratio illos & prudentia docebit, etiam rem suam sic melius stabiliri posse, si Coronæ fidi permaneant, quàm, his. populi partibus ita in præsens Commodum obsequentes, ut Salutem meam & Honorem neglígant omnino, vel prodant. Quanto minus interim causæ est credendi Hominibus, tanto magis me Deo applicabo.
units.tr: Moreover, just as the best part of Scotland never deserted me, so I believe that most of them have not gone so far from me, nor, like that prodigal, have they used up all their love and reverence towards me, that I despair of their return. For, besides those bonds of nature and conscience by which all are bound, reason and prudence will teach them that their own affairs can be better secured if they remain loyal to the Crown, than if they obey these popular factions so as to gain present advantage and wholly neglect or betray my safety and honour. The less cause there is for trusting men at present, the more I will commit myself to God.

units.la: Tribulationes cordis mei multiplicatæ sunt; de necessitatibus meis, erue me. *
units.tr: My heart's troubles are multiplied; deliver me from my necessities.

units.la: Dirige Servum Tuum in semitis piæ illius simplicitatis quæ omni alia Politica præstantior.
units.tr: Direct Thy servant in the paths of that pious simplicity which excels all other policy.

units.la: Libera me à complicatis eorum viribus, quibus tantum incest serpentinæ astutiæ, ut innocentiam Columbarum obliviscantur.
units.tr: Free me from their combined strength, which has so much of serpent-like cunning that they forget the innocence of doves.

units.la: Etiamsi manus ad manum fuerit, non prævalant in animam meam, in Conscientiæ meæ & Honoris proditionem.
units.tr: Even if hand be joined to hand, they shall not prevail against my soul, to the betrayal of my conscience and honour.

units.la: Tu (Domine) potes inflectere utriusque partis corda in utraque Gente, quod fecisti olim hominibus Judah & Israël ut eo David restituerent fidcli[?] ardore, quo illum nuper levitate & impetu fuerant persecuti.
units.tr: Thou, Lord, canst turn the hearts of both parties in each nation, as Thou once didst for the men of Judah and Israel, so that they might restore David with the same faithful ardour with which they had lately pursued him with fickleness and fury.

units.la: Custodi mihi Amorem Veritatis & Rectitudinis, nec desperabo de subditorum affectibus in Me quandoque rediturus.
units.tr: Keep for me the love of truth and uprightness, and I shall not despair of my subjects' affections, that I may one day return to them.

units.la: Tu maria exundantia reciprocari, & retro cogis concedere intra fines à Te praestitutos.
units.tr: Thou dost cause the overflowing seas to ebb, and drive them back to keep within the bounds Thou hast set.

units.la: Deus Meus In Te confido, ne erubescam, ne irrideant me Inimici mei, non gaudeant super me, non de me jubilent.
units.tr: My God, I trust in Thee; let me not be ashamed, let not my enemies mock me, let them not rejoice over me, let them not exult over me.

units.la: Confundantur omnes iniqua agentes supervacue, revertantur quærentes animam meam.
units.tr: Let all who act wickedly without cause be confounded; let those who seek my soul be turned back.

units.la: Integritas & æquitas custodiant me, quia Te exspecto Domine.
units.tr: Let integrity and uprightness preserve me, for I wait for Thee, O Lord.

units.la: Libera Ecclesiam Tuam (Domine) ex omnibus suis angustiis.
units.tr: Deliver Thy Church, O Lord, out of all her distresses.

units.la: 14. De Fœdere.
units.tr: 14. Concerning the Covenant

units.la: SCoti isti Presbyterales haud vulgari Auxiliorum stipendio invitandi, nullo alio pretio in partes trahuntur quam animarum pignore posito, Ipsis scilicet qui illos evocabant, Solenni Pacto & Fædere constrictis.
units.tr: These Scots Presbyterians, to be lured by no ordinary reward of military pay, are drawn into the cause by no other price than a pledge of souls, namely of those who summoned them, bound by a solemn pact and covenant.

units.la: Multæ hîc piæ Machinæ, & Religiosi prætextus afferuntur ad oppugnandum Episcopatum vel prorsus demoliendum. Hunc nempe Grandem Illum Cacodæmona, quem (terriculamentis nonnullis adjectis) odio vulgi, & pavoribus objiciunt, Solenni Carmine & Exorcismo ex Ecclesia omni modo abigendum; postquam eam mille annos obsederit, ex quo primo Christianismus in hac Insula plantatus, quique præscripto Universasi temporis simul & præxeos [?]in cæteris omnibus Ecclesiis, usque ab Apostolorum sæculo, ad hanc proximam Centuriam, innititur.
units.tr: Many pious devices and religious pretexts are put forward here to assail episcopacy or to pull it down altogether. They wish to drive out, by solemn chanting and exorcism, that great Cacodaemon from the Church by every means, having first added some scare-stories to rouse the hatred and fears of the common people. They say he has besieged the Church for a thousand years, ever since Christianity was first planted on this island, and that he has held his ground, by the prescription of time and by the practice of all other Churches, from the age of the Apostles down to this last century.

units.la: Sed frustra causam hic agit Antiquitas: Presbyterismus velut adolescens hæres, nimis diu Patrem vixisse ratus, & Episcopalis Cathedræ, & Authoritatis impatiens; (proventus enim cedunt Laicis) omni astu molitur, ut Episcopatu fluctibus obruto, sibi faciat in Angliam appellendi copiam, quemadmodum nuper etiam in Scotia eodem Fœderis artificio emersit.
units.tr: But antiquity pleads its case here in vain. Presbyterianism, like a young heir who thinks his father has lived far too long, and who cannot endure an episcopal see or authority (for the revenues pass to the laity), strives by every trick to overwhelm episcopacy with waves, so that it may gain for itself an opening to land in England, just as it recently emerged in Scotland by the same covenanting contrivance.

units.la: Quanquam plurima mihi in hoc Fœdere displiceant (in quo, subinde periculosa admodùm & ambiguâ limitatione Authoritas mihi præfinitur) illud maximè demiror, quod consilium illis fuerit in Disciplina & Regimine Ecclesiastico: nec minùs hanc agendi rationem, ut Juramentis scilicet & Fœderibus ita Res planè Novas promoverent. Durum certè, haud minori quàm Juramenti vinculo, ut quis in ea obligetur, vel contrà, de quorum morali necessitate haud constat; sed quæ adhuc sub Iudice plæraque, doctorumque & piorum hominum controversiis agitata: in quæ, ut vel ipsi juremus, vel ab aliis Iurari exigamus, haud certè potest cum judicio illo & certitudine propria constare, nec cum eâ in alios diverse sententes Æquitate, & Candore, qui Religionem decet: quæ non æquè solum disceptare sed dissentire etiam permittit, in materiâ duntaxat probabili.
units.tr: Although I dislike very many things in this Covenant (in which my own authority is prescribed to me, at times by a limitation that is very dangerous and ambiguous), I am most astonished at this one thing: that they meant to make innovations in church discipline and government, and that they chose to bring about such entirely new things by means of oaths and covenants. It is surely a hard thing that a man should be bound by an obligation no less strong than an oath, or the reverse, when it is not clear that there is any moral necessity for it; these are matters still under debate, and for the most part they are disputed among learned and pious men. To swear to such matters ourselves, or to require others to swear to them, cannot possibly agree with that judgement and certainty proper to us, nor with that fairness and candour toward others who hold different opinions, which befits religion. Religion permits not only debate on such matters but also dissent, provided the matter is merely probable.

units.la: Iuramenta vero Populo imponere, ut in rebus dubiis periculosum, ita prorsus in illicitis damnabile: illic vero prorsus supervacaneum, ubi superiora jam Legum, & Religionis vincula, in necessaria officia obligarunt.
units.tr: To impose oaths on the people is, in doubtful matters, dangerous, and in unlawful matters utterly damnable; in matters where the bonds of the higher laws and of religion have already bound men to necessary duties, it is entirely superfluous.

units.la: Neque video quo pacto conciliare possunt Innovans hoc Fœdus, & Juramentum, cum nuperâ illâ suâ Protestatione, quâ tueri susceperant Religionem in Ecclesia Anglicana Sancitam; istî præsertim qui Disciplinam inter Momenta Religionis accensent.
units.tr: Nor do I see how this innovating Covenant and Oath can be reconciled with that recent Protestation of theirs, by which they had undertaken to defend the religion established in the Church of England; especially for those who count discipline among the principal points of religion.

units.la: Sed nunquam nimis se credunt Ambitiosi homines, laqueos, & tendiculas hujusmodi vulgi credulitati struxisse: his enim fere actibus, & pietatis suco arctius quarunt sibi populum obstringere, metu scilicet perjurii intentato; cum revera probi omnes & prudentes, satis se jam diu ligamentis suis prioribus, Religionis, Fidelitatis, Legum, Deo juxta & Hominibus obstrictos putarent.
units.tr: But ambitious men never believe that they have laid snares and nets of this kind sufficiently for the credulity of the common people. By such acts, and with the juice of piety, they seek to bind the people more tightly to themselves, namely by threatening the fear of perjury; whereas in truth all honest and prudent men had long thought themselves already bound, by their earlier ties, to religion, fidelity, and the laws, to God as well as to men.

units.la: Quæ quidem tanta sunt, ut nulla posterior stipulatio, ( excogitata & imperata à paucis hominibus in aperta Factione versantibus, absque meo Consensu, & nullo simili Exemplo præeunte, vel potestate à Divinis vel Humanis Legibus derivata ) satis unquam videatur cordatis hominibus, vel solvendo, vel relaxando moralia illa & æterna obsequii vincula quæ & Deo & Mihi præstanda, subditorum conscientiis incumbunt.
units.tr: These ties are so strong that no later stipulation, devised and imposed by a few men engaged in open faction, without my consent, with no similar precedent before it, and with no power derived from divine or human laws, ever seems sufficient to sensible men either to dissolve or to relax those moral and eternal bonds of obedience which lie upon the consciences of subjects, and which are owed both to God and to me.

units.la: Nunc verò, ( prout res se habent ) minus Deo & Mihi displicebunt boni Viri, si fi[?] Fœdus suum catenus, quâ honestè & licitè possint, observarint, cùm, quâ suâ[?] charitate, tales esse nonnullos existimem, qui hoc solùm fine & mente susceperunt, ut Religionem in puritate, & Regnum in pace tuerentur. Ad diversos his fines & media, nulla ratio est cur se teneant obligatos; nec revera persuaderi unquam poterunt (in quibus quicquam falis Conscientiæ) vel optima sua Consilia (nedum ea quorum indices Ambitio & Factio manifestior) per illicita quæcunque media sub suspiciosò Fœderis titulo promovere; nisi velint, ancipites & periculosas Novitates & nulla prorsus Authoritate munitas, exploratis & Juramento pactis Deo simul & Mihi Officiis, & nulla omninò dispensatione tollendis, anteponere.
units.tr: Now, as things stand, good men will displease God and me less if they keep their covenant so far as they honestly and lawfully can. For I believe, out of my own charity, that there are some who undertook it with this one purpose and intent: that they might defend religion in its purity and the kingdom in peace. There is no reason why they should bind themselves to other ends and means different from these. Nor indeed can they ever be persuaded (in whom there is any grain of conscience) that their best counsels, let alone those whose ambition and faction are plainer, can be advanced by any unlawful means under the suspect title of a covenant, unless they are willing to place doubtful and dangerous novelties, supported by no authority at all, before the duties owed to God and to me, duties which are established by certain obligations and cannot be removed by any dispensation whatsoever.

units.la: Quin ad facile etiam credo & spero, plurimos, qui hoc Fœdus inierunt, in hac usque sententia perstare, nullo Voto, Juramento, Pacto posteriori obliterari posse Typos Illos, & Characteras, quos Justa & Legitima Juramenta, prius animis Ipsorum insculpserant.
units.tr: Indeed, I readily believe and hope that most of those who entered this covenant still hold to this opinion: that no later vow, oath, or pact can wipe out those impressions and characters which lawful and just oaths had earlier engraved on their minds, before.

units.la: Iam verò, quod istas Fœderationes suspicioni magis facit obnoxias, illud est communem esse hanc & quasi tritam viam in omnibus Reipublicæ & Ecclesiæ Factiosis hujusmodi Perturbationibus. Tunc enim Zeli Forma maximè, & exquisitæ pietatis persona induitur, cùm perniciosissima meditantur vafri homines contra omne fixum & sacrum in Religione & Legibus: quas his machinulis suis (velut cochlea quadam adtorquente subtiliter quidem, sed valide) sensim primò & occulta inflectione à Nota sua Regula, & consuetudine abducunt, ut obsequentiores deinde fiant eorum cupidini, qui sub larva Sacrorum Fœderum, sibi omnia subjicere moliuntur.
units.tr: Now, what makes these confederacies all the more open to suspicion is that this is the common and well-worn path in all such disturbances of the commonwealth and the Church. For the form of zeal and the appearance of exquisite piety are then most put on, when crafty men are plotting the most destructive designs against everything fixed and sacred in religion and the laws. By these little contrivances they draw them, as if by some screw that turns subtly but forcefully, first gradually and by a hidden bending from their accustomed rule and custom, so that afterwards they become more compliant to the desires of those who, under the mask of sacred covenants, labour to subject everything to themselves.

units.la: His tamen Funiculis & quasi intortis viminibus haud sperandum est diutius tenere conscientias, quàm dum Vis illis adsit plicatrix: statim enim quisque sibi Pontifex fit, & illa facilè solvit ligamina, quæ non aliquod è Verbo Divino præceptum, sed Astutia[?] Factionis, vel Terror indidit; quæque vel superflua erant prius obligatis, vel cum fraude & injuria imposita, si eo consilio posterius imponi deprehenderint, ut justæ illæ priores & necessariæ obligationes, vel pro tempore ceciderint, vel omnino diffolvcrentur.
units.tr: Yet one must not expect to hold consciences by these cords and, as it were, twisted withies any longer than force is at hand to twist them. For at once each man becomes his own pontiff, and easily loosens those bonds which were imposed not by any precept from the Word of God but by the cunning of a faction or by terror. Those bonds were either superfluous for the men already bound, or they were imposed with fraud and injury, if men discover that they were laid on afterwards with the purpose that the earlier, just and necessary obligations should either lapse for the time being or be altogether dissolved.

units.la: Raro certe vel nunquam id agunt Me-dia ista Illicita ut ad Officium suum melius adigantur homines, sed ut Partibus accedant firmiores. Atque adeò parum refert, quid de piis Fœderum clausulis exequaris, modò, Consiliis & Partibus, & Principali horum Fini adhæreas.
units.tr: Rarely, if ever, do these unlawful means serve to bring men more effectively to their duty; they serve rather to win firmer adherents to a party. And so it matters little what you make of the pious clauses of the covenants, provided you cling to their counsels, their party, and its chief end.

units.la: Video enim, Istius Authores, Fœdus suum velut Manna objicere (non utique è Coelo demissum) sed in hoc non absimile, quod sit gustui cujuslibet, & Palato conforme. Susceperis modo, quocunque sensu, per illos licet, seu diverso ab aliis, seu contrario; cautum sit, provisum, reservatum, quod lubet, modo, ne præcipuo illi adverseris, quod in Me & Ecclesiam machinantur. Satis habent, si auctarum sibi (quoad speciem) Partium opinionem acquirant. Ita parum meminerunt homines, Deo non illudi
units.tr: For I see that the authors of this covenant hold it out like manna (not indeed sent down from heaven), but in this respect not unlike it: that it suits the taste and palate of anyone. You may accept it, provided only that, in whatever sense you like, whether one different from or contrary to others, you take care, provide, and reserve whatever you please; so long as you do not oppose that chief aim of theirs, which they plot against me and the Church. It is enough for them if they win for themselves a reputation for a party increased in numbers, at least in appearance. Thus men little remember that God is not mocked.

units.la: In hoc sensu latiori, opinor, multos Mihi satis & Ecclesiæ benevolos in hoc Fœdus jurasse qui non ea stultitiâ aut superstitione censendi, ut quicquam pietati, & fidei manifestè repugnans sint propterea magis admissuri, qui revera hûc potius delapsi sunt, ad evitandam vim & ruinam recusantibus plane imminentem, quam, quod illud omnino æstimarent, aut impensius huic essent addicti.
units.tr: In this wider sense, I think, many who are sufficiently well-disposed toward me and the Church have sworn to this covenant. They are not so foolish or superstitious as to think that they should be more ready to admit anything which is manifestly repugnant to piety and faith. Rather, they have really slipped into it chiefly to avoid the force and ruin that were plainly hanging over those who refused, and not because they thought well of it in itself or were more devoted to it.

units.la: In quo forsan latitudo generalium quasi rundam clausularum nonnihil illos potest juvare: quale illud conandi & agendi quod fieri potest, & pro loci & muneris sui rationes atque etiam secundum verbum Dei, per hæc enim, revera, nulli datur licentia evagandi extra limites bonæ conscientiæ, qui omnes fixi & certi sunt, vel generaliter in Dei lege, vel speciatim in Regni legibus, quatenus hîc particularia officia in exercitio suo segulantur.
units.tr: In this matter the breadth of certain general clauses, as it were, may help them somewhat: such as the clause of striving and acting as far as can be done, and according to the reasons of one's place and office, and also according to the word of God. For by these clauses in truth no one is given licence to wander beyond the limits of a good conscience, which are all fixed and certain, either generally in the law of God or specifically in the laws of the kingdom, insofar as the particular duties here are followed in their exercise.

units.la: Utinam vero qui se jactant maximè Fœderatorum nomine, intra licitos illos fines se continerent, ad quos Deus Ipsos vocavit; certè enim nullâ aliâ ratione commodius expiarent hanc in prima suscepti-one temeritatem, quæ tunc clarè fiet perspicua, cum, (præter id, quod justâ & legitimâ Authoritate cujus mandato susciperetur, destituitur) jam palam ultrà fines ibi expressos, & prætensos, imò & contra etiam procedit. Ego interim libens ignoscam, qui in hoc Fœdus jurati hactenus tantùm observant, intra eos Legum, Pietatis & Fidelitatis terminos, qui nec detrimento sint Mihi nec Ecclesiæ, nec Paci Publicæ: quibus ire adversum, nulla vocatio legitima obligabit.
units.tr: Would that those who boast most of the name of Covenanters kept within those lawful bounds to which God has called them! Certainly by no other means would they more fittingly atone for this rashness in their first undertaking. That rashness will become clearly evident when, besides lacking the just and lawful authority by whose command it was undertaken, it now openly proceeds beyond the limits expressed and claimed there, and even against them. Meanwhile I willingly pardon those who, sworn to this Covenant, have so far observed it only within the bounds of laws, piety and fidelity, which are a detriment neither to me nor to the Church, nor to public peace. No lawful summons will bind anyone to go against these.

units.la: Quod ad illam Ecclesiæ Reformationem, (quæ sic-passim in hoc Fœdere ostentatur) haud vel æquum vel decorum existimo, ut ex paucorum Theologorum iniquiore consilio, (qui ductili suo & servili ingenio, ad quid vis subdito agendum & obsequendum parati, etiam adversus superius suum judicium, Professionem & Praxin) ita turpi probro aut suspicione aspergatur Doctrina & Disciplina Ecclesiæ Anglicanæ; quale nunquam antea factum audivi, vel ab ullâ foris Ecclesiâ (quæ Reformata appellari meruerat) vel domi etiam à candidis & eruditis hominibus, quorum omnium judicia merito pluris facio, quam istorum cujusvis factione corrupti.
units.tr: As for that Reformation of the Church (which is everywhere displayed in this Covenant), I do not think it fair or seemly that the doctrine and discipline of the Church of England should be so shamefully stained with infamy and suspicion by the more unjust counsel of a few theologians. These men, with their pliable and servile disposition, are ready to do or obey whatever a superior demands, even against their own judgment, profession and practice. I have never heard of such a thing done before, either by any Church abroad (which deserved to be called Reformed), or at home by upright and learned men, whose judgments I rightly value far above those of anyone corrupted by the faction of these men.

units.la: Nemo certè propenfiori quam ego ftudio, in debitas omnes Reformationes ferctur, maturo modò judicio, & conscientiâ bonâ suscipiantur, atque in ea solum procedant, quæ æqua priùs deliberatione habita ). ex Dei Verbo,& Recta Ratione evincentur pravè admissa; Hic vero plus ultrò exhibui,quàm vel ea, quæ liberrima, plenissima, prudentiffima erant Parlamenta, unquam adhùc expetebant.
units.tr: Certainly no one is more inclined than I am toward all due reformations, provided they are undertaken with mature judgment and a good conscience, and proceed only in those matters which, after fair deliberation, are shown from God's Word and right Reason to have been wrongly admitted. Yet here I have offered more than the most free, most full and most prudent Parliaments have ever sought.

units.la: Nimis clarè vero constat ex iis quæ infequuta sunt, Reformationis hujus Consilium nihil aliud fuisse, quam ut dejecto de gradu Episcopatu, & in Presbyteratum commutato, fundis suis & reditibus spoliaretur Dei Ecclesia. Nulli enim hactenus magis in Legitimo suo Jure violati fuerunt quam Episcopi, cæterique Ecclesiastici. Hi statim ut pinguissimæ ferarum, mactan-di: Reliquus Schismatum & Hæresium macer Grex tolerari haud ægrè impetrabit. Sic ob vineam suam Naboth reus factus Blasphemiæ. Ita usque perspicio, utcunque vela impleverit Religionis Spiritus, Utilitatem solam esse Circinum, quo cursum suum Factiosi homines in seditiosis hisce Motibus gubernant.
units.tr: It is only too clear from what has followed that the aim of this Reformation was nothing other than this: with the episcopate cast down from its rank and changed into presbytery, God's Church should be stripped of its lands and revenues. For no one has hitherto been more violated in their lawful right than the bishops and the other churchmen. Like the fattest beasts, they are to be slaughtered at once; the remaining lean flock of schisms and heresies will easily obtain toleration. So Naboth, because of his vineyard, was made guilty of blasphemy. Thus I plainly see that, however much the spirit of religion may fill their sails, utility alone is the compass by which factious men steer their course in these seditious movements.

units.la: Deo Gratias ago; quanquam maximè omnium expositus fuerim Tentationi huic Sacrilegæ, ut Terras Ecclesiæ, & Provcn-tus [?] invaderem, (qui à Coronæ munificentia impriinprimis profecti, de Illa tenentur, atque huc tantum legaliter consensu meo possunt reverti) semper tamen ita ab his abhorruit anima mea, ut Sacrilegis hujusmodi Reformationibus nunquam vel minimum pertentarer: illud interim vehementer percupiens, Episcopos, caeterosque Ecclesiasticos ita semper posse Reformari, ut, quae Majorum meorum pia Munificentia Deo & Ecclesiae donavit, tum quaecunque alia additamenta Christianae beneficentiae accesserint, & mereri digne possint & recte administrare.
units.tr: I give thanks to God. Although I have been more exposed than anyone to this sacrilegious temptation, to invade the lands and revenues of the Church (which, having come chiefly from the bounty of the Crown, are held by it, and can return hither only with my lawful consent), my soul has always so abhorred such things that I have never in the least attempted such sacrilegious reformations. Yet I most earnestly desire that bishops and other churchmen may always be so reformed that what the pious generosity of my ancestors gave to God and the Church, and whatever other additions of Christian beneficence have come, they may both deserve and rightly administer.

units.la: Nulla vero unquam (ut spero (necessitas Me aut Meos huc impellet, ut Agros Sacerdotum usurpare velimus aut vendere, quod & Pharaonis Theologia; & vera pietas Iosephi respuebat. Tam iniquum prorsus videtur Pietatis juxta, & Rationis oculo, ut munus omnium sanctissimum debitis suis incitamentis fraudetur, & (quale illud alterius duro corde Pharaonis) subducto stramine pensum augeatur: quod fecerunt nonnulli, persequentes oppressam Ecclesiam usque ad Rubrum Mare Belli Civilis, unde solo Miraculo salvari supererat, Illi, inquam, & Mihi, qui hunc maximum mihi Titulum & praecipuam Gloriam duco, ut sim Defensor Ecclesiae, tum in vera Fide, tum in justis suis commodis, a Sacrilegio & Apostasia perinde abhorrens.
units.tr: Yet I hope that no necessity will ever drive me or mine to wish to seize or sell the fields of the priests, which both the theology of Pharaoh and the true piety of Joseph rejected. It seems altogether as unjust, to the eye of piety and of reason alike, that the most holy office should be defrauded of its due incentives, and (as with the hard-hearted Pharaoh) the task be increased while the straw is withdrawn. Some have done this, pursuing the oppressed Church even to the Red Sea of civil war, whence only a miracle remained to save it. Those, I say, and I, who count this my greatest title and chief glory, to be the defender of the Church, both in true faith and in its just advantages, abhorring sacrilege and apostasy equally.

units.la: Vivam potius (cum Decessore meo Henrico Tertio) Eleemosynis Ecclesiæ fultentatus, quàm è Præsulum & Ministrorum ore Panem suum violenter eripiam.
units.tr: I would rather live (with my predecessor Henry III) sustained by the alms of the Church than violently snatch my bread from the mouths of prelates and ministers.

units.la: Proximum huic deinde futurum est, ad Ieroboami modum reformari: ut consecrentur è populo vilissimi Sacerdotes in Isra-el[?]; aureosque Illos vitulos colant, Ecclesiæ patrimonio, & dote locupletatos; quod quam cessit foeliciter Principi Illi, Sacerdotibus & Populo, fatis notum est, nec proculdubio hîc aliter futurum, si qui hactenus in Tutela erant Regum & Reginarum, qui Nutricii Patres & Matres huic semper Ecclesiæ exiterunt, ad eorum demensum vivendum habeant, qui jam satis ostenderunt, quid à se Duri Patris quid Malignæ Novercæ exspectandum.
units.tr: The next step would then be to reform things after the manner of Jeroboam: that the vilest men from the people be consecrated as priests in Israel, and that they worship those golden calves, enriched with the patrimony and endowment of the Church. How happily that turned out for that prince, the priests and the people is well known. Nor would it doubtless turn out otherwise here, if those who hitherto were under the guardianship of kings and queens, who have always been the nursing fathers and mothers of this Church, were to live according to the mind of those who have already shown well enough what is to be expected from a harsh father or a wicked stepmother.

units.la: Quod si paupertas Scotiæ crimen hîc aliquanto extenuaret, in hac tamen ubertate & copia Anglia rapi sic proventus Ecclesiæ, nullo modo excusare licet, aut invidiam deprecari.
units.tr: But even if the poverty of Scotland somewhat lessened the guilt here, in England, so rich and abundant, to plunder the revenues of the Church in this way can in no wise be excused or its odium averted.

units.la: Ego vero nec id precari à Deo ausim, ut avertat illa à Regno & Ecclesiæ calamitosa, quæ Ministrorum Paritatem & Indigenam haud dubie sunt secuta: cum sic prorsus videamur vel tentare Deum, vel illudere, ea mala deprecantes quorum Causæ & Remedia sunt in nostra potestate: cum his non uti[?] flagitium sit, illas, non devitare
units.tr: Indeed I would not dare to pray to God that he avert those calamities from the kingdom and Church which have undoubtedly followed the parity and independency of ministers. For we seem either to tempt God or to mock him if we pray against those evils whose causes and remedies lie in our own power. Since it is a disgrace not to use these remedies, it is equally a disgrace not to avoid those evils.

units.la: Abunde est, quo damna Reipublicæ sine Ecclesiæ ruinâ resarciantur. Illius quidem libenter Restaurator audiam, haud tamen eâ conditione, ut sub obtentu publici æris liberandi, hujus merito dicar Oppressor. Satis erat quæ contraxit causa improba, hoc vero pacto dissolvere, multo foret deterius. Deus faxit, ut nec Ego hec Mei funus unquam huic culpæ affines.
units.tr: It is enough that the losses of the commonwealth be made good without the ruin of the Church. I would gladly hear myself called the restorer of the former, but not on the condition that, under pretext of freeing public money, I should deservedly be called the oppressor of the latter. It was enough to dissolve by this means what a wicked cause had contracted; to do so in this way would be far worse. God grant that neither I nor mine should ever be bound to this guilt, not even at my funeral.

units.la: Ad te Domine preces meas dirigo, enixe obtestans ut hanc subditis meis ignoscas temeritatem jurandi, & acriorem in illis postea sensum efficias, quo illa justa, moralia, nullatenus remittenda vincula à Verbo Tuo & Regni Legibus conscientiis eorum imposita, accuratius in posterùm observent, à quibus multi Pietatis[?], aut Reformationis respectus satis erunt illos obsolvendo, nedum in Partem adversam transfire permittent.
units.tr: To you, Lord, I direct my prayers, earnestly beseeching you to pardon my subjects this rashness of swearing, and to make their feeling sharper afterwards, so that they may more carefully observe those just and moral bonds, not to be loosened, which your Word and the laws of the realm have imposed on their consciences. From these bonds many considerations of piety or reformation would be enough to release them, let alone allow them to pass over to the opposite side.

units.la: Fac ut serò tandem cogitent, nil violentum & injurium cum Religione constare.
units.tr: Grant that at last they may come to think that nothing violent and unjust agrees with religion.

units.la: Tu nullius Sacrilegium approbas, qui sic Zelum suum offendit in detestando Idola.
units.tr: You approve of no sacrilege, you who thus show your zeal in detesting idols.

units.la: Tu per Regum Sapientissimum docuisti, laqueum esse homini Sanctum devorare, ac postea ad vota converti.
