units.tr: You, Lord, know with what distress of mind I endure these evils from my subjects, for whom I have always desired the best; and for this reason I feel most keenly that they compel me to do evil to them, while I punish their wrongdoing. Since I am punished on both sides, as victor and as vanquished alike, grant me a double portion of your Spirit and that measure of grace which alone will suffice for me.

units.la: Quemadmodum me habuisti miserrimum, ita maxime facias reformari; ut non solum eò fœlix sim, ut civilium dissidiorum finem videam, sed Instrumentum etiam fiam præcipuum reddituræ Pacis,*& in Regnis meis fœliciter stabiliendæ.
units.tr: As you have made me most wretched, so may you above all cause me to be restored; so that I may be happy not only in seeing an end to civil dissensions, but may also become the chief instrument of restoring peace and of establishing it happily in my kingdoms.

units.la: Sit diversarum Partium una æmulatio, ut se invicem ratione, & moderatione animi exsuperent, & ea postremo sui abnegatione, quæ deceat illos qui cogitant mutuis nostris dissidiis scindi publicum, & id Bonis maxime expedire ut fit omnium concordia.
units.tr: Let there be one rivalry of the different parties, that they may surpass one another in reason and moderation of mind, and at last in that self-denial which befits those who consider that the public is torn apart by our mutual dissensions, and that it is most expedient for good men that there be concord among all.

units.la: Sin Tu (Domine) qui ob peccata nostra calamitates Belli induxisti, pergas adhuc ob peccata Belli fœlicitatem Pacis denegare, & nos usque detinere in calamitatum circulo, des Mihi tamen Famulo Tuo & fidelibus meis (licet oppressis) Subditis ea tandem pace frui[?], quam nec Mundus dare potest, nec eripere.
units.tr: But if you, Lord, who on account of our sins brought on the calamities of war, should still go on to deny the happiness of peace on account of sins, and keep us constantly within the circle of calamities, nevertheless grant to me, your servant, and to my faithful subjects (though oppressed), to enjoy at last that peace which neither the world can give nor take away.

units.la: Ne Mihi sanguinem Subditorum meorum impu-averis[?], animo valde reluctanti, & dolore summo effusi in illa justa mea & necessaria defensione, sed me pretioso illo lava Sanguine, à Magno illo Pacificatore Iesu Christo propter Me effuso, quem Me brevi confido ex his omnibus angustiis liberaturum: novi enim Iubilationem Impiorum brevem esse, & gaudium Hypocritæ ad instar puncti.
units.tr: Do not impute to me the blood of my subjects, shed with my mind greatly reluctant and with the deepest grief in that just and necessary defence of mine; but wash me with that precious blood of the great Peacemaker Jesus Christ, shed on my behalf, who, I trust, will soon deliver me from all these distresses: for I know that the rejoicing of the impious is brief, and the joy of the hypocrite like a moment.

units.la: 20. De Reformationibus Temporum.
units.tr: 20. Of the Reformations of the Times.

units.la: NUlla adeô invidenda est Gloria, quâm quæ ex debita Ecclesiæ vel Status Reformatione acquiritur, nisi cùm sint deformitates ejusmodi, ut ipsa Motum incidentium, & Novitatum incommoda bonum Reformationis exsuperent.
units.tr: No glory is to be envied so much as that which is won by the due reformation of the Church or of the State, unless the deformities are of such a kind that the disorders caused by the upheaval and the troubles of novelties outweigh the good of the reformation.

units.la: Hunc licet mihi Deus honorem negaret, ut Instrumentum fiam tam præclari Operis, quoquo modo tamen efsectum lætarer.
units.tr: Although God may deny me this honour, that I should become the instrument of so distinguished a work, I would nonetheless rejoice that it had been accomplished in any way.

units.la: Grata sanè in initio Parlamenti hujus studia fuere, ut quicquid Temporum Indulgentia, vel corruptela morum pravi induxerat reformaretur: jam non minùs discrucior, cùm his Turbis Factionum libertatemParlamenti oppressam videam, cumque Legum extantium, & Religionis sancitæ (quæ Mensura & Canon Reformationis esse debuerant (nullam prorsùs rationem haberi, & eâ porrò iniqui-tate, tate, & populari assentatione Affectibus quorundam & Opinionibus obsequutum in detrimentum Publici, & Reformatæ Religionis ingens Scandalum.
units.tr: At the beginning of this Parliament, indeed, the aim was gratifying: that whatever the indulgence of the times or the corruption of morals had introduced should be reformed. Now I am no less tormented, since I see the liberty of Parliament crushed by these tumults of factions, and no account taken of the laws in force or of the established religion, which ought to have been the measure and rule of reformation. Instead, with such iniquity and popular flattery, the passions and opinions of certain men have been indulged, to the detriment of the public and of the reformed religion, and to enormous scandal.

units.la: Quanta enim hinc continuò facta est omnis Ordinis & Regiminis Ecclesiastici dissolutio, quæ Novitatum, Schismatum & corruptissimorum Dogmatum licentiofa invectio, quæ in Sacris Administrationibus Indecentia pariter & Confusio, quæ in Jura & Fundos Ecclesiarum Invasiones Sacrilegæ, qui Cleri contemptus & consumeliæ, quæ in Me denique dehonestamenta & injuriæ, omnes statim ab hoc strepitu Reformationis insecutæ (ut à calidis Radiorum stricturis magni imbres) omnes mecum unà saniores testes erant mœstissimi & spectatores.
units.tr: For how great was the immediate dissolution of all ecclesiastical order and government that followed from this; what licentious introduction of novelties, schisms and most corrupt doctrines; what indecency and likewise confusion in the sacred administrations; what sacrilegious invasions of the rights and endowments of the churches; what contempt and insults toward the clergy; and what, finally, dishonours and injuries against me. All of these, following at once from this clamour of reformation (as heavy rain follows hot flashes of lightning), were witnessed, along with me, by saner observers, who were most sorrowful spectators.

units.la: Omnium vero Errorum origo est, quod Populares ferè clamores & Furor, vulgo Zeli famam, & Communis omnium Voti obtineant, unde paucis placendi studio publicè omnes plærumque læduntur.
units.tr: The origin of all errors is that popular clamour and frenzy, commonly called zeal, win the reputation and the common wish of all; and so, through the eagerness to please a few in public, nearly everyone is generally harmed.

units.la: Certe optimè tunc initur Reformandiratio, atque optimè demum perficitur, cùm moderatè & libere, & nullis Partium studiis prosequamur; contrà Factiosæ molitiones multo plures offendunt, quam placent.
units.tr: Certainly reform is best begun when we pursue it moderately, freely and without party aims, and it is best finished in the same way. On the contrary, factious schemes offend far more than they please.

units.la: Ultro me paratum ostendi omnes in Re Ecclesiastica, & Religione discrepantias, liberæ Synodi consultationi, vel Convocationi rite electæ permittere, cujus tandem decretis (cum omnium essent suffragia inclusa) verisimile est omnes acquieturos.
units.tr: I have shown myself ready, of my own accord, to let all differences in ecclesiastical matters and religion be examined by a free Synod or a duly elected Convocation, and it is likely that all will acquiesce in its decrees, since the votes of everyone would be included.

units.la: Conventum illum Theologorum quos (more quodam insolito & extraordinario) Domus Vtraque ad deliberandum de Ecclesiasticis adhibuerunt, hactenus tantum non probo, quòd nec legitime congregati nec electi fuerint; nec totius Cleri Anglicæ partes sustineant, neque omnino liberè & incorruptè agere possint, cùm (etiamsi nulla alia vis fieret) intra certos tamen limites & fines constringantur.
units.tr: That Assembly of Divines whom Both Houses, by a certain unusual and extraordinary method, have employed to deliberate on ecclesiastical matters, I have so far scarcely approved, because they were neither lawfully gathered nor chosen. Nor do they represent the parts of the whole English clergy, and they cannot act freely and uncorruptly at all, since, even if no other force were applied, they are nonetheless confined within certain limits and bounds.

units.la: Illud enim haud facile credam, tot homines doctrinæ & pietatis nomine insignes, qui Liturgiam & Regimen Anglicanæ Ecclesiæ haud ita pridem (in præcipuis) probaverant, adeo derepente consensuros in utrunque extirpandum, (cum Illud saltem ignorare non possent si non Apostolica institutione, at Primitiva & Vniversali Praxi defendi) modo integra fuisset suffragandi libertas, nec Diversæ Factionis potentia occultas spes & metus instillando in eos tandem valuissent, ut has simul promoverent plenissimas periculi Novitates, nullo espectu habito ad superiorem suam [?]entiam & Praxin, vel ad rem & existimationem totius Cleri communem, pretâ Ordinis, Doctrinæ, & Religionis curâ, contra omnia denique Veterum Ecclesiarum exempla, Leges Regni constitutas, & consensu mMeum, qui cernere nunquam impetrabit adversus [?]am illam lucem, quâ Intellectus meus in hoc Articulo illustratur.
units.tr: For I could hardly believe that so many men, distinguished for their learning and piety, who not long ago approved the Liturgy and the government of the English Church (in its chief points), would so suddenly agree to root out both. They could not at least be ignorant that the former is defended not by apostolic institution but by primitive and universal practice. Yet they would have agreed had the freedom to vote remained whole, and had the power of the opposing faction not prevailed by instilling secret hopes and fears into them, so that they promoted together these most dangerous novelties. No regard was had for their own earlier judgement and practice, or for the common interest and esteem of the whole clergy; under the pretext of care for order, doctrine and religion, they set aside all the examples of the ancient Churches, the constituted laws of the kingdom, and my consent. Such men will never gain the power to see against that light by which my understanding is illumined in this matter.

units.la: In rebus enim ejusmodi, quæ non [?]erindè ex professo rationi aut Fidei aut Bonis Moribus adversantur, & circa quæ in Scriptura haud ita clarè & distinctè præcipitur, ibi certe perpetua & universalis Praxis Ecclesiæ optima est quam sequamur Regula.
units.tr: For in matters of this kind, which do not plainly and openly oppose reason, faith or good morals, and on which Scripture does not command so clearly and distinctly, the perpetual and universal practice of the Church is surely the best rule to follow.

units.la: Quod ad me attinet, promptus eram vel donare Presbyteratui vel restituere, quicquid Episcopatui conjunctus intra Rationis & Prudentiæ terminos postulasset: ut vero ita penitus invadat illam Potestatem, & Gladio afferat, & Antiqui illius Ordinis Jura aboleat, id nec justum in Episcopatum nec Presbyteratui tutum existimo, nec ullo modo vel Ecclesiæ vel Reipublicæ convenire.
units.tr: As for me, I was ready either to give to the presbytery or to restore whatever, within the limits of reason and prudence, belonged to the episcopate. But that they should so entirely invade that power, put it to the sword, and abolish the rights of that ancient order, I judge neither just for the episcopate nor safe for the presbytery, nor in any way fitting for either the Church or the Commonwealth.

units.la: Moderata certe consilia haud difficulter secuta fuisset debita Reformatio; atque ea forsan quæ longè gratior fuisset iis Ipsis Theologis, qui ipsi prius decepti multa postea Gravitatis specie aliorum consilia promovebant quæ haud dubiò jam satis detexerunt, licet spes suas delusas & offensam præ metu dissimulent.
units.tr: Surely due Reformation would have followed moderate counsels without difficulty, and perhaps those counsels would have been far more welcome to the very Divines themselves. They, first deceived themselves, afterwards promoted, under a show of great gravity, the counsels of others, which no doubt they have by now sufficiently uncovered, although out of fear they conceal their disappointed hopes and their offence.

units.la: Speciosa vero illa & Popularia Christi scilicet Gubernationis, Throni, Sceptri, Regni (quod certè nunquam dividitur, nec quod istorum est bifrons) tum illud integræ & Absolutæ Reformationis æquè facile est cuivis Novæ Formæ appingere, quam pulcherrimos colores deformi Imagini.
units.tr: That showy and popular catchword, forsooth, of Christ's Government, Throne, Sceptre, Kingdom (which is surely never divided, nor two-faced as theirs is), and then that of entire and absolute Reformation, is as easy to attach to any new form as the finest colours are to a deformed image.

units.la: Fenestras interim in Ecclesiis (satis tempore deformatas) confringere, Cruces etiam (quæ Civilia apud nos monumenta potius quàm Religiosa) evertere, Busta mortuorum violare & Epitaphia eradere, quibus solum admonebantur Posteri quas Deo debent gratias in majori luce versantes Omnes porro Ministros Sacris publicè operantes suo penitus arbitrio, & (quâ privatim pollent, Facultati permittere (ut merito ambigat Christianus, quibus tandem AMEN subjiciat, vel, ne forte cum periculo in errores aut Blasphemia consentiat, vel insulsa forsan alia aut ridicula, ab audacibus plærunque & indoctis temere inter Preces officia & Cōciunculas jacta) quin edere passim Catechismos, & Confessiones Fidei reconcinnare, quasi nulla priùs extitisset in hac Ecclesia doctrina sana omninò aut perspicua circa vel ipsa Fidei elementa, quàm Quinquennii hujus proximi deliberatio hoc negotium integrè maturasset:
units.tr: To break the windows of churches (already disfigured enough by time), to tear down crosses too (which among us are civil monuments rather than religious ones), to violate the tombs of the dead and erase their epitaphs, by which posterity, living in greater light, were merely reminded of the thanks they owe to God; further, to leave all ministers who perform sacred offices in public entirely to their own judgement, and to allow them, by whatever faculty they have in private, to do as they please, so that a Christian may rightly doubt to which he should append his AMEN, lest he perhaps agree, with danger, to errors or blasphemy, or to some other insipid or ridiculous thing rashly thrown in among prayers, offices and little sermons by mostly bold and unlearned men; not to mention scattering catechisms everywhere and re-fashioning confessions of faith, as if no sound and wholly clear doctrine on the very elements of faith had existed before in this Church, until the deliberation of this most recent quinquennium had fully ripened the business.

units.la: Istaquidem omnia & his similia, quæ vulgò fieri solent (ne nil facere videantur) ab his Reformationum larvis quibus breve aucupantur Plebis Gratiam (quæ his Novitatum illecebris non secùs ac Pueri Imagunculis vehementer quidē sed non diu afficitur) tantum abest ut merean-tur Reformationis laudem, ut revera (quantum ad Charitatem, Pietatem, Rectum Ordinem, & Mores spectat) turbida magis omnia & querula & confusa relinquantur, quàm, ubi primò inchoaverant.
units.tr: All these things and similar ones, which are commonly done (lest they seem to do nothing), are masks of Reformation by which they catch the brief favour of the common people. The people, like children with little pictures, are affected by these allurements of novelties strongly, indeed, but not for long. These things are so far from deserving the praise of Reformation that, in fact, as regards charity, piety, right order and manners, everything is left more troubled, querulous and confused than when they first began.

units.la: Haud enim facili operâ mala illa priora & detrimenta maxima pensare licebit aut corrigere, satis carè ab illis conciliata, & necessariò semper futura, ni remedia debita adhibeantur.
units.tr: Indeed, it will not be easy to make up for and correct those earlier evils and very great losses, which were gained carelessly enough from them and which will always remain unless suitable remedies are applied.

units.la: Id utinam seriò tandem & unanimiter vellent Dei opus agere, non suum. Multis sanè[?] incommodis obviam itum fuisset, in Religionem (prout dignum erat ) priò loco spectâssent.
units.tr: Would that at last they would seriously and unanimously be willing to do God's work, and not their own. Surely many inconveniences would have been avoided had they looked first to religion (as was fitting).

units.la: Illud vero haud absurdè existimaant nonnulli, Ecclesiæ & Status Regimen, tot Legibus firmatum & diuturna Consuetudine fixum haud ita statim diffluxurum, & in novas suas Formas fundi facile, nisi ad Ignem prius Belli Civilis colliquesceret, in quo facti potiores, statuerant Me & Subditos meos universos ad procumbendum adigere, & adorandas Imagines erectas ab Illis & fabricatas: Sin id Christi Spiritus in horum hominum pectoribus (Charitatis, nimirum, & Mansuetudinis & Sapientiae) insedisset, quantum in linguis Nomen Christi & ipsissima Reformandi Regula jactabatur, haud dubie (illius Benedictione) tum in Christi Gloriam, tum in Bonum Ecclesiae, Honoremque Religionis & Veritatem efficacius multo valuisset.
units.tr: Some, however, think it not absurd that the government of the Church and State, confirmed by so many laws and fixed by long-standing custom, would not so readily dissolve or pour itself easily into its new forms, unless first it were melted down in the fire of civil war. In that war the stronger faction had resolved to force me and all my subjects to prostrate ourselves and to adore the images that they had erected and made. But if the Spirit of Christ, namely of charity, meekness and wisdom, had settled in the breasts of these men, then, as far as the name of Christ and the very rule of reforming were bandied about on their tongues, undoubtedly by His blessing it would have worked far more effectively both for Christ's glory and for the good of the Church, and for the honour and truth of religion.

units.la: Qui reformare volunt publice, in se primum agant, & experiantur in corde suo quae in alios constituunt: intus enim si quid fuerit detorme, vereor, ut qui de Publico videntur solliciti, in ea Privata Consilia pertrahantur quae Publico Bono multum obstabunt.
units.tr: Those who wish to reform in public should first act upon themselves and test in their own hearts what they propose for others. For if anything within is deformed, I fear that those who seem anxious about the public will be drawn into those private plans which will greatly hinder the public good.

units.la: Recta quidem ratio Reformandi Ecclesiam minime omnium consistit cum Civilis Status perturbatione, nec oppressa Fidelitate crevit unquam Religio, cujus haec pars praecipua & Ornamentum est. Proximum enim a praecepto illo Deum Timc[?], subjicitur Regem Honora. Instaurabitur (haud dubito) Christi Regnum Meo neutiquam everso, & cùm studia & affectus cessaverint haud utique Boni Christiani censebuntur qui Boni Subditi esse desierint.
units.tr: Right reason for reforming the Church is by no means compatible with disturbance of the civil state. Religion has never grown when loyalty was crushed, and loyalty is its chief part and ornament. For next to the precept Fear God comes Honour the king. It will be restored (I have no doubt) Christ's kingdom, with my kingdom in no way overthrown. And when zeal and passions have ceased, those will by no means be counted good Christians who have ceased to be good subjects.

units.la: Christi certe Regimen in stabilimentum Regni Mei, non in ruinam cedet, cùm meum ab Illo acceptum profitear, atque id unicè in votis habeam ut in Gloriam Illius & Ecclesiæ Bonum administretur.
units.tr: Christ's government will tend to the establishment of my kingdom, not to its ruin, since I acknowledge mine to have been received from Him, and I have this one wish: that it be administered to the glory of Him and the good of the Church.

units.la: Si id ferió laborassent nonnulli vel quid hoc sibi vellet intellexissent à Christo Regi, facta illa sua & dicta dissolutiora quibus & mihi & sibi invicem injurii fuerunt, multo rectius fuissent moderati.
units.tr: If some had earnestly laboured at this, or had understood what this meant, from Christ the King, then their deeds and words, by which they were more dissolute and injurious both to me and to one another, would have been far more moderately conducted.

units.la: Quemadmodum vero Boni Fines nunquam iusta efficient prava Media, ita nec ex malis Principiis bona unquam fiet conclusio, ni miraculo quodam suæ Misericordiæ lucem Deus è tenebris, è confusione ordinem, & è perturbationibus nostris Pacem creare destinaverit.
units.tr: Just as good ends never make wicked means just, so from bad principles no good conclusion will ever follow, unless by some miracle of his mercy God has determined to create light out of darkness, order out of confusion, and peace out of our disturbances.

units.la: Tu Domine, qui solus potes Coronam nobis dare pro cinere, & sublatâ Hypocrisi veritatem reddere, ne has nobis permittas Pharisaicas ablutiones pro Christiana Reformatione imponere.
units.tr: You, Lord, who alone can give us a crown for ashes and, taking away hypocrisy, restore truth; do not permit us to impose these Pharisaical washings in place of Christian reformation.

units.la: Intus illi sunt nobis Nævi maximi, & turpitudines, fac ut in nos ipsos severe agamus, & ab Animis nostris Reformatio incipiat, ut perspicaci Iudicio, & integro Corde accedentes, quae in Ecclesia aut Statu perperam facta sunt, idonei simus reformare.
units.tr: Within us are great blemishes and foulness; grant that we deal severely with ourselves, and that reformation begin from our own souls, so that, approaching with a keen judgement and an upright heart, we may be fit to reform what has been done amiss in the Church or the State.

units.la: Cor mundum crea in Nobis Deus & Spiritum rectum innova in visceribus nostris, ut tuo ductu simul & tua Benedictione in Tuam omnia Gloriam faciamus.
units.tr: Create a clean heart in us, O God, and renew a right spirit within our inmost parts, so that under your guidance and by your blessing we may do all things to your glory.

units.la: Miserere deformitatum & vulnerum, quae temerarii & saevi Reformatores huic Ecclesiae & Statui inflixerunt; exstingue Factionum flammas sub praetextu Reformandi accensas.
units.tr: Have mercy on the deformities and wounds which rash and cruel reformers have inflicted on this Church and State; quench the flames of factions kindled under the pretext of reforming.

units.la: Et quemadmodum per haec mutuo dissidia, & confusiones palam omnibus facere voluisti quam sint pravi nonnullorum fines; & infirma Iudicia; ita ex his flammis educas nos purgationes, praeeunte Christiana magis, & plus in se charitatis habente Reformatione, ubi nihil vindictae aut ambitus, avaritiae denique aut sacrilegii polleat in eorum consilia, quibus opus tam insigne & bonum, & jam maxime necessarium aequo & licito more peragendum providentia tua demandaverit; ut internae pietatis felicitate auctiti ego simul & populus etiam Pacis externa beneficio rectius nobis[?] in posterum discamus.
units.tr: And just as through these mutual disagreements and confusions you chose to show plainly to all how wicked the ends of some are and how weak their judgements, so from these flames lead us to purgation, with a reformation that goes before us, more Christian and more full of charity, where no vengeance, ambition, avarice or sacrilege prevails in the counsels of those to whom your providence has entrusted a work so remarkable, good and now most necessary, to be carried out in a fair and lawful manner; so that, made happy by inner piety, I and the people may also learn better for the future the external benefit of peace.

units.la: XXI. De Epistolis Regiis interceptis, & evulgatis.
units.tr: XXI. On the Royal Letters Intercepted and Published.

units.la: Literas meas fuisse interceptas, opportuna erat Hostium Malitiæ, & præter spem occasio, quâ tamen honestè & civiliter uti ignorabant. Nec sane arbitror, apud æquos & probos æstimatores quicquam in illis repertum itâ mihi in probrum cessisse, quam sic turpiter fuisse divulgatas, in eorum infamiam.
units.tr: That my letters were intercepted gave my enemies' malice an opportunity they welcomed, a chance beyond their hopes, though they did not know how to use it honourably and courteously. Nor do I think that anything found in them has turned to my disgrace in the eyes of fair and upright judges, so much as their having been shamefully published has turned to their infamy.

units.la: Tunc enim maximè se probat virtus, generosi animi vera indoles, cùm in hostes maximè liceat, nec ullâ magis humanitate afficimur, quàm quæ ab iis defertur[?] à quibus minimum speravimus. Hanc à me gratiam inire poterant chartas meas celando: in quibus cum essent veriora quædam, atque etiam arcana, certè[?] aliquid hîc civilitatis necessarium duissent homines non plane Barbari: Nec vera quicquam unquam inhumanius factum est, quàm eas publicè omnium exponere.
units.tr: For virtue is then most clearly proved, and the true nature of a noble mind shows itself, when it is most permitted to act against enemies. Nothing moves us more than kindness shown to us by those from whom we had hoped for least. My enemies could have won this favour from me by concealing my papers. Among them were some truer things, and even secrets, and men who were not altogether barbarous would surely have thought some measure of courtesy necessary here. Nothing has ever been done more inhumanely than to expose them all publicly.

units.la: Cùm verò secus vellet Providentia, haud utique molestè fero Pectus meum (quod Divinæ Omniscientiæ approbarestudeo ) palam jam coram Mundo retectum fieri, fine fucis illis omnibus & speciosis ad populum ornamentis, quæ in Publicis Epistolis & Orationibus solent. Vtinam vel in penitissimos animi mei sensus introspicere liceret Subditis meis; certe nil aliud deprehenderent, quàm quâ curâ & amore distractus sim, non quo Iura mea magis, quàm ut pacem eorum & fœlicitatem conservem, & quàm ingenti mœrore conficior, eos ita in perniciem suam delusos.
units.tr: But since Providence willed otherwise, I by no means take it hard that my heart, which I strive to have approved by the Divine Omniscience, is now openly laid bare before the world, without all those false and showy embellishments to the people that are usually found in public letters and speeches. Would that my subjects might look into the innermost feelings of my mind! Surely they would find nothing else there than the care and love that have drawn me on, not for my own rights more than for the preservation of their peace and happiness, and how deeply I am crushed with grief that they have been so deceived to their own ruin.

units.la: Nec quicquam amplius ex his literis malevolentia ullius consecuta est, quam, quod omnibus notum fecerim quàm constanti animo fuerim in Vxorem meam, Leges, & Religionem; Mella legent apes, ubi virus fugit Franca.
units.tr: Nor has any malice gained anything more from these letters than this: I have made known to all how steadfast I have been in regard to my wife, the laws, and religion. Bees will gather honey where the poison flees the Franca.

units.la: Quod explicare me voluerim angustiis (in quas me Hostes adegerant) licitis & honestis Foederationibus initis, nemo sane vituperabit qui me amat & Rempublicam, cùm haud fieri omnino possit, ut sint fœlices Subditi Mei Me misero, vel pace sua & Immunitatibus Me oppresso potiantur. Satis patet, ad hoc unicè nonnullos collimasse, ut {*}Absalonis exemplo, atroci aliquo facinore latius indies fieret dissidium, & exacerbatam utramque partem ita à se invicem distraherent, ut nulla spes esset postea redintegrandi.
units.tr: As for my wish to explain myself in the straits to which my enemies had reduced me, by lawful and honourable alliances, no one who loves me and the commonwealth will blame it, since it is quite impossible for my subjects to be happy while I am wretched, or to enjoy their peace and immunities while I am oppressed. It is plain that some aimed at this one thing: that, after the example of Absalom, by some dreadful deed the division might grow wider day by day, and by exasperating each side they might so drive them apart that no hope of ever reuniting them would remain.

units.la: Has verò, ut & cæteras Injurias non solum ( Deo Gratias ) æquo satis animo ferre possum, sed (quæ mea est Charitas) ignoscere.
units.tr: These injuries, as well as the others, I can not only bear with sufficient calm, by God's grace, but also, by my own charity, forgive.

units.la: Ea interim fuit Animi mei integritas ut non multùm metueret à stylo lædi: licet enim arcani fiducia in idgenus Literis majorem fortè in scribendo licentiam permitteret & malignorum cavillis obnoxiam, nunquam tamen principalis mei consilii innocentiam vel tam male intelligere, vel sinistre interpretari possunt, ut non omnibus fiat perspicuum, me nil magis exoptâsse, quàm ut omnia fœliciter componerentur, Iustitiæ & Honoris ratione habita: idque non ex meâ magis quam populi sententiâ, eorum saltem quibus aliqua supererat aut amoris in Me aut fidei scintilla: quibus etiam ipsæ hæ Literæ clare demonstrabunt, me & Rei meæ privatæ & Regni mei curas posse & negotia (arte quâ Principem decet) capessere; quod non libenter de me credi volunt Hostes mei, quasi ex aliorum Præscripto &
units.tr: My integrity of mind was such that I did not greatly fear being harmed by my pen. For although confidence in secrecy may have allowed me somewhat more freedom in writing a letter of this kind, and so exposed me to the jibes of the malicious, they could never so misunderstand or wrongly interpret the innocence of my chief purpose as to keep it from being plain to all that I desired nothing more than that everything be settled happily, with regard to justice and honour. And this I desired not so much from my own judgement as from that of the people, at least of those who still had some spark either of love toward me or of faith. These same letters will also clearly show that I can take up the cares and affairs both of my private estate and of my kingdom with the skill that befits a prince. My enemies do not willingly believe this of me, as if I lived by the dictation of others, and of those whom they have branded with the name of "evil counsellors"

units.la: Dictato viverem quos Pravorum Consu!-
units.tr: and (they say) lived by dictation,

units.la: sorum nomine infamarunt.•
units.tr: ... and have defamed under that name.

units.la: Jam forsan me respicient nonnulli ut meorum Consiliorum Authorem, & cùm alium non habeant in quem litem intendant, in me posthac omne odium effundent, quamquam id semper illis ægrè fuerit, ut vel ullâ animi mei libertate gauderé, vel conscientiæ meæ luci obtèperarem, quem sibi planè addici & mancipari volunt, sua inprimis consilia à Me probari debere existimantes qui tam diù contra me Bellum gesserunt.
units.tr: Now perhaps some will look upon me as the author of my own counsels, and since they have no one else to bring their suit against, they will pour all their hatred upon me from now on. Yet it has always been painful to them that I should enjoy any freedom of mind, or obey the light of my conscience. They wish me to be wholly bound over and enslaved to them, reckoning that, since they have waged war against me for so long, their own counsels above all must be approved by me.

units.la: Satis quidem fuisset illius diei victoria, cùm accesserunt in prædam Litera mex, ad explendam illam Famæ popularis ambitiosissimam sitim: siquidem apud vulgus hominum benè tantum audiunt prospera,contra adversa & afflicta conditio omni statim contumeliâ excipitur, quasi Bona Fortuna Umbra semper effet virtutis, & non frequentius turpia & injusta facinora in hoc Mundo prosequeretur.
units.tr: Indeed the victory of that day would have been enough, when my letters fell into their hands as spoil, to satisfy that most ambitious thirst for popular fame. For among the common people men hear only of prosperity with approval, while an adverse and afflicted condition is at once met with every insult, as if good fortune were always the shadow of virtue, and did not more often pursue base and unjust deeds in this world.

units.la: Verùm illis qualicunque successu nunquam fatis muniri videtur & commendari causa ejusmodi, quæ à Turbis auspicata de Aura Populari dependet. Has ergo suis consiliis utiliffimas ducunt victorias quæ famam & exftimationem meam apud populum pessundent. In horum enim pectoribus, omnes Amoris, Reverentiæ, Fidei scintillas ita penitùs sopitas aut extinctas cupiunt, ut nunquam possint reaccendi in illum ardorem, quo vel Mea vel Legum, vel Regnorum meorum Libertates (quas omnes pariter eversas cupiunt) vigeant amplius aut restituantur; existimatione mea ereptâ via pulchre sternitur ad eripiendum mihi vitam & Regnum: Regno enim indignus jam nec vitâ dignus judicabor. Accurata igitur sævitiâ pariter & astutiâ cogunt prius exequias Honoris Mei celebrare, ut mox interitu meo parentetur. Sed haud dubio veram illam Dei Justitiam, nec errori nec affectibus obnoxiam posse aliquando & velle perversa hominum studia, & consilia evertere; Potest ille efficere, & (ut spero) efficiet, ut in bonum meum cedant quæ in me pessima Inimici vel cogitarint, vel fecerint.
units.tr: But to them no success of any kind seems ever sufficient to fortify and recommend a cause of this sort, one that was begun by the mobs and depends on the popular breeze. They therefore count those victories most useful to their plans which will ruin my fame and reputation among the people. For they desire that every spark of love, reverence and faith in their hearts be so deeply smothered or extinguished that it can never be rekindled into that glow by which my liberties, or those of the laws and of my kingdoms (which they equally wish overthrown), might flourish again or be restored. Once my reputation has been snatched away, the way is nicely paved for taking from me my life and my kingdom: for I shall then be judged unworthy of the kingdom, and then of life too. With careful cruelty and cunning alike, they force me first to celebrate the funeral of my honour, so that afterwards it may be laid to rest with my death. But without doubt that true justice of God, which is subject neither to error nor to passions, can at some time, and will, overturn the perverse designs and counsels of men. He can bring it about, and (as I hope) will bring it about, that the worst things which my enemies have either planned or done against me turn to my good.

units.la: Nil me interim aliud existimo hâc Literarum interceptione, quàm tot Chartulas tantum perdidisse. Quantum vero Illis perierit Humanitatis famæ (quæ cùm omnibus debetur, certè omnium maximè ab iis qui singulare præ se ferunt pietatis studium) quantum etiam Reverentiæ & Honoris Regi suo debiti, & præsens ætas & futura optimè judicabit.
units.tr: Meanwhile I count nothing lost by this interception of my letters except so many little sheets of paper. As for how much of the reputation for humanity they have lost (which is owed to all, and certainly most of all by those who profess a special zeal for piety), and how much reverence and honour owed to their own king, the present age and the future will judge very well.

units.la: Sed nec Ipsas Eorum conscientias arbitror ita penitùs in stuporem datas, ut non sensu aliquo secreto afficiantur pudoris illius & Infamiæ quæ inhonesta facinora comitatur, utcunque publicâ adulatione, & populari Gratiâ commendata.
units.tr: Yet I do not think their consciences are so utterly stunned that they feel no hidden sense of that shame and infamy which accompany dishonourable deeds, however much such deeds may be commended by public flattery and popular favour.

units.la: Certe nunquam sperabunt Deo posse approbari turpem hujusmodi rem & indecoram; modo velint meminisse quâ Deus olim benedictione illam Nohæ Filiorum verecundiam & filialem in Patrem teneritudinem compensavit, cum nullâ contra Parentis infirmitate vel excusari posset Chami impudentia, vel ab execratione illa liberari ut esset Servus Servorum; quæ (vereor) ut sit illis hæsura, qui actibus plenis probri & placere student Populo, & hoc sibi Patrocinium firmare.
units.tr: Certainly they will never hope that such a shameful and indecent thing can be approved by God, if only they will remember how God once rewarded the modesty of Noah's sons and their filial tenderness toward their father, when Ham's impudence could be excused by no weakness of his parent, and he could not be freed from that curse, that he should be a servant of servants. I fear that this curse will cling to those who, by acts full of disgrace, strive to please the people and to confirm this as their defence.

units.la: Haud vero magis vel defendi possunt vel fœlicem exitum sortiri illa eorum malitiosa consilia, qui hac me ratione cogitabant summæ apud Populum ignominiæ & ludibrio exponere, officii illius valde immemores quo modeste celare jubebantur, si quid verè in Patriæ parente indecorum comperissent, quod tamen (Deo Gratias) neutiquam factum est, sed illius potius Gratiâ perfectum, ut mihi non secus (quàm olim Davidi evenerat) reverentiam porro conciliârit ipsa hæc Literarum vulgatio, quâ me ut Vilem Personam, omni prorsus exutum Majestate, & nulla posthac fide aut existimatione dignum exhibere omnibus voluerunt.
units.tr: Nor can those wicked plans of theirs be defended, or hope for a happy outcome, which in this way intended to expose me to the greatest ignominy and ridicule before the people, forgetting very much the duty by which they were bidden to conceal modestly whatever they might truly have found unbecoming in the parent of the country. That, thanks be to God, has by no means happened; rather, by God's favour, the very publication of these letters has so worked that reverence toward me has not been diminished, just as it once came to David. They wished to display me as a worthless person, stripped altogether of majesty, and deserving of no faith or esteem from now on.

units.la: Tu vero (Domine) qui Sapienti tua & cuncta disponente Providentiâ ordinas ea quae videntur in humani rebus incertissima, fac ut constantem suam in Me Misericordiam agnoscam, etiam ubi in[?] me maximam licentiam Hostibus meis permissi.
units.tr: But you, O Lord, who by your wise and all-ordering Providence arrange those things among human affairs that seem most uncertain, grant that I may acknowledge your constant mercy toward me, even when you have permitted my enemies the greatest licence against me.

units.la: Tu qui olim Achitophelis consilia difflasti, & in bonum tui David, & exitium Authoris convertisti, ita & horum potes machinamenta subvertere qui hæc mea secreta evulgando, odio me volebant & contemptui Populi exponere. Tuam Omniscientiam appello Testem Integritastis mea, quam iniqua & falsa sint illa valdè probrosa, quæ hac Chartarum mearum occasione Hostes mei pessimi interpretes de me vulgo credi postularunt.
units.tr: You who once scattered the counsels of Ahithophel, and turned them to the good of your David and to the ruin of their author, can also overturn the schemes of those who, by publishing these my secrets, wished to expose me to hatred and to the contempt of the people. I call your Omniscience to witness my integrity, and how unjust and false are those deeply shameful charges which my worst enemies, as interpreters of these papers of mine, have demanded be believed of me by the common people.

units.la: Malum quod in Me machinati sunt, & sollicitè ita procurarunt, ita in Caput Ipsorum revertatur, ut induantur pudore, & operiantur sicut diploide, confusione sua.
units.tr: May the evil they have plotted against me, and so diligently arranged, turn back upon their own heads, so that they may be clothed in shame and covered, as with a double garment, by their own confusion.

units.la: Vides Domine, quàm id omni studio agunt, ut Honorem meum deturpent, sensa animi detorqueant, & vestigia exprobrent Unctii Tui.
units.tr: You see, Lord, how eagerly they labour to disfigure my honour, to twist the feelings of my mind, and to heap reproaches upon the footsteps of your Anointed.

units.la: Me verò Corde illo dinè[?], quo libenter contumelias accipiam Tui causâ, & Tuæ Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: But give me that worthy heart with which I may gladly accept insults for your sake and for your Church.

units.la: Hunc in Me firma animum, ut tuo maximè studeam honori: meum tibi curæ fore nil dubito, vel me enim Potestati illi & Majestati restitues (quam nonnulli tuo permissu ita quærunt cripere) vel illa corona imperitiæ Christianæ patientiæ, tibi usque pertinacis per gloriam & ignominiam, per infamiam & bonam famam servire.
units.tr: Fix in me this firm resolve, that I may above all strive for your honour. I have no doubt that my cause is a matter of concern to you: either you will restore me to that power and majesty which some, by your permission, seek to snatch from me, or you will grant me that crown of Christian patience, so that I may serve you constantly through glory and dishonour, through infamy and good report.

units.la: Tu (Domine) fons es Bonitatis & Honoris, tu eximia Majestate induëris: fac me tuæ Excellentiæ qua sapientia Iustitia & misericordia superas, aliquo saltem modo participem, nec jam illo destituar Honoris & Majestatis portione di-gna Loco in quo me collocasti, qui es Exaltator Capitis mei & Salus mea.
units.tr: You, Lord, are the fountain of goodness and honour; you are clothed in surpassing majesty. Grant that I may at least in some measure share in your Excellence, in which you surpass all in wisdom, justice and mercy, and that I may not now be deprived of that portion of honour and majesty worthy of the place in which you have set me, you who are the exalter of my head and my salvation.

units.la: Duc me Domine tuâ Gratiâ ad eam veram solum & æternam Gloriam.
units.tr: Lead me, Lord, by your grace, to that true and eternal glory alone.

units.la: 22. Cum abiret Rex ab Oxonio & se ad Sco-tos reciperet.
units.tr: 22. When the King was leaving Oxford and retiring to the Scots.

units.la: QVanquàm tria mihi Regna Deus dederit, nullibi tamen locus restat, ubi jam tutum caput ( tuto simul Honore ) deponam. Ita enim ostendere volebat Deus se tutissimum esse perfugium, & arcem omnium munitissimam in qua oportet confidere.
units.tr: Although God has given me three kingdoms, nowhere is there left a place where I may now safely lay down my head (and my honour with it). For God wished to show that He is the safest refuge and the strongest fortress in which one ought to trust.

units.la: In his rerum angustiis non tam Homines quàm Deum respicio. Sic Illi visum est facere: atque adeò Me penitus & afflictas res meas in Illius misericordiam conjicio, cujus unius arbitrio manus omnium & corda imperantur.
units.tr: In these straits I look less to men than to God. It has seemed good to Him to act thus, and so I commit myself and my afflicted affairs wholly to His mercy, by whose sole decision the hands and hearts of all are ruled.

units.la: Quod viribus negat providentia, prudentiæ forsan orsan concedet. Advocata in consilium necessitas jubet ut incolumitati meæ prospiciam, lissimulato[?] me illinc habitu subducens ubi præcipuum robur supererat, ut eorum jam idem experiar qui has primùm Turbas inchoârunt; forte his tandem instrumentis usurus est Deus ad hæc omnia honorificè componenda.
units.tr: What providence denies to my strength, it will perhaps grant to my prudence. Necessity, called into council, bids me look to my own safety: by dissembling and withdrawing from here in a different guise, to where the chief strength still remained, so that I may now try the same thing as those who first began these tumults. Perhaps God will at last use these same instruments to bring all these matters to an honourable settlement.

units.la: Hæc fortè de illis fiducia exuet eos armis, & vincet: quòd me Illis sic ultrò crediderim, affectus eorum arctiùs astringet, qui ita crebrò profesi sunt non se in Me[?], sed pro Me pugnare.
units.tr: Perhaps this confidence will strip them of their arms and conquer them: since I have trusted myself to them so readily, it will bind their feelings more tightly, those who have so often professed that they did not fight against Me, but for Me.

units.la: Ænigma jam hoc explicandum est, & occasio illis offerenda quâ jam orbi testentur, non se ea quæ agunt, sed quæ dicunt, velle.
units.tr: This riddle must now be solved, and an opportunity must be offered to them by which they may now testify to the world that they wish not what they do, but what they say.

units.la: Deo verò hîc custode opus est, consilium-que & solatium à Conscientia meâ petendum. Tradam corpus licet in istorum manus, animam tamen Deo & mihi integram servare decrevi, nullâ unquam necessitate cogendus vel Honori meo renunciare, vel à Iudicio deflectere.
units.tr: Yet here I need God as my guardian, and I must seek counsel and comfort from my conscience. Although I will hand over my body into their hands, I have resolved to keep my soul whole for God and for myself, never to be forced by any necessity either to renounce my honour or to turn aside from my judgement.

units.la: Quod vi rapere volebant, jam his ultro donabitur, tam insolito genere præsidentiæ, ut jam merito pudore afficiantur, si id re non præstent quod debent, & quod verbis sunt sæpè protestati.
units.tr: What they wished to seize by force will now be given them freely, by such an unusual kind of protection that they will rightly be overcome with shame if they do not perform in deed what they ought, and what they have so often professed in words.

units.la: Haud enim Deo satis visum est, ut militari meo Robore ad me tuendum destituar, nisi eorum etiam Arma implorem, qui licet ex officio officiò me tueri debeant, adhuc tamen censentur in hostium numero.
units.tr: For God did not think it enough that I should be deprived of my military strength for my defence, unless I also implored the arms of those who, although by their office they ought to defend me, are still counted among the enemy.

units.la: Ita variæ sunt res humanæ, & in eo sæpè difficili Statu res Principum versatur, ut in quo collocant illi præsidium, ibi maximum subsit periculum, & quod credunt periculum in salutem vertatur.
units.tr: Human affairs are so varied, and the position of princes often turns on so difficult a state of affairs, that where they place their protection, there the greatest danger lies, and what they think is danger turns into safety.

units.la: Eo jam redactus sum, ut, qui strenuè meis Partibus hæserunt, sint à me relinquendi, ut ad Castra inimica confugiam: forsan hanc Pacis rationem fœlicius initurus, quàm illam Belli, quò & sanguinis effusio sistatur, & jam vulnera facta coalescant, dum sim interim haud perinde de Mea, quàm de Meorum incolumitate sollicitus, ut qui majora potius velim pericula tentare quàm constantem eorum Fidem extrema pati.
units.tr: I am now reduced to this: that those who have stuck to my side vigorously must be abandoned by me, so that I may flee to the enemy's camp. Perhaps I shall enter upon this course of peace more happily than that of war, so that the shedding of blood may be stopped and the wounds already made may close. Meanwhile I am not so anxious about my own safety as about the safety of my people, since I would rather undergo greater dangers than suffer their steadfast faith to be put to the last test.

units.la: Est & aliqua in lusitando peritia, scire jam vincere non posse, & maturè desinere, quàm frustra certare.
units.tr: There is also some skill in gambling: to know when one cannot now win, and to stop in good time rather than strive in vain.

units.la: Id jam summo studio agendum, ut Judicium meum amplius confirmem, simque juxta Ratione & Religione instructior; ne libertatem Animæ meæ simul tradere videar, aut Conscientiam illis mancipare, quos vel ab initio oportuerat Argumentis potiùs quàm Armis in hæc nova sua postulata Consensum meum exorasse.
units.tr: The thing to be done now, with the greatest care, is to strengthen my judgement further, and to be better instructed in reason and religion, lest I seem to surrender the freedom of my soul at the same time, or to hand over my conscience to those whom from the beginning it would have been right to win over to these new demands of theirs by arguments rather than by arms.

units.la: Nullus apud me (Deo gratias) successus fucum vero facit, aut fraudem, nec jam minus in hoc rerum articulo verba mea animo respondebunt, quàm si essent (prout Regis inter Subditos esse decuerat) plena pote-statis.
units.tr: No success, (thanks be to God), makes a false show of the truth or a fraud in my eyes; nor, in this crisis of affairs, will my words be any less in accord with my mind than if they were (as it became a King among his subjects) full of power.

units.la: Vis maxime Divina Ratio est: nunquam inopem Me virium putabo, dum hac integrē & liberē frui liceat. Nulla externa Fortunæ Eclipsis hac Me luce innatā fraudabit. Quicquid extra Deus negabit roboris, intus à Gratia Illius (uti spero) in constanti animo suppleb-itur, non ut negem præfractè quod concedi par est, sed ne quid ejusmodi concedam quod Ratio & Religio jubent negare.
units.tr: The greatest strength is the divine reason: I shall never think myself deprived of strength while I am allowed to enjoy this reason whole and free. No external eclipse of fortune will rob me of this light implanted in me. Whatever strength God denies me outwardly, He will make up inwardly through His grace, (as I hope) in a steadfast mind; not so that I may refuse stubbornly what it is right to grant, but so that I may not grant anything of such a kind that reason and religion bid me refuse.

units.la: Nec Me interim minorem factum existimabo, dum hanc Conscientiæ integritatem custodiam quæ Mihi sola Gemma superest digna servari.
units.tr: Nor, meanwhile, will I think myself made less, while I keep this integrity of conscience, which alone remains to me as a jewel worthy to be preserved.

units.la: O Tu Animarum Moderator Supreme, qui Conscientiis nostris solus imperas: licet ignorem quid agere debeam, oculos meos ad Te dirigo. In tutelam tuæ Misericordiæ me semper committo.
units.tr: O Thou Supreme Governor of souls, who alone rulest our consciences: although I do not know what I ought to do, I direct my eyes to Thee. I always commit myself to the protection of Thy mercy.

units.la: Quemadmodum Me servasti in die prælii, ita & adhuc potes vim Tuam in infirmitate mea ostendere.
units.tr: As Thou didst keep me in the day of battle, so still canst Thou show Thy power in my weakness.

units.la: Sis Tu mihi in nocte obscurissima Columna Ignis quâ illuminari simul possim & dirigi, & in die Tribulationis ferventissima sis Columna nubis Me inumbrans & protegens.
units.tr: Be Thou to me in the darkest night a pillar of fire, by which I may at the same time be enlightened and directed, and in the most fervent day of tribulation be a pillar of cloud, shading and protecting me.

units.la: Tu nosti (Domine) Me nulla penitus animi pervicacia sed justissimis argumentis persuasum, a Ratione, Honore, Religione dutis hæc & Capitis mei, & Pacis, & Incolumitatis periculum adiisse, ut Me iis opponerem qui hæc vi mihi extorquere voluerant.
units.tr: Thou knowest, O Lord, that I am by no means obstinate in mind, but persuaded by the most just arguments, drawn from reason, honour and religion, that I have undertaken this danger to my head, to peace and to safety, so that I might set myself against those who wished to extort these things from me by force.

units.la: Ne Tu justa sinas mentis meæ propositæ cum externo robore flaccescere: comitetur me usque Bona Conscientia in hac solitudine & derelictione.
units.tr: Do not allow, in Thy justice, the purpose of my mind to wither together with outward strength. Let a good conscience accompany me everywhere in this solitude and abandonment.

units.la: O ne prodam unquam Rationis meæ Facultatem, & illam Arcem Animæ meæ, quam Tu mihi tuendam credidisti.
units.tr: Oh, may I never betray the faculty of my reason, and that citadel of my soul which Thou hast entrusted to me to guard.

units.la: Deduc me super Semitas Iustitiæ, & ostende mihi salutare tuum. Fac ut placeant tibi Viæ meæ & tunc inimicos quoque convertes ad Paccm.
units.tr: Lead me along the paths of justice, and show me Thy salvation. Make my ways pleasing to Thee, and then Thou wilt also turn my enemies to peace.

units.la: 23. Cum Scoti Regem Anglis traderent, & de Custodia Holmbeiana.
units.tr: 23. When the Scots were handing the King over to the English, and concerning the custody of Holmby.

units.la: IN hoc tamen Scotos istos coram Mundo absolvo, quòd me haudquaquam fefellerint, nunquam enim Illis amplius quàm Hominibus pat est, credidi, siab iis divendardolet eos hoc maximè facere, & multò Serva-tore meo cariùs me æstimari.
units.tr: In this, however, I acquit these Scots before the world: they have not deceived me at all. I never trusted them more than men are to be trusted. Although I grieve that they were selling them, they did this most of all, and my Saviour valued me far more dearly than they did.

units.la: Sunt hæc alia insuper experimenta, quibus Deus Me voluit, Inconstantiam Humanam explorare, ut me penitiùs in se defigat nunquam Illos deserente qui in Ipsum crediderint; quassetur licet arundo Ægyptiaca subter volam illius cui innititur, Rupes tamen Israëlis in æternum manebit.
units.tr: There are also these other trials, by which God has willed to test human inconstancy, so that he may fix me more deeply in himself, never forsaking those who have believed in him. Although the Egyptian reed may be shaken by the hand of him on whom it leans, the Rock of Israel will remain forever.

units.la: Dei me jubet Providentia à cæteris omnibus ad seipsum confugere, ut in Illo Me fruar, qui Me nimis perdidi, cùm in aliis Spes extrà collocaverim.
units.tr: The providence of God bids me flee from all others to himself, so that I may enjoy him in whom I had too greatly lost myself, since I had placed my hopes outside him in others.

units.la: Soli jam & Captivo (eò enim jam redactus sum) satis otii superest quo de Mundi Vanitate, & Inconstantia cogitem.
units.tr: Now alone and captive (for to that I am now reduced), I have enough leisure left to think about the vanity and inconstancy of the world.

units.la: Id Deo expedire visum est, ut Me Uxore mea, Liberis, Exercitu, Amicis, & Libertate destituat, ut sim unicè Illius, qui est Unus Omnia.
units.tr: God has thought it expedient to deprive me of my wife, children, army, friends, and liberty, so that I may belong wholly to him who is the One who is All things.

units.la: Parvi refert inter Infælices numerari, modò Nigro Impiorum Catalogo inter Sacrilegos Principes non ascribar.
units.tr: It matters little to be counted among the unhappy, provided I am not written down in the black catalogue of the impious, among sacrilegious princes.

units.la: Nulla quæcunq; coarctatio animam meam illaqueabit, nec id unquam à Me impetrabitur, quo vel Hostibus meis insolentiam augeam, vel Amicis pudorem, vel Nomen meum reddam execrabile.
units.tr: No restraint whatever shall ensnare my soul, and this shall never be obtained from me: that I should increase the insolence of my enemies, or the shame of my friends, or make my name detestable.

units.la: Nihil est quod triumphent detento Corpore, cùm Ipse Animam retineam in nil adversus Conscientiam expugnari firmam.
units.tr: My enemies have nothing to triumph over, though my body is detained, since I myself keep my soul firm, so that nothing can be forced against my conscience.

units.la: Quod hi vocant Pertinaciam, id à Deo reputabitur honesta Conscientia, à qua Ratio non minus & Religio, quàm Honor meus vetat recedere.
units.tr: What these men call obstinacy, God will reckon as an honest conscience, from which reason and religion no less than my honour forbid me to withdraw.

units.la: Patet jam, haud ita in Pravos Confiliarior quam in Bonam Conscientiam huc usque pugnatum, nec illis unquam animum fuisse Me ad Parlamentum retrahere, quàm ad Ipsis prius obsequendum animum meum pertraxissent.
units.tr: It is now plain that the struggle has been waged not so much against wicked counsellors as against my good conscience. Nor was it ever their intention to draw me back to Parliament; rather they wished to have first drawn my mind into obedience to themselves.

units.la: Si quod petunt nonnulli concederem, effem[?] is profecto quem cupiunt, non eo Rex potior, sed & Homo & Christianus multo deterior.
units.tr: If I were to grant what some are asking, I would indeed be the man they desire, not a better king by that, but also a much worse man and Christian.

units.la: Quod Turbae & Arma non poterant, numquam à Me impetrabit Captivitas æquè cum illis intuta Principi, sed non magis formidanda.
units.tr: What crowds and arms could not do, captivity will never obtain from me. It is equally unsafe for a prince, but no more to be feared.

units.la: Nulla mihi nassa fiet metus hominum, nec animam impediet Libertatis amor. Præstat enim ab aliis quàm ab Me ipso prodi, & ut Libertatis lytron Conscientia persolvat; quod enim mihi maximè cupiunt facere Inimici injurium, sine meo consensu non pos-sunt.
units.tr: Fear of men will be no snare for me, and love of liberty will not hold back my soul. For it is better to be betrayed by others than by myself, and let conscience pay the ransom of liberty [λύτρον]. What my enemies most desire to do to me, they cannot do wrongfully without my consent.

units.la: Dum id integrum solum habeam cum Ratione[?] negare, maximam eorum malitiam frustrabor, qui nec rectè uti sciunt quæ jam olim concesseram, nec quid aliud à Me postulare, quàm ut in Meam & Meorum perniciem operam meam velim commodare.
units.tr: While I keep that whole power, to deny with reason, I shall frustrate the great malice of those who know neither how to use rightly what I long ago granted, nor to ask anything else of me than that I should be willing to lend my efforts to my own and my people's ruin.

units.la: Immo etiamsi Me interimant, faxo, nulla erit causa cur contemnant, nec mihi tanti Libertas & vita ipsa, quanti pax Conscientiæ cum Coronæ meæ Honore & Salute Populi conjunctaꝫ queis sim uno forsan Verbo magis nociturus, quàm quæcunque Belli mala: dum, ut paucis indulgeatur, cunctos pessundem[?].
units.tr: Indeed, even if they kill me, I will see to it that there is no cause for them to despise me. Liberty and life itself are not so dear to me as the peace of conscience joined with the honour of my crown and the welfare of my people. With one word I might perhaps do more harm than whatever evils of war there are, provided that so that a few may be indulged, I do not ruin all.

units.la: Reviviscent (Deo juvante) Leges nostræ, & cum iis Subditorum Meorum obsequium & amor, modò ne Meo Consensu sepeliantur eo Probri & Injustitiæ Tumulo, qui à nonnullorum violentia effoditur.
units.tr: Our laws will revive (God helping), and with them the obedience and love of my subjects, provided they are not buried by my consent in that tomb of reproach and injustice which is dug open by the violence of some.

units.la: Si non aliàs hæc liceat redimere quàm Libertatis meæ aut Mortis pretio, en Me ultro paratum dependere.
units.tr: If these things cannot be redeemed in any other way than at the price of my liberty or my death, behold, I am ready to pay it of my own accord.

units.la: Nulla fors Regi verè calamitosa, quæ secum Animæ Ipsius & Populi & Posterorum servitutem non trahit.
units.tr: No misfortune is truly calamitous for a king that does not bring with it the slavery of his own soul, of the people, and of posterity.

units.la: Cernent forsan futura sæcula in quod præsens ultrò amat cæcutire: & ostendet Deus aliquando Populo meo, Me pro Illis potiùs optâsse, quàm cum Illis pati; etiamsi plane constaret Me in eorum servitutem assentientem posse in aliquam libertatem restituì, satius duco unum Regem vel de extremis periclitari, quàm tot in Eos Tyrannos confirmare: quod Deus avertat, quicquid de Me facturus est, qui Me in solitudine meâ solum esse nosse finit.
units.tr: Perhaps future ages will see what the present loves to be blind to. God will someday show my people that I preferred to suffer for them rather than with them. Even if it were quite certain that by consenting to their servitude I could be restored to some liberty, I think it better that one king be endangered at the extremes than that so many be confirmed as tyrants over them. God forbid this; whatever he is going to do with me, he who allows me to know that I am alone in my solitude.

units.la: Tu enim (Domine) infinite Bonus & Magnus semper mecum es, cujus potior vita præsentia est, & cui servire Libertas consummatissima. Agnosce Me Famulum Tuum, nec jam querar amissam libertatem Christiano & Homine & Rege dignam.
units.tr: For you, Lord, are infinitely good and great, always with me; your presence is a better life, and to serve you is the most perfect liberty. Acknowledge me as your servant, and I shall no longer complain of the lost liberty, which is worthy of a Christian, a man, and a king.

units.la: Tua tamen usque Benedictione adsit Ratio mihi ut homini, ut Christiano Religio, & constans cura, ut Regi, Iustitiæ.
units.tr: Yet may your blessing always be with me: may reason be present to me as a man, religion as a Christian, and constant care for justice as a king.

units.la: Cæteris licet omnibus ornamentis externis dispoliari permiscris, maneant illa semper salva per quæ Te fruor, & quæ eripi mihi invito non possunt.
units.tr: Though you permit me to be stripped of all external ornaments, may those things always remain safe through which I enjoy you, and which cannot be taken from me against my will.

units.la: Nullo Igne afflictionum efferuescant ullæ animi perturbationes, ut in iræ impotentiam, aut spurcos metus ebulliant. Multi dicunt non est Salus Ipse in Deo Suo, Leva Signum super Me, nempe lucem vultus tui, nec iam amplius Libertate, nec Salute, nec Maiestate indigebo.
units.tr: Let no fire of afflictions make any disturbance of the mind boil over into the impotence of anger or into base fears. Many say, "There is no salvation for him in his God." Lift up the light of your countenance upon me; then I shall lack no more liberty, salvation, or majesty.

units.la: Illum mihi Constantiæ des, & Patientiæ mo-dum, quem præsens mea Conditio desiderat.
units.tr: Grant me that measure of constancy and patience which my present condition requires.

units.la: Robur meum dissipatur, Spes ab hominibus destituitur, ipse Captivus detineor, O ne elongaveris Domine, ne Inimicus meus nimium contra Me invalescat.
units.tr: My strength is wasted, hope is taken from me by men, and I am held captive myself. O Lord, do not go far away, lest my enemy grow too strong against me.

units.la: Tanquam prodigium factus sum multis, Tu adjutor fortis & asylum prævalidum
units.tr: I have become a wonder to many, but you are a strong helper and a most mighty refuge.

units.la: Fac mecum Signum in bonum, ut videant qui oderunt Me & confundantur, quoniam Tu Domine adjuvisti Me & consolatus es Me. Spiritu principali confirma Me, ut & faciam voluntatem Tuam, & patiar quod tibi placuerit.
units.tr: Make a sign of good with me, so that those who hate me may see and be confounded, because you, Lord, have helped me and comforted me. Confirm me with a princely spirit, so that I may both do your will and bear whatever has pleased you.

units.la: Miserere mei Deus quoniam in Te confidit anima mea, & in umbra alarum tuarum sperabo[?] donec transeat iniquitas.
units.tr: Have mercy on me, O God, for my soul trusts in you, and in the shadow of your wings I shall hope until iniquity passes by.

units.la: Exurge Domine, eripe Me, ne longè facias miserationes tuas à Me. Etiamsi Me occidas, in tua tamen Misericordia & Servatoris mei meritis confidam.
units.tr: Arise, O Lord, deliver me; do not put your mercies far from me. Even if you kill me, I will still trust in your mercy and in the merits of my Saviour.

units.la: Scio quod Redemptor meus vivit: Et si ambulavero per vallem umbrae mortalis, nihil mali timebo.
units.tr: I know that my Redeemer lives, and if I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil.

units.la: 24. Cūm Regi sui Sacellani interdicerentur.
units.tr: 24. When the King's Own Chaplains Were Forbidden to Him.

units.la: CUm sic Dei Providentiae visum fuerit Me Civilibus Solatiis, & caetero omni famulatu orbare, nulla re commodius arbitrabar omnium posse absentiam supleri, quàm Sacellanorum meorum Contubernio; quos & ob munus suum revereor, & ob fidem diligo: Horum enim doctrinâ pietate & precibus Me sic melius sperabam potuisse tum incommoda caetera tolerare, tum in futuram meorum restitutionem, & sanctiorem usum praeparari, dum adjutus horum pietate spiritualem messem Gratiae inter tribulos & spinas, & post duram Afflictionum Arationem perciperem.
units.tr: Since it had seemed good to God's providence to deprive me of civil comforts and every other kind of service, I judged that nothing could better make up for all these absences than the company of my chaplains, whom I revere for their office and love for their faith. I hoped that through their teaching, piety and prayers I could bear my other hardships better, and be prepared for my future restoration and a holier use of it, while, aided by their piety, I might reap a spiritual harvest of grace among briars and thorns, and after the hard ploughing of afflictions.

units.la: Nunquam sanè mihi magis necessaria fuerat nec expetita magis,opera eorum & auxilium, qui Pietatem cum Iudicio & Religionem cum mente sana conjunxerant.
units.tr: Never indeed had the work and help of those who joined piety with judgement and religion with a sound mind been more necessary to me, or more desired.

units.la: Quâ me clauserunt solitudo ad cæteras meas Tentationes ut Desertum accedit: quos enim mihi obtrudunt Comites quâvis sunt solitudine tristiores.
units.tr: The solitude in which I am shut up adds to my other temptations like a desert; for the companions they force on me are sadder than any solitude.

units.la: Jam si mea Vectigalia aut Jus Militiæ, vel Regnorum aliquod postulâssem, haud mirarer denegantes quod illa improba Politice ideo vetat restitui, ne hoc facto faterentur se injuste usurpasse: Cum vero Sacellanorum meorum Spirituale mihi solatium abnuerint, durius mecum & inhumanius actum videtur, quàm quod unquam à Christianis factum est, vel in infimæ sortis vinctos, vel maximorum facinorum reos; qui, etiamsi Legis severitate aliis vitæ commodis priventur, tamen Religionis misericordiâ, beneficio fruuntur Cleri sui, ut quæ simul nolit Corpora perimi, & Animas damnari.
units.tr: Now if I had asked for my revenues or my right of military service, or for some of my kingdoms, I would hardly be surprised that they refused, since shrewd policy forbids restoring such things, lest by doing so they admit they had unjustly usurped them. But since they have denied me the spiritual comfort of my chaplains, I think I am being treated more harshly and inhumanly than Christians have ever treated anyone, even men held in the lowest rank of prisoners or guilty of the greatest crimes. Though by the severity of the law these are deprived of other comforts of life, yet by the mercy of religion they enjoy the benefit of their own clergy, since it does not wish both bodies to be destroyed and souls to be damned.

units.la: At neque hoc mihi permissum in angore meo, ut à quocunque Bono Angelo sustenter; (Is enim mihi jure optimo videtur Doctus Pius & Prudens Theologus, quales certe Meos omnes exopto.)
units.tr: But I am not even permitted, in my anguish, to be sustained by any good angel; (for he seems to me, with the best right, a learned, pious and prudent theologian, such as I certainly wish all my men to be.)

units.la: Quibus prius dividiæ erat Me Regem esse, jam molestum est esse Christianum; ita me omnibus quærunt spoliare, quasi id etiam verentur ne vel Salva mihi Anima superesset.
units.tr: Before, it was a matter of dispute whether I was king; now it is a trouble to be a Christian. So they seek to despoil me of everything, as if they feared that even a saved soul might be left to me.

units.la: Nulla Charitas clementius interpretari potest tam præfracte negatum postulatum æquissimum, ut mihi nonnulli è Sacellanis adessent.
units.tr: No charity could interpret more kindly so stubbornly refused a most reasonable request, that some of my chaplains might be present with me.

units.la: Cogitabam hoc mecum aliquando, ideo forsan ab Illis (licet parum Christianè) negatum, quòd ægrè ferrent Me meos Theologos suis Ministris ante ponere, quos (licet alias forsan virtute & pietate laudabiles) haud tamen rebar idoneos qui remedia mihi in præsens aut solatia adhiberent, quorum quidem nonnulli magna harum Calamitatum Causa, & vulnerum meorum extiterunt.
units.tr: I sometimes thought to myself that perhaps they refused this (though not very Christianly) because they were vexed that I put my own theologians before their ministers; whom (though perhaps praiseworthy in other respects for virtue and piety) I did not think fit to apply remedies or comforts to me for the present. Some of them indeed have been a great cause of these calamities and of my wounds.

units.la: Quin etiam inter eorum Saniores nodum ea in Sacris unanimitas & conjunctio Cordium exspectanda est quam in ejusmodi officiis mecum unâ & pro Me peragendis, vehementer desidero; cùm eorum plærique, Judiciis vel à meò diversis, vel in meum suspiciosis, vel omninò adversantibus, haud unquam eo concentu harmonico (qui maximè in precibus & cæteris Sacris requiritur, ut cum fructu præstemus) vel cum meo sint Spiritu vel cum eorum Ipse, concordaturi. Aurea enim hic Regula & Perfectionis Vinculum in illo mutuo amoris & charitatis consistit.
units.tr: Indeed, even among the wiser of them I earnestly long for that agreement and union of hearts in sacred matters which should be expected in such duties performed with me and for me. For most of them, with judgements either different from mine, or suspicious of mine, or altogether hostile, will never agree in that harmonious accord (which is especially required in prayers and other sacred acts, if we are to perform them with fruit), either with my spirit or with their own. For here the golden rule and the bond of perfection consist in that mutual love and charity.

units.la: Sunt Remedia nonnulla pejora morbis, & plane consolatores ejusmodi major ipsa calamitas, cum (velut amici illi Iob) non confirmare animum patientiâ studeant, sed eò velint perducere, ut repudiatâ & proditâ Innocentiâ suâ de Divina Misericordia desperet, & juste laras [?] agnoscendo eorum injurias, confirmet insolentium inimicorum manus, & corda magis faciat indurari.
units.tr: Some remedies are worse than the diseases, and such consolers are a greater calamity than the calamity itself. For, like those friends of Job, they do not strive to strengthen the mind by patience, but want to lead it to the point where, rejecting and betraying its own innocence, it despairs of divine mercy; and, as if justly acknowledging their injuries, it strengthens the hands of insolent enemies and makes hearts harder.

units.la: Ita valde faveo Ecclesiasticis ( qui in se dignum quid habent tanto munere ) ut hac causa praecipuè rem meam in discrimen adduxerim, quod pertinaci conscientia in tuendo iis Jura sua perstiterim, quos, quò magis ut pupillos intuebar sub Sacrilegis oculis constitutos saevorum & rapacium Reformatorum, eo ampliùs ex officio meo ducebam. Patrem Me & Patronum Illis pariter & Ecclesiae praestare, quanquam malè mihi à nonnullis haec gratia rependitur, in ea forsan tempora victuris, quibus non minùs de mea calamitate, quàm de ingrato suo errore serio doleant, luantque contumelias illas & parvipendium, cui & se & ordinem suum fecerunt obnoxium.
units.tr: So I greatly favour churchmen (who have something worthy in themselves for so great an office), and for this cause in particular I have put my affairs in peril, because with stubborn conscience I persisted in defending their rights. The more I regarded them as orphans placed under the sacrilegious eyes of savage and rapacious Reformers, the more I felt bound by my office to act as a Father and Patron to them and to the Church alike. Though this favour is badly repaid to me by some, who in times to come, when they will be alive, will grieve no less over their own serious error than over my calamity, and will lament those insults and that disparagement to which they have made both themselves and their order liable.

units.la: Hos interim omnes miserëor , sperno neminem: id saltem credebam merito mihi potuisse indulgeri, ut eos mihi peculiares adsciscerem, qui & Judicio meo probatissimi erant, & Sententiæ maximè conformes. Quod cùm non impetraretur, multo potius duxi (etiam cum aliqua Impietatis suspicione) nullis Precibus interesse, quàm simulare Me eorum participem quibus nec Cor meum adstipulari, nec lingua potest respondere AMEN, nisi Intellectui meo prorsus obluctari, & in animam meam velim mentiri.
units.tr: Meanwhile I pity all of them; I despise none. I thought at least I could rightly have been granted this, that I might take as my own those who were most approved by my judgement and most in agreement with my opinion. Since this was not obtained, I thought it much better (even with some suspicion of impiety) to take part in no prayers at all, than to pretend to share in those to which neither my heart can agree nor my tongue respond AMEN, unless I struggled altogether against my understanding and wished to lie to my own soul.

units.la: Prorsus in Sacris hujusmodi & Solennibus Officiis nec profana mihi placet audacia, nec insulsa, & sensu destituta pietas, sed eo judicio & humilitate & gravitate peragi, quâ se supplex demonstret, & de Dei Majestate, & de Ecclesiæ Honore sollicitum, tum & suam Vilitatem cogitasse, atque illud etiam non ignorasse, vel quid fas à Deo peti, vel quo modo Peccatorem decet Divinam Misericordiam pro seipso & aliis implorare.
units.tr: Indeed, in sacred and solemn offices of this kind, neither profane boldness nor a silly piety devoid of sense pleases me. They should be carried out with that judgement, humility and gravity by which a man shows himself a suppliant, anxious about God's majesty and the Church's honour, and mindful of his own lowliness, and not ignorant either of what is fitting to ask of God, or of how a sinner ought to implore divine mercy for himself and others.

units.la: Juxta omnes illæ Preces offendunt, in quibus aliquid protervius, rusticius, perturbatius auditur; cum hic absit necesse vel humilitas in Deum, vel in homines charitas, vel quæ ipsi officio reverentia debetur.
units.tr: So all those prayers offend in which anything more insolent, rustic or disorderly is heard; for there is lacking either the necessary humility before God, or charity towards men, or the reverence due to the office itself.

units.la: Fateor mihi magis arridere, ut meditatas probe, & studio adlaboratas Conciones, ita eas Precum Formas Publicas, quæ tum Ecclesiarum, tum Christiani cujusvis necessitati magis sunt consentaneæ, quia in his multo exploratius habeo quibus Cor meum debeo adjungere, quàm in cujusquam extemporanea Facultate licuerit, quam quidem ut minimè interdictam velim publica occasione exigente, ita liberrimè tunc posse exerceri censeo in privatis illis nostris secessibus, ubi nec officii solennitas, nec verecundus aliorum respectus tantum in ritu exteriori curā desiderat: quanquam lux Intellectus & Affectuum fervor sint illa maximè necessaria in Sacris omnibus Officiis, sive sint illa Solennia, seu ex occasione nata, solitaria, vel cum aliis conjuncta.
units.tr: I confess I am more pleased by sermons carefully meditated and diligently worked out, and likewise by public forms of prayer, which suit the needs of the Churches and of any Christian better. For in these I have much more certain knowledge of what I ought to join my heart to, than the extemporary ability of any man could give. I would not wish such ability to be forbidden at all when public occasion demands it, but I think it may be exercised most freely then in those private retreats of ours, where neither the solemnity of office nor the respect due to others requires care for outward ritual alone. Yet the light of understanding and the fervour of the affections are most necessary in all sacred offices, whether they are solemn or arise from an occasion, whether they are solitary or joined with others.

units.la: Æqui interim homines existimabunt Me eâdem prorsus ratione Sacellanos Meos Eorum Ministris prætulisse, quâ Liturgiam præfero Directorio. In illa semper eductus, & exercitatus fui; in hoc nondum initiatus, & plane novus. Quod tametsi melius callerem, haud unquam Illius ductu (tanquam certa ulla Regula & precum Canone) persequi liceret aut investigare devias eorum aberrationes extra omnem semitam & regulam, qui huic ita praeclaro instituto & inprimis utili applaudunt; quanquam & jam etiam a plurimis sperni coepit & obsolescere, non secus ac illæ Preces nostræ publicæ, ab iis maxime fastiditæ, quorum magna pars pietatis in illa Plebi gratissimo maledicentiæ argumento versatur, ut debacchentur scilicet in Liturgiam & Regimen Ecclesiæ & exponant (quæ possunt) ludibrio. Mihi potius denuncietur Væ foli, quam illud audiam horrendum Væ vobis Hypocritis, quod quidem merito formidarem, si quæ corde respuo, ea precibus expetere simularem:
units.tr: Fair-minded men will judge that I preferred my chaplains to their ministers for the same reason that I prefer the Liturgy to the Directory. I have always been brought up and trained in that; in this I am not yet initiated, and am quite new to it. Although I might know it better, I could never, under its guidance (as under some certain rule and canon of prayer), track down the wayward aberrations of those who applaud this so excellent and especially useful institution, straying outside every path and rule. Yet it is already beginning to be despised and to fall into disuse by very many, no differently from our public prayers, which are most scorned by those a large part of whose piety consists in that topic of slander most pleasing to the common people, so that they rage against the Liturgy and the government of the Church and expose them (as far as they can) to ridicule. Let rather the Woe to the lonely be pronounced upon me, than that I hear that dreadful Woe unto you, Hypocrites, which I would rightly fear if I pretended to seek by prayers the things I spurn in my heart:

units.la: Forte nonnulli eorum arbitrantur Me satisfungi posse Sacerdotis erga Deum officio, licet Principis nequaquam in homines.
units.tr: Perhaps some of them think that I can fulfil the priestly duty towards God, though by no means the princely duty towards men.
