units.la: Vtrunque sane Munus (non nego) Regium pariter & Sacerdotale eidem bene posse Personæ competere, quemadmodum etiam antiquitus sub eodem prorsus Nomine Juri Primogenituræ connexa erant. Potiores quos imitarer non habui, quam illos Reges inclytos David & Salomonem, non Corona & Sceptro illustriores, quam piis Psalmis, & Divinis Parabolis; unde hic Ecclesiastæ nomen obtinet, ille meruit Prophetæ appellari: Tituli revera multo ampliores (ubi digne collocantur) quam quoscunque Romani Imperatores à devitiis Gentibus ufurparunt ; cum fit longè Gloriosius Verbo Animas hominum ad Ecclesiam Dei convertere, quam Eos Gladio subigere in servitutem.
units.tr: I do not deny that both the royal and the priestly office can well belong to the same person, as anciently under the very same name they were joined to the right of primogeniture. I had no more notable models to imitate than those famous kings David and Solomon, no more illustrious for crown and sceptre than for pious Psalms and divine Parables. Hence the one obtained the name Ecclesiastes, and the other deserved to be called a Prophet. These titles are truly far greater (when rightly bestowed) than any the Roman emperors have usurped from conquered nations, since it is far more glorious to convert men's souls to the Church of God by the Word than to subdue them to servitude by the sword.

units.la: Cùm verò (ita Dei Providentiâ ordinante) Regum ferè semper fuerint & Sacerdotum munera Ecclesiastarum quoque & Principum tam in Judaicis quàm Christianis Ecclesiis discriminata, dolet Me in id necessitatis devenisse, ut vel idem sim mihi utrumque, vel neutris fruar.
units.tr: Since (by God's providence so ordaining) the offices of churchmen and of princes have almost always been kept distinct, both in the Jewish and in the Christian churches, it grieves me that I have been brought to such a necessity that I must either be both of these to myself or enjoy neither.

units.la: Qui enim Regiâ Me Potestate & Dominatu spoliant, non minori violentiâ adnituntur, ut Sacramentis, Precibus, Concionibus (vel per plurimos Menses) interdicat, ni mihi Ipse fiam Sacellanus.
units.tr: For those who strip me of royal power and lordship press no less violently that I be denied the sacraments, prayers and sermons (for many months at a time), unless I myself become my own chaplain.

units.la: Clerum certè cùm (ut Rex Christianus) tutari debeam ita ab Illis vicissim Donorum suorum & Orationum beneficium exspecto, quas ideò meis & aliorum efficacius reor valituras, quòd à mentibus magis illuminatis, & minùs turbido affectu fluunt, quàm eorum fermè solent qui negotiis sæculi implicantur. Porrò hæc æstimandum est acceptiora officia, & majori benedictionum incremento cumulari, quæ sunt rite peracta, & Muneris illius præscripto, ad quod à Deo & Ecclesia peculiari modo designantur nonnulli, & consecrantur.
units.tr: Since I ought, as a Christian king, to protect the clergy, so in turn I look for the benefit of their gifts and prayers. I think these will avail more effectively for me and for others because they flow from minds more enlightened and from an affection less clouded than is usually the case with those who are caught up in the affairs of this age. Moreover, those services are to be judged more acceptable, and are heaped with a greater increase of blessings, which are duly performed according to the prescription of that office, for which certain men are specially designated and consecrated by God and the Church.

units.la: Licet enim quoad sensum latiorem Spiritualis Regiminis, (quo quævis pia Anima Christi subjicitur, & per Illius merita quotidiè se & Cultum suum in Oblationem Deo sistit) unusquisque Fidelium, & Rex & Sacerdos dici Possit ( cùm Regali Sacerdotio induatur ) Si tamen Ordinem Ecclesiasticum & Externam Politiam specteimus, æquè certò secutura est Religionis confusio, si quisque partes Ecclesiae aut Sacerdotis agat, quàm foret in ea Republica ubi omnes Regnum ambirent.
units.tr: For although, in the wider sense of spiritual rule (to which every pious soul is subject in Christ, and through His merits daily presents itself and its worship to God as an offering), every one of the faithful may be called both king and priest (since he is clothed with a royal priesthood), yet if we look to the ecclesiastical order and the external polity, confusion in religion will certainly follow if everyone takes on the parts of the Church or of the priest, just as it would in a commonwealth where everyone aspired to the kingdom.

units.la: Ego multo modestioribus Principiis, & (ut opinor) piis magis innutritus sum: coscius impotentiæ meæ Spiritualis, eò impensius æstimo & desidero omnia illa pietatis subsidia quæ mihi à sanctis & probis Ministris ( sive illi Episcopi sint seu Presbyteri ) administrari possunt in his angustiis, in quas (Deo permittente) ita à Subditis meis sum redactus, ut nil sit amplius quod eripiatur præter vitam residuum, nec mihi ultra quicquam expectendum, (in quo minùs atbitrabar vel offensam eorum, vel suspicionem irritare qui mihi hoc tàm districtè negarunt) quàm ut aliquod mihi saltem in Animae meae levamen, & solatium suppeteret.
units.tr: I have been brought up on much more modest principles, and (as I think) more pious ones. Conscious of my spiritual weakness, I value and desire all the more eagerly those aids of piety which can be administered to me by holy and upright ministers (whether they be bishops or presbyters) in these straits to which I have been reduced by my subjects, God permitting, so that nothing remains to be taken from me except my remaining life, and nothing more is left for me to expect. (In this I thought I would not provoke either their offence or their suspicion, since they have so strictly denied me this), except that at least some relief and comfort for my soul might be available to me.

units.la: In hunc enim finem Illos nominavi, quorum vita probro omni (quod sciam) vacua, tum Doctrina & Pietas non minùs, quàm in Me Fides perspecta, adversus quos nihil est quod objiciant, nisi forsan quod sint maximè idonei, studiisque in Me nimium propensi.
units.tr: For I have named those men for this purpose: men whose lives, so far as I know, are free from all reproach, and whose learning and piety are no less well proved than their fidelity towards me. Against them they have nothing to object, except perhaps that they are very well qualified and too inclined towards me in their zeal.

units.la: Sed neque hæc prima opera est (licet omnium præcipua) quâ ab illis coactus sine aliorum Ministerio defungor, quanquam ægrius Me fatear Sacellanis meis quàm cæteró omni Famulitio carere, quodque mihi ab Vxoris & Liberorum divortio proximus certe (imo major in nonnullis) dolor, cùm ab his plus forsan humanis affectibus indulgeatur[?] in praesens, Illi in Gratiae Caelestis incrementum prosint.
units.tr: But this is not the first task (though it is the chief of all) by which I am compelled by them to go without ministry from others. Yet I confess that I am more grieved to lack my chaplains than to lack every other service. And the sorrow of separation from my wife and children is certainly close to this (indeed greater in some respects), since, at present, those things are perhaps indulged too much in human affections, while they may serve to increase heavenly grace.

units.la: Hoc Me solatur, quod his Mediis Ordina-rius necessariò destitutos solet Deus Donis suis & Gratiâ extraordinario quodam modo supplere.
units.tr: This consoles me: that God is accustomed to supply, by His gifts and in some extraordinary manner by His grace, those who are necessarily deprived of these ordinary means.

units.la: Si Me Spiritus illius erudire & infirmitates meas (quod spero) adjuvare voluerit orantis, legentis, meditantis, haud jam alio Oratore aut Doctore opus.
units.tr: If His Spirit will be pleased to teach me and (as I hope) to help my weaknesses while I pray, read and meditate, there will be no need of any other speaker or teacher.

units.la: Ad Te igitur, Deus Meus, has jam Preces meas solitarias dirigo: quod alienae opis deest per immediatam tui Spiritus assistentiam supple, qui & tenebras meas solum illustrare potest, & excitare torporem.
units.tr: To You therefore, my God, I now direct these my solitary prayers: supply by the immediate assistance of Your Spirit what is lacking of another's help, who alone can both illuminate my darkness and rouse my sluggishness.

units.la: O Tu Sol Iustitiae Sacer Fons Caelestis Lucis & Ardoris, Clarifica cor meum & accende, docens Me simul, & pro Me intercedens. In Te Omnis Plenitudo, A Te Omnis abundantia; Per Te Omnis acceptatio, Tu mihi in societatem, in solatium sufficis. Tu Rex meus es, esto mihi & Propheta, & Sacerdos Regas Me, erudias Me, pro Me precare, & mihi semper praesens sis.
units.tr: O You Sun of Righteousness, holy fountain of heavenly light and warmth, enlighten and kindle my heart, teaching me at the same time and interceding for me. In You is all fullness, from You all abundance; through You all acceptance. You are sufficient for me as my fellowship and my comfort. You are my King; be to me also Prophet and Priest. Rule me, teach me, pray for me, and be always present to me.

units.la: Valuit olim in Te colluctatio Jacob in illo Sacro duello, cùm nemo esset praeter Te qui assisteret. Tu Illum roborc[?] donasti quo Te vincere, & grata quadam violentia benedictionem à Te ex-torquerct.
units.tr: Once Jacob's wrestling prevailed with You in that holy contest, when there was no one beside You to help. You gave him strength by which he might overcome You, and by a certain pleasing violence he wrung a blessing from You.

units.la: O respicias Me Famulum Tuum (pro infinita[?] tua Misericordia) olim satis felicem conjunctis illis omnium & sociatis precibus, quarum fervor affectionum mearum in Te frigus accenderet, cum ad Domum Tuam simul veniremus, simul in illa convenieremus, voce jubili & laetitia adorantes Te in unitate Spirituum, & in Vinculo Pacis.
units.tr: O look upon me, Your servant (in Your infinite mercy), who once was happy enough when we joined together in the common and united prayers of all, whose fervour would kindle the coldness of my affections towards You, when we came together to Your house, and met there together, adoring You with a voice of joy and gladness, in the unity of the Spirits and in the bond of peace.

units.la: O ignoscas mihi omissas occasiones felices, vel in quod bonum oportuit, minus adhibitas.
units.tr: O pardon me the happy occasions I let slip, or used less than I ought, for good.

units.la: Iam voluntate tua factum est, ut sim velut Pelicanus in deserto, vel Passer Solitarius in tecto, vel ut pruna quaedam dispersa & disjecta ab illis simul congestis scintillationibus & mutua pietatis effervescentia, qua ille Sacer Ignis Gratiarum tuarum accenderetur melius in Ara cordis mei, tum aleretur magis & augesceret, ut hinc Precum Sacrificia, & thymiamata laudum ad te debitae oblationes ascenderent.
units.tr: Now by Your will it has come about that I am like a pelican in the wilderness, or a lonely sparrow on the housetop, or like a live coal scattered and cast away from those sparks gathered together by them and from the mutual warmth of piety, by which that holy fire of Your graces would be kindled more fully on the altar of my heart, and then fed and grown more, so that from there the sacrifices of prayers and the incense of praises, offerings due to You, might rise up.

units.la: Sed O Tu qui non conteris calamum quassatum & linum fumigans non extinguis, ne aspernetris illam precum mearum infirmitatem, & has animae meae suppressiones in hac aerumnosa solitudine, ad quas jam Me necessario adigunt, qui sic ( nulla charitate ) ea negant subsidia, quaeis[?] vehementer egeo, nec minus desidero.
units.tr: But O You who do not break the bruised reed nor quench the smoking flax, do not despise this weakness of my prayers and these suppressions of my soul in this wretched solitude, to which those who thus deny (with no charity) the aids which I greatly need and desire no less, now necessarily drive me.

units.la: Sit O Cordium istorum duritiei[?] mihi tantum occasio qua erga Te magis, & pro illis emolliar. Accendatur per illorum odia meum amor, & iniquissima spretione[?] pii desiderii preces meae ad Te magis excitentur: Surdi cum sint isti & inexorabiles Tu mihi aurem propterea magis advertas, qui es Deus exorari facilis, non aggravata est auris[?] tua ut non possit, nec cor durum ut nolit audire, nec manus abbreviata, ut salvare nequeat Me supplicem tuum desolatum.
units.tr: Let the hardness of those hearts be to me only an occasion of turning more towards You, and of being softened for them. Let my love be kindled by their hatreds, and let my prayers of pious desire be more stirred up towards You by their most unjust scorn. Since they are deaf and inexorable, may You therefore turn Your ear to me all the more, for You are a God easily entreated. Your ear is not so heavy that it cannot hear, nor is Your heart so hard that it is unwilling to listen, nor is Your hand so shortened that it cannot save me, Your desolate suppliant.

units.la: Tu Me ab hominibus permisisti externis illis mediis privari in Ecclesia tua à Te institutis, haud vero me illa prohibent Internæ Gratiæ communione, quam tu Cordibus humilium solus inspiras.
units.tr: You have allowed me to be deprived by men of those outward means instituted by You in Your Church, but those means do not hinder me from the communion of inward grace, which You alone breathe into the hearts of the humble.

units.la: O Me talem efficias, & jam (nullus dubito) docebis Me, exaudies Me, adjuvabis Me. Cor enim contritum & humiliatum Deus non despicies.
units.tr: O make me such a one, and (I doubt not) You will now teach me, hear me, help me. For God will not despise a broken and humbled heart.

units.la: Tu Me (Domine) una opera potes & Templum tibi & Sacerdotem, Victimamque & Altare efficere, dum à Corde humili Solitarius inter Sacras Meditationes, Preces fervidus, & non ficitas lachrimas Me quotidie tibi sistam Oblationem, qui Me tibi preparas, in Me habitas, & à Me dignaris accipere.
units.tr: You, O Lord, can by one work make me both a temple for You and a priest, both victim and altar, while, solitary among the holy meditations, fervent in prayers, and shedding unfeigned tears from a humble heart, I present myself to You daily as an offering. You who prepare me for Yourself, dwell in me, and deign to accept me from me.

units.la: Tu secretis (Domine) reparationibus, & miraculosa infusione effecisti, ut pugillum farinæ non deficeret Viduæ, nec Lecythus olei imminucretur durante illa Fame & Siccitate.
units.tr: By secret restorations and a miraculous infusion, O Lord, You caused the handful of flour not to fail the widow, nor the jar of oil to be diminished, during that famine and drought.

units.la: O Animam meam intuearis, nunc quasi Viduam quandam desertam & desolatam: Ne Salvificæ istæ Veritates quas jam antea addidici è memoria mea elabantur, nec illæ dulces Spiritus Tui effusiones quas aliquando sensi, desituant Cor Meum in hac fame ordinarii illius salubris alimenti quo Anima mea reficeretur.
units.tr: Look upon my soul, now like a widow forsaken and desolate. Let not those saving truths which I learned before slip from my memory, nor those sweet outpourings of Your Spirit which I once felt, cease to nourish my heart in this famine of that ordinary wholesome food by which my soul was refreshed.

units.la: Quod tamen malim sustinere quam ab eorum manu pabulari, qui panem meum miscent cineribus & vinum felle, qui Me torquent potius quàm docent, & quorum ora in acerba convitia, quàm in amicas preces, promptiora.
units.tr: Yet I would rather endure this than be fed by the hand of those who mix my bread with ashes and my wine with gall, who torment me rather than teach me, and whose mouths are readier for bitter reproaches than for friendly prayers.

units.la: Tu (Domine Veritatis) nosti, quàm frequenter Sacras tuas Scripturas in perniciem meam pervertunt. Cum nil hîc difcrtius præcipiatur, quàm ut pareant mihi simul, & incolumem conservent. O ne sit Illis in condemnationem.
units.tr: You, O Lord of Truth, know how often they pervert your Holy Scriptures to my ruin. Yet nothing is commanded here more plainly than that they should obey me and keep me safe. O may it not be to their condemnation.

units.la: Nosti Domine nonnullos qui Orationes longas orantes fratrum suorum Domos, & Regus, & Dei denique comederunt.
units.tr: You know, Lord, that some, while making long prayers, have devoured the houses of their brothers, and kingdoms, and finally the house of God.

units.la: Oleum eorum ne offendat Caput meum, nec Corroborantia Pharmaca Cor meum opprimant, contra iniquitatem eorum semper precabor.
units.tr: May their oil not offend my head, nor their strengthening medicines weigh down my heart; against their wickedness I will always pray.

units.la: A Veneno sub linguis eorum, à labiorum Illorum laqueis, ab Igne Verborum & Gladiis libera Me semper (Domine) & mecum unà illos fido & pio Corde, qui bene volunt animæ meæ, & prosperitate illius delectantur, quíque suis orationibus sublevare quærunt hanc mæstitiam Famuli Tui & solitudinem, Deus meus, & Rex meus.
units.tr: Free me always, O Lord, from the poison under their tongues, from the snares of their lips, from the fire of their words and from their swords; and with me, keep those who wish well to my soul and delight in its prosperity, with a faithful and devout heart, and who seek to relieve by their prayers this sorrow and loneliness of your servant, my God and my King.

units.la: 25. Meditationes Pœnitentiales & Vota in Solitudine Holm- bejana.
units.tr: 25. Meditations of Penitence and Vows in Solitude at Holmby.

units.la: Verba mea auribus percipe (Domine) intellige clamorem meum, intende vocem Orationis meæ, Rex meus ac Deus meus, quoniam ad Te orabo.
units.tr: Give ear to my words, O Lord; consider my cry, hearken to the voice of my prayer, my King and my God, for unto Thee do I pray.

units.la: Dixi enim in excessu mentis meæ, projectus sum à facie oculorum tuorum, at tu exaudisti vocem orationis meæ cùm ad te clamarem.
units.tr: For I said in my haste, I am cast out from before thine eyes; yet Thou heardest the voice of my supplication when I cried unto Thee.

units.la: Si Iniquitates observaveris Domine, Domine quis sustinebit? Sed apud Te propitiatio est & propterea timeris.
units.tr: If Thou, Lord, shouldest mark iniquities, O Lord, who shall stand? But there is forgiveness with Thee, and therefore Thou art feared.

units.la: Agnosco peccata mea coram Te, quæ Conditio mea reddit graviora, illâ dignitatis celsitudine pondus omnibus adjiciente.
units.tr: I acknowledge my sins before Thee, which my condition makes the graver, since the height of my dignity adds weight to every one of them.

units.la: Ignosce mihi Privata mea, & Subditorum meorum peccata eo usque mihi imputanda, quatenus illam quam dedisti Potestatem in Tuam Gloriam & Populi Bonum non exerui. Tu Me nunc à Gloria & Libertate Regia in eam sortem dejecisti, ut à propriis meis Subditis Captivus detinear. Merito Domine si præpotentem tuam manum considero, quia in plurimis contra Te rebellavi.
units.tr: Forgive me the sins of my own person, and those of my subjects, which are to be imputed to me so far as I have not exercised the power Thou gavest me for Thy glory and the good of the people. Thou hast now cast me down from royal glory and liberty into such a lot that I am held captive by my own subjects. Justly, Lord, do I consider Thy all-powerful hand, for I have rebelled against Thee in very many things.

units.la: Quin Tu mihi licet aliàs coarctato Cor meum in Te dilates, & in Me Gratiam Tuam.
units.tr: Yet Thou canst, though otherwise I am straitened, enlarge my heart towards Thee, and enlarge Thy grace towards me.

units.la: Multum infra existenti pietatem Davidis, sed ærumnis æquali; da mihi etiam solatia, & misericordias Davidis fideles.
units.tr: I am far below the piety of David, but equal to him in afflictions; give me also comforts, and the faithful mercies of David.

units.la: Dolor ille in pœnitentiam ob peccata mea esto mihi argumentum te hæc mihi condonasse.
units.tr: Let that sorrow for my sins, which leads me to repentance, be to me a proof that Thou hast forgiven me these things.

units.la: Ne tibi exigua videantur quæ sumus hactenùs Ego & Regna mea passi mala, licet haud pro merito castigaveris.
units.tr: Let not what my kingdoms and I have suffered so far seem small to Thee, although Thou hast chastised us less than we deserved.

units.la: Respice in Me Domine & miserere mei, quia unicus & afflictus sum Ego.
units.tr: Look upon me, Lord, and have mercy on me, for I am alone and afflicted.

units.la: Tribulationes cordis mei multiplicatæ sunt: de angustiis meis erue Me.
units.tr: The troubles of my heart are multiplied; bring me out of my distresses.

units.la: Oblitus es misereri Deus, & continebis in iræ misericordias tuas ?
units.tr: Hast Thou forgotten to be merciful, O God? Wilt Thou shut up Thy tender mercies in anger?

units.la: Memor esto miserationum tuarum antiquarum, & misericordiarum tuarum à seculis.
units.tr: Remember Thy former compassions and Thy mercies, which have been from of old.

units.la: Nisi credidissem Me visurum Bonum Domini in Terrà viventium, animum despondissem.
units.tr: Unless I had believed that I should see the goodness of the Lord in the land of the living, I would have despaired in spirit.

units.la: Ne in rebus secundis peccata nostra fraudent nos ab adversarum beneficio.
units.tr: Let our sins not defraud us of the benefit of adversity, lest we prosper in prosperity.

units.la: Quin hæc per Ignem exploratio scoriam illam absumat, è diuturna pace & copia contractam.
units.tr: Rather, let this trial by fire consume that dross which has been gathered from long peace and plenty.

units.la: Has si velis ærumnas producere, O ne Gratiam tuam subduxeris; quod deest fortunæ semundioris[?] patientia & pœnitentia supple.
units.tr: If Thou wouldest bring these afflictions, O do not withdraw Thy grace; supply by patience and repentance what is lacking in a more prosperous fortune.

units.la: Et si nondum Ira tua auferatur, sed manus tua adhuc extenditur, vertatur (oro) contra Me, & contra domum Patris mei, oves autem istæ quid fecerunt?
units.tr: And if Thy wrath is not yet taken away, but Thy hand is still stretched out, let it be turned, I beg, against me and against my father's house; but these sheep, what have they done?

units.la: Satient mcæ[?] perpessiones eorum Malitiam qui sunt mihi pariter & Ecclesiæ infensi; Sed nec ultima eorum sævitia Charitatem meam unquam exuperet.
units.tr: May my sufferings satisfy the malice of those who are equally hostile to me and to the Church; yet let not even their utmost cruelty ever overcome my charity.

units.la: Procul à Me facessat omnis vindictæ cogitatio, nec mihi percat patientiæ merces, tibi Gloria.
units.tr: Far from me let every thought of revenge depart, and let not the reward of my patience perish; let the glory be Thine.

units.la: Quemadmodum mihi cor dedisti ad condonandum facile, ita & Tu (precor) condones, quæ adversus Te & Me deliquerunt.
units.tr: As Thou hast given me a heart ready to forgive, so Thou also (I pray) wilt forgive those who have sinned against Thee and against me.

units.la: Et nunc (Domine) quoniam mihi Cor dedisti quo ad Te precer, audi & accepta quæ coram Te vota facio.
units.tr: And now, Lord, since Thou hast given me a heart with which to pray to Thee, hear and accept the vows I make before Thee.

units.la: Si Me & Regna mea in misericordia velis reminisci, perpetuando lucem Evangelii tui, & veram inter nos Religionem stabiliendo:
units.tr: If Thou wilt remember me and my kingdoms in mercy, by perpetuating the light of Thy Gospel and establishing among us the true religion:

units.la: Reddendo Legum beneficium, & debitam Iustitiæ administrationem:
units.tr: by rendering the benefit of the laws and the due administration of justice:

units.la: Compescendo illa plurima in Ecclesia Schismata & Factiones in statu:
units.tr: by restraining those very many schisms and factions in the Church and bringing them to an end:

units.la: Restituendo Me & meos in Iura illa antiqua & Decessorum nostrorum Gloriam:
units.tr: by restoring me and mine to those ancient rights and to the glory of our predecessors:

units.la: Si Tu velis convertere corda Populi mei, ut Tibi pietate, mihi fidelitate, sibi invicem charitate uniantur:
units.tr: if Thou wilt turn the hearts of my people so that they are united to Thee in piety, to me in fidelity, and to one another in charity:

units.la: Si hæc tandem velis Flammas extinguere, & Civilis Belli fomitem subtrahere:
units.tr: if at last Thou wilt quench these flames and remove the tinder of civil war:

units.la: Si nos publice consulendi libertate benedixeris, & Honorem Parlamentorum ab insolentia Plebis liberaveris:
units.tr: if Thou wilt bless us with freedom to consult publicly, and deliver the honour of the Parliaments from the insolence of the common people:

units.la: Si Me à magno Peccato custodiveris, ne quicquam adversus Conscientiam meam ratum faciam, maximè ne in Sacrilegas rapinas, & Ecclesiae Tuae spolia consentiam;
units.tr: if Thou wilt keep me from great sin, so that I do nothing against my conscience, and above all that I do not consent to sacrilegious plunder and the spoils of Thy Church:

units.la: Tunc laudabit Te anima mea, & magnificabo nomen Tuum in laude coram Populo.
units.tr: then shall my soul praise Thee, and I will magnify Thy name in praise before the people.

units.la: Tunc Mihi vel Coronis meis pretiosior erit tua Gloria, & illa cura praecipua, ut vis verae Religionis & puritas simul promoveatur.
units.tr: Then Thy glory will be more precious to me than my crowns, and that chief care, that the strength of true religion and its purity be advanced together.

units.la: Tunc in Iustitia regnabo Populum, & Regna Mea in aequitate.
units.tr: Then I shall reign over the people in justice, and my kingdoms in equity.

units.la: Tunc a Manu Tua immediatè agnoscetur (sicut Ius Legitimae Successionis) ita clemens Regnorum meorum, & omnis Gloriae eorum Restauratio.
units.tr: Then shall be acknowledged immediately from Thy hand (as is the right of lawful succession), so gracious a restoration of my kingdoms and of all their glory.

units.la: Si Me rursum in Pace, & Honore meo salvo, incolumem ad hanc Urbem meam Praecipuam & Parlamentum reduxeris.
units.tr: If Thou wilt bring me back again into peace, with my honour safe, unharmed to this my chief city and Parliament.

units.la: Si in manus meas iterum Gladium Iustitiae punientem simul & tutantem commiseris..
units.tr: If Thou wilt again entrust to my hands the sword of justice, which punishes and at the same time protects.

units.la: Tunc Orbis (faciam) intelligat, & ipsi Hostes Mei percipiant beneficium illius propositi, & Christianae Charitatis voti quod ad Te jam facio Domine.
units.tr: Then, I will do so, the world shall understand, and my very enemies shall perceive the benefit of that purpose and of the Christian charity which I now make to Thee, O Lord.

units.la: Nempe, ut jam omnibus ignosco (Christi causa) quaecunque in Me deliquerint, ita nunquam Manum Meam contra quenquam futuram, ut ob privatam ullam offensam ulciscar praeterita.
units.tr: Namely, that just as I now forgive everyone (for Christ's sake) whatever they have offended against me, so I will never raise my hand against anyone, so as to avenge past wrongs for any private offence.

units.la: Satis invicem luimus in scelerato hoc Bello; propter Te jam Domine, & Redemptoris Mei charitatem, illud firme in corde meo statuo omnes modos Amuciftiæ, & Indemnitatis experiri, quò & metus omnes pellam, & suspiciones oblivione sepeliam.
units.tr: We have paid each other enough in this wicked war; for Thy sake now, O Lord, and for the love of my Redeemer, I firmly resolve in my heart to try every means of friendship and indemnity, so that I may both drive out all fears and bury suspicions in oblivion.

units.la: Tuis ita in Me & Meos misericordiis potiar ut Veritatem & Pacem firme volo.
units.tr: Let me so enjoy Thy mercies towards me and mine that I firmly desire truth and peace.

units.la: Auribus percipe orationem meam Domine non è labiis dolosis prodeuntem.
units.tr: Give ear to my prayer, O Lord, which does not come from deceitful lips.

units.la: Benedictus Deus qui non repulit orationem meam, nec misericordiam suam a Me subduxit.
units.tr: Blessed be God, who has not rejected my prayer, nor withdrawn His mercy from me.

units.la: Anima Mea devolve super Dominum viam tuam: Spera in eo, & ipse faciet.
units.tr: Commit thy way unto the Lord; trust also in him, and he shall bring it to pass.

units.la: Sin Tu nolis Me & Meos restituere, quis sum ego qui tibi insulsum tribuam?
units.tr: But if Thou wouldest not restore me and mine, who am I that I should offer thee anything unsavoury?

units.la: Tu (Domine) dedisti & abstulisti. Sit nomen Domini Benedictum: Laudetur Nomen Domini,
units.tr: Thou (Lord) hast given and Thou hast taken away. Blessed be the name of the Lord; let the name of the Lord be praised.

units.la: Fœlix sit Populus Meus & Ecclesia, si nun[?] mecum una, at sine Me.
units.tr: Let my people and my Church be happy, if not with me, yet without me.

units.la: 26. Cum Rex in Holmbeja interciperetur, & quæ inde distractiones in Utraque Domo, Exercitu & Urbe consecutæ.
units.tr: 26. When the King was seized at Holmby, and the divisions which followed from this in both Houses, the Army and the City ensued.

units.la: QVam Personam mihi jam impositurus est Deus, vel quid agere omnino aut pati velit in hac Nova rerum Scena haud sum valdè sollicitus. Modico usu Artisex evadet qui Honestatis tantum & Virtutis partes susceperit.
units.tr: What Persona God is about to assign me, or what He wishes me to do or suffer on this new stage of affairs, I am not greatly troubled to know. An actor becomes skilled after little practice if he has taken up only the parts of honesty and virtue.

units.la: Hac Mei raptione ostendunt, vix eo usque dejici Regem posse, ut non momentum sit aliquod & Pondus, parti in qua conspicitur, allaturus.
units.tr: By this seizure of mine they show that the King can scarcely be cast down so far that he will not bring some momentum and weight to the side on which he is seen.

units.la: Motus iste (prout alii horum Temporum) Eccentricus prorsus & Irregularis, cui tamen haud facile vel resistat quispiam, vel sistat. Præstat rapi torrente, quàm frustra brachio contra obniti. Nempe Gemellorum colluctatio quos idem nuper uterus inclusit; dum in Majorem certat Minor prævalescere. Quod tam diu venati sunt Presbyterales, volunt jam Independentes eripere.
units.tr: This movement, like others of these times, is wholly eccentric and irregular, yet no one can easily either resist it or halt it. It is better to be swept away by a torrent than to strive in vain against it with one's arm. This is indeed the wrestling of twins whom the same womb recently enclosed, while the Minor strives to prevail over the Major. What the Presbyterales hunted for so long, the Independentes now want to snatch away.

units.la: Omninò aliter fieri non potest, quin à Centro semel ductæ Lineæ à se invicem statim diducantur, atque eo latiori intervallo quo recedunt longiùs à Puncto Unitatis.
units.tr: It cannot in any way come about otherwise: lines once drawn from a Centre immediately diverge from one another, and the farther they recede from the Point of Unity, the wider the gap between them.

units.la: Enimverò ut Babelis Exstructores à divisione ad confusionem labantur, haud perinde mirandum: ut verò ii qui simulant ædificare Ierusalem ita linguâ & manu invicem dividerentur, malum profecto augurium est, & aliquid in se habere videtur Zelotarum furoribus simillimum, quorum maximè intestinis dissidiis Fatum Urbis illius & suprema clades debebatur.
units.tr: That the Exstructores of Babel slid from division into confusion is not so very surprising. But that those who pretend to build Jerusalem should be divided among themselves in tongue and hand in this way is surely an evil omen, and seems to have something very like the frenzies of the Zealots, whose internal dissensions above all brought about the fate and final destruction of that city.

units.la: Muto jam Custodes & Carcerem, manet eadem Captiva conditio; hæc me spes solatur, istos, qui se Populi libertatum ita strenuos vindices profitentur, haud ita Regis suæ libertati in omnibus posse adversari: quod enim suis conscientiis donandum postulant, meæ sunt iniquissimè negaturi.
units.tr: The guards are now mute and the prison remains, and the same captive condition remains. This hope comforts me: that those who profess themselves such vigorous champions of the people's liberties cannot be so opposed to their King's liberty in everything. For what they demand must be granted to their consciences, they will most unjustly deny to mine.

units.la: Atque hîc magis ingenuè videntur agere, quàm quâ erant Presbyterales inhumanitate; qui id maximè lamentari soliti, exigi sic ab Illis ut essent Legibus conformes, jam Exactores sunt omnium acerbissimi, ut Novellis suis Dictatis obtemperetur, licet nulla adhuc Legum authoritate firmatis, quod sine meo consensu nunquam fiet.
units.tr: And here they seem to act more ingenuously than they did with the inhumanity of the Presbyterians. Those who used most to lament that they were forced by them to conform to the laws are now the most bitter exactors of all, so that their new decrees may be obeyed, though not yet confirmed by any authority of law; which will never happen without my consent.

units.la: Patet jam, Independentes ex hoc Rivalium suorum famulatu manumissos se penitus arbitrari, cum rem tanti momenti, (quale est Me Exercitui custodiendum tradere) nullo alio mandato nisi suo jure exequuntur.
units.tr: It is now clear that the Independents think themselves wholly freed from the servitude of their Rivals, since they carry out a matter of such importance (such as entrusting my custody to the Army) by no other command than their own right.

units.la: Qui hæc in Regem suum audent, quidvis facile porro aggredientur quod in animum semel induxerint, nullo metu aut verecundia deterriti.
units.tr: Those who dare these things against their King will readily undertake anything further that they have once resolved upon, deterred by no fear or shame.

units.la: Proximè jam ad Vrbem turbatur, terrore intentato & minis tum in Illam, tum in Domum utramque, quæ jam frustra iisdem repetitis Tumultibus mox & hos & illos priores (quorum nulla adhuc inquisitio nulla prorsus animadversio eut[?] pœnitentia extiterat) codem[?] una luunt supplicio, in præsenti pavore & Distractionum speculo peccatum suum contemplantes.
units.tr: Next, the City is thrown into turmoil, with terror and threats directed both at it and at both Houses. These, by the same tumults repeated in vain, soon pay the penalty together, both these and those earlier ones (for which no inquiry, no punishment at all, and no repentance has yet come), contemplating their sin in present fear and in the mirror of their divisions.

units.la: Stupidè cœcum esse oportet, qui hic Manum Dei non videt: ut, qui ipsi Tumultuantes invitabant primò, & initium fecerunt Exercitui, jam ab iisdem ob Tumultus castigentur.
units.tr: One must be stupidly blind not to see the hand of God here: that those who themselves first invited the rioters and began the attack on the Army are now punished by the same rioters for their riots.

units.la: Ita difficile est intra unum peccatum continere, nec nova insuper facere, dum superiora novissimis puniantur. Qui enim Me non ita dudum & utriusque Ordinus plurimos à Primis illis licentiosis Tumultibus pulsos ita placidè & libenter spectabant, jam & ipsi in Castra confugiunt, ut sint à Tumultuantibus tuti.
units.tr: So it is hard to keep within one sin and not to commit new ones besides, while earlier ones are punished by the latest. For those who not long ago watched so calmly and gladly as very many of both Orders were driven out by those first licentious riots, now themselves flee into the camp so as to be safe from the rioters.

units.la: Sed quis hæc jam expediat Ænigmata? qui se prius ex Utroque Ordine mecum una ab his furoribus subtraxerant, Desertores Parlamenti habiti sunt, & in perpetuum exclusi, qui vero permanebant, & beneficio Tumultuum utebantur, hi unici erant Senatores: Contra jam, Locum suum deserentes & profugi secum unà Authoritatem Parlamentariam auferunt, debacchantur in Tumultus, & se vi armatâ restituunt, dum qui manent adhuc in statione sua fixi Hortatores Tumultuum audiunt, libertatisque & Honoris Parlamentarii Proditores.
units.tr: But who can now explain these riddles? Those who earlier withdrew from these frenzies together with me from both Orders were regarded as deserters of Parliament and excluded for ever. But those who remained and made use of the riots, these alone were the Senators. On the contrary, now those who desert their place and flee take the Parliamentary authority with them, rage into riots and restore themselves by armed force, while those who still remain fixed at their post hear the instigators of riots, and are betrayers of liberty and of parliamentary honour.

units.la: Adeo ultra Leges omnes & Regulas Vis pollet; dumque magis quid in præsens expediat, homines quàm Conscientiam spectent & illam Normam Justitiæ immutabilem, fit plærumque ut dum aliorum Judices sedeant scipfor[?] maximè condemnent.
units.tr: So far does force prevail beyond all laws and rules. And while men look more to what is expedient for the moment than to conscience and that unchangeable norm of justice, it generally happens that while they sit as judges of others, they condemn themselves most of all.

units.la: Jam Tumultus grande Crimen! jam Authores eorum & Fautores prodigiosæ Audaciæ rei, nuper animo in Parlamentum benevolo, & necessarii valde adjutores.
units.tr: Now a riot is a great crime! Now its authors and abettors are guilty of monstrous audacity, Parliament's lately well-disposed friends, and very necessary helpers!

units.la: Ita (quod olim narratur de illo Præsule Germano à forecibus & muribus interemptò) acris sequitur vindicta & deprehendit eos, qui se Numero securos, & obsequio in Populum munitissimos existimabant.
units.tr: So (as is told of that prelate Germanus, who was killed by shears and mice) sharp vengeance follows and catches those who thought themselves safe in their numbers, and most fortified against the people by their obedience.

units.la: In quos jam Leges nil possunt, Deus propriis ipsorum scelerinbus[?] & manibus etiam castigabit.
units.tr: Against these the laws can now do nothing; God will punish them with their own wicked hands.

units.la: Hoc interim Divinæ Justitiæ opus Ipse maximo dolore & miseratione intueor, cum sim in Urbem & Parlamenta animo valde benevolo; ut non possim non serio deplorare, duo haec Regni nostri conspicua maxime & insignia Corpora tam indigna se pati vel facere.
units.tr: This work of divine justice I myself behold with the greatest grief and pity, since I am very well disposed towards the City and the Parliaments. So I cannot but seriously deplore that these two most conspicuous and distinguished bodies of our kingdom should suffer or do such unworthy things.

units.la: Bené tamen hactenus processit, quòd ista gravis utcunque conquassatio, in terrorem tantum, & in domandos spiritus, non ad ruinam processit, nunquam enim tam malè de hac Urbe opinatus sum, ut de futuro illius obsequio & fide desperaverim, quae licet praesens forsan error obtenebret, nunquam penitus Malitia extinguet.
units.tr: Yet so far things have gone well: this heavy shaking, however it came about, has amounted only to terror and to the taming of spirits, and has not gone on to ruin. For I have never thought so badly of this City that I have despaired of its future obedience and fidelity, which, though present error may darken it, malice will never wholly extinguish.

units.la: Tota utinam ab illis sic procella transfierit; quos non secus contemplor ac Christus ipse Ierusalem, precibus meis & lachrymis & moerore dignissimos, cùm multo olim graviores dispersiones prospiciam necessario illis eventuras, qui merâ suâ petulantiâ in officio manere noluerant: cum sit quaedam fatalis occaecatio voluntariae comes & supplicium: ut jam nec liberum sit postea vel aerumnas defugere qui maturè de peccatis resipiscere nolebant, vel unquam frui Pacis gaudio qui Consilia Pacis aspernabantur. Id enim tandem reperient, Fratres istor[?] in malo proximè in Hostes abituros, cùm sit nil difficilius, quàm ut sint Improbi diù unanimes.
units.tr: Would that the whole storm might pass over them in this way; I regard them no differently than Christ himself regarded Jerusalem, most worthy of my prayers, tears and grief. For I foresee that far heavier dispersions must necessarily come upon those who, out of mere wantonness, were unwilling to remain in their duty. There is a certain fatal blindness, the companion and punishment of wilful sin, so that it is not then free either to escape troubles for those who were unwilling to repent of their sins in time, or ever to enjoy the joy of peace for those who spurned the counsels of peace. For at last they will find that those brothers of theirs in evil will soon go over to the enemy, since nothing is more difficult than for the wicked to remain of one mind for long.

units.la: Haud enim fieri potest ut felici exitu terminentur vaga ista & dissoluta Consilia, quae videntur mobili quodam potius gyro circumacta, quàm rectâ Rationis lineâ directa ad illud Publicæ Salutis Centrum, Leges, in quas omnes utinam Partes tandem desinant.
units.tr: For these vague and loose counsels cannot possibly end happily. They seem driven round by a sort of moving whirl, rather than directed by the straight line of reason towards that centre of public safety, the laws, into which I wish all parties would at last come to rest.

units.la: Quod quidem erit multo facilius, cùm jam penitus perspectum habuerint, quàm sit multo fœlicius notis Legibus parere, quàm diversis hominum voluntatibus quantumvis blanda pollicentium.
units.tr: This will indeed be much easier once they have fully perceived how much more happily it is to obey known laws than the wills of men, however flatteringly they promise.

units.la: Hæc enim Vulgi studia qui res novas fere & illicitas prosequuntur, velut motus violenti statim languent, & in contumacem fere definunt morositatem; verso etiam nonnunquam in Illos impetu qui in has Illos furias perpulerunt.
units.tr: For these popular enthusiasms, which pursue new and almost unlawful things, soon flag like violent movements, and nearly always end in stubborn obstinacy; sometimes, too, the attack is turned against those who drove them into these frenzies.

units.la: Quod ad Exercitum spectat (eo forte excusatiorem quod Militari more in rem suam agant Stipendia & Indemnitatem postulantes) necessarium sane duco Paci publicæ, ut his quamprimum (quoad fas est) satis fiat. Horum enim ut ratio habeatur inprimis cupio, qui utcunque in adversa mihi acie steterint, ob fortitudinem tamen & in deposcendis periculis audaciam eoufq; sunt æstimandi, ut vehementer exoptem mihi nunquam tales defuturos, qui Me, Leges & Regna in ejusmodi Pace tueantur, cujus ipsi non minùs quam alii fructus sentiant.
units.tr: As for the Army (perhaps the more excusable because they act in their own cause in the military manner, demanding pay and indemnity), I certainly consider it necessary for public peace that these demands be satisfied as soon as possible (so far as right allows). For I especially desire that their case be taken into account, who, however they stood against me in the opposing line, are to be valued for their courage and their boldness in facing dangers. So I earnestly hope that men like these will never be wanting to me, who would defend me, the laws and the kingdoms in such a peace, the fruits of which they themselves feel no less than others.

units.la: Tu vero Domine qui in Sacrosancta Trinitate es perfecta Unitas, intuere illos pro tua Misericordia, quos in Justitia tua divisisti.
units.tr: But you, Lord, who in the most holy Trinity are perfect Unity, look upon those whom you have divided in your justice, in your mercy.

units.la: Libera Me à contradictionibus Populi, & fac ut id potius cogitem, quam sit his precibus meis & miseratione opus, qui contra Me nuper conjunctis viribus pugnantes jam contra se invi-ccm[?] bellum parant, ad perpetuandas Regnorum miserias.
units.tr: Deliver me from the contradictions of the people, and grant that I may rather think of how little these my prayers and this pity are needed by those who, having lately joined forces against me, now prepare war upon one another, to perpetuate the miseries of the kingdoms.

units.la: Patefacias omnibus semitas Pacis, à qua deflexerunt, quæque non in divisis Partium volun-tatibus sed in debita Legum observatione con-sistit.
units.tr: Show all men the paths of peace, from which they have turned aside, a peace that lies not in the divided wills of the parties but in the due observance of the laws.

units.la: Fac ut libens eam, quocunque Providentia Mc[?] Tua deductura est: & sis mecum perpetuò, ut in Mundi instabilitate & mutationibus Tuam videam Constantiam.
units.tr: Grant that I may gladly follow it wherever Thy providence shall lead me, and be with me always, that amid the instability and changes of the world I may see Thy constancy.

units.la: Eum Me efficias qualem maxime volueris, ut eâ Pace & tranquillitate fruar quam Tu solus impertis.
units.tr: Make me such as Thou most desirest, that I may enjoy that peace and tranquillity which Thou alone bestowest.

units.la: Averte (Oro Domine) gravem Iram Tuam Grandibus istis & Populosis Urbibus imminentem, quibus sua Copia fomes Luxuriæ est, & opulentia vertitur in lasciviam, qui multitudinis suæ fiducia in securitatem proni & hac demnm[?] securitate repentinis fiunt miseriis obnoxii.
units.tr: Turn away (I pray, O Lord) Thy grave wrath, hanging over these great and populous cities, in which their abundance is the fuel of luxury and their wealth turns into wantonness; who, trusting in their multitude, become prone to security, and by this very security become liable to sudden calamities.

units.la: Da quò videant oculos, quò meditentur corda, quò amplectantur voluntates, & animos denique ut faciant quæ ad Tuam Gloriam, & Publicam Pacem spectant, ne Calamitas eorum superveniat, tanquam Vir Armatus.
units.tr: Give them eyes to see, hearts to meditate, wills to embrace, and finally minds to do what pertains to Thy glory and the public peace, lest their calamity come upon them like an armed man.

units.la: Fac ut sciant, nunquam illis posse Inimicos deesse, qui abundant peccato, nec diu arma retenturos, aut perniciem effugituros, qui sic manu superba Contra Te & clarissima Conscientiarum suarum testimonia perseverantes pugnare plus adversos seipsos quam Me pugnant, dum peccatis suis tuæ Iustitiæ, a divitiis aliorum Injuriis, à Numeris suis Tumultuantibus, & ab his Confusioni exponuntur.
units.tr: Make them know that enemies never fail those who abound in sin, nor will they long keep their arms or escape destruction, who persist so proudly in fighting against Thee and against the clearest testimony of their own consciences: they fight more against themselves than against me, while by their sins they expose themselves to Thy justice, by their injuries to the riches of others, by their own tumultuous numbers, and by these to confusion.

units.la: Quanquam prompte admodum & alacriter in exitium meum coiverint, ne-, faxis, cum eorum ruina procumbam.
units.tr: Although they have come together so promptly and eagerly for my destruction, do not allow me, I pray, to fall with their ruin.

units.la: Fac ne nimis cogitando, vel quid Illi fecerint vel quæ Ipse (in initio præsertim) passus fuerim, immemor fiam Illius Servatoris mei Crucifixi, ut Ignorantia valeat in veniam Causa, & in ipsis Mortis angoribus ad Te precor, Domine, Pater Ignosce quia ignorant quid faciunt.
units.tr: Do not let me, thinking too much either on what they have done or on what I myself (especially at the beginning) have suffered, become forgetful of my Saviour Crucified, so that ignorance may count as a cause for pardon; and in the very agonies of death I pray to Thee, O Lord, Father: forgive them, for they know not what they do.

units.la: Lachrymas quas negarunt mihi in calamitosissima mea Fortuna, fac Tua Gratia ut pro seipsis profundant, qui quo minus pro Me doleant, eo impensius pro se debent ingemiscere.
units.tr: The tears they have denied me in my most calamitous fortune, by Thy grace make them shed for themselves; for the less they grieve for me, the more earnestly they ought to lament for themselves.

units.la: O ne Sanguis Meus super Eos & Filios eorum, quos fraus nonnullorum & prava studia, non propria sua malitia ad Me Crucifigendum instigavit.
units.tr: O let not my blood be upon them and their children, whom the deceit of some and their perverse designs, rather than their own malice, incited to crucify me.

units.la: Tu vero Domine potes & velis Me per has meas (quemadmodum olim Redemptorem meum) perpessiones exaltare simul & perficere, in quibus plus Misericordiæ tuæ quam Iustitiæ, vel humanæ sævitiæ agnosco.
units.tr: But Thou, O Lord, canst and wilt exalt and perfect me through these my sufferings, as once my Redeemer, in which I recognise more of Thy mercy than of justice or of human cruelty.

units.la: 27. Ad Principem Walliæ.
units.tr: 27. To the Prince of Wales.

units.la: FILI MI,
units.tr: MY SON,

units.la: SI ad Te hæ Chartæ (cui inprimis destinantur) pervenerint unà cum aliis nonnullis (in quibus privata sensa animi mei & rectissimè intuentis Conscientiæ explicui circa res præcipuas in hoc Novissimo Motu agitatas) hactenùs forsan utiles erunt, ut judicium Tuum de præteritis (quibus in pietatem uti optimè uti est) accuratius edoceatur, tum ratio aliqua ostendatur, quâ præsentibus malis mederi liceat, & in futurum (si sic Deo visum fuerit) occurrere.
units.tr: If these papers, which are chiefly intended for you, reach you together with some others (in which I have set out my private thoughts, and those of my conscience, which sees most rightly, on the main matters debated in this latest upheaval), they may prove useful so far: your judgement on past events (by which you can make good use for piety) may be more accurately informed, and some plan may be shown by which present evils may be remedied and future ones met (if God so wills).

units.la: Fallitur interim mihi sic optimè tædium & injuria longæ detentionis minuitur, cum hujus otii Mei & solitudinis fructum aliquem Me dignum, Tibi utilem percipiam; ne vel Tu deinceps vel quisquâ alius Causam meam ab Eventu æstimet, nec ab Infœlicitate Judicium; eo quidem graviore, quod in partem tantum ipse veneris & alii, quos juxta ac Me ipsum charos habeo, & quorum indignæ per-pessiopessiones mihi. sunt propriis meis longè accepbiores.
units.tr: Meanwhile I am pleasantly deceived in this way: my weariness and the injury of my long detention are lessened, since I gain some fruit from this leisure and solitude that is worthy of me and useful to you. Then neither you from now on nor anyone else will judge my cause by its outcome, nor judgement by misfortune. This is all the more so because you and others, whom I hold as dear as myself, have come into only a part of the trouble, and their undeserved sufferings are far more bitter to me than my own.

units.la: Hoc vero Tibi in prudentiam ultra alios Principes accessit, quòd annos aliquot ætatis tuæ maturescentis in patientiæ exercitio & duris temporibus exegisti, sub quibus Pietas non minus quàm Virtutes cæteræ Morales & Politicæ (velut surculi in hyeme sati) fœliciùs fere succrescunt, quàm in calore & serenitate meliorum temporum, vel inter illa voluptatum blandimenta, quæ in Pace & rerum affluentia Aulis Principum nimis hærent, quæque omnem Veræ Virtutis & Honoris herbam vel stirpitùs evellunt, vel sat habent Frondibus earum & marcescenti specie ornari, nullo fructu in publicum ,l[?] in quod utinam serió cogitarent Principes se & natos maximè & à Deo destinatos.
units.tr: Moreover, this has added to your prudence beyond other princes: you have spent some years of your maturing youth in the exercise of patience and in hard times. Under such conditions piety, no less than the other moral and political virtues (like shoots sown in winter), grows up more happily than in the heat and calm of better times, or amid those flattering pleasures which cling too closely to the courts of princes in peace and plenty. These pleasures either tear up by the roots every herb of true virtue and honour, or are content to adorn it with its leaves and a withering show, bearing no fruit for the public. Would that princes would seriously consider this for themselves and their children, especially those whom God has destined for rule!

units.la: Jam, quæ vis sit diversæ educationis Sacra Pagina ostendit in exemplis Davidis & Rchoboam[?], quorum alterum multæ ærumnæ in florentissimum Regnum præpararunt, hic Aulæ Salomonis sœlicitate nimiâ emollitus est; atque adeo cum grandi detrimento Honoris & Pacis, tum ipsius etiam Regni mutilatione, corruptus ab eorum adulationibus, qui (non secus ac muscæ æstivis fructibus) rebus Principum fecundis indivulsè hærent, dum adversis tandem ut hyeme abigantur.
units.tr: Holy Scripture shows in the examples of David and Rehoboam how great the force of different upbringing is. The one was prepared by many hardships for a most flourishing kingdom; the other was softened by the excessive prosperity of Solomon's court. He was corrupted, with great loss of honour and peace and even the mutilation of the kingdom itself, by the flatteries of those who, like flies on summer fruits, cling inseparably to the fruitful circumstances of princes, until at last in adversity they are driven off, as in winter.

units.la: Te vero magis exopto Carolo illi Bono quam Grandi similem: Deum spero utrumque effecturum, cùm in Te dona collata & Gra-tias tias ita statim exerceri voluerit, atque eo prorsus modo quo vitiosi affectus optimè possint extirpari, & in eadem demum studia & virtutes Regias præparari, quibus, eorum in quos Te Deus constituerit, & amorem maximè potes conciliare & saluti consulere.
units.tr: I wish you to be like that good Charles rather than great. I hope God will bring about both, since he has willed that the gifts and graces bestowed on you be exercised at once, and in exactly the way by which vicious affections can best be rooted out, and by which you are prepared for the same studies and royal virtues. By these you can best win the love of those over whom God has set you and provide for their safety.

units.la: A Deo auspicari te quàm maximè cupio, & cum Deo finire, qui est Rex Regum, & Supremus Regnorum dispensator, qui dejicit alios, alios extollit.
units.tr: I most earnestly wish you to begin with God and to end with God, who is King of kings and supreme dispenser of kingdoms, who casts down some and raises up others.

units.la: Verus Principis honos in promovenda Dei Gloria, in tuenda vera Religione & Ecclesiæ Bono consistit, tum Potestatem Civilem ea Iustitiâ & Honore administrando qui Bono Publico maximè conducat.
units.tr: The true honour of a prince consists in promoting God's glory, in defending true religion and the good of the Church, and in administering civil power with that justice and honour which most serves the public good.

units.la: Florentem te satis præstabit Pietas, à miseria saltem immunem custodiet: quamquam levi admodum damno afficitur, qui in salutem Animæ perdit omnia.
units.tr: Piety will make you prosper well enough, and will at least keep you free from misery. Yet he suffers only a very slight loss who loses all things for the salvation of the soul.

units.la: Ad hoc Centrum veræ fœlicitatis direxit Deus suâ misericordia, & (ut spero) etiam directurus est nigras illas omnes ærumnarum lineas super Me eo fine productas ut per has ad se propius adduceret. Tu jam Calicem [?] libâsti, quem ego large hausi, quod ut Dei Pharmacum accipio, quod deest suavitatis salubritate compensans.
units.tr: To this centre of true happiness God, in his mercy, has directed, and (as I hope) will yet direct, all those black lines of troubles drawn out over me, with this end: that through them he might bring me nearer to himself. You have now tasted the cup [?], which I have drunk deeply. I receive it as God's medicine, which, though lacking in sweetness, makes up for it by its wholesomeness.

units.la: Id vero tibi expeto potissimùm, (quod & spero jam factum) ut in Religione firmus radiceris, quam ego semper existimavi in Ecclesia Anglicana (cujus Tu alumnus es) optimè fuisse institutam, opto verò ut Ratione & Iudicio rata fiat illa Educationis Scripturæ nec aliorum Traditis & Consuetudini solùm debeatur.
units.tr: This above all I desire for you (and I hope it has already come about): that you be firmly rooted in religion, which I have always judged to have been most excellently established in the English Church, of which you are a pupil. But I wish that this education rest on reason and judgement, grounded in Scripture, and not be owed solely to the traditions and customs of others.

units.la: In hac districtè edico ut perstes : ut cujus maximè doctrina Dei Verbo, & Primitivis Exemplis Disciplina respondet, pauculis tantum emendatis quæ alibi declarata sæpe Illis sed frustra proposui.
units.tr: In this I strictly charge you to persevere: to hold to that doctrine which most closely agrees with God's Word and whose discipline matches primitive examples, with only a few corrections, which I have often set out to them elsewhere, but in vain.

units.la: Vt firmus sis Religioni non erit in animæ magis quàm in Regnorum Pacem, cùm Deus Te illis restituerit.
units.tr: Your firmness in religion will be no less necessary for the peace of the soul than for the peace of kingdoms, when God restores you to them.

units.la: Illud enim plærunque videre est, hunc Perduellionis Diabolum se in Angelum Pacis transformare, & inter Veteris Serpentis astutias esse, Novam lucem simulare. Exclamanti in Illos conscientiæ factionumq; & seditionum reos peragenti, os statim obturant Religionis strepitu, hortanti ad Pacem & patientiam Pietati ipsi Zelum contra vociferantes reclamant.
units.tr: For it is commonly seen that this Devil of rebellion transforms himself into an Angel of Peace, and that among the wiles of the old Serpent is to pretend to a new light. When someone cries out against those guilty of faction and sedition, and of misusing conscience, they at once stop his mouth with the clamour of religion. When someone exhorts to peace and patience, they cry out against piety itself, claiming zeal.

units.la: Quamobrem,nisi hic fixo sis animo, & confirmato, nunquam deerunt tentamenta: queis sub Obtentu Reformationis Tibi pariter & Tùis perniciem struent, hoc enim colore hominum deterrimi exitiosa sua consilia ordiuntur.
units.tr: Therefore, unless you are firm and settled in purpose, there will never be lack of attempts. Under the pretext of reformation they will plot ruin for you and yours alike, for it is under this colour that the worst of men begin their deadly designs.

units.la: Præter enim quod ipsa Novitas vulgi satis per se illecebra est, gestit quisque æmulo studio famam Zeli externâ Reformatione acquirere, ita propriam melius Impietatem & turpitudinem velare sperantes quò severiorem in alios Cénsuram exercent.
units.tr: For apart from the fact that novelty itself is attraction enough for the crowd, each person eagerly seeks, with rival zeal, the reputation of zeal through external reformation. They hope thus to veil their own impiety and baseness better, the more severely they exercise censure on others.

units.la: Vide ne Factionem ullam foveas à Religione ( in Ecclesia constituta, & Judicio tua consona ) ex professo discrepantem : cuicunq; enim Parti adhæseris, haud ita Illos demercberis qui in Regiam Religionem ire prompti, quàm Illos penitus inconciliabis, qui se spretos primùm exi-stimabunt ut deinde opprimantur. Eam ergo rationem instituas quæ mansuetudine & charitate æquissimâ controversias (quæ apparent, & offensas removeant, vel ita firmâ & valida Potestate utaris, ut nulli Parti assentari necesse habeas, nec ab ulla metuere. Si enim aliqua Te huc impulerit necessitas ut precariam ab illis opem exspectare oporteat, periisti. Devorabit Columbam Serpens, nec minùs ab ullis Iustitiæ, fidei, humanitatis speraveris, quàm quos Pietas sua fecit Proditores. His quicquid in rem suam fore putant, Dei Causa est : sub vexillis pietatis producuntur omnes vafræ Ambitionis artes maxima securitate & plausu populi : Vox Iacobi auditur, sed Esavi manus duras senties.
units.tr: Take care not to foster any faction that openly dissents from religion (as established in the Church and agreeing with your judgement). For whichever party you cling to, you will not win over those who are ready to go over to the royal religion so much as you will utterly alienate those who will first think themselves despised and then be oppressed. Therefore devise such a plan as removes the controversies and offences that arise by the most equitable gentleness and charity; or else use such firm and strong authority that you need not flatter any party, nor fear any. For if some necessity drives you to expect aid from them as a favour, you are lost. The serpent will devour the dove, and you will hope in vain for justice, faith or humanity from those whom their own piety has made traitors. Whatever they think will serve their own interest, they call the cause of God. Under the banners of piety all the crafty arts of ambition are brought forward, with the greatest security and applause of the people. The voice is Jacob's, but you will feel the hands of Esau as hard.

units.la: Nil mihi per annos complures levioris momenti videbatur, quàm Factio Presbyteralis in Anglia, ita publicè constitutis morem gesserunt, nec revera quoad speciem multi erant, vel in Ecclesia aut Statu pollens factio : ut vero Irâ & odiis divelli invicem coeperunt homines & in partes secedere (non secus ac pravi solent humores in partem malè affectam defluere, unde fit inflammatio in Corpore) ita omnes Novarum rerum avidi illi Parti potissimum adhæserunt, quæ tunc maximè plausibili, & insigniori Pietatis notâ distincta à cæteris videbatur.
units.tr: For many years nothing seemed to me of less moment than the Presbyterian faction in England. Those who were publicly constituted obeyed it, and in appearance it was not large, nor a faction powerful in Church or State. But when men began to be divided by anger and hatred, and to secede into parties (just as bad humours are wont to flow into a diseased part, whence inflammation arises in the body), all those eager for novelties clung especially to that party which then seemed most plausible and distinguished from the rest by a more conspicuous mark of piety.

units.la: Omnes in initio Factiones minores officiosè admodum Presbyteratui magno omnium Domino famulabantur, donec tempus & Fortuna Belli (cùm jam melius erudirentur, quid ex usu magis foret singulis) hortabantur ut forte divisa (quæ nuper sub Uniformis Religionis nomine eadem omnibus esse videbatur) peculiarem, jam quisque rationem capesserent, quâ lucro suo maximè & fortunæ consuleret, unde non solùm labefactata est & ad internecionem pene redacta Ecclesia & Respublica, sed ipse etiam Presbyteratus qui jam omnia Spe devoraverat.
units.tr: At first all the lesser factions very obsequiously served the Presbytery, the great Lord of all. But when time and the fortune of war had taught them better what was more advantageous to each, they were urged (since what had lately seemed the same for all under the name of uniform religion was now divided) to each seize a peculiar plan by which to look best to their own gain and fortune. Whence not only the Church and Commonwealth were shaken and brought almost to ruin, but the Presbytery itself, which had already devoured everything in hope.

units.la: Nil igitur Tibi magnum videatur aut contemnendum in quo de Pace Ecclesiæ aut Religione agitur, ut negligentior fias propterea vel in maturè reformando, vel efficaciter coercendo Errores illos & Schismata, quæ licet parva in initio instar volæ manus appareant, seditiosis posteà Spiritibus ut vehementibus ventis impulsi toto Cælo repente offunduntur.
units.tr: Therefore let nothing seem great or to be despised to you in which the peace of the Church or religion is at stake, lest you become more negligent either in reforming in time or in effectively curbing those errors and schisms. Though at first they appear small, like the palm of a hand, afterwards, driven by seditious spirits as by violent winds, they suddenly spread over the whole sky.

units.la: Cum Deo primum & Animæ Tuæ & Ecclesiæ debitum feceris, Veritatem & Unitatem Religionis profitendo simul & conservando, proxima tibi esse debet (ut in quâ cardo felicitatis tuæ valde vertitur) Civilis Cura Iustitiæ, cujus Regula & optimè administrandi norma Leges sunt in his Regnis (ad Te Jure hæreditario deventuris) constitutæ; quæ admirabili planè mistura ita Subditorum Industriæ[?], Libertati, cæterisque commodis favent, ut satis interim Regiæ Majestati & Prærogativæ relinquatur; modo Rex fuerit ejusmodi, qui Populum suum pro Subditis non pro Servis habeat; hujusmodi enim subjectione, quemadmodum optimè conservatur Pax eorum & salus & peculiares cujusque proprietatcs, ita nec Jus tuum violabitur nec illa Populi Libertas ingenua, quæ in percipiendis Laboris sui fructibus, Legumque, in quas Ipsi consenserc, beneficio consistit.
units.tr: Since you will first have paid your debt to God, to your own soul and to the Church, by professing and at the same time preserving the truth and unity of religion, your next concern should be civil care for justice, on which the hinge of your happiness turns. The rule and the standard of good government in these kingdoms, to which you will succeed by hereditary right, are its laws. By a wonderfully balanced mixture they favour the industry of the subjects, their liberty and their other advantages, while still leaving enough to the royal majesty and prerogative, provided the king is the sort who regards his people as subjects, not as slaves. For under such a relationship their peace, their safety and each man's own property are best preserved, and neither your right is violated nor that free liberty of the people, which consists in enjoying the fruits of their labour and the benefit of the laws to which they themselves have consented.

units.la: Nunquam Caput Tuum premat Corona ejusmodi sub cujus pondere totum Corpus labascat, quod in partibus infirmatum nil jam Capiti vicissim honoris, roboris, Incolumitatis referet, sed debilitari [illegible, ~5 letters] faciet & procumbere.
units.tr: May no crown ever weigh down your head so heavily that the whole body sinks beneath it. A body weakened in its parts will return no honour, strength or soundness to the head in turn, but will be made to grow feeble [illegible] and to fall prostrate.

units.la: Optimè Prærogativam tuam exercebis & ostendes si relaxes Legum magis quàm intendas rigorem, cùm Tyrannide ex Lege agente, nil deterius.
units.tr: You will best exercise and show your prerogative if you relax the rigour of the laws rather than stretch it, since nothing is worse than tyranny that acts through the law.

units.la: In his duobus præcipuis conservatione Religionis stabilitæ & Legum, puto Me minimè vanum futurum, si dixero probra ista in Me coram Mundo congesta in Martyrii honorem apud Conscientiam meam cessura, cùm hi Regni Mei perturbatores nihil aliud fere contra Me afferunt, quàm quod Leges & Religionem Sancitam Novationibus Illorum prætulerim.
units.tr: On these two chief points, the preservation of the established religion and of the laws, I think I shall not be vain if I say that those reproaches heaped upon me before the world will, to my conscience, serve rather to my honour as a martyr. For the disturbers of my kingdom bring against me almost nothing else than that I have preferred the laws and the sanctioned religion to their innovations.

units.la: Id enim facio revera, & semper faciam dum potioribus argumentis convincar, quàm quibus hactenus Me oppugnârunt Turbis, Præliis, Carceribus.
units.tr: Indeed I do this, and I always shall, until I am convinced by stronger arguments than those with which they have so far attacked me: tumults, battles, prisons.

units.la: Illud nondum intelligo, nec tibi unquam spero fore persuasum: Tutum esse Regi in cujuscunque Factionis gratiam turbare Leges, in quibus res maximè Publica, & Bonum Populi involvitur.
units.tr: This I do not yet understand, nor do I hope it will ever be made plain to you: that it is safe for a king to disturb the laws, in which the very public affairs and the good of the people are involved, to gratify any faction whatever.

units.la: Quid de Me Deus facturus est, vel quâ Me tandem ratione his (quas à Subditis Meis iniquissimè, ab illo juste patior) ærumnis expediet, adhuc ignoro, nec sum admodum sollicitus quid injuriæ mihi fiat ab hominibus, dum quod rectum videtur coram Deo retineam.
units.tr: What God will do with me, or by what means he will at last bring me out of these troubles (which I suffer most unjustly at the hands of my subjects, but justly at his), I still do not know. Nor am I much anxious about what wrong is done to me by men, so long as I keep what seems right before God.

units.la: Ultro omnia largiebar ad Reformationem aut securitatem necessaria, quæ Honestas, Conscientia, Ratio permisit, ea solum excipiens in quæ consentire non possum sine Summa Animæ Meæ, tum Ecclesiæ & Populi injuria, tum in Te præcipuè proximum Regnorum & indubitatum Hæredem.
units.tr: I have freely granted everything needful for reformation or for security that honour, conscience and reason allowed, excepting only those things to which I cannot consent without grave injury to my own soul, and to the Church and the people, and above all to you, the next heir of the kingdoms and their undoubted successor.

units.la: Ad quæ si post excessum meum Te Divina Providentia (cui nil arduum omnino) perduxerit, id imprimis moneo & præcipio, ut seriò tecum velis perpendere superiores illas seu veras seu imputatas malorum causas, ut sic melius in posterum effugias.
units.tr: If, after my death, divine providence (for which nothing is at all difficult) brings you to these matters, I above all advise and charge you to weigh earnestly with yourself those former causes of evils, whether true or imputed, so that you may the better escape them in future.

units.la: Nunquam ita cujusquam Consilio, Prudentiâ, Fide nitaris in rebus illis Primæ Magnitudinis Pietate scilicet & Justitia, ut Judicio tuo proprio diffidas vel aliis causam des suspicandi, cum verisimile sit multo Te rectius & firmius Coronæ & Regni commodis, quam quenquam alium velle consulere.
units.tr: Never so rely on the counsel, prudence or fidelity of anyone in those matters of first importance, namely piety and justice, that you distrust your own judgement or give others cause to suspect you. For it is probable that you will wish to look after the interests of the Crown and the kingdom far more rightly and firmly than anyone else.

units.la: Caye ne ullam Factionem irrites acerbitate quorundam & pervicacia, quos huic curæ præfeceris, qui affectibus suis nimium & proprio animi impetu acti, vel nonnullâ opinionum discrepantiâ in rebus levioribus (extima tantum Ora & Suburbiis Religionis) in rigidiora forsan asperantur.
units.tr: Take care not to provoke any faction by the harshness and obstinacy of certain men whom you put in charge of this business, who, driven too much by their own passions and by the impulse of their own minds, or by some difference of opinion in lesser matters (only the outer edges and suburbs of religion), may perhaps grow more rigid.

units.la: Siquidē hîc leniter connivendo & Christiana Charitate tolerando facile vires eorum infirmābis quas pertinaciùs obluctando confirmas: dum pars contempta & oppressa in eas semper conspirationes ire promptior, unde sint meliùs expleturi illam vindictæ libidinem in Illos suos, ut vocant, Persequutores, in qua præsto opitularur Vulgi miseratio, in eos semper propensi qui videntur Religionis causâ dura pati.
units.tr: For if you wink leniently here and tolerate in Christian charity, you will easily weaken the strength of those whom you confirm by opposing them too stubbornly. The party that is despised and oppressed is always more ready to conspire, whence they will be the better able to satisfy that lust for revenge against those whom they call their persecutors, and in which the pity of the common crowd gives them ready help, for the crowd is always inclined towards those who seem to suffer harshly for the sake of religion.

units.la: Illud interim videndum, ut hoc fiat in ejusmodi Discrepantiis quæ nec Legibus præfractè nec Politiæ adversantur, nec Fundamenta Religionis constitutæ (quod omninò non serendum) oppugnant.
units.tr: Meanwhile it must be seen to that this is done in such differences as neither stubbornly oppose the laws nor are hostile to the polity, and do not attack the established fundamentals of religion (which must by no means be tolerated).

units.la: Semper solidam pietatem, & Fundamentaler illas Veritates queis & Corda & Vitæ emendantur, integra prorsus Justitiâ nec favore minùs propugnes.
units.tr: Always defend, with complete justice and no less favour, solid piety and those fundamental truths by which hearts and lives are amended.

units.la: Vide ne illæ in Sacris Circumstantiæ & exterior Religionis Forma omnia præmia doctrinæ industriæ & pietatis auferant, quin integerrimo oculo & manu dispertiantur in omnes probitate & scientia laudatos.
units.tr: See to it that those circumstances of sacred matters and the external form of religion do not take away all rewards from learning, industry and piety, but rather that they be distributed with the most upright eye and hand among all those praised for integrity and knowledge.

units.la: Ita Corda tibi optimorum & plurimorum etiam conciliabis, qui etiamsi non sint optimi, tamen satis delectantur, cum sic asperi calles virtutis sæcularibus præmiis levigentur.
units.tr: In this way you will win over the hearts of the best and of the many, who, even if they are not the best, are nevertheless sufficiently pleased when the rough paths of virtue are smoothed by worldly rewards.

units.la: Vides Me diversis factionibus & inter se pugnantibus conflictatum (ita enim revera appellandæ sunt, quæ constitutis in Ecclesia & Statu refragantur) qui, ut primùm Communes Adversarios (id est omnes Mihi & Legibus adhærentes) expugnaverant, statim mutuis ita inter se æmulationibus scindebantur, ut essent multo plùs invicem quàm Illis Primis suis Hostibus infensi.
units.tr: You see that I have been harassed by various factions, fighting among themselves (for that is truly what they must be called, those which oppose what is established in Church and State). As soon as they had overcome their common enemies (that is, all who cling to me and to the laws), they were at once so split by mutual rivalries that they were far more hostile to one another than to those first enemies.

units.la: Tempus hæc aliquando dissipabit, cùm Privat Ambitus & Avaritiæ exerent se tandem & emicabunt dura Cornua nuper molli Illo Pictatis [?], Reformationis, Libertatis involucro abscondita. Pari sint utcunque sævitiâ, justiori tamen Odio prosequimur quos in Ovium Vestimentis Lupos deprehendimus.
units.tr: Time will one day scatter these things, when private ambition and avarice at last put forth and thrust out the hard horns that have lately been hidden under that soft cloak of piety, reformation, liberty. Yet, however equal their savagery, we pursue with a more just hatred those whom we find to be wolves in sheep's clothing.

units.la: Quod ad delusum vulgus attinet, qui meræ Cordis simplicitate opportuni magis fiunt huic fraudi, id te monitum volo, ut (quemadmodum non est eadem tibi cum aliis necessitas simulato & vafrè agendi, ita) vera pietate & virtute & constanti in Populum bonitate, eos omnes superare contendas qui hæc maximè amant ostentare: sic enim nec deprendi metuës (quæ illos semper exercet sollicitudo qui personati vivunt) nec justas Spes Populi frustraveris, quas majores merito reponent in vera Principis Virtute, quàm cujuscunque factiosa Novitate.
units.tr: As for the deluded common people, who through the simplicity of their hearts are more easily made victims of this fraud, I want you to be warned that, just as you do not have the same need as others to act by pretence and cunning, so you should strive by true piety, virtue and constant goodness towards the people to surpass all those who love most to display these things. For thus you will neither fear being detected (which worries those who live in masks) nor will you frustrate the just hopes of the people, which they will rightly place in the true virtue of a prince rather than in the factious novelty of anyone whatever.

units.la: Cum-vero has Moles Factionum velut Montes gelu horridos, radiis Divinæ Misericordiæ & virtutis Tuæ splendore solveris penitus & colliquaveris, & vulgus hactenus delusum intellexerit nullos magis fortunis & conscientiis suis inimicos, quàm qui se vindices præcipuos & Patronos jactant eo tantum consilio ut in utrasque invadant, cave ne ullâ animi impotentiâ ultionem in eos mediteris, quos peccatum suum & stultitia satis castigabit.
units.tr: When you have wholly dissolved and melted these masses of factions, which stand rough with frost like mountains, by the rays of divine mercy and the splendour of your virtue, and when the common people, hitherto deluded, have come to understand that no men are more hostile to their fortunes and consciences than those who boast that they are the chief avengers and patrons of them, and do so with the sole aim of invading both, take care that you do not, in any unrestrained passion of mind, plan revenge against those whom their own sin and folly will punish well enough.

units.la: Cum autem hanc Factionum & æmulantium invicem studiorum venenatam cuspidem eduxeris, omni Arte Regiâ & Clementiâ ad medicanda hæc vulnera incumbas eo temperamento adhibito ut non sit dolor remedii morbo æqualis.[?]
units.tr: When you have drawn out the poisoned point of this faction and of the rival zeals against one another, apply yourself with all royal art and clemency to healing these wounds, using such moderation that the pain of the remedy is not equal to the disease.

units.la: Ultro detuli Impunitatem & Amnestiam tàm amplam ut vel omnes complecteretur qui se Legi obnoxios dubitarent, & futuras suspiciones & metus excluderet.
units.tr: I have already offered an indemnity and an amnesty so broad that it would embrace all who doubted whether they were liable to the law, and would shut out future suspicions and fears.

units.la: Quem à Te etiam observari morem cupio, quoties hæc vel petunt homines vel sint parati accipere, ut eo modo largiaris, quo non mera necessitate aut Politicis rationibus expressa, sed à Christiana Charitate voluntario profecta videantur.
