units.tr: I also wish you to observe this custom: whenever men either ask for these things or are ready to accept them, grant them in such a way that the gift appears not to be extorted by mere necessity or political reasons, but to have proceeded voluntarily from Christian charity.

units.la: Nihil Mihi aliud jam superest nisi posse condonare etiam iis qui Me omnibus spoliârunt, atque hîc Dei gratiam agnosco, quod sim animo in hoc paratissimo, nec Me minus consolatur hæc Gratia, quam quæ unquam Deus dedit jucundissima, cùm sit Divini in Me Amoris certius indicium, quàm ulla in rebus secundis fœlicitas.
units.tr: Nothing more now remains for me except to be able to forgive even those who have stripped me of everything. In this I acknowledge the grace of God, that I am most ready in mind to do so; and this grace consoles me no less than any most joyful gift God has ever given, since it is a surer sign of divine love towards me than any happiness in prosperous circumstances.

units.la: Illud interim mecum credas velim, plærosque eorum qui deliquerint, nulla hæc prorsus malitia, sed.vel fálsis rumoribus deceptos, vel errore corruptos admisisse.
units.tr: Meanwhile I would have you believe, with me, that most of those who have done wrong committed it not out of any malice at all, but having been either deceived by false rumours or corrupted by error.

units.la: Atque adeo in futurum nullos arbitror fidum magis obsequium præstituros, quàm quos erroris sui & Iniquitatis conscios acres posthac agitabunt pœnitentiæ stimuli, & vehementius desiderium priores defectus compensandi.
units.tr: And so I think that in future none will show more faithful obedience than those whom the goads of repentance, pricking them sharply, will drive, conscious of their error and wrongdoing, and whom a stronger desire to make up for their past failings will drive.

units.la: Te verò ut fors tua sublimior non permittit in singulare certamen descendere, ita multum infra celsæ mentis indolem ducas[?] vindicta cogitare, vel in plures iram effundere.
units.tr: Since your lofty station does not permit you to descend into single combat, you will think it far beneath a noble mind to plan revenge or to pour out anger on many.

units.la: Quo magis conscius es animi omni Populum virtute demereri solliciti, eò obsequii eorum & amoris securior pœnam facile ob priora omittes: Plus synceræ haud dubio voluptatis capies uni alicui ignoscens, quàm si mille castigaveris.
units.tr: The more conscious you are of a mind anxious to win the people's favour by every virtue, the more securely, on account of their obedience and love, you will easily set aside punishment for past offences. Without doubt you will take more pure pleasure in pardoning one single person than if you had punished a thousand.

units.la: Hæc ad Te Scribo.neutiquam desperans de Divina in Te misericordia & Subditorum affectu, quod utrunque promeriturum confido, licet reverà apud Deum nihil, nisi Ipsius misericordia, mereamur.
units.tr: I write these things to you, by no means despairing of God's mercy towards you or of the affection of your subjects, both of which I trust will be earned, although in truth before God we deserve nothing except his own mercy.

units.la: Si id Deo expedire videatur, ut Me & Te illis restituat, quæ à Legi tributa eripi nobis per Subditos, sine atroci scelere non possunt, erit posthac in Pace opportunitas Te liberius paulo admonendi de iis quæ ad Dei Gloriam Tuum Honorem & Pacem Regnorum spectant. Sin ita res nostrae se habeant, ut nunquam faciem meam denuo tueri liceat (& Me Deus in hoc lævo carcere & tenebris (quod ad consummanda nonnullorum consilia unum deest) inhumari volucrit, ubi nullius benevoli alloquio nec conspectu frui datur) id enixe a Te peto & obtestor Patris jure & Regis, ut nihil inde offensiore sis[?] animo vel tantillum iniquiore in Religionem in Anglia stabilitam.
units.tr: If it seems expedient to God to restore Me and you to those rights which, due to the law, cannot be wrested from us by subjects without atrocious crime, then there will be an opportunity in peace to admonish you somewhat more freely about those things which concern God's glory, your honour and the peace of the kingdoms. But if our affairs stand so that I may never again look upon my face (and God wills that I be buried in this loathsome prison and darkness, which is all that is lacking to complete the schemes of some, where I am not permitted to enjoy the address or sight of any well-wisher), then I earnestly ask and beseech you, by the right of a father and a king, that you be in no way more offended in mind, or the least bit less favourable, towards the religion established in England.

units.la: Hanc enim serio exploravi, & post accuratam disquisitionem & plurima utrinque disceptata optimam omnium esse concludo, non in genere solum ut Christianam, sed speciatim insuper ut Reformatam; ut quæ mediam viam tenet inter pompam superstitiosæ Tyrannidis, & cerebrosæ Anarchiæ obscuritatem.
units.tr: For I have examined this seriously, and after careful inquiry and much debate on both sides I conclude that it is the best of all, not only in general as Christian, but also specifically as Reformed; as one which holds the middle way between the pomp of superstitious tyranny and the frenzied anarchy's obscurity.

units.la: Quod non ita tamen accipi velim, quasi non in primâ ejus delineatione, doctrinâ utcunque & disciplina eximiâ (id quod in aliis figuris contingit) expolitius posset. aliquid & limatius fieri: quod & factum fuisset leni manu adhibita, nisi præceps nonnullorum vecordia & vesani impetus eam feram mutationem postulassent, quæ lineamenta & formam confunderet.
units.tr: Yet I do not wish this to be taken as if, in its first outline, it could not be made somewhat more polished and refined in its doctrine and discipline, however excellent these are, as happens with other figures; and this would have been done with a gentle hand, had not the headlong folly and mad onslaught of some demanded a harsh change which would confound the outlines and form.

units.la: Quod vero a quibusdam objicitur, scandalum hic magnum fieri Religioni in Anglia, facile illis (vel saltem apud Te) refelles, si cogitaveris neminem fere eorum, qui hujus proximi Belli contra Me & Ecclesiam & Leges Authores aut incentores extitere, vel omnino amplexum hanc Doctrinam, vel ex Præscripto vixisse Protestantium in Anglia Professionis; quæ nec has tradit Regulas, nec ulla ostendit hujusmodi ante istos Exempla.
units.tr: As for what some object, that a great scandal is being caused here to religion in England, you will easily refute them (or at least in your own eyes) if you consider that hardly any of those who were the authors or instigators of this very recent war against me, the Church and the laws either wholly embraced this doctrine or lived by the rule of the Protestant profession in England; which neither teaches these rules nor shows any such examples before those men.

units.la: Verum est, eam & olim fuisse nonnullorum audaciam ut ferocius quædam à Principe & Parlamentis petierint, ea obscure minitantes, quæ nunc isti (ejusdem farinæ, sed deteriori spiritu) exequuntur. Cave interim ne ob fictum antiquorum & rabiosum Zelum quicquam veræ pietati detraxeris, ex Fructu enim utrunque dignosces, nec ideo Vini, aut Ficus aspernanda suavitas, quia cardui forsan & vepres hos fructus ostentant, ut arboribus cæteris dominentur.
units.tr: It is true that some have long had the audacity to demand more fiercely certain things from the Prince and the Parliaments, threatening obscurely those things which now these men (of the same stamp but with a worse spirit) carry out. Beware, meanwhile, lest on account of the feigned and frenzied zeal of the old ones you detract anything from true piety; for you will know both by their fruit. Nor is the sweetness of wine or figs to be scorned because thistles and brambles perhaps display these fruits so that they may dominate the other trees.

units.la: Quin nec à Parlamentis propterea abhorrendum censeo, à quibus rite constitutis (Libertate sua & Honore incolumi) nulla fiet Majestatis diminutio, sed occasio potius subministrabitur mutuis invicem officiis certandi, amorisque & obsequii & fiduciæ commercia inter Principem & Populum exercendi.
units.tr: Nor do I think that one should therefore abhor the Parliaments, from which, when rightly constituted (their Liberty and Honour intact), no diminution of majesty will come; rather, an occasion will be given for vying with each other in mutual services, and for carrying on exchanges of love, obedience and trust between the Prince and the People.

units.la: Quod haud dubie evenisset in hoc Nigro Parlamento (licet primis Electionibus multo ambitu corruptis) si ab insolentia vulgi, & Tumultuantium Magisterio immunius se conservasset, quorum tristi exitu admonitos spero in posterum futuros sollicitiores in tuenda Liberrate & Dignitate (quæ ejusmodi decet Conventus, & tum demum futura cum hoc vulgi jugum projecerint) cum res publica in Principis simul & Populi communi Bono versatur.
units.tr: This would undoubtedly have happened in this Black Parliament (although it was corrupted in the first elections by much canvassing) if it had kept itself more free from the insolence of the crowd and the mastery of rioters. I hope that, warned by their sad end, they will in future be more careful in protecting liberty and dignity (which befit such an assembly, and which will only be secure once they have thrown off this yoke of the mob), since the commonwealth turns on the common good of the Prince and the People alike.

units.la: Ut cedat optimè universis, nulla melius ac[?]tione efficietur, quam si æquo, honesto & gravi more Omnes simul consilia in commune conferant, publico omnia consensu agantur sine Tumultu & Tyrannide, non enim ideo nos fame necare oportet, quia salubres cibi nonnullis in nauseam & morbum vertuntur.
units.tr: So that all may turn out for the best, nothing will be more effective than that everyone, in a fair, honest and serious manner, bring their counsels together for the common good, and that everything be done by universal public consent, without tumult and tyranny. For we ought not to starve ourselves to death because wholesome foods turn to nausea and sickness in some people.

units.la: Sin eò res devenerit, ut in Jura nostra Regia nunquam amplius restituamur, & id scilicet vera Dei Justitia poscente perstituri [?] sint usque Subditi Mei in peccatis suis, & prospero scelere deludendi: Spero Gratiam Divinam id in Te & Me effecturam, ut simus æque carendo Diademati ac gestando pares; quod profecto tanti non est ut inhonestis, sordidis, & impiis conditionibus aut servari mereatur, aut ab humo sustolli. Firmus Pietati & Virtuti maneas, nunquam Regnum deerit.
units.tr: But if things come to the point that we are never restored to our royal rights, and, as true divine justice demands, my subjects remain in their sins and are to be deluded by prosperous wickedness, I hope that divine grace will bring it about in you and me that we are as equal in lacking the diadem as in wearing it. This is truly not so great a thing that it deserves to be preserved by dishonourable, base and impious conditions, or to be raised up from the ground. Remain firm in piety and virtue, and the kingdom will never be lacking.

units.la: In hoc vero potissimum Honori tuo consules, quo omne promptius reverentiam & amorem detuleris, & in præsidium porro te stiteris Uxori Meæ, Matri Tuæ, de Me plurimis nominibus optime meritæ, & in his præcipue, quæ (cum Me tot prius liberis summæ spei auxisset, quos omnes unà cum Matre Amori Tuo & fidei commendo) raro magnanimitatis & Patientiæ exemplo pro Me & Te simul & nobiscum unà perpessa est.
units.tr: In this especially you will consult your honour, by which you will more readily win all reverence and love, and you will stand forth as a protection for my wife and your mother, who has deserved very well of me in many respects, and especially in this: that, although she had already enriched me with so many children of highest promise, all of whom I commend to your love along with your mother, she has suffered alongside me, with magnanimity and patience rarely matched, for me and you together and with us both.

units.la: Deum Omnipotentem veneror quicquid de Me facturus est, qui Innocentiâ Meâ & illius Gratiâ involvor satis & munior, ut te An-choram protollat vel potius Calamitofis his Regnis & dura Hyeme jactatis utque tuâ demum Prudentiâ, Iustitia, Pietate restaures, quæ stultitia quorundam & nequitia ita pene pessum dederunt ut nil integrum in Ecclesia vel Statu reliquerint, nil Coronæ, Proceribus, Clero, Communitati, nil quod ad Leges, Libertates, Fortunas attinet, quod ad Ordinem, Honorem, Conscientiam & Vi-tam.
units.tr: I venerate Almighty God, whatever he is about to do with me, for I am sufficiently wrapped in and fortified by my innocence and his grace. May he raise you up as an anchor, or rather, for these kingdoms battered by calamity and a harsh winter, may you by your prudence, justice and piety restore what the folly and wickedness of some have so nearly destroyed that they have left nothing whole in the Church or the State: nothing of the Crown, the Peers, the Clergy or the Commons; nothing that pertains to laws, liberties or fortunes; nothing to order, honour, conscience and life.

units.la: Sin vero Me penitus extinxerint, (haud enim scio an huc quoque processura sit hostium malitia & furor, & ex dictis quorundam & factis non obscura suspicio) quamvis illud non dubitandum, exclamaturum meum sanguinem ad Cœlos usque ob vindictam, Deum tamen obtestor, ne iram suam velit in illam maximam partem effundere, qui fraude & artificio & simulata Ducum Sanctitate decepti: quos interno prius horrore cruciatos manet atrox aliquando supplicicium.
units.tr: But if they have utterly extinguished me (for I do not know whether the malice and fury of the enemies may go even this far, and from certain sayings and deeds of some there is no obscure suspicion of it), then, although there is no doubt that my blood will cry out to heaven for vengeance, I nevertheless beseech God not to wish to pour out his wrath on that greatest part of them who were deceived by fraud, trickery and the feigned holiness of their leaders. A harsh punishment awaits them at some time, after they have first been tormented by inner horror.

units.la: Cæteris in Me optimè affectis, nihil sit (Deum precor) quod Me extinctum desiderent, ita valde voveo & spero, ut Virtutes Tuæ conspectæ in fœlicitatem omnibus sufficiant.
units.tr: As for the rest, who are very well disposed towards me, let there be nothing (I pray God) that would make them long for my death. So greatly do I wish and hope this, that the virtues of yours, seen by all, will suffice for the happiness of everyone.

units.la: Eos vero quos perperam in Me admissorum poenitentia subierit, (ut jam lubens condono verbo Christiani Regis) ita in posterum non dubito quin sis vere fideles habiturus, amoremque & obsequium Mihi debitum promptos Tibi cum fœnore rependere.
units.tr: As for those whom the repentance for wrongs committed against me has brought back (as I now gladly pardon, in the words of a Christian King), I do not doubt that in future you will have them truly faithful, and that they will readily repay to you, with interest, the love and obedience owed to me.

units.la: Breviter, quicquid ego mente agitavi bonum Tu perficias, cùm Facultatem Deus dederit; multa palam tuli Me facturum, plura facere volebam, si Tempora fuissent secundiora.
units.tr: In brief, whatever good I have devised in mind, may you carry out, when God gives you the ability. I bore many things openly, and I would have done more if the times had been more favourable.

units.la: Fraus ista statim evanescet, & persona passim dilabetur. Nec iste fucus & larva Religionis (quâ se hactenus texit Rebellio) amplius horum turpitudinem & dehonestamenta velabit: Satis enim haec mea detentio, & inhumana tractatio demonstrant quàm sint de Me hi homines (quod ita valdè simulabant) solliciti.
units.tr: That deceit will immediately vanish, and the persona will slip away everywhere. Nor will this mask and false face of religion (under which rebellion has hitherto covered itself) any longer conceal their baseness and disgrace. For this my detention and inhuman treatment show plainly how anxious these men (who pretended so greatly) are about me.

units.la: Fœliciora Te (ut spero) exspectant Tempora; cùm calamitate sua edocti Subditi idjam[?] verum repererint, pietatem in Deum & in Regem Fidem haud posse sine peccato & miseria divelli.
units.tr: Happier times (as I hope) await you, when your subjects, taught by their calamity, will at last have discovered that piety towards God and towards the King, and faith, cannot be separated without sin and misery.

units.la: Deus Tibi benedicat, & in Justitia Regna, in Vera Religione animam, in amore Dei & affectu Populi tui Honorem tuum semper stabiliat.
units.tr: May God bless you, and may He always establish your honour: your kingdoms in justice, your soul in true religion, and your standing in the love of God and the affection of your people.

units.la: Sin Ille meo interitu consummandam hanc eorum perfidiam voluerit, sit memoria Mei & nomen in Te usque superstes, ut Patris Tui Amantissimi, & trium Florentissimorum Regnorum Regis, quem Deo ornare placuerat non Sceptro solium & Imperio, sed ea porro dignitate, ut plurimas contumelias Ipsius causa perpessus immatura tandem morte raperer, dum illud unice studuerim ut Jura Ecclesiae, vim Legum, Privilegia Parlamentorum & Libertates Populi conservarem, & Conscientiam Meam, insuper mille Regnis chariorem.
units.tr: But if He wills that this treachery of theirs be brought to completion by my death, may the memory of me and my name survive in you, as the name of your most loving Father and King of three most flourishing kingdoms, whom God was pleased to adorn not with a sceptre, a throne and empire only, but with such dignity that, having suffered many insults on its account, I was at last snatched away by an untimely death, while I studied above all else to preserve the rights of the Church, the force of the laws, the privileges of the Parliaments and the liberties of the people, and my conscience, which I hold dearer than a thousand kingdoms.

units.la: Scio Deum posse (spero etiam & velle) Me restituere; nec de Illius misericordia, nec de Populi Mei amore & miseratione desperabo.
units.tr: I know that God is able (and I hope and trust that He is willing) to restore me; nor will I despair either of His mercy or of my people's love and compassion.

units.la: Eveniat licet quod pessimum; Id saltem confido Me Tibi in multo melius Regnum praecessurum; quod Deus mihi, & Me illi praeparavit per Servatorem meum Iesum Christum, cuius misericordiae Te & Omnes Meos commendo.
units.tr: Let whatever is worst come to pass; this at least I trust, that I shall go before you to a kingdom far better than yours, which God has prepared for me and me for Him through my Saviour Jesus Christ, to whose mercy I commend you and all my people.

units.la: Vale; dum sit rursus congrediundi copia, si non in Terris, at in Cœlis.
units.tr: Farewell; until there is again an opportunity of meeting, if not on earth, then in heaven.

units.la: 28: Meditationes de Morte, postquam Domus utraq; de- nunciasset, nil amplius cum Rege Tractan- dum, & de Arctiori ejus Custodia in Arce Carisbrokiana.
units.tr: Meditations on Death, after both Houses had denounced him, nothing more was to be dealt with by the King, and concerning his closer custody in Carisbrooke Castle.

units.la: Superest jam satis otii & nimis-causæ ut de Morte mediter, & Me illi parem: Pauci enim admodum passus restant inter Carceres Principum & Sepulchra.
units.tr: There now remains enough leisure and too much reason for me to meditate on death and to make myself its equal, for only a very few paces remain between the prisons of princes and their sepulchres.

units.la: Quòd hoc spatium cogitandi habeo, Dei indulgentia est: quod hanc tristem occasionem, hominum sævitia.
units.tr: That I have this space for thinking is by God's indulgence; that this sad occasion comes from human savagery.

units.la: Præter enim commune illud omnibus Mortalatis onus, ea insuper accedunt dura onera, queis Me premunt aliorum Ambitiones, Timores, Suspiciones, cæteræque impotentium animorum sævæ perturbationes, queis livore & odio efferatis etiam Vita sua foret insuavis, si quid esset quod in Mea delectaret.
units.tr: Besides that common burden laid on all mortals, there are added these hard burdens, with which the ambitions of others, their fears, suspicions, and the other savage disturbances of impotent minds press upon me. Enraged by envy and hatred, they would find their own life unpleasant too, if there were anything in mine that could delight them.

units.la: Deo Gratias habeo, nec in fecundis meis nova erat mihi hæc Meditatio, nunquam importuna existimanda, cum sint illa tam incerta: Est enim Mors Ecclipsis ejusmodi, quæ in sudo æque fit ac in nubilo Tempore.
units.tr: I thank God that, even in my prosperous days, this meditation was not new to me, and it should never be thought untimely, since those things are so uncertain. For death is an eclipse of such a kind that it happens in clear weather just as much as in cloudy weather.

units.la: Meæ vero diuturnæ & acerbissimæ ærumnæ illos natura hostes infensissimos Vitam & Mortem apud Me reduxerunt in gratiam. Illo Terrore communi prorsus liberor, & isti mihi peculiares horrores multum jam mitigantur: licet enim Mors mea tetra illa & horribili specie appareat, qua Me maxime percellere omni æstu nituntur Hostes isti feri & implacabiles, qui jam de fæce hauriunt quicquid est virulentiæ exprimentes: Deo tamen semper laus sit, hæc contemplor ut aspera quidem spicula, sed non veneno mortifera, cum vel hæc Redemptor Meus Ipse jam extraxerit, vel suæ Mortis porrexerit salutare Antidotum: quæ ut immatura, injusta, pudenda, probris omnibus & ludibriis exposita, superavit quicquid possum timere.
units.tr: But my long and most bitter troubles have reconciled to me those enemies, by nature most hostile, Life and Death. I am quite freed from that common terror, and those horrors peculiar to me are now much mitigated. For although my death appears in that grim and dreadful form with which these fierce and implacable enemies strive most of all to strike me down, drawing from the dregs whatever virulence remains, still, may God always be praised. I regard these as sharp darts, indeed, but not deadly with poison, since my Redeemer Himself has now drawn out the poison, or has offered the saving antidote of His own death. That death, though untimely, unjust, shameful, and exposed to every reproach and mockery, has overcome whatever I can fear.

units.la: Nunquam ita experimento didiceram, quàm sit Bona Conscientia convivium, vel quid valeat murus aheneus sani & integri animi Constantiæ, quam in hoc congressu propiori, ubi manu conferta cum hac Mortis Meditatione dimicavi.
units.tr: I had never learned by experience so well how much a good conscience is a feast, or what the brazen wall of a sound and whole spirit's constancy is worth, as in this closer encounter, where I fought, shoulder to shoulder with that resolve, against this meditation on death.

units.la: Non tam diu vixi, ut vitæ tædeat, nec tàm male ( opinor ) ut vel pudeat vivere, vel pertimescam mori: verum est, in iis Me malis versari, ut sit abunde aliquando cur cupiam mori, nisi illud cogitarem maximam eam esse Christianæ vitæ gloriam mori quotidie, dum fide viva & spe vitæ melioris vincit illas mortes quotidianas, queis sic per partes occidimur, & simus indies nobis ipsis superstites; id enim revera mors est, Salute, Honore, Libertate privari, & solatiis eorum qui sunt nobis charissimi, & vitæ vita.
units.tr: I have not lived so long that I am weary of life, nor so badly (I think) that I should be ashamed to live or dread to die. It is true that I am in such troubles that at some time there will surely be cause enough for me to wish to die, were it not that I reflect that the greatest glory of the Christian life is to die daily. By living faith and hope of a better life, one conquers those daily deaths by which we are slain piece by piece, and we are every day survivors of ourselves. For this is truly death: to be deprived of safety, honour, and liberty, and of the comforts of those who are dearest to us, and of life itself.

units.la: Vitam meam quidem ( cùm Rex sim ) in nullâ æquè re humana arbitror ac in Populi amore ac benevolentia sitam, ob quam mille mortes subii, atque adeo spero Me non hìc penitus interiisse: id tamen aggressi sunt Hostes mei mendaciorum veneno & vi Armatâ, illum mihi primum Subditorum amorem & obsequium jugulare, & mox cuncta vitæ Gaudia, quæ ex his potissimum percepi.
units.tr: My life (since I am a king) I think rests in nothing human so much as in the love and goodwill of the people, for which I have undergone a thousand deaths; so I hope I have not utterly perished here. Yet my enemies have attacked this with the poison of lies and with armed force, seeking first to cut my throat, namely the love and obedience of my subjects, and soon after all the joys of life which I have chiefly received from these.

units.la: Paruam jam mihi vitæ reliquerunt; nucleus tantum & puramen superest quod à cæteris malitia auferatur, cùm sint omnia mihi extincta sòlatia, quæ mihi vitam reddant expetibilem.
units.tr: They have already left me only a small life; only the kernel and the chaff remain, which malice has not taken from the rest, since all the consolations that could make life desirable to me have been extinguished.

units.la: Ne vero (Anima mea) ne vitam illam vel dolore nimiam, vel molestam tædio putes, in qua Deus occasiones suppeditat si non agendi at ferendi eâ Christianâ Patientiâ in Bona Causa & forti animo, unde maximum vitæ decus, & è morte lucrum accedat.
units.tr: But lest you think, my soul, that this life is too excessive in pain or too troublesome in weariness, know that God supplies occasions in it, if not for acting, at least for enduring with Christian patience in a good cause and with a brave spirit. From this comes the greatest honour of life and gain from death.

units.la: Christianam enim fortitudinem si quis recte æstimet, pusilli est animi mori cupere, quia tædet vivere, & quo vacui arguimur illa vere Heroicâ & Christiano digna Celsitudine quæ se optime ostendit in has fortiter ærummnas sustinendo, quæ, quamdiu in hoc Corpore versamur, semper Nos velut umbra consectantur, contractiores nonnunquam aut purrectiores, prout sol rerum secundarum vel in Meridiem ascendit vel in occasum declinat, qui, cum totus abfuerit, rore Cœli optime compensatur.
units.tr: For if anyone rightly weighs Christian fortitude, it is the mark of a small spirit to desire to die because one is weary of living. By this we are convicted of lacking that truly heroic and Christian loftiness which best shows itself in bravely bearing these troubles. As long as we dwell in this body, they always pursue us like a shadow, sometimes shorter and sometimes longer, according as the sun of prosperous things either climbs to the south or declines to the west. When that sun is wholly absent, it is best made up for by the dew of heaven.

units.la: Sunt quidem Afflictiones, velut ille Sampsonis Leo, primo suo Insultu terribiles, sed à quibus suavitatem expresserit qui hic audet colluctari, & vincere, nec ægro nimis animo & imbecilli ferat superesse his Cucurbitis marcescentibus, dum cum Deo versari permittatur.
units.tr: Afflictions, indeed, like Samson's lion, are terrible at their first onset, yet he who dares to wrestle with them here and conquer them squeezes out sweetness from them. Nor should a sick and feeble spirit think it too much to remain under these gourds that wither, while it is permitted to dwell with God.

units.la: Me quandoque moriturum (ut Hominem) certissimum; posse Me Regem mori, manu Subditorum (violentâ, repentinâ, sævâ[?] Morte, in robusta ætate, in medio Regnorum, spectantibus Amicis, nec auxilium ferre valentibus, & Triumphantibus Inimicis & Illudentibus Vivo, Morienti, Mortuo,) tot sunt simul Argumenta cur fiat valde credibile, ut vix sperare ab Hominibus meliora Deus jubeat, licet ab Illius misericordia nil despe-rem..
units.tr: That I, as a man, am most certainly to die some time; that I, a king, could die by the hand of my subjects, by a violent, sudden, savage death, in robust age, in the midst of my realms, with friends looking on and unable to bring help, and enemies triumphing and mocking the living, the dying, and the dead: so many arguments together make it very credible that God bids us hope for nothing better from men. Yet from His mercy I despair of nothing.

units.la: Novi vitam meam, à Malitia Diaboli, & impiorum hominum unicum jam diu scopum peti, esse tamen sub Dei custodia, cui, non ideo ut vitam longiorem eblandiar, sic Me volo ostendere paratum mori, sed ab Ipso humiliter pendere cupio, & Me totum Illius voluntati tum in Vita tum in Morte (quocunque eas ordine dispensare placuerit) submittere. Arduum fateor negotium tot diversis Mortis horroribus (queis Me Deus tentari permittit) sed pari omnibus atrocitate conflictari, dum vel furores cogitem repentinæ trucidationis: vel illas Iudiciorum Formas, quas forsan Hostes mei (non secus ac Illi Christi interfectores) sunt usurpaturi, ut solennmore[?] quadam truculentia per hæc Justitiæ ludibria Malitiam suam confummeant: quod tamen astu necessario ideo forsan sunt facturi, ut hæc Pompa percuntis minus mei misereantur homines, in quem ut Noxium animadverti ex Jure credent (Principem videlicet à Subditis!) Ipsi interim non ignorantes nullam Divinam aut Humanam Legem hoc Illis concedere, ut sine Me in quempiam alium, nedum in Me quicquam statuant, quique omnibus Sacris (coram Deo & hominibus) vinculis Me tueri obligati, jam Perjurium suum quæ runt hoc Iustitiæ pallio obtegere.
units.tr: I know that my life has long been the one aim of the Devil's malice and of wicked men, yet it lies under God's keeping. I do not want to flatter myself with a longer life, but I wish to show Him that I am ready to die. I desire to depend humbly on Him and to submit myself wholly to His will, both in life and in death, in whatever order He is pleased to dispose them. I admit it is a hard task to struggle with equal dread against so many diverse horrors of death, by which God permits me to be tempted, when I think of the fury of a sudden slaughter, or of those forms of judgment which my enemies, no differently from Christ's killers, are perhaps going to adopt, so that with a certain solemn savagery they may complete their malice through these mockeries of justice. Yet they will perhaps do this deliberately, so that men may feel less pity for this pomp of one who is perishing, whom they believe they rightly punish as a guilty man, namely a prince by his subjects! Meanwhile they themselves are not unaware that no divine or human law grants them this, that they should decide anything without me, much less against me. They are bound to protect me by every sacred tie, before God and men, and now they seek to cover their perjury with this cloak of justice.

units.la: Misera sane conditio, ut quis Hostes suos habeat Accusatores, Actores, Iudices, sed illa omnium deploratissima, ut hæc Subditorum insolentia in Regem audeat, eorumque qui rei hujus cladis maximè, Mei sanguinis effusione suas volunt lavare ab Illo tanto cruore innoxio, cujus nunc coram Deo & hominibus (& in conscientiis suis credo) clarè damnantur, iniquissima illa postulat.z Turbus primum, mox Armis prosecuti. Nec ex ulla; fere causa magis viles & abjecti homines tam ferociter plerumque & timida quadam sævitia exercent usurpatam in legitimos Dominos potestatem, quàm conscientiâ injustè usurpatæ: jactent quicquid velint de Justitia in Delinquentes, vetera illa figmenta & larvas ad celanda illa horrida & monstrosa consilia, qui Jus & Fructum Vineæ obtinere alias non poterant, ni Hærede dejecto & interfecto.
units.tr: A wretched condition indeed, that someone should have his enemies as accusers, prosecutors, and judges. But the most desperate of all is that this insolence of subjects dares to act against the king, and that those who most want to wash their guilt in this disaster by the shedding of my blood, that great innocent blood whose guilt they are now clearly condemned for, before God and men (and I believe in their own consciences), demand this most unjust thing: first by tumults, then pursued by arms. Nor do men who are almost any more vile and abject exercise power usurped over lawful lords with such fierce and timidly savage cruelty than those whose consciences tell them the power was unjustly usurped. Let them boast as much as they like about justice against offenders, and use those old fictions and masks to hide their horrid and monstrous plans, since otherwise they could not obtain the right and fruit of the vineyard unless the heir were cast out and killed.

units.la: Maximum apud Hos crimen meum est, quòd Verbo meo noluerim Me Ecclesiamque & Statum simul perdere, vel illis copiam facere ut hoc Gladio impune perficerent, qui ambitione & Avaritia immensâ nullis à Me concessis vel satiari, possunt unquam vel mansuefieri.
units.tr: My greatest crime in their eyes is that I would not, by my word, lose myself, the Church and the State together, nor allow them to accomplish it with impunity by this sword. Through immense ambition and avarice, they can never be satisfied or made gentle by anything I concede.

units.la: Nec credibile est illis unquam persuasum fore Regnum Illud Carduorum quòd à nonnullis erigitur (asperum, imbecille, sterile in Deum & homines) unquam alias posse efflorescere, nisi Regio eorum sanguine, quibus Jus ad Regnum, irrigetur.
units.tr: Nor is it credible that they will ever be persuaded that that Kingdom of Thistles, which some are raising up (rough, feeble, and barren toward God and men), can ever otherwise flourish, unless it is watered with the royal blood of those who have the right to the kingdom.

units.la: Dei fiat voluntas: haud ambigo quin Hunc sit olim habitura Innocentia Mea Præsidem sibi maximum & Patronum, qui jam solus Judex est, & quem solum agnosco Regum Regem, non Majestate solùm, & eminenti Potentia superiorem, sed peculiari magis cura & sollicitiori custodia illos ambientem, qui cùm sint maximi in Terris Iustitiæ, Legis, Religionis Vindices, tot periculis jacent obnoxii, quot sunt Homines, vel Dæmones qui hæc omnia volunt confundi.
units.tr: May the will of God be done. I do not doubt that my innocence will one day have Him as its greatest protector and patron, who alone is already the judge, and whom alone I acknowledge as King of Kings, superior not only in majesty and eminent power, but who also surrounds with a special care and a more watchful custody those who, though they are the greatest vindicators of justice, law and religion on earth, lie exposed to as many dangers as there are men, or demons, who wish all these things to be overthrown.

units.la: Verum non ita diu patietur Deus in Babele sua exaltari, qui hanc Regum ossibus exstruunt, & sanguine cæmentant.
units.tr: But God will not long suffer His Babel to be exalted, those who build this kingdom of the kings' bones and cement it with blood.

units.la: Vltores mortis meæ (certum habeo) interfeipsos [?] reperient, & quæ in Me fecerunt multa mala, pœnas olim ab Illis repetentes, qui in nulla alia re fuerunt quàm in his malis concordes.
units.tr: The avengers of my death (I am certain) will find themselves among themselves [?], and they will one day exact punishment from those who, agreeing in nothing else, were in agreement in these many evils they have done to me.

units.la: Clamor sanguinis mei non ferendus eo tandem impellet, ut nulla meliùs ratione expiandum credant, quàm eorum vicissim fundendo, qui meum juxta cum illis sitierunt.
units.tr: The cry of my blood, not to be borne, will at last drive them to believe that there is no better way to expiate it than by shedding in turn the blood of those who thirsted for mine together with them.

units.la: Quæ sit tristis omnium confusio interitum meum secutura, nimis certis argumentis præsagio ex his quæ dudum vidi in hoc Statu rerum afflictissimo: in quo Deus (qui solus potuit) sæpè causam meam asseruit [?], nec impune Illis esse permisit, quorum Confœderatio in scelere maximum hic videbatur præsidium; quibus causa est abunde cur metuant ne sit amplius illos distracturus, & ultione mutuâ perditurus.
units.tr: What sad confusion of all men will follow my death, I foresee with all too certain arguments from what I have long seen in this most afflicted state of affairs: in which God (who alone could) has often vindicated my cause [?], and has not allowed those to go unpunished whose confederacy seemed in their crime to be the greatest protection; they have ample cause to fear that He will scatter them further and destroy them by mutual vengeance.

units.la: Ego Mortem spero vincere Christi Virtute & Amore, qui Victoria Resurrectionis Suæ & Ascensionis Gloria Vim omnem Mortis absorpsit. Proximum mihi ingens solatium est, non mihi solum hunc honorem haberi, ut, exemplo Illius Justitiae causa patiar ( Tyrannidis utcunque & Injustitiae foedis criminibus aspersus) sed & vestigia sequar Charitatis, quae pulcherrima docet ratione & ulcisci hostes nostros & vincere. Hac ergo Dei gratia instructus & ignoscere illis possum, & precari, ne illis velit ulterius sanguinem meum imputare, quam hactenus tantum, ut intelligant quam valde opus habeant. Christi sanguine, ut sint puri nostro sic effuso.
units.tr: I hope to overcome Death by the virtue and love of Christ, who by the victory of His Resurrection and the glory of His Ascension swallowed up all the power of Death. My next great comfort is that this honour is granted me, that by the example of Him I suffer for the sake of justice (though stained with the foul charges of tyranny and injustice), and I also follow the footsteps of charity, which most beautifully teaches us by reason both to avenge ourselves on our enemies and to conquer them. Instructed therefore by this grace of God, I am able both to forgive them and to pray that He will not wish to impute to them my blood any further than hitherto, only so that they may understand how greatly they need the blood of Christ, that they may be made clean by ours thus shed.

units.la: Nullam aliam in praesens Hostes mei Regulam Justitiae praeter suam Voluntate agnoscunt: hanc Vi mensurant, successu urgent; in hoc enim sibi blandiuntur, tutor se fore meo periculo, & in mea morte suam vitam; illud interim non cogitantes, quod quemadmodum maxima ad peccandum tentamenta felicitatis quadam apparentia tecta saepius & involuta porriguntur, ita severam Dei iram maxime perfici, cum facinorosa sua consilia nefarii homines consummaverint.
units.tr: My enemies at present acknowledge no other rule of justice than their own will; they measure it by force and press it by success. For in this they flatter themselves that they will be safe at my peril, and that in my death lies their life; meanwhile not considering that, just as the greatest temptations to sin are most often offered covered and wrapped in a certain appearance of happiness, so the severe wrath of God is most fully accomplished when wicked men have carried out their criminal plans.

units.la: Deo gratias ago, haud magis enixe Me precari ut hoc a Me violentae Mortis acerbum poculum, quam ut ab Illis transfeat Iracundia, quos vel mei desertores sparsit sanguis meus, vel incumbentes aut assentientes Morti meae temeravit.
units.tr: I give thanks to God that I pray no more earnestly that this bitter cup of violent death may pass from me, than that wrath may pass from those whom my blood has scattered, either as my deserters, or has defiled as those who lean toward or assent to my death.

units.la: -Circumscripsit Dei voluntas, & conclusit Meam: Ea mihi in Morte voluptas, nullam e vindicta voluptatem capere; Hoc Christianum in Inimicos, Regem in Subditos decet*
units.tr: -The will of God has limited, and has enclosed mine: it is my pleasure in death to take no pleasure from revenge; this befits a Christian towards enemies, and a king towards subjects.

units.la: Nil Mihi possunt eripere, quod non libens amittam cum Deo visum fuerit per has manus adimere. Compensabit infinita sua Misericordia, queis nunc humana iniquitate æquum putat me privare.
units.tr: They cannot take from me anything which I will not willingly lose, when it has seemed good to God to take it away through these hands. His infinite mercy will make up for what they now think it right, through human iniquity, to deprive me of.

units.la: Decus Mortem sequuturum totum illud exsuperat, quo vel potiri hic poteram, vel cogitare.
units.tr: The honour that will follow death surpasses entirely all that I could either possess here or conceive.

units.la: Non illas graves amplius & invidiosas hujus Mundi Coronas desiderabo, cum Me Deus misericordia coronaverit, & in Gloria Gratias suas consummaverit, & hanc umbram Terrestrium Regnorum illo vere Cœlesti permutaverit.
units.tr: I shall not desire those heavy and envied crowns of this world any more, since God has crowned me with mercy, and has brought His graces to completion in glory, and has exchanged this shadow of earthly kingdoms for that truly heavenly one.

units.la: Quod ad Mundi probra, & imputatæ Tyrannidis calumnias, ipsa posthac Mei Interemptorum necessaria & acerba sævitia satis omnes per se confutabit.
units.tr: As for the reproaches of the world and the slanders of the tyranny imputed to me, the very necessary and bitter cruelty toward those who have murdered me will henceforth refute them all sufficiently by itself.

units.la: Horum interim qui optimi & cordatissimi sunt fidem salvam mihi & amorem manere non dubito, quorum multi Me lachrymis & precibus prosequuti sunt, libenter in meam gratiam vel mecum una morituri.
units.tr: Meanwhile I do not doubt that the best and most judicious of these men keep their faith and love for me intact; many of them have followed me with tears and prayers, willingly ready to die for my sake, or with me.

units.la: Excusabunt hi facile si qui fuerint lapsus humani, & nihilo minus officium suum ut Regi præstabunt, cum sit nulla tanta a Religione necessitas, quæ sub obtentu puniendi cogat Subditos omnia Principum crimina superare, quæ etiamsi fuisset, hic certe locum non habet, ubi tam prolixa in publicum compensatio facta est, quæque ne publice gauderetur privata Ambitio elusit:
units.tr: These will readily excuse, if there have been any human lapses, and nonetheless they will perform their duty to the King, since there is no such great necessity from religion that, under the pretext of punishing, it compels subjects to overlook all the crimes of princes; and even if there were, it certainly has no place here, where such a lengthy compensation has been made in public, and which private ambition has eluded, lest it be rejoiced over publicly:

units.la: Credo esse nonnullos manfuetioris ingenii, qui è ruina Mea minùs creverunt, qui jam stimulos aliquot asperiores & conscientiæ morsus sentiunt, cùm jam facinorum suorum effigiem, & lineamenta quasi expressa in similibus aliquot pœnis agnovere, qui certe vix sperare jam possunt pollices manuum & pedum integros sibi diù mansuros, qui (quasi ungues tantum præscesturi) mihi Robur maximum amputarunt.
units.tr: I believe there are some of gentler disposition, who have grown less from my ruin, who now feel some sharper goads and bites of conscience, since they have recognised in some similar punishments the likeness and almost the outlines of their own crimes; they can hardly hope that their thumbs and toes will remain whole for long, they who (as if about to cut off only the nails) have amputated my greatest strength.

units.la: Infolentiores vero & contumaciores potest Deus insolenti quâdam & inusitatâ plaga (velut Corah & illius confortes in Principem simul & Sacerdotem murmurantes) opprimere, ut nempe Terræ filii (infima illa & contemptissima Populi pars) os in illos aperiat, & (justissimo Dominationis male partæ pejus gestæ fastidio) hauriat penitus & absorbeat (ille ipse inquam Populus) cujus maximè su'cimento[?] subnixi, hæc in Me & Ecclesiam & Statum construxerunt.
units.tr: But God can crush the more insolent and obstinate with some strange and unusual plague (like Korah and his companions, who murmured against the prince and the priest together), so that the sons of the earth (that lowest and most despised part of the people) open their mouth against them, and (by the most just disgust at a dominion ill-gotten and worse managed) the very people, I say, on whose support they relied to build these things against me, the Church and the state, drink them down and swallow them up entirely.

units.la: Solatium Mihi in Morte præcipuum est illa Pax quam spero cum Deo factam: ad cujus rigidum Tribunal non verebor comparere, & illam causam afferere inter Me & Hostes meos (nullo merito meo infensos) Gladiq tamdiù disputatam, haud dubitans quin illius rectissimo judicio istæ omnes argutiæ refellentur, queis (Sophistarum magis quàm Christianorum more) à successu argumenta in causam faciunt, quasi sic Deus ostenderit illam sibi approbari, cujus sapiens Providentia multa sæpe permittit evenire, quæ à Revelato Dei Verbo ( solâ Bonæ Conscientiæ & Actionum clara, statâ, tutâ Regula ) multum abest ut comprobentur.
units.tr: The chief comfort to me in death is that peace which I hope is made with God: before whose rigid tribunal I shall not hesitate to appear, and to set forth that cause between me and my enemies (who are hostile to me without any merit of mine), long disputed by the sword, not doubting that by His most righteous judgment all those subtleties will be refuted, by which (in the manner of sophists rather than Christians) they make arguments for their cause from success, as if God had thereby shown that it was approved by Him, whose wise providence often permits many things to happen, which are far from being approved by the revealed Word of God (the sole clear, fixed, safe rule of a good conscience and of actions).

units.la: Atque adeo confido, Causæ meæ Justitiâ & Conscientiæ Rectitudine Me tanto Illis suturum in Foro Dei superiorem, quanto Illos supra Me extulit Fortuna in illo Vulgi judicio; qui non cogitat plurima sæpe hominum facinora ad Cælos usque attolli plausu mundi, qui si ex injustitia & scelerato fine censeantur, ex Inferno ascendunt: Quin nec Aura illa secunda quæ Piratæ velum implet, statim ipsius latrocinia & rapinas excusat.
units.tr: And so I am confident that by the justice of my cause and the rectitude of my conscience I shall be as far superior to them in the court of God, as Fortune has raised them above me in that judgment of the crowd; which does not consider that very many deeds of men are often lifted up to the heavens by the applause of the world, which, if they are judged by injustice and a wicked end, rise up from Hell. Nor does that favourable breeze which fills the pirate's sail at once excuse his robberies and plunder.

units.la: Multo interim libentius & alacrius fero perdidisse hanc litem (quam coactus admodum suscepi, ad affercendas Leges Regni, Libertatem & Honorem Parlamentarium, Jura Coronæ, justas Subditorum Immunitates, & veram Religionem Christianam in Doctrina, Disciplina, cæterisque incitamentis & præmiis debitis) quàm si multo Bello potiori ad hæc omnia opprimenda valuissem; id quod nonnulli jam palam faciunt, quicquid priùs simulaverant.
units.tr: Meanwhile I bear much more willingly and cheerfully that I have lost this suit (which I undertook, though greatly under compulsion, to assert the laws of the kingdom, the liberty and honour of Parliament, the rights of the Crown, the just immunities of the subjects, and the true Christian religion in doctrine, discipline, and the other fitting incentives and rewards) than if I had prevailed in a far more powerful war to crush all these things; which some now openly do, whatever they had earlier pretended.

units.la: Plurimum interim mihi proderit Patientia amicorum & Preces ad mitigandam hujus poculi amaritudinem, quam ut à Dei manu (si sic fieri necesse fit) libentius accipiô & haurio, quàm ab illis porrigitur eâ sæva & impia manu contra Me toties levatâ.
units.tr: Meanwhile the patience of my friends and their prayers will greatly help me to soften the bitterness of this cup, which I accept and drink more willingly from the hand of God (if it must be so done), than it is offered by those cruel and impious hands raised so often against me.

units.la: In his autem extremis, plus Hostibus videor quàm Amicis debere: illi finem imponent ærumnosæ hujus vitæ peccatis simul & doloribus, hi forsan Me utrisque adhuc volunt[?] conflictati.
units.tr: In these last extremities, I seem to owe more to my enemies than to my friends: the former will put an end to this troubled life together with its sins and sorrows, the latter perhaps wish me, still struggling with both, to continue.

units.la: Ero plus quam Victor corroborante Me Christo propter quem (Veritatis, Ordinis, Pacis Authorem) haftenus perpetior. In horum enim maxime gratiam contra Errores, Factiones, Confusionem pugnavi.
units.tr: I shall be more than a Victor, with Christ strengthening me, on whose account (the Author of Truth, Order, Peace) I have suffered until now. For it was chiefly for their sake that I fought against Errors, Factions, Confusion.

units.la: Mors jam violenta (si subire oporteat) nihil aliud est quàm Mortalitas coronata Martyrio; ubi naturæ Debitum ex peccato contractum valebit in donum Deo à Patientia & Fide oblatum.
units.tr: A violent death (if it must be undergone) is nothing other than Mortality crowned with Martyrdom, where the Debt of nature contracted through sin will count as a gift offered to God by Patience and Faith.

units.la: Quod humillimè obtestor ut in Misericordia accipiat, & licet Mors ut à Deo immissa, sit peccati mei stipendium, ut vero ab hominibus inflicta summum aliorum in Deum & Me Crimen: quemadmodum tamen spero ita remissa mihi fore peccata mea, ut nihil ex his inamarescat magis Mortis poculum, ita Deum enixè precor ut illis ignoscat, ad quos Crimen Mortis meæ spectat maximè.
units.tr: I humbly beseech Him to accept this in mercy. Although death, as sent by God, is the wages of my sin, as inflicted by men it is the greatest Crime of others against God and me. Yet as I hope my sins will be forgiven me, so that the cup of death may be no more bitter for this, so I earnestly pray God to forgive those to whom the guilt of my death chiefly pertains.

units.la: Illustriora erunt multò Charitatis nostræ in Illos Trophæa, quàm Eorum in Me male administratæ Victoriæ.
units.tr: The Trophies of our Charity towards them will be far more illustrious than the Victories they have won through their mismanagement of me.

units.la: Prosperò quantumvis sint peccato usi, poenitentiâ opus est, ut sit veniæ locus, quam vehementer illis à Deo exposco: nè ve[?] Mors mea ab illis temporaria illorum æterna vindicetur; ita enim mecum reputo, multo minus deprecari oportere præsentaneum cujuscunque Regis interitum, quàm vel minimi e Populo damnationem æternam.
units.tr: However prosperously they have used sin, repentance is needed, so that there may be room for pardon, which I earnestly beg for them from God; lest my death be avenged on them with a temporal penalty and their punishment be eternal. For I reason with myself that one ought much less to pray for the immediate death of any king than for the eternal damnation of even the least of the people.

units.la: Mihi satis ex voto erit, si Me in fluctus expositò tutò Navis ad portum appellat (mirum licet videatur haud aliàs mitigari à Nautis posse quam procellam excitarunt nisi Navigularium suum in Mare deturbando.)
units.tr: It will be enough for my wish if, having been set out upon the waves, the ship brings me safely to harbour. (Strange as it may seem, the sailors cannot otherwise calm the storm they have raised than by throwing their own man overboard into the sea.)

units.la: Deo gratias habeo, nulla hostium immanitas obstabit quo minùs ad illam paratus accedam! quibus in hoc saltem frustra erit malitia, quod non sint voluptatem habituri animam unà cum corpore perimendi: de cujus salute, dum & ipsi videntur & alios jubent desperare, satis clarè ostenderunt haud de eâ efficvaldè sollicitos.
units.tr: I thank God that no savagery of enemies will stand in the way of my approaching that end prepared. In this at least their malice will be in vain: they will not have the pleasure of destroying the soul together with the body. Concerning its salvation, while they seem to despair of it and bid others do so, they have sufficiently shown that they are not very concerned about it.

units.la: Quorum sæva custodia, & nulla Charitas Sacellanorum subsidia arcentium, aperuit Mihi potius quàm obstruxit viam ad Thronum Cœli.
units.tr: Their cruel custody, and the refusal of any charitable help from the chaplains, has opened my way to the throne of Heaven rather than blocked it.

units.la: Ubi tu habitas Rex Regum qui imples Cælum & Terras, qui es Fons Vitæ Æternæ, in quo nulla Umbra Mortis.
units.tr: Where you dwell, King of Kings, who fill Heaven and Earth, who are the Fountain of Eternal Life, in whom there is no shadow of death.

units.la: Tu Deus juste Mortem nobis infligis, & Misericors Servator ex illa liberas, & in illa conservas.
units.tr: You, O just God, inflict death upon us, and you, merciful Saviour, free us from it and preserve us in it.

units.la: Præstat nobis ipsis mori & in Te vivere, quàm vivendo Nobis, Te fraudari.
units.tr: It is better for us to die to ourselves and live in you, than by living to be defrauded of you.

units.la: O Illa Mortis Mea acerbitatem ut Hominis & Regis augentia prosint in Incrementa Gratiarum, & Solatia Animæ ut Christiano.
units.tr: O that the bitterness of my death, as a man and a king, may serve to increase grace, and the consolations of my soul, as a Christian.

units.la: Si Tu mecum sis futurus Domine, nulla sentiam nulla pertimescam mala, etiamsi ambulem in valle lethali Umbræ.
units.tr: If you are going to be with me, Lord, I shall feel no evil and fear no evil, even if I walk in the valley of the shadow of death.

units.la: Cum Morte luctari quivis potest infirmus licet & mortalis, superiorem vero in hac lucta fieri, tuæ Gratiæ opus est qui es Deus Omnipotens & Immortalis.
units.tr: Anyone, even weak and mortal, can wrestle with Death; but that I should prevail in this wrestling is the work of your grace, you who are God Omnipotent and Immortal.

units.la: Tu qui nosti expertus Servator Meus quid sit mori mecum ut Hominem, fac Me vicissim cognoscere, quid sit tecum per Mortem ad Vitam (Deus Meus) transire.
units.tr: You, my Saviour, who have experienced it, know what it is to die with me as a man. In turn, make me know, my God, what it is to pass with you through Death to Life.

units.la: Emoriar licet, scio tamen Te Redemptorem Meum in æternum vivere, etiam Me occidendo addis animum, ut Tibi de Vita Æterna securus credam.
units.tr: I shall die, yet I know that you, my Redeemer, live for ever. Even as you kill me, you add courage, so that I may believe securely in you concerning eternal life.

units.la: O ne favorem Tuum subtraxeris Vita longè potiorem.
units.tr: O, do not withdraw your favour, which is far better than life.

units.la: O ne procul à Me abscesseris, quàm enim prope imminet violenta & sæva mors, ignoro.
units.tr: O, do not depart far from me; for how near violent and cruel death impends, I do not know.

units.la: Vt Omnipotentia Tua (Deus) palam facit, ita potest Omniscientia evertere improba eorum consilia qui conjuravere perniciem meam, vel conjurabunt.
units.tr: As your Omnipotence, O God, makes plain, so your Omniscience can overturn the wicked plans of those who have conspired, or will conspire, my destruction.

units.la: O per Eorum malum animum bonam Tuam voluntatem patefacias.
units.tr: O, reveal your good will through their evil minds.

units.la: Veniam das Mihi, ut Homini, Orare, ut hoc à Me transeat poculum, sed Christianum docuisti Christi exemplo adjicere, Non Mea sed Tua voluntas fiat.
units.tr: You grant me, as a man, to pray that this cup pass from me; but you have taught the Christian, following Christ's example, to add: Not my will, but yours, be done.

units.la: Etiam (Domine) una fiat & eadem voluntas nostra dum in Tuam Mea convertatur, ne sit ulla in Me tanta vitæ cupiditas, quàm ut faciam & feram Voluntatem Tuam tàm in Vita ac Morte.
units.tr: Lord, let our will also be one and the same, while mine is turned into yours, so that there may be in me no such desire for life that I should do and bear your will rather than in life and in death.

units.la: Quemadmodum credo te mihi omnes vitæ meæ condonasse errores, ita spero etiam & Mortis propulsaturum terrores.
units.tr: Just as I believe you have forgiven me all the errors of my life, so I hope you will also ward off the terrors of death.

units.la: Fac ut libens, telinquam hoc Mundi Nihilum, ut in Te cunctis solide fruar, qui mihi Christum fecisti in vita lucrum, in Morte Incrementum.
units.tr: Grant that I may gladly leave this nothingness of the world, so that I may solidly enjoy you in all things, you who have made Christ my gain in life and my increase in death.

units.la: Sint licet fui in Me & in Te officii Intercremptores Mei valde immemores, ne te habeant propterea Misericordiæ Tuæ in Illos immemorem.
units.tr: Though those who have been my murderers may be very forgetful of their duty to me and to you, let not your mercy be forgetful of them on that account.

units.la: Quid enim lucri erit in sanguine meo, vel quid & Regnis commodi, si hi Animâ suâ multentur?
units.tr: For what gain will there be in my blood, or what advantage to kingdoms, if these men are punished in their souls?

units.la: Imo (Domine) non ii solum qui Legitimam Potestatem oppugnarunt, sed qui usurparunt penitus & in Me obverterunt, licet valde mereantur Damnationem, in se non recipiant.
units.tr: Indeed, Lord, not only those who have attacked lawful power, but also those who have wholly usurped it and turned it against me, although they richly deserve damnation, may they not bring it upon themselves.

units.la: Tu Filium Tuum Crucifigentibus Servatorem eundem præstitisti, uno opere ab Illis violenta, & pro Illis voluntaria patientem.
units.tr: You offered the same Saviour to those who crucified your Son: one deed, violent on their part, and voluntarily suffered on his part for them.

units.la: O Vox Sanguinis Illius pro Interfectoribus Meis exaudiatur, & Clamorem Sanguinis Mei ex adverso obruat.
units.tr: O let the voice of that blood be heard for my slayers, and let it overwhelm the cry of my blood against them.

units.la: Fac illos capaces Misericordiæ Tuæ de peccatis suis prius convincendo, nec deludant & perimant Animas suas, falsis amplius Justitiæ in eadem meam coloribus, quos Potestatis iniquissimè usurpatæ conscientia maximè omnium in hos furores extimulat.
units.tr: Make them capable of your mercy by first convicting them of their sins, and do not let them deceive and destroy their souls any more with false colours of justice in my case, which the conscience of having most iniquitously usurped power stirs up above all to these frenzies.

units.la: Tu Domine cognoscis Illorum in Me misericordias valde mendaces, valde immanes, qui se de salute mea sollicitos simulantes nil nisi perniciem struebant.
units.tr: You, Lord, know their very false and very savage pretended mercies towards me: feigning concern for my salvation, they were plotting nothing but my destruction.

units.la: O ne cum illis agas ut Viris Sanguinum & dolosis, sed vincas eorum sævitiam Tua Misericordia, Mea Charitate.
units.tr: O, do not deal with them as with men of blood and deceit, but overcome their savagery by your mercy and mine by charity.

units.la: Et cum de Sanguine Meo inquisiveris, ò sparge Eorum temeratas licet at pœnitentes animas Filii tui Sanguine, ut Interfector Angelus prætereat.
units.tr: And when you call me to account for my blood, O sprinkle their defiled yet repentant souls with the blood of your Son, so that the destroying angel may pass over.

units.la: Quanquam nimis angusta Regna Mea viderentur quæ Me & Illos simul caperent, capax Illud tamen Misericordiæ Tuæ Immensæ Regnum Me & Illos simul complectatur.
units.tr: Although my kingdoms might seem too narrow to hold me and them together, may that kingdom of your immense mercy, able to contain it, embrace me and them together.

units.la: Cum reconciliati Tibi (Domine) ejusdem Redemptoris Sanguine, longe supra evademus ambitiosa illa desideria, & unde fera hæc odia procreantur.
units.tr: Being reconciled to you, Lord, by the blood of the same Redeemer, we shall rise far above those ambitious desires and above that from which these savage hatreds are born.

units.la: Et cum in Me Manus eorum incubuerint crudeli maximè & gravi pondere, O in brachia cadam teneræ Tuæ, & æternæ Misericordiæ.
units.tr: And when their hands fall upon me with cruel and very heavy weight, O let me fall into your tender arms and into eternal mercy.

units.la: Dimitte (Domine) Famulum Tuum in Pace, nam viderunt oculi Mei Salutare Tuum.
units.tr: Lord, let your servant depart in peace, for my eyes have seen your salvation.

units.la: Vota dabunt, quæ bella negarunt.
units.tr: They will give vows which wars denied.

units.la: FINIS.
units.tr: THE END.

units.la: EXPLICANTVR NONNVLLORVM CAPITVM pauca quædam obscuriora.
units.tr: EXPLICATION OF CERTAIN CHAPTERS, a few rather obscure points.

units.la: CAP. I.
units.tr: CHAP. I.

units.la: QVibus partium studiis Deputatorum Electiones.] Innuit præcipue illas Deputatorum ab Oppidis & Municipiis, qui cùm à paucis admodum crearentur facile erat Nobili cuiquam aut Factiosò quem vellet eligendum obtrudere. In his magna Fraus eorum & Ambitus, qui in Regem & Ecclesiam malevoli.
units.tr: To what extent the elections of the Deputies were governed by party zeal. He means especially those Deputies from the towns and boroughs, who, since they were chosen by very few people, it was easy to impose on any nobleman or factious man whom they wished to be elected. In these there was great fraud and ambition, and they were ill-disposed towards the King and the Church.

units.la: CAP. I- I.
units.tr: CHAP. I. I.

units.la: Comitis Straffordiæ] Is erat Thomas Wentworthius Prorex Hiberniæ, qui Læsæ Majestatis postulatus cùm se egregiè defendisset, Lege post latâ condemnatus est, cui Rex (summa vi adhibitâ) invitissimus tandem assensit.
units.tr: Earl of Strafford. This was Thomas Wentworth, Lord Deputy of Ireland, who, when he was accused of high treason, defended himself with great skill, but was condemned after a law had been passed; the King, under great pressure, very unwillingly at last gave his assent to it.

units.la: Legi Damnatoriæ] Illi scilicet recens latæ quæ illum condemnabat.
units.tr: Of the condemnatory bill. That is, the bill just passed which condemned him.

units.la: N Vociferantium Justitiam.] Is enim clamor erat furibundae Plebis [Justitia, fiat Justitia] magnis interim agminibus Parlamenti Curiam & Aulam circumstantes, b his praecipue instigatae, qui timebant ne haec Lex perferretur.
units.tr: Of those clamouring for justice. For this was the outcry of the furious common people, "Justice, let there be justice," meanwhile standing around the Parliament house and the Court in great crowds, roused especially by those who feared that this law would be carried through.

units.la: Scitum illud posterius.] quo cavebatur, ne deinceps obtineret haec in Straffordii causa procedendi ratio, cum sint alias exempla Parlamentaria maxime apud Anglos Authoritatis.
units.tr: That later resolution. By which it was provided that henceforth this method of proceeding in the case of Strafford should not prevail, although there are other Parliamentary precedents of the greatest authority among the English.

units.la: CAP. III.
units.tr: CAP. III.

units.la: Quinque Ordinis Illius Membra.] Hi erant Joannes Pymmius, Joannes Hamdenus, Denselus Holl[?]ius, Arthurus Hafelrigius, & Guilielmus Strodius, quibus, cum Regi deferrentur seditionum capita, postquam denunciasset accusationem, misso ad Domum Inferiorem satellite, spretus illic & repudiatus, perrexit ipse in Domum ut praesens in Iudicium repeteret.
units.tr: The Five Members of That House.] These were John Pym, John Hampden, Denzil Holles, Arthur Haselrig, and William Strode, against whom, when the heads of the sedition were reported to the King, after he had given notice of the accusation, and a sergeant had been sent to the Lower House, the sergeant was spurned and rejected there, and the King himself went into the House to demand them in person for judgment.

units.la: CAP. IV.
units.tr: CHAP. IV.

units.la: Illa Episcoporum Declaratio.] qui cum essent pars Domus Procerum male habiti a Populo & perterriti ut in Domum venire non auderent, protestabantur se pro irritis habituros quae absentibus Ipsis perlata, unde plurimi in Carcerem conjecti.
units.tr: That declaration of the bishops.] who, since they were part of the House of Lords, being roughly treated by the people and so terrified that they did not dare to come into the House to attend, protested that they would hold as void whatever was passed in their absence, whereupon many were thrown into prison.

units.la: Alba Aula.] Domus Regia Londini.
units.tr: Whitehall.] The royal palace at London.

units.la: CAP. V.
units.tr: CHAPTER V.

units.la: Legem de Triennali Parlamento.] Ut cum prius Parlamenta ad arbitrium Regis crebrius nonnunquam aut rarius indicerentur, nuper per plures annos intermissa, jam singulis Trienniis necessario cogerentur.
units.tr: The law concerning the Triennial Parliament. That whereas Parliaments had formerly been summoned at the King's discretion, sometimes more often and sometimes less often, and had lately been suspended for several years, they should now necessarily be called every three years.

units.la: Vi postea, & professa hostilitate infectum reddere. ] Id enim de Rege spargebant, quasi Exercitum nuper contra Scotos conscriptum Vrbi vellet admovere, ut Parlamento vim faceret.
units.tr: Afterwards to undo it by force and open hostility. For they spread this report about the King, as if he meant to move the army lately raised against the Scots towards the City, so as to do violence to Parliament.

units.la: CAP. VI.
units.tr: CHAPTER VI.

units.la: Negativae Vtcis.[?] ] Ita enim vocatur illud Regis suffragium quo contradicit libere cuicunque rogationi, & rata omnia facit, vel irrita.
units.tr: The Negative Vote. For that is what the King's assent is called, by which he freely opposes any bill whatever, and makes all things valid or void.

units.la: CAP. VIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER VIII.

units.la: Cum ab Hulla. ] Hulla Oppidum in Anglia maritimum cujus Arx est munitissima, magnum Regis Hoplophylacium, cujus praefectus Johannes Hothamius Regem illuc venientem exclusit, atque initium bello dedit, qui deinde inclinatæ fidei suspectius cum majore ratu Filio ab ipsis Partis suæ hominibus Capite multatus est.
units.tr: Hull, a maritime town in England, whose castle is very strongly fortified and holds the great royal arsenal. Its governor, John Hotham, shut out the King when he came there and so gave the start to the war. Later, suspected of leaning toward the failing cause, he was beheaded by men of his own party, with greater reason than the King's son.

units.la: Arcis Londinensis Colle. ] Loco supplicii.
units.tr: Of the hill of the London Castle. At the place of execution.

units.la: CAP. IX.
units.tr: CHAPTER IX.

units.la: Supervacua Verborum Parenthesi. ] Ita enim in omnibus ad Duces Belli mandatis Regis semper Personam excipiebant, cum a nullo minus abstinerent.
units.tr: Superfluous words in parentheses. Thus in all the commands given to the generals of war, they always spared the King's person, while abstaining from nothing less.

units.la: Nonnulli recesserint. ] Multi ex utroque Ordine quibus nihil perniciosius, quam si in Regem æquiores crederentur.
units.tr: Some withdrew. Many from both orders, to whom nothing was more harmful than being thought more fair towards the King.

units.la: Lex illa de Radice & Germine. ] Ea enim verba erant rogatæ Legis, ut Hierarchia Ecclesiæ in Radice & Germine aboleretur, quod & frequens usurpabant in seditiosis Orationibus & Clamoribus.
units.tr: That law concerning root and branch. For these were the words of the proposed law, that the hierarchy of the Church should be abolished root and branch, a phrase they often used in seditious speeches and outcries.

units.la: Ita enim omnes vocabant, qui Regi adhærebant, in defensione Prærogativæ suæ & Legum, quos invisos Populo reddebant ut malos Consiliarios, & Arbitrarii Regiminis Promotores, &c.
units.tr: For thus they called all who adhered to the King, in defence of his prerogative and the laws, whom they rendered odious to the people as evil counsellors and promoters of arbitrary government, etc.

units.la: CAP. X.
units.tr: CHAPTER X.

units.la: Id enim quo Populum facerent, ubique venditabant se Regis commodis studere, & si sibi auscultaret Gloriosissimum effecturos.
units.tr: For, in order to win over the people, they everywhere boasted that they were devoted to the king's interests, and that if the people would listen to them they would make him most glorious.

units.la: Æ quolibet Rege Angliæ in Inauguratione sua susceptum.
units.tr: Taken from every King of England at his inauguration.

units.la: CAP. XI. Quam Tyrones sint valdè in Re Politica.]
units.tr: CAP. XI. How very inexperienced men are in matters of state.]

units.la: Multi valdè adolescentes, & tenui fortuna & educatione, Municipiorum praesertim Deputati.
units.tr: Many very young men, of slender means and little education, especially deputies of the boroughs.

units.la: Rescripti Verba. ] Authoritatem [?] dantis Eligendi.
units.tr: Words of the rescript.] The authority [?] of the one granting the power to elect.

units.la: CAP. XII. Rebellione Hibernica.]
units.tr: CAP. XII. The Irish Rebellion.]

units.la: Quæ (turbatis rebus in Anglia sed nondum Bello declarato) erupit.
units.tr: Which broke out while affairs in England were in turmoil but war had not yet been declared.

units.la: Præposterum illum rigorem. ] Qui nec illis locum veniæ relinquebant, proscriptis fortunis & sub hasta positis; cum nondum Illos in potestatem redegissent.
units.tr: That preposterous severity. ] Which left them no room for pardon, their estates being proscribed and put up for sale, although the rebels had not yet been brought under control.

units.la: Armorum aliquâ Cessatione. ] Nempe ut Anni unius induciae fierent, quod factum est ex Sententia eorum qui Regi erant à Consiliis in Hibernia, id vehementer flagitantibus Primariis Belli Ducibus.
units.tr: A certain cessation of arms. ] Namely, that a truce of one year should be made, which was done on the advice of those who were the King's counsellors in Ireland, the chief commanders of the war vehemently demanding it.

units.la: CAP. XIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XIII.

units.la: Lex illa Pacificationis. ] Quâ nuper omnes controversiæ inter Regem & Scotos, qui non ita pridem Arma moverant, compositæ videbantur & dirempte.
units.tr: That law of Pacification. By which, lately, all the disputes between the King and the Scots, who had not long before taken up arms, seemed to be settled and ended.

units.la: Regimen à Iesu Christo institutum[?]. ] Id enim passim Illi crepabant quasi suum illud esset peculiare.
units.tr: Government instituted by Jesus Christ[?]. For the Scots kept clamouring about this everywhere, as if it were their own peculiar possession.

units.la: CAP. XIV.
units.tr: CHAPTER XIV.

units.la: De Fœdere. ] Crescente Regis Fortuna cum jam pars adversa inclinaret, evocatis in auxilium Scotis in Fœdus seu Ligam una juravere.
units.tr: On the Covenant. As the king's fortunes were rising, and the opposing side was already declining, they called in the Scots to help and all swore together to a Covenant, or League.

units.la: Cujus Capita erant præcipua, se Religionem Reformatam in Scotia in Doctrina, Disciplina, Cultu & Regimine conservaturos, contrà, Religionem in Anglia (velut omnium corruptissimam) in his quatuor præfatis, reformaturos, Regimen verò Ecclesiasticum per Episcopos (quod una cum Superstitione, Hæresi, Schismate, Impietate copulantur) penitus extirpaturos: Parlamentorum Privilegia & Regnorum Libertates illimitatò defensuros, Regiam autem Personam & Authoritatem cum Limitatione, in Verâ Religionis Libertatumque Regnorum conservatione (quâ clausulâ, quandocunque libuerit debitam Regi obedientiam subtrahere, quod prætexant decesse non potest) denique Omnes Malignantes & Incendiarios ( quo nomine Omnes Regi adhærentes vel in hoc Fœdus non consensurus includerant ) se deserere conaturos & ad cognitionem Publicam & pœnas trahere.
units.tr: Its chief articles were these: that they would preserve the Reformed Religion in Scotland in doctrine, discipline, worship and government; that, on the contrary, they would reform religion in England (as the most corrupt of all) in these four aforementioned respects; and that they would utterly root out the ecclesiastical government by bishops (which, they said, is joined together with superstition, heresy, schism and impiety); that they would defend without limit the privileges of Parliaments and the liberties of the kingdoms; and that they would defend the royal person and authority only with a limitation, namely in the true preservation of religion and the liberties of the kingdoms (by which proviso they could always find a pretext for withdrawing the due obedience owed to the king whenever they pleased); and finally, that they would endeavour to root out all "Malignants" and "Incendiaries" (under which name they included all who adhered to the king, or who would not consent to this Covenant) and to bring them to public trial and punishment.

units.la: Extat Liber singularis, Judicium Universitatis Oxoniensis de Solenni Liga & Fœdere, in quo singuli Illius Articuli accuratissime examinantur & refelluntur.
units.tr: There is a separate book, the Judgment of the University of Oxford on the Solemn League and Covenant, in which each of its articles is most carefully examined and refuted.

units.la: CAP. XV.
units.tr: CHAP. XV.

units.la: Dei Causa. Bono Fini. ] Verba multum ab illis usurpata præsertim à Concionatoribus è Suggestis in Regem inter manibus[?].
units.tr: For God's cause. For a good end. Words much used by them, especially by the preachers from the pulpits against the King, in their hands[?].

units.la: Forisque laccissimus[?]. ] Quando fuit in Hispania, à Iesuitis & ipso Pontifice.
units.tr: Outside, most harassed[?]. When he was in Spain, by the Jesuits and by the Pontiff himself.

units.la: Religionum farrago. ] In qua trecentas nonnulli Sectas numerant.
units.tr: A medley of religions. In which some count three hundred sects.

units.la: Papistarum auxilia. ] Quorum alii ex Officio Illi militârunt, multi cum alias salvi esse non poterant[?], in Regis Castra compulsi.
units.tr: Auxiliaries of the Papists. Some of whom served him from duty, while many, since they could not otherwise be safe, were driven into the King's camp.

units.la: Pravos Consiliarios. ] Hos enim in omni Declaratione vehementer exagitabant, vel potius sub hoc Nomine Regem ipsum.
units.tr: Wicked counsellors. For these they vehemently harangued in every declaration, or rather, under this name, the King himself.

units.la: CAP. XVI.
units.tr: CHAP. XVI.

units.la: Ludibria in Libro utentes. ] Eo enim audacia ventum erat, ut Ministros in Ecclesiis legentes deturbarent è Sede, & Librum inibi laccrarent[?]; & multa alia Facta & impia.
units.tr: Mockery in the use of the Book.] For things had gone so far in their boldness that they pulled the ministers from their seats while they were reading in the churches, and tore the Book there; and many other deeds, both wicked and impious.

units.la: Æque verba ac sensum? ] Ita enim Directorium quod Liturgiae vice substituebatur Argumentum praescripsit & Materiam Orationum, caeterarumque Sacrarum Celebrationum, permissa Verborum Libertate.
units.tr: Words as well as sense? ] For the Directory, which was substituted in place of the Liturgy, prescribed the subject and matter of the prayers and of the other sacred services, with liberty of words allowed.

units.la: Pars.maxima subsignarent.] Cum alia Lege in Anglia initiari Sacris Ordinibus non possint.
units.tr: The greater part signed.] Since by no other law can men be admitted to the sacred orders in England.

units.la: Quod pro Me totics Orare instituit.] Ter enim vel quater in Matutino Officio pro Rege oratur.
units.tr: That it ordered prayer for me so often.] For three or four times in the Morning Service prayer is said for the King.

units.la: CAP. XVII. Christi Gubernationis ; Sceptri. ] Quibus Libri eorum & Concionces abundant. CAP. XVIII. Tractatu Uxbrigensi.] Uxbrigia Oppidum in Anglia inter Oxonium (in qua Rextum age- bat) & Londinum media, in qua tertio jam Belli Anno missis utrinque Delegatis agebatur de Pace, sed cum nihil aequi impetrari potuisset, frustra. CAP. XX. Conventus Theologorum Insolito more.] Quia mos solitus & legitimus erat, ut Mandato Regis praecunte[?], certi Theologi a Clero in suis seor- sim Provinciis deputarentur in Synodum, quae sua Jura & Privilegia habebat, cum jam pauci essent duntaxat in Concilium vocati quos Uter- que Confessius nominaverat. CAP. XXI. Literas meas interceptas.]
units.tr: CAP. XVII. Christ's Government; Sceptre. With which their books and sermons abound. CAP. XVIII. The Uxbridge Treaty. Uxbridge, a town in England midway between Oxford (where the King was staying) and London, where in the third year of the war, with delegates sent by each side, negotiations for peace were carried on, but since nothing fair could be obtained, they came to nothing. CAP. XX. An Assembly of Divines in an Unusual Manner. For it was the customary and lawful practice that, by the King's command coming first, certain divines were appointed by the clergy from their separate provinces to the synod, which had its own rights and privileges. But now only a few were summoned to the council, those whom each party had nominated. CAP. XXI. My intercepted letters.

units.la: A prælio illo infeinfœlicißimo Nasbejensi cum cætera Regia su-pellectile, & mox odiose divulgatas.
units.tr: From that most unhappy battle of Naseby, together with the rest of the royal baggage, and soon spread abroad to his discredit.

units.la: CAP. XXII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXII.

units.la: Dissimulato habitu. ] Nempe Ecclesiastico, quo duobus vel tribus comitatus ad Scotorum Castra confugit.
units.tr: Disguise laid aside. ] Namely, the ecclesiastical habit, in which, attended by two or three companions, he fled to the Scottish camp.

units.la: CAP. XXV.
units.tr: CHAP. XXV.

units.la: Beneficio Cleri sui. ] Alludit ad id quod in Anglia appellatur Beneficium Cleri, nempe Gratia quædam in nonnullis Capitalibus Iudi-ciis indulta, quâ convictus malefici, si partem aliquam Sacræ Paginæ ut Clericus, id est, Latine legerit, à Capitali Sententia liberatur.
units.tr: Benefit of his clergy. ] He alludes to what in England is called benefit of clergy, namely a certain grace granted in some capital trials, by which a convicted felon, if he reads some part of Holy Scripture as a clerk, that is, reads it in Latin, is freed from the capital sentence.

units.la: CAP. XXVI.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXVI.

units.la: Hac Mei raptione. ] Rex in Holmbeja Custoditus, dum ageretur in Domo Utraque de remittendo Exercitu, nocte quadam à Cohorte Armata interceptus est, & ad Exercitum per-ductus, unde Magnæ Mutationes insecutæ.
units.tr: This seizure of mine. The King, while held in custody at Holmby, was seized one night by an armed troop, while the Houses were debating the disbanding of the army, and was taken to the army, whence great upheavals followed.

units.la: ERRATA.
